x: A reference for every part of the engine: layout, building, formats, subsystems, platforms and verification status. The short introduction — why the engine exists and what problems it solves — is in the README. Rules for agents that change the engine are in AGENTS.md.

engine/ core/ Fixed (Q47.16), Vec3, Random (PCG32), Hash, ECS data/ JSON without floats (numbers go straight to fixed-point) sim/ deterministic simulation, commands, replays net/authority/ authoritative network sessions for FPS world/ spatial structures and chunked world streaming gfx/ RHI + Metal, GL (ES3/WebGL2/GL3.3) and Vulkan (opt-in, docs/vulkan.md) backends, render to texture render/ 3D rendering: lighting, shadows (shadow map + PCF), fog, tone mapping; Dear ImGui over the RHI; glTF/OBJ models, PBR materials, skeletal and procedural animation platform/ window/input/loop: macos, ios, android, web, windows, linux assets/ shared engine assets (Noto Sans font with Cyrillic, OFL) modules/rts/ generic RTS layer: types from data, orders, A*, combat, economy, construction, production, garrisons (Mushroom Wars), roads, fog of war, AI view/ — draws any type from the "view" block in rules.json engine/actor/ actor host on ECS (former modules/fps): movement, combat, vehicles, streaming and match state for any project apps/ fps/ standalone FPS client and server client/ the game (menu, match with bots, HUD, minimap, mouse and touch) editor/ map editor (terrain, objects, roads, players, validation, bot test, Build menu) headless/ bot matches and replay checks without graphics modelview/ viewer for models, clips, materials and every type of a game tools/mcp/ MCP server through which AI agents work with the editor tools/aiversebuild/ packager: exe / app / Xcode project / Gradle project / web templates/ skirmish/ "Iron and Gold" — a Warcraft/Red Alert-style sample mushrooms/ "Mushroom Clash" — a Mushroom Wars-style sample showcase/ Iron and Gold rules with imported models (glTF, OBJ, animations) platform/ packaging templates (Info.plist, Gradle project, HTML shell)

The editor on macOS is AIVERSE Studio (HTML5 UI over the native engine, apps/studio-native + apps/studio-web): ./studio_mac.command [project] builds and opens it. Workspaces Scene / World / Look / Animate / Character / Logic / Publish hold every former editor window as a panel; the Scene has transform tools and brushes (terrain, paint, tiles, fields, objects, roads, rivers), Play runs the game in place, the Agent panel drives the project with Claude Code, Publish builds. The ImGui editor below stays for Linux (and as a fallback on Windows). On Windows the same Studio runs as AiverseStudio.exe (WebView2 UI, Vulkan Scene and Game views): studio_windows.cmd [project] builds and opens it (Visual Studio 2022, CMake, Node.js; at run time the WebView2 Runtime, built into Windows 11, and a Vulkan driver). Both shells are thin: everything else is the shared apps/studio-native/StudioHost (mac/Main.mm Cocoa + Metal, win/Main.cpp Win32 + Vulkan). Floating panel windows and drag-and-drop from Explorer are macOS-only for now. cmake -S . -B build/mac -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release # requires Xcode and CMake cmake --build build/mac -j 8 open build/mac/AiverseEditor.app # editor (project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/skirmish) open build/mac/AiverseGame.app # game ./build/mac/aiverse_tests Another game in the editor: AiverseEditor.app/Contents/MacOS/AiverseEditor --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/mushrooms. To make the game start with a different data set, pass -DAIVERSE_CONTENT_DIR=~/.aiverse/packages/templates/mushrooms.

Each editor process can open its own project with --project <folder>. Without --listen the first instance takes MCP port 47321; if the port is busy, the OS assigns a free one. The actual port is shown in the status bar; the Agent window adds it to the connection config (aiversemcp --port <port>). An automatically assigned port may change after the editor restarts. --listen <port> pins an exact port (on conflict MCP does not start), --listen 0 disables MCP. The link is authenticated with a per-session token file next to the port (~/.aiverse/agent-link/<port>.token, owner-only); see mcp-agent-link.md. Existing MCP clients do not switch between windows on their own.

./build/mac/aiversebuild --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/skirmish --target macos # Builds/macos/<Name>.app (ad-hoc signed) ./build/mac/aiversebuild --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/skirmish --target ios # Builds/ios/xcode/AIVERSE.xcodeproj + simulator build ./build/mac/aiversebuild --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/skirmish --target android # Builds/android/<Name>-release.apk when SDK/NDK and gradle are present ./build/mac/aiversebuild --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/skirmish --target web # Builds/web (requires emsdk) ./build/mac/aiversebuild --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/skirmish --target windows # .exe via mingw-w64 (brew install mingw-w64) or sources + build.bat ./build/mac/aiversebuild --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/skirmish --target all Output goes to <project>/Builds/<platform>/ — only finished builds and the size report. Everything intermediate (CMake trees, packs, re-encoded audio, the Gradle project, xcodebuild data, the editor's size estimate) lives in the hidden Builds/.temp/, which can be deleted at any time. With --generate-only the Gradle project for Android Studio goes to Builds/android/<Name>. The packager removes the old visible _build, _pack, _audio, _estimate folders itself. The same is available in the editor: the Build menu. Generated iOS and Android projects are self-contained (engine sources and content are copied into them), so they can be handed over. For iOS on a device: open the project in Xcode and choose a team under Signing (or --team <TeamID>, or "appleTeamId" in game.json). Identifier, name, version, orientation and icon (icon.png, 1024×1024; generated if missing) are in game.json.

h: Build toolchains: check and automatic install
x: Before building, aiversebuild checks what the platform needs and looks for it beyond PATH (an editor launched from Finder only sees /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin): Homebrew (/opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin), ~/.local/bin, ~/Library/Python/*/bin, ~/emsdk, $EMSDK, ANDROID_HOME / ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, ~/Library/Android/sdk, ~/Android/Sdk, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Android\Sdk, JAVA_HOME, /usr/libexec/java_home, Visual Studio (vswhere) and its own folder ~/.aiverse/toolchains. Found folders are added to PATH for child processes. Platform Needs Installed automatically web CMake, Python 3, Emscripten (emsdk), Ninja — optional emsdk (≈ 400 MB download, ≈ 1.5 GB on disk), CMake + Ninja (≈ 50 MB) android JDK 17–23, Android SDK (platform 35, build-tools, platform-tools), NDK, CMake from the SDK, Gradle everything: Temurin JDK 17, command line tools + sdkmanager (licenses accepted), NDK ≈ 700 MB, Gradle 8.10.2 macos Xcode Command Line Tools, CMake CLT — through Apple's installer (xcode-select --install), CMake ios Xcode (App Store), CMake CMake windows (on Windows) Visual Studio 2022 / Build Tools (C++), CMake CMake; VS — a hint with a winget command linux C++ compiler, CMake CMake aiversebuild --check-toolchain web # what is present and what is missing (--json for the editor and MCP) aiversebuild --install-toolchain web # install what is missing (or one id: emsdk, cmake, jdk, android-ndk, gradle, ...) aiversebuild --project ... --target web --install-missing # install and build right away Without --install-missing, missing tools stop the build with exit code 3 and the line AIVERSE_MISSING_TOOLCHAIN web: emsdk (the editor recognizes it). In the editor, the Build window shows for the selected platform what was found (paths, versions) and what is missing, with an Install automatically button and an "Install missing tools automatically" checkbox; progress is in the Console (text can be selected and copied; "Open logs folder" opens <engine>/logs). Agents do the same over MCP: toolchain_check, toolchain_install, build_start {"installMissing": true}. Everything is installed into ~/.aiverse/toolchains (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.aiverse\toolchains; another folder — the AIVERSE_TOOLCHAINS_DIR variable) without sudo and without system changes: emsdk/, py/ (a venv with cmake and ninja), cmake/, ninja/, jdk-17/, android-sdk/, gradle-8.10.2/. Re-running is safe (finished parts are skipped). To remove everything installed, delete that folder. Exceptions: Command Line Tools are installed by Apple's installer, and if the user's Android SDK is found, sdkmanager installs the missing packages into it.

Game content (the game folder + engine/assets) goes into a build as a single file content/content.rpak: each file is zstd-compressed separately, identical files are stored once, already compressed formats (png, ogg, mp3, …) are stored as is. The engine mounts content.rpak automatically; files in the pack take precedence over files in the folder, so without a pack (during development) everything works as before. platform::mountPack("patch.rpak") mounts a pack on top (patch, DLC). Every build prints a size report and writes it to dist/<platform>/size-report.txt. aiversebuild ... --no-pack # ship folders as is (debugging) aiversebuild ... --pack-level 9 # zstd level (default 19 for Release, 3 for Debug) assetpipe pack -o content.rpak ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/skirmish engine/assets=engine # build a pack by hand assetpipe list content.rpak # files, sizes, compression assetpipe verify content.rpak # unpack everything and check hashes assetpipe extract content.rpak out/ assetpipe diff old.rpak new.rpak # what changed between versions (for patches) What the build does not need is listed in .rpakignore in the game folder (masks *, ?; folder/ — directories only). Hidden files (.git, .DS_Store), *.rpl replays and nested *.rpak are always skipped. Pack builds are reproducible: identical content gives a byte-identical file; the pack's "content hash" identifies the data set.

For packaged client builds, packaging.engineModules can select optional native engine modules. Omitting the field keeps the historical defaults; an explicit empty array disables every selectable module. The supported names are auto (detect modules from project assets and settings), strata (virtual geometry staging), runtime-autolod (generate missing LODs at runtime), vulkan (Windows, Linux, Android only), spine (Spine UI animation and its Lua API), gamepad (controller input and action bindings), fx (SpectraFX particles and the RTS effect bridge), fbx (runtime FBX import using ufbx), legacy-models (runtime VOX/VXL, PLY/STL, 3DS, DAE, MDX/MDL, 3DO and W3D loaders), obj (runtime OBJ loader), blp (BLP1/BLP2 texture decoding), city-client (persistent city server client), and the simulation systems that run only when their data asks for them: traffic (rules "traffic"), bw-ai (rules ai.controller: "bw"), encounters, commerce, careers, arsenal (rules blocks of those names) and mapgen (maps or world bodies with a "generate" block). ["auto"] selects Spine and gamepad from game.json, FX from project JSON and FX assets, model importers/BLP from source files, and the simulation systems from the composed rules, per-map rules overrides and map blocks (every JSON under maps/ and the maps game.json lists). The packager rejects data that needs an excluded simulation system. A model with a <source>.glb sidecar does not need its source-format loader. Detection is conservative: unused source files may keep a loader in the build, while runtime-generated paths, script-only calls, city connections, Strata and runtime LOD generation require explicit names such as ["auto", "city-client"]. The absence of engineModules retains the legacy defaults. A target-specific packaging.targets.web.engineModules or similar overrides the shared list. For example, "packaging": {"engineModules": [], "targets": {"windows": {"engineModules": ["vulkan"]}}} builds without these optional modules except for Vulkan on Windows. Declare runtime-autolod when the game relies on runtime LOD generation; otherwise prepare LODs before packaging. Declare spine if game.json defines Spine views or UI Lua scripts call the spine table. The packager rejects declared Spine views when this module is excluded; script-only use must be listed explicitly. Declare gamepad if game.json has gamepad settings or the game is intended to support controllers. The packager rejects declared gamepad settings when the module is excluded. Declare fx if the game has fx/fx.json, GPU routes, graph assets, or scripts that request particle effects. The packager rejects known FX resources when fx is excluded; script-only requests emit a runtime warning and no effect. Declare fbx when the client must import FBX at runtime. Without it, convert FBX assets to GLB before packaging; the loader reports a clear error for FBX without a converted .glb sidecar. Host conversion tools retain FBX support. Declare legacy-models if clients load any of those model formats directly. Without it, convert them to GLB before packaging. Host conversion tools retain the legacy loaders. Declare obj if the client loads OBJ directly; otherwise convert OBJ assets to GLB before packaging. Host conversion tools retain OBJ support. Declare blp if the client reads BLP textures, including BLP images referenced by model files. Without it, convert those textures before packaging. Host conversion tools retain BLP support. Declare city-client if the game uses the AIVERSE_CITY server connection. With the module excluded, setting AIVERSE_CITY produces an error when a match starts. Declare the simulation systems the data uses (or use auto). Each excluded system is replaced by an adapter in engine/game/disabled/ (CMake aiverse_game_module, options AIVERSE_GAME_WITH_*). The adapter keeps the system inactive, so games that do not use it run, hash and save exactly as with the full module; data that needs it fails at match start with a readable error (Web bu

Formats the engine does not know (zip, tar, dmg, archives of other games) are added as unpacker plugins without rebuilding the engine: a folder with unpacker.json and a program in any language (protocol: tools/unpackers/PROTOCOL.md). Unpackers run only in build tools: a foreign archive becomes files inside an .rpak, and the game still reads only .rpak. Out of the box: zip (and .oramap), tar, dmg, Warcraft I/II archives (.WAR/.SUD/.INS), Westwood .PAK (Dune II, Lands of Lore, Kyrandia), Z by the Bitmap Brothers (.PAC, .RSC). assetpipe formats # which formats are known assetpipe probe ~/Downloads/Warcraft2/war2/DATA/* # what these files are assetpipe list MAINDAT.WAR # what is inside assetpipe import -o war2.rpak MAINDAT.WAR=imported/war2 SFXDAT.SUD=imported/war2/sfx assetpipe unpackers new tools/unpackers myformat # scaffold for a new unpacker assetpipe unpackers check # check all plugins Every command has --json — that is how the MCP server calls them. game.json can list "imports", and aiversebuild unpacks them into the pack during the build ("optional": true — if the file is missing on this machine, the build goes on without it). A pack with imported third-party content is flagged "external": such builds are for personal use only and must not be committed or distributed.

An importer turns your copy of a classic game into a game folder for the engine. Dune II and Total Annihilation are available now: python3 tools/importers/dune2/import.py --source "~/Downloads/Dune II" --out ~/AiverseGames/dune2 aiversebuild --project ~/AiverseGames/dune2 --target macos The result is a 2D game in the engine's format (docs/game-format.md, "2D games"): a top-down camera, 66 campaign missions with a tile layer (tilesets/dune.json from ICON.ICN: sand, rock, dunes, mountains, spice with autotiling), unit sprites from SHP (5 directions with mirroring, tank turrets layered over the hull) and buildings from ICN tiles (construction, ruins, animation), house colour from magenta shades. Plus rules.json (our Dune II balance on engine blocks), CPS images and WSA animations as PNG, VOC sounds → WAV + audio.json, names in English and Russian. Terrain is approximate: the original landscape generator is not used, bases stand on rock, spice comes from Field=, mission quotas are triggers. Infantry, the ornithopter and the carryall are still drawn as 3D shapes. The folder is marked "external": true — it must not be committed or distributed. Total Annihilation (tools/importers/ta): the archives of your copy (.hpi, .ufo, .ccx, .gp3, read by the hpi unpacker: header cipher, LZ77 and zlib chunks) or an extracted folder: python3 tools/importers/ta/import.py --source "~/Games/TotalA" --out ~/AiverseGames/ta Units (units/*.fbi) become types with costs, worker / build time, health, speed, sight, radar / sonar / jammers, stealth, air / naval / hover / underwater layers, extractors, wind / tidal generators, metal makers, air repair pads and commanders; build menus come from guis/*.gui and download/*.tdf; weapons (weapons/*.tdf) from range, reload, damage, area, velocity, anti-air and torpedo flags; stockpiled weapons (nukes) become abilities with a stockpile, interceptors an intercept, explosions death blasts; features (features/**.tdf) reclaimable nodes; maps (maps/*.tnt + .ota) heightfield maps with water below the sea level, start positions, features, metal spots, wind and tide. .3do models and .gaf textures are copied next to them (the engine reads them itself). Scale: 1 cell = 16 TA pixels. Not converted: unit scripts (.cob; use procedural animation), sounds, campaign missions, the metal map of tiles (metal spots come from metal features). The folder is marked "external": true.

A project is a folder anywhere on disk (game.json, rules.json, maps/, ...). Its root holds the project file <Name>.aiverse — opened with a double click, like .uproject in Unreal or project.godot. game.json stays the game manifest (read by the client, aiversebuild, packs); .aiverse only marks the folder as a project and stores editor information: {"format": 1, "name": "My Strategy", "engine": "0.2.0", "manifest": "game.json", "created": "2026-10-28"} It is created with the project (hub "New project", MCP create_project); an older project without it gets one on first open in the editor. Templates in templates/*/ already have one (it is not copied into a new project: that gets its own). Everywhere the editor accepts a project path, both .aiverse and the folder work: aiverse_editor "My Strategy.aiverse", --project, "Open…" in the hub (shows .aiverse and project folders), recent projects, MCP open_game, aiversebuild --project x.aiverse. .aiverse does not go into a build. Projects made before the AIVERSE rename keep their <Name>.rtsproj: it opens the same way everywhere, is rewritten in place and is never renamed; when a folder has both, .aiverse wins. Double click. On start the editor associates .aiverse with itself (per user, without admin rights) if there is no association or it points to another editor instance; it does not override another program you chose. Manually: "Project → Make the editor the default app for .aiverse"; the state is shown at the bottom left of the hub. Disable with AIVERSE_FILE_ASSOC=off. macOS: the com.aiverse.project type is declared in the Info.plist of AiverseEditor.app (platform/macos/EditorInfo.plist.in; the rtsproj.icns document icon is drawn by aiverse_projicon from the editor logo apps/editor/branding/icon_1024.png); the editor registers the bundle in LaunchServices (lsregister -f) and becomes the default handler. A double click and open -a AiverseEditor x.aiverse open the project in the running editor (if the map has unsaved changes, it asks whether to save). Windows: HKCU\Software\Classes\.aiverse (+ .rtsproj) → AIVERSE.Project (icon %USERPROFILE%\.aiverse\icons\rtsproj.ico, command "<aiverse_editor.exe>" "%1"). If Windows already has another program chosen for .aiverse, the hub suggests "Open with → Always". Linux: the application/x-aiverse-project type (~/.local/share/mime/packages/aiverse-project.xml), ~/.local/share/applications/aiverse-editor.desktop (Exec=<editor> %f), icons in ~/.local/share/icons/hicolor, the default app in ~/.config/mimeapps.list; update-mime-database, update-desktop-database, xdg-mime are called if installed.

The Make a game button in the projects window (and Project → Make a game…): give a folder or a link with art, music and texts, describe the idea (or nothing — the wizard chooses itself) and get a finished .aiverse project: a game on a suitable template, a step-by-step tutorial (hard) and in-battle hints (soft), levels with stars and rewards, meta (menu, upgrades, shop, daily reward, profile, settings), ads and purchases if wanted, languages, an icon and a splash screen from the art. The wizard plays through the tutorial with a bot and checks the levels itself; what was assigned and what to check is in the project's WIZARD.md. For agents: MCP game_make_options / game_make_plan / game_make. Details: game-wizard.md.

An object type is a set of optional blocks; whatever is set, the object can do: Block Meaning health health, armor, armor type, regeneration move speed, layer (ground/air/naval), radius structure a building with a footprint size on the grid weapons range, damage, damage type, cooldown, projectile, splash, which layers it hits cost resources, time, supply produces / builds what it trains / what it builds gather / resourceNode / dropoff resource gathering (Warcraft/StarCraft) income / storage + resource "kind": "flow" flow economy (Total Annihilation) supply provides supply requires tech tree garrison + entersGarrison garrison buildings, sending a percentage of troops, capture (Mushroom Wars) view appearance: shape, scale, color Global: resources, damageTable (damage type × armor type), supplyCap, victory. Map: size, terrain (rows: . ground, ~ water, # rock, , no building, = ford; heights), players and teams, starting resources, objects, roads, roadsOnly.

A game is translated without changing rules.json: names in the data are text in the game's source language, translations live in <project>/lang/<language>.json under keys like type.footman, resource.gold, map.valley.title… Menu and HUD strings are in engine/assets/lang/ (currently English and Russian); a game can override any of them. // game.json "sourceLanguage": "en", "languages": ["en", "ru"] ./build/mac/aiverse_i18n extract --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/skirmish --lang de --write # lang/de.json skeleton, new strings marked // TODO ./build/mac/aiverse_i18n check --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/skirmish # placeholders, plural forms, untranslated strings The language is chosen as follows: the player's choice in the menu (remembered) → the system language → the game's source language. For testing: --lang ru, AIVERSE_LANG=ru, the pseudo-language --lang qps (all strings distorted and longer — untranslated text and overflow are obvious). Plural forms follow CLDR ("1 second / 2 seconds / 5 seconds"). More: engine/i18n/README.md.

The client's menu, HUD, command card, minimap and pause are RmlUi documents (.rml markup, .rcss styles), not code. The engine draws them through its RHI (GL/Metal); fonts go through stb_truetype (Latin + Cyrillic). Default documents: engine/assets/ui/ (menu.rml, hud.rml, theme.rcss). A game overrides any file by putting ui/<same name> into its folder: for example, only ui/theme.rcss — its own colours with the default markup. The game font is fonts/ui.ttf. Data comes from the game model (the field list is in a comment in hud.rml); button presses become simulation commands (apps/client/ClientUi.cpp). Sizes are in dp — the UI scales with screen density; on touch devices the root has the touch class (bigger buttons). F8 in the client opens the RmlUi debugger (element tree, styles, log). The game skin is ui/skin.rcss (loaded after theme.rcss in every document: colours, borders, buttons, layout) and the heading font fonts/title.ttf (family title). Each prototype in templates/ has its own skin. The portrait layout (@media (orientation: portrait)) is in the engine theme; on a PC, check it with --size 540x960. Texts in documents are written as keys @menu.play: the translation is taken from engine/assets/lang (and the game's lang/) when the document loads; changing the language in the menu reloads the documents. On-screen keyboard (engine/ui/UiKeyboard.*): built on RmlUi, opens when an input field gets focus on touch devices (on a PC — AIVERSE_OSK=1). Layouts (en, ru, symbols; Shift, Caps on double tap, language switch) are in keyboard.json, the look in keyboard.rml / keyboard.rcss; a game replaces any of these files in its ui/. If the cursor is at the bottom of the screen, the keyboard moves to the top. Multiplayer (lobby.rml, apps/client/Lobby.cpp): server address and name, quick play through server queues, the room list (join / watch), your own room (slots, bots, ready state, start, chat). The match is run by NetClient: attach(sim), advance(dt) instead of sim.advance(dt), commands come from slot match().localSlot (0 — spectator); bots the server assigned to this client are computed here too.

The simulation is bit-identical on every platform: fixed-point only, its own RNG, commands in canonical order, checksums in replays. Verified: Linux x86-64 (GCC, Clang, MinGW), Linux ARM64 (GCC), macOS ARM64 (AppleClang) — identical match checksums.

A single forward pass: sun (Lambert + specular), a shadow map fitted to the visible part of the map and snapped to texels, hardware PCF (1/4/9 taps), hemispheric ambient, distance fog, ACES. Shadow quality is chosen by GPU (low for old Mali/Adreno/PowerVR) and can be changed in the pause menu.

engine/net is multiplayer for any game on the engine, with no game code. Only commands travel over the network: the simulation is deterministic, so everyone has the same state. Transport: UDP with its own reliability layer (iOS, Android, PC) and WebSocket (HTML5; on native — a fallback when UDP is blocked). Address: host[:27015], udp://…, ws://host:27016. Rollback lockstep. The server confirms each tick's input: when commands from all players have arrived or the deadline (lagToleranceMs) has passed; late commands move to the next tick — one lagging player does not stop the others. The client does not wait for confirmation: it plays ahead with its own commands and, on divergence, restores a snapshot and re-simulates (a snapshot takes ~10 µs). rollbackWindow: 0 is classic lockstep for weak devices. The aiverse_server does not need the game content: rooms (slots, bots, spectators, ready state, data version check), automatic matchmaking through queues from server.json (Elo rating with a widening window, a shared map, team balance, filling with bots), checksum comparison (desync), replays (aiverse_headless --replay plays them), reconnection, delayed spectators. Leaving = surrender. A player who left (or did not return within reconnectGraceSec) surrenders with a command in the shared input stream: the outcome is decided by the simulation, identically for everyone, and is visible in the replay. Rating is deducted. Server verdict. If nobody confirmed the outcome (everyone left, results disagree), the server replays the match in a background thread on its own game data ("games" in server.json) and decides the winner itself. Reconnection: after a network drop the client reconnects on its own (NetClient(address, …) or setReconnect), the simulation keeps running — the server sends only the input after the last confirmed tick. If the game was restarted, the client receives the whole history and re-simulates the match from the start. In the game: NetClient (engine/net/NetClient.h) handles the lobby and the match. The game builds a Simulation from match() and calls attach(sim), then advance(dt) instead of sim.advance(dt); the UI still submits commands through sim.submit(). Texts: the server sends no ready-made phrases — only localization keys with arguments (NetText): players in one match may use different languages. The client translates them with net::translate(loc, event.text) and net::displayName(...) from engine/net/NetLocalize.h; strings live in engine/assets/lang/*.json under net.*. Queue names in server.json are keys too ("@net.queue.1v1"). ./build/mac/aiverse_server --config apps/server/server.json # UDP 27015, WebSocket 27016 ./build/mac/aiverse_netbot --server 127.0.0.1 --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/mushrooms --queue 1v1 # a bot in the queue ./build/mac/aiverse_netbot --server ws://127.0.0.1:27016 --project ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/mushrooms --queue 1v1 ./build/mac/aiverse_net_tests # network tests docker build -f apps/server/Dockerfile -t aiverse-server . # server in a container For wss:// (a game page served over HTTPS), put a TLS proxy (nginx, Caddy) in front of the server.

engine/audio is a mixer, sound banks from data, procedural synthesis and music; output goes through miniaudio (CoreAudio, AAudio/OpenSL ES, Web Audio, WASAPI, ALSA/PulseAudio). engine/audio turns simulation events into sounds; it writes nothing into the simulation. No device — the game runs silently. No audio.json — the game simply has no sound. A game's audio is the audio.json file next to game.json (another name: "audio" in game.json). The full format is in docs/game-format.md, section audio.json; in short: { "volume": { "sfx": 0.9, "music": 0.6, "voice": 1, "ui": 0.7, "ambient": 0.7 }, "sounds": { "sword": { "files": ["sfx/sword1.ogg", "sfx/sword2.ogg"], "pitch": [0.9, 1.1], "maxInstances": 3, "cooldown": 0.06 }, "alarm": { "file": "voice/under_attack.ogg", "bus": "voice", "priority": 10 }, "blip": { "synth": { "wave": "square", "freq": [880, 440], "duration": 0.08 }, "bus": "ui" } }, "music": { "menu": "music/menu.ogg", "match": { "files": ["music/a.ogg", "music/b.ogg"], "shuffle": true } }, "events": { "died": "death", "underAttack": "alarm", "notEnough.gold": "need_gold" }, "weapons": { "bow": { "attack": "bow_release", "hit": "arrow_hit" } }, "abilities": { "heal": "heal_cast" }, "types": { "footman": { "select": "footman_what", "move": "footman_yes", "died": "death_human" } } } What Meaning formats WAV, OGG Vorbis, MP3, FLAC; "synth" — a sound from parameters (sine/square/saw/triangle/noise, frequency sweep, envelope, vibrato, filter, layers) buses sfx and ambient are positional (3D: attenuation, panning, height); voice, ui, music are not distance spatial: attenuation model, ranges, "air" (highs fade with distance), reverb grows with distance, speed of sound; a sound can have its own ranges and far — a distant variant with a crossfade maxInstances, cooldown, priority thinning out in big battles: 40 archers don't produce 40 identical shots groups shared limits for several sounds (all melee, all explosions, a whole bus): max, cooldown, which to drop — farthest (default: distant combat does not cut off what is on screen), oldest, quietest, none events (cues) attack hit miss died spawned trainStarted ready buildPlaced buildDone gathered captured lost playerDefeated victory defeat notEnough notEnoughSupply noRoom researched levelUp ability readyToPlace sold regionClaimed wave lowPower upgraded message underAttack baseUnderAttack select move attackOrder buildOrder click error sound lookup type → weapon/ability by id → events music playlists menu, match, battle, victory, defeat (and match.<map>); crossfade, intro + seamless loops, layers by combat intensity, transitions on beats/bars, stingers, ducking under voice compression at build time aiversebuild re-encodes audio per platform: ADPCM for effects, Vorbis for music, lower sample rate, mono; desktop/mobile/web profiles in audio.json → build; --audio off — no re-encoding Combat sounds are heard only where there is no fog of war; "we are under attack" comes with a pause and only if the camera is looking elsewhere. Volume (master and music) is in the pause menu and stored in userDataDir/audio.cfg. On a phone, audio pauses when the app goes to the background. Debugging without a sound card: AIVERSE_AUDIO=null (a real audio thread without hardware), AIVERSE_AUDIO=off, AIVERSE_AUDIO_CAPTURE=/tmp/mix.wav — record everything that played into a WAV.

A type is drawn from its "view" block: a built-in shape ("shape") or a model file ("model") — glTF 2.0 (.glb, .gltf + .bin + images) and OBJ + MTL. Everything goes through one pipeline: PBR materials (metallic-roughness): base colour, normal, metallic-roughness, occlusion, emissive; opaque / mask / blend transparency, double-sided, unlit, material variants (KHR_materials_variants), overrides in "materials". Player colour: on the whole material, by a mask texture, by texture alpha (as in Warcraft III) or by vertex alpha. Skeletal animation on the GPU (4 influences, any number of bones), clips per unit state (idle, move, attack, gather, build, die, spawn, hit, cast…), smooth transitions, layers with a bone mask (attacking with the upper body while walking), stride speed from the actual speed. Procedural animation on any model node or shape: bobbing, spinning (mills, propellers), wheels by distance travelled, turret aiming at the target, recoil, leaning into turns, falling and sinking on death and more; driven by states and combat events. Quality tiers for materials (low / medium / high) are chosen by GPU, like shadows; AIVERSE_MATERIALS=low|medium|high overrides it for testing. Crowds: clips are baked into a texture, identical units are drawn with instancing (300 animated units — 61 draw calls instead of 1801); model LODs by distance; animation off screen and far away updates less often. Advanced animation: walk/run blend space, additive clips (breathing, recoil), foot IK on terrain, head turning towards the target, vehicles tilting on slopes, morph targets (blend shapes) on the GPU. Sockets: a weapon in the hand, cargo on the back (by the carried resource), projectile launch points, effect points (smoke, fire, exhaust); clip events and GameView::events()/effects() for sound and particles. Stages: scaffolding and construction stages, a damaged variant by health, dissolve on spawn and death, selection outline, a translucent ghost while placing a building, portraits. Formats: also FBX (ufbx) and compressed KTX2 textures (ETC2/BC/ASTC, staying compressed on the GPU); Collada, 3DS, PLY, STL; MagicaVoxel .vox and .vxl/.hva voxels (Tiberian Sun, Red Alert 2); classic RTS models from the user's copy of the game: Warcraft III .mdx/.mdl (+ BLP), Total Annihilation .3do, C&C Generals .w3d (+ DDS). Everything else assimp reads (.blend, .lwo, .x, .ms3d, .md2/.md3, .smd, .b3d…) is converted to glTF by the modelconv utility: the editor does it itself on open and save, and the packager puts only the result into the package. Materials on request: a shared materials.json library (inheritance via base), assigning a material to a model node ("assign": {"Turret": "steel"}), procedural seamless textures with normal maps and player-colour masks; the Materials window with a preview and the MCP operations material_* / texture_generate for agents. A broken model does not break the game: the type is drawn as a shape and the reason goes to the editor console. Viewing: aiverse_modelview model.glb@Walk or aiverse_modelview --game ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/showcase (every type of a game, as the game draws it); in the editor — the Models window (clips, nodes, materials, portrait, reload when the model file is saved). Example: ~/.aiverse/packages/templates/showcase; full format: models.md.

Dynamic lights are designed for old Android devices (Mali-T, Adreno 3xx/4xx): all lights are drawn into a small light map above the visible ground, and the shader takes light with a single texture sample however many lights there are. Tiers: off, low (128² map, updated every other frame), medium (256²), high (+ 8 per-pixel lights with specular). Chosen by GPU, like shadows; manually: AIVERSE_LIGHTS=…. If frames keep missing the budget during a match, the client lowers lights and shadows step by step (the most expensive and least noticeable first) and restores one step after a heavy battle; choosing shadows manually in the menu turns this off (AIVERSE_ADAPTIVE=off). Type and combat lights — view.light (campfires, forges, glowing mushrooms), flashes from shots, hits and explosions, projectile lights (attackLight, projectileLight, hitLight, deathLight), ability lights (abilityLights; by default the colour follows the effect: damage — orange, healing — green), halo glows instead of expensive bloom. Fog of war hides the flashes. Day and night, weather — the lighting block in game.json or in a map: time, dayLength, nightLevel, clouds, wind, storm (cloud shadows and lightning, identical in replays), preset: desert, snow, volcanic, overcast, cave (underground: eternal night, light only from sources). At night emissive materials glow brighter and lights reflect on water. Map lights — the lights array in a map (lanterns, campfires, lava). Contact shadows and AO — soft spots under units and around buildings, on every tier (contactShadow, contactShape on the type). Editor — the "Lighting" window: preview of the time of day and storms, light quality tier, list of lights. For agents: light_add, light_update, light_delete, light_list, lighting_set, view_lighting. The field format is in the header of engine/view/game/GameLights.h. Test variables: AIVERSE_TIME_OF_DAY, AIVERSE_NIGHT, AIVERSE_CLOUDS, AIVERSE_STORM.

An agent building a game without code checks mechanics precisely, not only with a bot match. scenario_run — a scenario on a copy of the open map (nothing is saved): clear (an empty map without objects, waves and starting units), spawn with names ("id": "foot", "count": 3 → foot#1..3, "foot" — all), commands by second (the same keys as play_command), bots for some slots, checks with a pass/fail result (alive, dead, count, hp, resource, event, trigger, variable, distance, status, result + comparison), watch + every (object state over time), events (event log). play_units / play_command — commands in a live test in the Game window (previously only inside the editor, now visible to MCP clients). Object references: ids from play_units, id names from the map or a filter {type, owner, tags, kind, area, near + radius}; queue: true — queue (Shift), ability by id. match_run — plus a log of fired triggers and events (event log by name). rules_lint — keys in rules.json and the map that the loader does not read (typos, a block in the wrong place), with a hint ("did you mean 'armor'?"). It runs on the real loader (JsonAccessLog in engine/data/Json.h); rules_set, rules_merge and map_validate report such keys immediately. rules_schema — part: "keys": every key the loader asks for in each block (types.*.weapons[]), collected across all games, and keys missing from docs/game-format.md; part: "doc" — the document itself. The simulation event kEvTriggerFired (for tools and presentation only, not part of the checksum). Branch agent-mech-tools.

Full-screen effects on top of the 3D scene are set with data: the "postfx" block in game.json (a map can override it). There is bloom, colour grading, LUT, vignette, tilt-shift, sun rays, FXAA, grain, aberration, sharpening, pixelation, posterization, tint and letterbox, plus ready-made sets (cinematic, vivid, noir, retro, miniature, sunset, winter, night vision). Each effect has minQuality. The tier is chosen by GPU: weak Android devices get "low", phones "medium", PCs "high"; AIVERSE_POSTFX overrides it. Without effects, post-processing costs nothing. Light effects are combined into one pass; heavy ones (bloom, FXAA, rays) add their own. Editor: the Post effects window (preview of tiers, a table of frame cost per device class). MCP: postfx_catalog/get/add/set/remove/preset/enable/estimate/lut_neutral, view_postfx. Responses to changes include an ms/frame estimate and warnings about heavy effects. Details: docs/postfx.md.

✅ Linux: client, editor, tests; Windows .exe (MinGW cross-build, run under Wine). ✅ Vulkan backend on Linux (Mesa lavapipe): every template renders as on GL, offscreen backend test; Windows MinGW build under Wine (winevulkan over lavapipe). ⏳ Vulkan on real GPUs, MSVC and Android (not built) — docs/vulkan.md § Verification. ✅ macOS: build, tests, running the game on Metal; aiversebuild → .app and an iOS project (+ simulator build). ✅ Web: builds (Emscripten 3.1.50), a match runs in headless Chromium (WebGL2/SwiftShader). ⏳ Android: the Gradle project is generated; the APK and an emulator run are in CI (job android), not built locally. ⏳ Windows on real hardware and iOS on a device — not run (in CI: MSVC build and iOS simulator build).

.github/workflows/ci.yml on every push to master/agent-* and on pull requests: Job What it does linux gcc and clang (x64) + gcc (ARM64), warnings as errors, tests, bot matches, screenshots under Xvfb windows-msvc Visual Studio 2022, tests, matches, aiversebuild --target windows windows-mingw MinGW-w64 cross-build, tests and matches under Wine macos universal Xcode build, tests, matches, aiversebuild → .app and an iOS project with a simulator build android .so via the NDK, APK via aiversebuild; in the emulator: launch → tap → background → return → "back" → relaunch, logcat checked for crashes web Emscripten, a match in headless Chromium, console and frame checks determinism compares match checksums (both games × 3 seeds) from all platforms — they must match bit for bit Screenshots, the APK, the web build and the .app are kept as run artifacts. Locally: # Windows .exe from Linux/macOS cmake -S . -B build/mingw -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=platform/cmake/mingw-w64.cmake # bot matches on every game → a checksum file (compare between machines with diff) .github/scripts/headless-checksums.sh build/linux-release/aiverse_headless sums.txt # smoke test of the web build node platform/web/smoke.mjs build/web Command-line parameters in the web build are passed through the URL: index.html?map=0&spectate = --map 0 --spectate. On-screen keyboard: platform::startTextInput(area) / stopTextInput() open and close it on iOS, Android and in mobile browsers (on desktop they do nothing). Text arrives as Char events in any language, Backspace/Enter as KeyDown/KeyUp; softKeyboardHeight() and the KeyboardChanged event report how much of the screen is covered at the bottom, and TextInputEnded reports that the user closed the keyboard. The UI (UiLayer) calls this itself on focus in <input type="text|password|search|email|number"> and <textarea>. Other mobile and browser features in Platform.h: safeAreaInsets() — insets for the camera notch, rounded corners, the home indicator and system bars (iOS, Android, mobile Safari/Chrome; 0 on desktop, on a MacBook with a notch — in full screen). setFullscreen() / isFullscreen(); built-in toggles — F11 (Windows, Linux, web), Alt+Enter (Windows). In the browser, full screen also locks the orientation (AppConfig::orientation). Android: the Back button reaches the game as Key::Escape; full screen with auto-hiding bars; a physical keyboard and mouse (Chromebook, DeX) produce ordinary key and mouse events. iPad: Magic Keyboard / Bluetooth keyboard, mouse and trackpad (right click, hover, scrolling). The clipboard works everywhere; in the browser Ctrl/Cmd+V reaches the game after the browser hands over the text. Web: userDataDir() is stored in IndexedDB — settings and saves survive a page reload.

Any platform SDK is connected as a plugin in its native language — Java (Android), Objective-C (iOS/macOS), JavaScript (web) or C++ — through one asynchronous bridge, engine/platform/Plugins.h. A game uses the shared APIs aiverse::store (purchases) and aiverse::ads (ads) from engine/services, and the provider is chosen per platform in game.json. Ready plugins in plugins/: App Store, Google Play, RuStore, Yandex Games (web: purchases and ads), Steam (purchases through the Inventory Service and DLC, Windows/Linux/macOS), Yandex Mobile Ads, AdMob, AppLovin MAX, ironSource (Unity LevelPlay). A build contains only the plugins the game selects ("plugins" in game.json or --plugins): no foreign SDKs, dependencies, manifest entries or Info.plist keys — CI checks this. For desktop debugging there are store and ads stubs (mock-store, mock-ads; AIVERSE_MOCK_STORE, AIVERSE_MOCK_ADS): the whole purchase flow runs without a phone, and the stubs are not compiled into release builds. aiversebuild writes the plugins into Gradle/the manifest, Info.plist/Podfile and HTML itself; build Google Play and RuStore separately: --plugins googleplay,admob and --plugins rustore,yandex-ads. Details: plugins.md.

.github/workflows/release.yml: a v1.2.3 tag (or a manual run with a game folder of your choice) builds every platform with aiversebuild and publishes a GitHub Release: Platform Output Signing (repository secrets) Windows installer (Inno Setup, no admin rights) + portable .zip WINDOWS_CERT_PFX_BASE64, WINDOWS_CERT_PASSWORD Android .apk and .aab for Google Play ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64, ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS, ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD macOS .app in a .zip, notarized MACOS_CERT_P12_BASE64, MACOS_CERT_PASSWORD (Developer ID) + an App Store Connect key iOS Xcode project; with a key — a TestFlight build APPLE_TEAM_ID, ASC_KEY_ID, ASC_ISSUER_ID, ASC_KEY_P8_BASE64 Linux .tar.gz — Web .zip; with DEPLOY_WEB_PAGES=true (repository variable) — published to GitHub Pages — Without secrets the release still comes out: the APK is signed with a debug key, the .app ad-hoc, Windows unsigned.

h: Prebuilt engine (the builds branch) and aiversemcp without a compiler
x: The prebuilt editor and tools are published on the builds branch: <platform>/AIVERSE-<version>-<commit>-<platform>.zip (currently windows x86_64 and macos arm64; linux x86_64 when the integrator publishes it). Inside is an AIVERSE/ folder with the engine sources at that commit (templates templates/, engine/assets, docs/ — the MCP server reads them) and AIVERSE/bin/ with the programs. Packaged by tools/release/package_engine.py, published by tools/release/publish_builds.py (AGENTS.md §8); the Linux package may come without the editor — only aiversemcp and aiverse_headless. The MCP server from the unpacked folder (bot matches and balance_* run inside aiversemcp, it does not need a separate aiverse_headless; the editor is optional, without it use --no-editor): # ARCHIVE is the path to the AIVERSE archive downloaded from index.json. unzip "$ARCHIVE" -d ~/aiverse # unzip keeps the executable bit ~/aiverse/AIVERSE/bin/aiversemcp --no-editor --engine ~/aiverse/AIVERSE --engine can be omitted in builds from commits where aiversemcp looks for the engine next to itself (engine/platform/EngineDir.h, like the editor); in earlier published builds it is required. With unpackers that do not restore permissions (Python zipfile), run chmod +x on the files in bin/. On macOS a file downloaded by a browser may get quarantined: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/aiverse/AIVERSE. Programs that download the engine themselves read index.json at the root of the branch (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromealex/AIVERSE/builds/index.json), not the README. Below is an example of a historical AIVERSE entry; in new builds the paths contain AIVERSE, and the rtsmcp key is kept: { "schema": 1, "repository": "chromealex/AIVERSE", "branch": "builds", "packages": [ { "platform": "macos", "arch": "arm64", "version": "0.2.0", "commit": "77126fa9", "file": "macos/AIVERSE-0.2.0-77126fa9-macos.zip", "url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromealex/AIVERSE/builds/macos/AIVERSE-0.2.0-77126fa9-macos.zip", "size": 43055202, "sha256": "c08044fd5a13648016f4d0f2184edb6054d338a814c2b2de2caab09b4cf4513d", "root": "AIVERSE", "rtsmcp": "AIVERSE/bin/rtsmcp", "editor": "AIVERSE/bin/RTSEditor.app", "headless": "AIVERSE/bin/rts_headless" } ] } packages go from newest to oldest; the first entry with the needed platform + arch is the latest build. platform: windows | macos | linux; arch: x86_64 | arm64 | universal (macOS fat) | null (not recognized) — determined from the aiversemcp header inside the zip. rtsmcp, editor, headless are paths inside the archive, or null if the program is not in the package; --engine is the root folder. On macOS, editor is an .app bundle. url points to a branch that is rewritten on every publish (5 versions per platform are kept): old entries disappear, so download from a fresh index.json and check sha256. New fields may be added; an incompatible format change will increase schema. Check: python3 tools/release/test_release.py [build/linux-release/aiversemcp] (CTest release_tools) — the index.json format, and with a path to aiversemcp — packaging a Linux package, unpacking it into a temporary folder and MCP calls from there without --engine (tools/list, create_project, map_generate, map_validate, map_ascii). Screenshot mode (AIVERSE_SCREENSHOT, AIVERSE_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES) steps exactly 1/60 s per frame, so frame N is the same on any machine.
glTF models and animation, audio, networking (lockstep), abilities and buffs from data, flow fields and RVO for large armies, AI improvements, C# scripting (AOT for iOS).

Besides Lua, a project can contain native/CMakeLists.txt and C++20 modules. They are added with aiverse_native_module(...) at build time and enabled by the nativeModules array in rules.json. Ticks, commands, rollback and state saving are supported; Lua and C++ work together. After changing C++ the game and the editor must be rebuilt. API, example and build instructions.

aiverse::meta — configurable shop/offers/crafting, currencies and items, quests and passes, daily rewards, energy, mail, leaderboards, chats and segments. Available to the project's native code without Lua/GPU; definitions are JSON, so the algorithms don't need to be generated again. Start: python3 tools/meta/scaffold.py --preset mobile --out <project>. Documentation: meta-game.md; for agents — skills/meta/meta-game/SKILL.md. Local policies work without a server; communication between devices and global leaderboards need a real backend. A ready cloud service is not part of the package. The full --with-ui preset adds friends/clans, an instance collection, equipment, merging, subscriptions and tournament leagues. aiverse::meta::Service executes operations atomically; tools/meta/server.py is a local HTTP/SQLite host with session checks. Included are browser meta screens and a catalog of short recipes for agents. Building, running and limits. full also includes 15 LiveOps groups: chests with pity, albums/trades, job queues, research/prestige, compound quests, events, clan wars, async PvP, party matchmaking, Elo/Glicko-2, referrals/promo codes, rewarded ads, offer chains, notifications and offline income. All parameters live in extensions.liveops; this preset does not install new separate UI screens or external SDKs. python3 tools/meta/catalog.py describe matchmaking prints only the needed schema and example. API, policies and limits.

Box3D is enabled with the AIVERSE_ENABLE_PHYSICS=ON flag; ordinary RTS projects don't need it. A separate example, aiverse_physics_demo, shows bodies, collisions, a pendulum and state saving. Building, API and integration limits.

The optional AIVERSE_ENABLE_CLOTH=ON module: its own XPBD cloth solver on the CPU or Metal compute, shared batches, temporal LOD, automatic sleeping and drawing dense meshes with one instanced draw. On the GPU, positions stay in video memory; unsupported backends use the CPU. The example can compare the GPU with a CPU reference and check sleep/wake. Standalone example, limits and measurements. Source on GitHub: docs/overview.md

The implementation lives on agent-engine-import; the source specification is engine-import-spec.md. The simulation and template checksums are unchanged. This is a working import foundation, not completion of every stage of the specification. The coverage and outstanding work below are part of the handoff to MAIN.

Python 3.8+; no Python packages are required. The executable launcher is tools/importers/port/aiverse_port (or use the explicit Python form below): python3 tools/importers/port/aiverse_port.py scan /path/to/UnityProject python3 tools/importers/port/aiverse_port.py extract /path/to/UnityProject --out /tmp/port.json python3 tools/importers/port/aiverse_port.py emit /tmp/port.json --out /path/to/Imported python3 tools/importers/port/aiverse_port.py /path/to/UnityProject --out /path/to/Imported --scale 1 --mode auto python3 tools/importers/port/aiverse_port.py report /path/to/Imported python3 tools/importers/port/aiverse_port.py item /path/to/Imported --id ITEM_ID python3 tools/importers/port/aiverse_port.py resolve /path/to/Imported --id ITEM_ID --how lua --reason 'Verified by scenario…' Every command prints JSON; failure exits with status 2. scan writes nothing. The input and output directories must not overlap. Do not run concurrent imports into the same destination. extract records source paths, complete serialized components, fields, script source and usage. emit writes a game manifest, rules, maps, .aiverse, copied assets, optional sprites/tiles/audio/fx, port.json, and JSON/Markdown reports. sourceRoot must still exist when emitting copied assets. Generated .rpakignore excludes the intermediate script index and reports from runtime packs. The manifest marks imported content external: true, which aiversebuild propagates into resource packs. --scale means cells per metre; --mode auto|2d|3d selects the scene plane and camera. Unity 3D flips Z; Unity 2D projects XY onto the ground plane. Godot Vector2 maps to XZ. Origins are translated to keep map positions positive. No ownership is invented: only an explicit Unity owner field is mapped, with an approximation warning. Source player numbering must be checked. lib/port/mapping.json defines field aliases. --mapping FILE adds or overrides aliases for supported targets. fireRate is interpreted as shots/second (reciprocal cooldown), explicitly marked approximate. Engine JSON cooldown/build times are seconds, not simulation ticks. Every inferred field has provenance, confidence and a target path.

.port-state.json stores generated file/type hashes. Edited or pre-existing files are preserved, including when an editor retained the ported marker. Rules merge per type; edited types lose that marker. New types can still be added. User changes to rules-level settings are preserved. Maps and binary files are protected as whole files. Obsolete generated files are not deleted. The state manifest is importer-owned; do not edit it. Resolution annotations survive repeat imports only while the item and its relevant source entity/script fingerprint are unchanged. A changed source reopens the item for review.

Open Project → Import engine project, or editor_window {id:"project_import", open:true}. Scan the source, choose destination/scale/2D/3D, then import. The UI runs the importer off the render thread and can open the result. Copy AI handoff copies an explicit task and opens the Agent window; it does not claim that an agent has been launched. The current base branch has no “Make a game” wizard. Integration with the separate agent-gamewizard branch remains for MAIN; no unrelated branch was merged. Registered operations (import settings can also be nested in options): port_scan {path}: source discovery, serialization checks, asset/scene/script lists. port_import {path,out,scale?,mode?,mapping?}: run extraction and emission. port_report {path?}: read the destination report (defaults to the open project). port_item {path?,id}: source item, components, linked scripts and generated types. port_resolve {path?,id,how,reason}: annotate verified work (rules, lua, native, dropped). Import is synchronous over MCP, like the existing VFX importer; large projects can take time. AIVERSE_PYTHON selects the interpreter. Windows shell metacharacters %, !, quotes and line breaks in command arguments are rejected rather than interpolated. Agent workflow: inspect missing items, consult rules_schema, implement suitable mechanics as data, then Lua, then a native module if required. Use scenario_run and bot matches to compare DPS, production time and movement speed. Compare screenshots when the source image is supplied. Resolve only verified work; explain intentionally dropped behavior. No C#/GDScript/Blueprint execution is mechanically translated.

h: World: terrain, roads, meshes and map markers (agent-unity-terrain)
x: Unity keeps native assets binary even with Force Text. Editor-saved files carry a type tree, so lib/unity/serialized.py (SerializedFile formats 9–22, little/big endian, Unity's built-in string table) reads every field by name with the standard library only. Files without a type tree (player builds) are rejected with a pointer to the fallback below. Source Engine result Terrain component + TerrainData (lib/unity/terrain.py) All tiles of a scene are merged in Unity world space. Map terrain.cornersFile (maps/<id>.r16, int16 1/16 units, heights × --scale), terrain.detail {scale k, file, splat} with k = min(4, heightmap samples per cell) capped at 1.2M samples, RGBA8 splat per detail sample. The map is cut to the terrain (and map-config) rectangle; objects outside are dropped and reported. Relief is visual unless the rules say terrain.model: "heightfield" (loads and simulates; slopes are then gameplay) TerrainLayer assets rules.terrain.layers (≤ 4, game-wide): the most painted layers with resolved textures win; textures copied to content/_terrain/*_repeat.* (kept out of atlases), scale = tile size × scale. Other layers fold into the palette layer they overlap most per tile Tree instances One terrain_tree_* type per prototype (prefab's first mesh, invulnerable) and one neutral entity per instance; rotation / width / height / colour are dropped Detail (grass) Density per prototype as maps/<id>.tileN.detailM.png + imported.details (map rectangle); the engine has no grass renderer, reported missing Embedded Mesh (class 43, EasyRoads3D baked roads, ProBuilder…) and built-in Cube / Plane / Quad / Cylinder / Sphere / Capsule content/_meshes/<id>.obj; world rotation and scale baked in, Z flipped, winding reversed; the entity keeps its position with yaw 0 Road components with baked splinePoints + roadWidth (EasyRoads3D v3 ERModularRoad) Road cells + under the ribbon, imported.roads polylines (map cells); rules.terrain.roads: false so the baked meshes are the visual Scene markers, by rules (lib/port/markers.json) start → player starts (players added as needed), area → areas.<name>_N rectangles (radius / Bounds), block → # cells under rotated Bounds, region → regions rows from polygons, grid → imported.grid (pathfinding config: node size, origin, node count; a different node size is reported with the matching --scale), bounds → ScriptableObject map config matched by map name → areas.map_bounds and map cut. entity: "drop" removes the marker object from the placed entities Every map also gets imported (ignored by the loader): markers with their source, class, fields and cell positions, roads, terrain tiles / height range, grid and bounds, so a later game port is data work. --mapping FILE may carry {"markers": [...]}; those rules are tried before the defaults. Rule keys: class (script class, namespace suffix), match (GameObject name regex), refType (managed reference class of a ScriptableObject, e.g. ME.BECS GDCMapData), when (field equality), kind, area, radius (number or field), bounds, points (dotted paths; the first part may be a local component reference), config/properties (grid), mapName/size/position (bounds; soft floats {rawValue} and FixedStringNBytes are decoded). The defaults describe Drone Fall (Ext-Client): GraphMask obstacles (type 0 → blocked, others → wall_N areas), extraction / summon / mob / crate points, FOW polygons, SpawnFlag starts, ExtPathfindingGrid + AgentTypesConfig, GD_Map-* (mapName, mapSize, mapPos). --include GLOB (repeatable, Unity) walks only matching scenes / prefabs; ScriptableObjects outside the globs are kept only when an included object references them, scripts are indexed only when used, and only referenced assets are copied. A game is a folder <project>/: game.json manifest: name, id, version, rules file, maps list, orientation, desktop window, icon, input rules.json resources, types (units/structures/objects), techs, factions, game rules, triggers maps/*.json terrain, players, objects, waves, triggers, areas, victory overrides audio.json sounds, music and which sound plays on which game event (optional: no file = silent) models/ ui/ ... assets (glTF models, textures, UI, sounds); 2D images may be packed into atlases (see Texture atlases) JSON allows // comments. Numbers are plain decimals (1.5, never 1e3): the simulation is fixed-point and deterministic. Seconds are game seconds, distances are map cells. Every block below is optional — the blocks present on a type decide what it can do.

game.json.postfx retains the original global HDR/bloom/color-grade settings. Optional game.json.prismaVolumes and map prismaVolumes add position-dependent camera looks (no gameplay/ECS simulation mutation). Each block holds {"volumes":[{"id":"area","shape":"sphere","center":[0,0,0],"radius":8,"blendDistance":3,"priority":4,"weight":1,"profile":{"effects":[{"type":"colorGrade","saturation":0.6}]}}]}. The map may override a game volume by identical id, or set "replace":true to discard game volumes. Supported shapes are global, sphere, and axis-aligned box (center + halfExtents). The profile uses the existing postfx effect schema. Only explicit profile hdr/enabled overrides global HDR or chain enable state. Engine/runtime C++ owners: engine/render/PrismaVolumeData.{h,cpp} and PrismaVolumes.h; see docs/prisma.md for full semantics and quality caveats. The postfx_* MCP operations remain compatible.

{ "name": "Iron and Gold", "id": "com.studio.ironandgold", "version": "0.1.0", "build": 1, "module": "game", "rules": "rules.json", "maps": [{ "file": "maps/valley.json", "title": "River Valley (1v1)" }], "orientation": "landscape", "icon": "icon.png" } "audio": another name for the sound file (default audio.json). "module": the game module — "rts", "fps", "voxel", or "scene". A "scene" project has no game module: it needs only game.json (name, id, version, build, "module": "scene", optional "background": "#rrggbb"). aiversebuild packages it with the minimal scene client (apps/client/SceneMain.cpp, CMake AIVERSE_SCENE_CLIENT): window or canvas, content pack and an empty scene cleared to the background colour — no simulation, renderer, UI, scripting or audio, and no engine/assets in the pack. Web Release with the default -Oz + LTO, 2026-11-21: about 150 KB to download (brotli: index.wasm 108 KB, index.js 40 KB). Projects without "module" remain RTS projects. "icons" and "splash": game icons for every platform and the loading screen — see "Icons and splash" below (the old single "icon" still works as the master icon). Optional "graphics": the RHI backend on Windows, Linux and Android — "gl" (default) or "vulkan", or per platform {"windows": "vulkan", "android": "gl"}. Vulkan falls back to GL when the machine has no driver; --gfx and AIVERSE_GFX override it (docs/vulkan.md). macOS / iOS use Metal, the web WebGL2. Optional "window" block: how the game window opens on desktops (macOS, Windows, Linux; phones and tablets are always fullscreen, the web build fills the page). Editor: Сборка → Окно игры (window «Сборка»). "window": { "mode": "windowed", "width": 1280, "height": 720, "minWidth": 960, "minHeight": 540, "keepAspect": false, "allowFullscreen": true, "macos": { "mode": "fullscreen" } } key meaning mode windowed (default: a normal resizable window), fixed (exactly width × height, no resizing or maximize), maximized (the whole desktop work area, still a window), fullscreen (macOS: native fullscreen in its own Space; Windows / Linux: a borderless window over the monitor) width, height content size in points (1280 × 720); also the size after leaving fullscreen / maximized resizable windowed only (true); "mode": "fixed" is the same as false minWidth, minHeight smallest size when resizable (0 = no limit) keepAspect resizing keeps width : height allowFullscreen F11 (Windows, Linux), Alt+Enter (Windows) and the green button (macOS) switch fullscreen (true) macos, windows, linux objects with any of the keys above that override them on that platform Runs with AIVERSE_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES (screenshots, CI) and --size WxH stay windowed at the asked size. Code: engine/platform/WindowSettings.h (parser, checks), AppConfig window fields, AppCallbacks::configure. Optional "ui" block: how the in-game UI (RmlUi documents) blends. "ui": {"blend": "linear"} makes translucent UI blend in linear light, as a Unity project in linear colour space does (faded icons, dims, glows and soft edges over lighter art come out lighter than with the default); "srgb" (default, also when the block is missing) blends the sRGB-encoded values, byte-identical to builds without the key. In linear mode vertex colours (CSS colours, opacity, vertex gradients) and images are decoded to linear light (images are premultiplied in linear light and uploaded as sRGB textures), font atlases stay coverage (alpha only), the UI is blended into its own sRGB-encoded layer and one full-screen pass composites it over the scene in linear light (skipped when the UI draws nothing). GPUs without sRGB render targets silently keep the default. Code: engine/ui/UiColor.h (curves, key), UiLinear.* (layer + composite, GLSL and MSL), RHI PixelFormat::RGBA8_sRGB, Device::copyColor. Optional "camera" block (2D games, see "2D games" below): {"projection": "ortho", "pitch": 90, "yaw": 0, "fov": 43, "zoom": 20, "zoomMin": 8, "zoomMax": 40, "pixelsPerCell": 32, "rotate": false}. The block may start from

key meaning supplyCap max supply/population (default 200) modes, matchModes, timedRules, matchStats, ruleSets match modes (domination, king of the hill, time limit, sudden death, battle-royal zones), presets picked by map matchMode, player statuses by time slots, match statistics: see "Match modes" ai {"controller":"builtin"} (default) or {"controller":"scripted"}. Scripted control makes the generic ComputerPlayer submit no commands in client, editor and headless. The game must provide its own controller; Lua handlers, human/network commands, combat, production and victory remain enabled. This is not the waves player flag and does not exempt players from defeat. maxQueue production queue length (5) costModel "upfront" (pay when ordering) or "progressive" (Total Annihilation: pay while building; stalls when short) sellRefund fraction refunded when selling a structure (0.5) buildRadius >0: structures only within N cells of own structures with extendsBase levelHeight visual height of one cliff level waveClock seconds; structures with waveSpawn release their units together on this clock (lane battlers) autoBuild {"pool": [types], "cost": {res: n}, "growth": 0.5} — a BUILD button: the sim picks a type from the pool and a spot next to the base automatically; cost grows by growth per structure already auto-built victory "noStructures" (default), "noUnits", "noEntities", "keyUnits" (lose when all key objects die), or an object: {"mode": "tickets", "tickets": 500, "drain": 1}, {"mode": "survive", "seconds": 600}, {"mode": "score", "seconds": 240, "keyLoses": true}, {"mode": "territory", "share": 0.9} (a team owning that share of all claimable cells wins; a player with no territory is out) fogOfWar {"mode": "full"} — fog of war: full (default: unexplored black, explored dim), explored (the whole map starts explored, enemies only in sight), none (no fog, everyone sees everything); shareAllies (true); lineOfSight (false: 3D visibility by heights and blockers, see "3D line of sight"); rockHeight (2: undug rock as an occluder). A map may override mode. The other keys are visual, see "Fog of war look" heights {"blockVision": true, "missUphill": 0.3, "rangePerLevel": 1, "damagePerLevel": 0.1} — cliff levels: lower ground can't see up, shots uphill can miss, higher ground adds range and damage. With terrain.model: "heightfield" the advantage is the height difference / levelHeight (fractional), missUphill scales with it (full chance from one level below) and vision follows real line of sight targeting {"overkill": false} — overkill: true (StarCraft II): automatic targeting skips enemies whose hp + shields are already covered by shots in flight and by the next shots of units that chose them earlier in the same pass, so a volley spreads over several targets. Manual attack orders are not affected; the estimate uses the weapon's raw damage (before armor) terrain {"model": "heightfield", "maxSlope": {"ground": 0.8, "sand": 0.6}, "buildSlope": 0.35, "uphillSpeed": 0.5, "downhillSpeed": 0.2, "eyeHeight": 1, "targetHeight": 0.5} — terrain model, see "Heightfield terrain". model: "levels" (default: cliff levels + ramps), "flat" (levels ignored), "heightfield". Other keys of this block are visual (view) and ignored by the simulation regions {"claimCost": {"food": 100}, "claimCostGrowth": 0.5, "buildOnlyOwned": true, "productionPerRegion": 0.1} — territory (Northgard; with flags: Z) upkeep [{"supply": 50, "gatherMult": 0.7}, {"supply": 80, "gatherMult": 0.4}] — gathering yields less with a big army (Warcraft III) armorTypes, damageTable "damageTable": {"pierce": {"heavy": 0.5, "light": 1.5}} multipliers by damage type → armor type resources see below types see below techs see below factions see below triggers see "Triggers" (also allowed in maps) scripts, viewScripts, scriptBudget Lua scripts of the game (also allowed in maps): ["scripts/rules.lua"] run in the deterministic simulation (integers and fx numbers, no floats), viewScripts only on the local mac

A big game does not keep everything in one rules.json. The loader assembles the rules from several files and lets entries inherit from shared bases (engine/data/JsonCompose.h). The simulation sees one document either way: same results, same checksums, old single-file games load unchanged. include — more files, paths relative to the file that lists them (inside the game folder): // rules.json {"include": ["rules/resources.json", "rules/units.json", "rules/abilities.json"], "supplyCap": 200, "victory": "noStructures"} // rules/units.json (may include further files itself) {"types": {"footman": {...}, "archer": {...}}, "include": ["heroes.json"]} Top-level objects (types, techs, resources, ai, ...) merge key by key; top-level arrays (playerAbilities, triggers, ...) append in reading order (the file's own content, then its includes, depth first); scalars (supplyCap) are set once. Entries keep the reading order, and the order of types is part of the game (types are numbered in it): moving types between files in another order is a different game for replays and network matches. A key or an array entry "id" defined in two files is an error naming both (rules/b.json: 'types.knight' is already defined in rules/a.json); so are an include cycle, a missing file and a path outside the game folder. Everything reads the assembled rules: client, network host, headless, replays, aiversebuild, the editor. Network and replay data hashes cover every included file. Packs ship the included files like any other data. The editor and MCP edit the rules as one document (rules_get / rules_set / rules_merge); saving writes each entry back into the file it came from and leaves unchanged files untouched. A new entry goes into the file that holds the previous entry of its collection (a new type lands next to the other types). rules_get returns files when the rules are split; game_file_write refuses rules files (use the rules ops). extends / abstract — an entry of a top-level collection (a member of an object of entries such as types, techs, statuses, or an array item with an "id" such as playerAbilities) starts as a copy of its base(s) in the same collection; its own keys go on top. Objects merge key by key, anything else (numbers, strings, arrays) replaces. "abstract": true entries are bases only: they are removed before loading (not types, not in the editor palette of the game). "types": { "_infantry": {"abstract": true, "health": {"max": 420, "armor": 2}, "move": {"speed": 2.6, "radius": 0.4}, "sight": 8, "cost": {"gold": 135, "time": 15, "supply": 2}}, "footman": {"extends": "_infantry", "name": "Footman", "weapons": [{"id": "sword", "range": 0.6, "damage": 12, "cooldown": 1.2}]}, "spearman": {"extends": "_infantry", "name": "Spearman", "health": {"armor": 1}, "weapons": [{"id": "spear", "range": 1.2, "damage": 10, "cooldown": 1.4}]} } extends takes a name or a list (applied left to right, then the entry itself); bases may extend other bases. Unknown bases and cycles are errors (types 'knight': extends unknown 'cavalry'). rules_get {"resolved": true} shows the entries as the game loads them; rules_lint checks the resolved entries. Levels are overrides. levels of abilities and player abilities already merge into the base entry (objects key by key, arrays of the same length element by element): write only what changes per level, "levels": [{"cooldown": 37.5, "effects": [{"duration": 5.5}]}], never a full copy of the ability.

"resources": { "gold": {"name": "Золото", "start": 500}, "ore": {"name": "Руда", "field": true, "regrow": 0.5, "cellMax": 100}, // Red Alert / Dune: harvested from map fields "metal": {"kind": "flow", "start": 500, "storage": 1000}, // Total Annihilation: income/expense per second, capped by storage "power": {"kind": "capacity", "deficitProduction": 0.5, "deficitDisables": ["defense"]},// Red Alert power: provided vs consumed "spice": {"capped": true, "storage": 1000}, // Dune silos: stock limited by storage "coins": {"global": true, "start": 100}, // with "storage": "buildings": not a good, stays player-wide "ore2": {"field": true, "convertsTo": {"credits": 4}} // delivered ore is credited as 4 credits each } Kinds: stock (default: gathered/earned, spent), flow (per-second income from income, spent while building in progressive mode; at 0 with negative income production slows by deficitProduction), capacity (sum of provides minus consumes; a deficit slows production and disables types with any tag in deficitDisables).

"move": {"speed": 2.8, "radius": 0.4, "mass": 0.64, "layer": "ground", "maxSlope": 1.6} maxSlope (heightfield terrain only): the steepest cell this type can enter (rise per cell); default terrain.maxSlope of its layer. At most 15 different values per game. radius is the real body size (cells): units keep r1 + r2 apart, weapon and ability ranges are measured edge to edge (range + both radii, structures by their footprint), and paths keep clearance from walls and buildings for bodies larger than half a cell (tight gaps cost more; nothing becomes unreachable). mass (default 4 * radius²) decides who yields when bodies overlap. Units that are fighting, holding position or working (gathering, building, digging) are anchored (x8) and are barely pushed; moving units (x2) push idle ones (x1) aside. A 0.03-cell dead zone and a per-tick push cap remove jitter. With movement.avoidance: "rvo" moving units steer around each other with reciprocal velocity obstacles (nearest neighbors, deterministic order). Idle allies in the way are asked to yield: they step to a free side cell and walk back once the way is clear, so a unit can pass a gap of standing units; units blocked by anchored ones re-path around them. movement.avoidance: "none" disables ORCA and mobile body separation, for games whose Lua formation logic supplies positions. It does not disable terrain pathfinding or combat. Keep real positive body radii; do not emulate this mode with near-zero radii. Melee units (range < 2) attacking a target pick a free slot on a ring around it (slots by angle, claimed per target, ties by entity index) and path around allies already fighting instead of pushing into the front rank; ranged units stop and shoot. A group given an attack-move spreads into an arc whose flanks run ahead. Flow fields (movement.flowField, off unless a game or map opts in; docs/pathfinding.md): big groups and hordes share one integration field per goal area instead of one path search per unit. jsonc "movement": {"flowField": {"minGroup": 12, // move / attack-move / patrol / right-click orders of >= 12 units (0 = never) "minCells": 0, // ... only for units at least this many cells from the goal (0 = all) "waves": true, // units released by map waves and lane waves march on fields "spread": 0.4, // goal area radius = 0.3 + spread * sqrt(units) (they arrive spread out) "maxFields": 64, "budgetMB": 32}} // cache: LRU of unreferenced fields beyond these A map may carry the same block ("movement": {"flowField": {...}} at the map's top level) to switch fields on for itself only (e.g. templates/lastcolony/maps/horde_plain.json, templates/planets/maps/big_planet.json). Fliers keep flying straight; units pushed off the field or stuck repeatedly fall back to their own A* path. Followers settle around the goal from the inside out (arrival contagion) and don't block each other. movement.blockedGoals: "nearest" (rules or map, default "search"): paths to a goal inside a structure or obstacle (attacking a building) end at the free cell around it nearest to the unit - much cheaper for hordes; different cells than the classic search, so it is opt-in (on in templates/lastcolony/maps/horde_plain.json). movement.pathfinding: "navmesh" (rules or map, default "grid"): unit paths on flat maps come from the engine navigation mesh (engine/nav, docs/navmesh.md): passable cells of each path layer merge into rectangles, A* runs over them and a funnel pulls the corridor into an any-angle path (fewer waypoints, ~7% shorter than 8-direction grid paths, cheap on 1024x1024 maps). Cliffs, ramps, slopes and structures are respected; searches it can't answer (start or goal off the mesh, unreachable goals, surround-allies paths) use the grid search as before. Planets keep the grid / HPA*. Different waypoints than the grid, so it is opt-in. movement.pathfinding: "hybrid" (rules or map): one portal graph for the map (the 16x16 HPA* clusters, at any map size) and a solver per cluster - navmesh rectangles in open clus
