Combine with charges ({"max": 1, "interval": 20}) for the gate's cooldown. Train commands without the flag queue as usual creep radius of creep it spreads (structures with "terrain": "creep" need it) fieldSpawner {"resource": "ore", "rate": 10, "radius": 3} — grows a resource field around it (ore mine, spice bloom) deploysTo unit → structure (MCV → Construction Yard) wreck {"metal": 100} — leaves a type "wreck" (define it with a resourceNode) to reclaim sellable default true for structures garrison {"max": 20, "unit": "mushroomling", "interval": 1.0, "capturable": true, "defense": 1.0, "decay": 1.0} — Mushroom Wars: grows units inside, sends them along road

"abilities": [ {"id": "storm", "name": "Буря", "target": "point", "range": 9, "cooldown": 12, "energy": 75, "level": 1, "autocast": true, "effects": [{"type": "damage", "amount": 80, "radius": 2, "damageType": "magic", "affects": "enemies"}]}, {"id": "heal", "target": "unit", "effects": [{"type": "heal", "amount": 60}]}, {"id": "roar", "target": "none", "effects": [{"type": "buff", "stat": "damage", "mul": 1.25, "duration": 15, "radius": 6, "affects": "allies"}]}, {"id": "stun", "target": "unit", "effects": [{"type": "stun", "duration": 2}]}, {"id": "wolves", "target": "none", "effects": [{"type": "spawn", "unit": "wolf", "count": 2, "duration": 60}]}, {"id": "blink", "target": "point", "range": 8, "effects": [{"type": "blink"}]}, {"id": "devotion", "aura": true, "radius": 7, "effects": [{"type": "buff", "stat": "armor", "add": 2, "affects": "allies"}]} ] target: none | self | unit | point (and structure | group | player, see "Abilities and effects"). affects: enemies | allies | all. Autocast abilities are also what the AI uses. Delivery (projectiles, areas, chains, channels), statuses, costs, charges, cast times and level tables: "Abilities and effects".

"techs": { "iron_swords": {"name": "Железные мечи", "cost": {"gold": 100, "time": 30}, "requires": ["blacksmith"], "effects": [{"tags": ["infantry"], "stat": "damage", "mul": 1.15}, {"type": "archer", "stat": "range", "add": 1}]} } An effect without tags/type applies to every type. Repeatable upgrades: "levels": 5, "costGrowth": 0.5 — the tech can be researched 5 times, each level re-applies its effects (multipliers compound) and costs cost * (1 + costGrowth * levelsDone); researched counts levels. Requirements can be types or techs (ages: a tech required by the next tier's types).

"factions": { "terran": {"name": "Терраны", "start": [{"type": "command_center", "offset": [0, 0]}, {"type": "scv", "offset": [3, 0], "count": 4}]} } Map players choose a faction and a start point; start objects spawn there.

Per-slot computer player: players[i].ai = {"preset": "rush", "firstAttackArmy": 3, ...} - a preset (easy, normal, hard, rush, defender, economist), then any rules ai knob (workersPerBase, firstAttackArmy, armyGrowth, maxAttackArmy, towers, scouts, invasionSize, climbWeight, exposureWeight, escalateSeconds, terrain) plus thinkTicks (1..3600, reaction time) and aggression (0.1..4). Order: bot defaults, rules ai, the slot's preset, the slot's keys. "ai": true (a computer slot marker written by importers) means no overrides. Unknown keys and out-of-range values fail loading with map players[i].ai.... Only decisions change, never stats; maps without it play exactly as before. MCP: player_set {player, ai}. { "name": "River Valley", "size": [64, 48], "players": [{"name": "Blue", "team": 1, "faction": "terran", "start": [8, 24], "resources": {"gold": 800}}, {"name": "Zombies", "team": 9, "waves": true}], "terrain": { "rows": ["....~~~~....", "..."], // one char per cell: . ground ~ water # blocked , no-build = shallow / ramp R rock "levels": ["000011110000", "..."], // cliff level per cell 0..9; units change level only over / ramps "heights": [0, 0, 16, ...], // optional fine visual height per cell (1/16 units) "corners": [0, 0, 16, ...] // optional heightfield: (w+1)*(h+1) corner heights, 1/16 units, row-major // or, for big maps: "cornersFile": "maps/<name>.r16" raw int16 little-endian, (w+1)*(h+1) values }, "fields": [{"resource": "ore", "rows": ["0000999000", "..."]}], // density digits 1..9 of cellMax (or {"center": [x,z], "radius": 3}) "regions": {"rows": ["AAAABBBB", "..."], "names": {"A": "Долина", "B": "Холмы"}}, // entity keys: "facing": degrees clockwise on screen from north (0 north, 90 east = default, 180 south, 270 west) "entities": [{"type": "townhall", "owner": 1, "pos": [9, 24]}, {"type": "goldmine", "owner": 0, "pos": [6, 16], "amount": 8000}, {"type": "ogre", "owner": -1, "pos": [32, 10]}], // owner: 0 neutral, 1..N players, -1 hostile creeps "roads": [["base_a", "village_1"]], // by entity id (Mushroom Wars) "roadsOnly": false, "areas": {"relic": [26, 4, 4, 4]}, // named rectangles [x, z, w, h] for triggers "waves": [{"time": 60, "player": 2, "at": [60, 24], "spread": 3, "spawn": [{"type": "zombie", "count": 10}], "every": 45, "growth": 1.3, "repeats": 10}], "victory": {"mode": "survive", "seconds": 900}, // overrides rules.victory "rules": {"topDown": {"escape": null}}, // per-map overrides of rules blocks (below) "triggers": [] }

A map may override tuning blocks of the rules for its matches: "rules": {"<block>": {...}} is merged over rules.json before anything parses it (engine/game/MapRules.cpp), so every block validates the merged result with its usual errors. Objects merge key by key (recursively); any other value — numbers, strings, lists such as an xp table — replaces the rules value; null removes the key ("escape": null switches the escape off on that map). "rules": { "topDown": {"escape": {"cooldown": 45}, "squad": {"fireWhileMoving": true}, "bot": {"orbRange": "weapon"}}, "raid": {"duration": 300, "pickupRadius": 2}, "progression": {"offerAt": "summonPoints", "xp": {"toNext": [10, 20, 35]}, "pauseOnOffer": true}, "encounters": {"mobs": {"zombie": {"aggroRange": 12}}, "preferTags": ["cargo"]} } Patchable: topDown.{respawn, move, aim, abilities, squad, escape, autoFire, bot} (not heroes/input: they decide who is steered and how commands are quantized), the whole raid, progression and encounters blocks. Any other block (types, resources, abilities, ...) is an error: map rules.types: this block cannot be overridden per map (allowed: ...). The map's own raid block (points, objectives by id) and progression.summonPoints still apply on top.

Presentation only: nothing here reaches the simulation. A missing file or audio device just means no sound. Malformed structure is an error (audio: sound 'x': unknown bus 'drums'); a missing or undecodable sound file, an unknown key, type, weapon or sound name is a warning and only that sound stays silent. { "volume": {"master": 1, "sfx": 0.9, "ui": 0.7, "voice": 1, "music": 0.6, "ambient": 0.7}, "spatial": {"minDistance": 10, "maxDistance": 55, "airAbsorption": 1500, "speedOfSound": 150, "reverb": {"size": 0.6, "damping": 0.45, "wet": 0.4, "near": 0.04, "far": 0.65}}, "groups": {"melee": {"max": 6}, "ui": {"max": 3, "bus": "ui", "steal": "oldest"}}, "sounds": { "swing": {"files": ["sfx/swing1.ogg", "sfx/swing2.ogg"], "pitch": [0.9, 1.1], "maxInstances": 4, "cooldown": 0.05, "group": "melee"}, "alarm": {"file": "voice/under_attack.ogg", "bus": "voice", "priority": 10}, "blip": {"synth": {"wave": "square", "freq": [880, 440], "duration": 0.08}, "bus": "ui"}, "boom": {"file": "sfx/boom.ogg", "minDistance": 14, "maxDistance": 80, "far": {"sound": "boom_far", "from": 0.25}}, "boom_far": {"file": "sfx/boom_far.ogg", "maxDistance": 120, "air": 0.5} }, "music": { "menu": "music/menu.ogg", "match": {"files": ["music/a.ogg", "music/b.ogg"], "shuffle": true, "loop": true, "volume": 0.8}, "battle": ["music/fight.ogg"] }, "events": {"died": "death", "underAttack": "alarm", "notEnough": "need_more", "notEnough.gold": "need_gold"}, "weapons": {"sword": {"attack": "swing", "hit": "clang"}, "bow": {"attack": "bow", "hit": "arrow_hit"}}, "abilities": {"storm": "thunder"}, "types": {"footman": {"select": "footman_what", "move": "footman_yes", "died": "death_human", "weapons": {"sword": {"hit": "clang_heavy"}}, "abilities": {"roar": "roar"}}} } volume: mix level per bus, 0..4 (default 1); the player's own volume settings multiply on top (client data model: volume master, music, sfx = every bus but music, percent; musicOn / sfxOn 1 / 0 switch a bus off without changing its volume; saved in the user folder's audio.cfg). "scripted": true: the game's scripts own the music and the UI sounds (the sound table, docs/scripting.md § Sound): the client never plays the menu / match / battle / victory / defeat playlists by itself, and starting or leaving a match stops only voices on the sfx bus.

Positional sounds are placed in 3D around the listener (the RTS client puts the ear on the view ray above the camera's focus; units on cliffs and flyers are higher). Distances are world units (map cells). Zooming out raises the ear, so the battle sounds farther away; the audible area grows with the square root of the zoom. key meaning model distance curve: inverse (default, natural), linear, exponential minDistance, maxDistance full volume up to min, silent at max (12, 60); the last 20 % of the range always fades out rolloff steepness of the curve (1) airAbsorption Hz of the low-pass at max distance: far sounds lose their highs (2500; false = off) reverb false, or {"size": 0.5, "damping": 0.5, "wet": 0.35, "near": 0.05, "far": 0.6} — near / far = reverb send at min / max distance: far sounds get roomy and lose their attack speedOfSound world units per second; distant sounds arrive late (0 = off; capped at 3 s) rear 0..1: sources behind the listener get duller and a bit quieter (0) The distance keys (model, minDistance, maxDistance, rolloff) are defaults for every sound; a sound can override them and add air / reverb multipliers (below).

key meaning file / files / synth exactly one. Files: WAV, OGG Vorbis, MP3, FLAC, paths relative to the game folder; files = variations, a random one per play, never the same twice in a row bus sfx (default), ambient, voice, ui, music spatial attenuated and panned around the camera when the event has a position; default true for sfx / ambient, false otherwise (announcements are heard anywhere) volume 0..4 (1) pitch number or [min, max] random per play (1) maxInstances at most this many of this sound at once (4; 0 = no limit); steal decides who makes room steal for maxInstances: farthest (default), oldest, quietest, none — see "groups" group a group name or an array of up to 4: limits shared with other sounds (see "groups") cooldown seconds between two starts (0) — 40 archers firing together make a few sounds, not 40 chance probability (0..1, default 1) that a play starts at all — barks and ambience that should not fire every time; a skipped play does not start the cooldown priority -100..100 (0): when all voices are busy, the lowest priority (oldest first) is stopped; a new sound below everything playing is dropped loop loops until stopped (false) model, minDistance, maxDistance, rolloff override the spatial defaults: small sounds (footsteps, swords) fade early, explosions carry far air multiplier of the air absorption, 0..4 (1; 0 = keeps its highs at any distance) reverb multiplier of the distance reverb send, 0..4 (1; 0 = always dry) duckMusic 0..1: music is lowered by this fraction while the sound plays (0.4 on the voice bus, else 0) sync now (default), beat, bar: start on the music's grid (stingers) compress, quality build-time codec for this sound's files (see "Compression at build time") far a distant variant: "boom_far" or {"sound": "boom_far", "from": 0.3} — both play together and crossfade from from (fraction of this sound's distance range) to max distance; the far sound keeps its own distances, so it can carry farther (a low rumble instead of a crack) synth — a sound made from parameters instead of a file (prototypes, playables); an object or an array of layers that are mixed: key meaning wave sine (default), square, saw, triangle, noise freq Hz, or [start, end] for an exponential sweep (440); for noise it is the grain rate duration seconds, 0.001..10 (0.2) attack, release seconds of fade-in / fade-out (0.005, min(0.1, duration)) volume 0..4 (1) duty square pulse width 0.02..0.98 (0.5) vibrato [rate Hz, depth], depth as a fraction of the frequency lowpass cutoff Hz (off) crush keep only N bits, 1..15 (off) delay seconds before this layer starts (0)

Limits shared by several sounds, so a big battle stays readable: six swords hitting at once sound like a fight, sixty sound like noise, and they hide the sounds that matter. "groups": { "melee": {"max": 6}, "missiles": {"max": 6, "cooldown": 0.02}, "explosions": {"max": 4}, "deaths": {"max": 4, "steal": "quietest"}, "ambient": {"max": 5, "bus": "ambient"} } key meaning max sounds of the group at once (0 = no limit, only cooldown) cooldown seconds between two starts of any sound of the group (0) steal who makes room when the group is full (below; default farthest) bus every sound on that bus belongs to the group: a limit per bus Sounds join with "group": "melee" (or ["melee", "loud"]: every group must have room). Variations (files) are one sound; a sound with a far variant counts once, and its far half stops with it. steal when full farthest the sound farthest from the listener stops; a new sound farther than all playing ones is not started — fighting off-screen never cuts off the fight on screen. Non-positional sounds: the oldest oldest the sound started first stops quietest the sound that is quietest now stops (content loudness measured at load, volume, bus, distance); a new sound quieter than all of them is not started none nothing stops: the new sound is not started A playing sound with a higher priority than the new one is never stopped for it; when the whole group is more important, the new sound is not started. Stopping fades in a few ms (no click).

Music streams from the files (OGG Vorbis recommended); changes crossfade. Playlists the client plays by name, all optional: menu, match, battle (replaces match while heavy fighting happens near the camera, back after ~15 s of calm), victory, defeat. A playlist named match.<map> (map file name without extension, e.g. match.valley) wins over match on that map; the same for battle, victory, defeat. "music": { "menu": "music/menu.ogg", "match": {"files": ["music/a.ogg", {"file": "music/b.ogg", "loopStart": 12.0}], "shuffle": true, "bpm": 96, "beatsPerBar": 4, "transition": "bar"}, "match.valley": {"layers": [{"file": "music/valley_base.ogg"}, {"file": "music/valley_drums.ogg", "intensity": 0.3}, {"file": "music/valley_brass.ogg", "intensity": 0.7}], "loopStart": 4.0, "loopEnd": 68.0, "bpm": 112} } A playlist is a file name, an array of entries, or an object: key meaning files entries played in order: a file name or {"file", "loopStart", "loopEnd"} (seconds). With loopStart the track plays its intro once and then loops from loopStart to loopEnd (default: the end) seamlessly until the music changes layers adaptive music instead of files: synchronized stems of equal length, looping together (loopStart / loopEnd on the playlist). A layer with "intensity": x fades in as the music intensity passes x; in a match the intensity follows the fighting near the camera, so a layered match builds up instead of switching to battle shuffle, loop shuffle the entries (no immediate repeats) / start over after the last one (false, true) volume 0..4 (1) bpm, beatsPerBar, offset beat grid (offset: seconds before the first beat); used by transition and by synced stingers transition switching away from this playlist waits for the next beat or bar (default bar when bpm is set, else now) Stingers are sounds on the music bus: "sync": "beat" or "bar" starts them on the playing music's grid. Any sound can duck the music while it plays: "duckMusic": 0.5 lowers it by half (default 0.4 for the voice bus, so announcements are always heard; 0 otherwise).

aiversebuild re-encodes the referenced sound and music files for each target before packing; the project folder is never changed. Profiles: desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux), mobile (iOS, Android), web. --audio mobile forces a profile, --audio off ships the files as they are; aiverse_audiopack --project <game> --profile mobile shows what a profile would do. "build": { "desktop": {"sounds": "keep", "music": "vorbis", "musicQuality": 0.6}, "mobile": {"sounds": "adpcm", "music": "vorbis", "musicQuality": 0.3, "maxRate": 32000}, "web": {"musicQuality": 0.25} } key meaning sounds, music codec: keep (file as is), pcm (16-bit WAV), adpcm (IMA ADPCM WAV: 4:1, nearly free to decode — short effects), vorbis (OGG: music, long sounds) soundQuality, musicQuality Vorbis quality -0.1..1 (0.5 / 0.4; mobile 0.4 / 0.3, web 0.4 / 0.25) maxRate resample anything above this rate (0 = never; mobile and web 32000) monoSounds positional sounds become mono: the mixer pans them anyway (true) longSound seconds: longer sounds (ambient loops, stingers) use the music codec (8) reencodeLossy also re-encode files that are already OGG/MP3 (false: lossy to lossy only loses quality) Defaults without a build section: desktop keeps everything; mobile and web use ADPCM for sounds and Vorbis for music at 32 kHz. Sounds on the music bus count as music. A sound or a playlist can override with "compress" and "quality". Re-encoded files get the extension of their codec and audio.json in the build points at them; a result that isn't smaller keeps the original. Loop points stay exact (Vorbis is sample-accurate; ADPCM pads a loop with its own start).

Which sound plays on which game event ("cue"). Lookup for an object: its entry in types, then its weapon / ability by id in weapons / abilities, then events. cue when heard by attack a weapon fires (weapons.<id>.attack first) everyone who sees the spot hit damage lands (weapons.<id>.hit of the shooter's type first) everyone who sees the spot miss a shot misses (uphill) everyone who sees the spot died an object dies (types.<id>.died) everyone who sees the spot spawned an object appears everyone who sees the spot ability an ability is cast (abilities.<id> first) everyone who sees the spot captured the player captures a building / point; for others: someone captured something in view owner lost the player's building / point was captured previous owner trainStarted, ready production started / a unit is ready owner buildPlaced, buildDone construction placed / finished owner readyToPlace, sold, upgraded, researched, levelUp, regionClaimed, lowPower, gathered as named owner notEnough, notEnough.<resource> can't afford (the resource-specific one first) owner notEnoughSupply, noRoom supply cap / no place for an automatic build (fallbacks: notEnough, error) owner underAttack, baseUnderAttack an enemy hits the player's unit / structure where the camera isn't looking; at most every 12 s owner select the player selects an own unit (types.<id>.select) player move, attackOrder, buildOrder the player gives an order (fallback: move) player victory, defeat, playerDefeated match end / another player is out player wave a scripted wave starts everyone message a trigger message its addressees (everyone for a message to all) click, error interface player "Everyone who sees the spot" respects fog of war; a spectator hears all world sounds and no player-only cues.

For Lua-owned front lines, see Territory brushes and scripted formations. The optional visual block terrain.territory also supports smooth: true (default false), transition (0..2 seconds, default 0.2) and lift (0..2 world units, default 0.045). On flat maps smooth mode filters ownership with a compact binomial kernel, reconstructs it bilinearly, applies a soft contour threshold, and interpolates changed cells over transition seconds. It uses the existing RHI mesh pipeline on both Metal and GL; material quality selects 4 subdivisions per cell (medium/high) or 2 (low). Fog memory is respected. Legacy square territory/room-floor rendering remains the default; smooth mode is for territory surfaces and does not draw room-floor tints. Planet visuals retain their existing renderer. Counts, capture tests and victory still use exact simulation ownership. The ground-overlay Metal shader uses the shared LightU lighting block (matching GLSL's U2 layout); older builds referenced the obsolete U2 MSL type and silently lost the entire layer. Shader/pipeline failures now report the backend error to stderr. "diggable": {"D": {"hardness": 3}, "G": {"hardness": 6, "yields": {"gold": 250}}, "J": {"hardness": 8, "yields": {"gold": 40}, "infinite": true}}, "territory": {"claimBy": "both", "startFromRegions": false, "startRadius": 3, "buildOnlyOwned": true}, "rooms": { "lair": {"name": "Логово", "cost": {"gold": 10}, "supply": 1}, "hatchery": {"cost": {"gold": 12}, "income": {"food": 0.05}}, "treasury": {"cost": {"gold": 15}, "storage": {"gold": 500}}, "library": {"cost": {"gold": 20}, "income": {"research": 0.02}, "work": {"yields": {"research": 1}}}, "training": {"cost": {"gold": 20}, "work": {"xp": 3, "cost": {"gold": 0.5}}} }, "hand": {"max": 8, "ownTerritoryOnly": true, "slapDamage": 5, "slapDuration": 10, "slapSpeed": 1.5, "slapWork": 1.5}, "possession": {"cost": {"mana": 100}, "drain": {"mana": 2}} Diggable terrain: map characters listed in diggable (one character, not . ~ # , = / R or a digit) are solid cells. Players mark cells with the dig command; idle digs workers dig marked cells next to ground they can reach; the cell becomes ground (paths update) and yields is credited (infinite: the seam stays). Reinforced walls (territory.fortify: {"time": 2.5}, seconds per cell; "fortify": 2.5 works too): idle claimer workers, once nothing is left to dig or claim, reinforce diggable rock 4-adjacent to own floor into walls of their keeper (MapGrid::wall = owner slot, drawn in the owner colour with masonry courses). Nobody else can mark or dig such a wall - the enemy has to take the floor behind it first: a wall that no longer touches its keeper's floor falls back to plain rock within a second (and can then be reinforced by whoever owns the floor). The keeper digs through own walls normally. diggable.<char>.fortifiable (default: true for plain rock, false for cells with yields or infinite) says which rock can be reinforced. Event fortified (value = cell, player = new owner, 0 when a wall fell). Dungeon Keeper: the AI keeper's imps do it on their own. Territory (per-cell owner layer, MapGrid::territory; GameState::territoryCells[slot] / territoryTotal for the HUD share): starts from map "territory": {"rows": ["..11..", ...]} (digits = player slots), from owned regions (startFromRegions) and startRadius cells around starting structures and start points. Claimed by claimer workers and/or units with claim (claimBy: workers, units, both). buildOnlyOwned: every footprint cell must be own territory. Losing a cell removes a room painted on it. Rooms are painted on own territory (paint command with a rect); cost is per cell. Effects scale with the player's total cells of the type: supply (creature capacity), income, storage, provides per cell; work is earned per creature working inside (yields per second, xp per second for types with hero levels, cost per second). Painting over another room replaces it; erasing refunds sellRefund. Creature needs (needs on a ty

"storage": "buildings", "roadNetwork": {"cost": {"stone": 1}, "speed": 1.5}, "types": { "storehouse": {"structure": {"footprint": [3, 3]}, "storehouse": {"capacity": 2000}}, "woodcutter": {"structure": {"footprint": [2, 2]}, "recipe": {"out": {"wood": 1}, "time": 10, "from": "wood", "radius": 8}, "cost": {"planks": 3, "stone": 2}}, "sawmill": {"structure": {"footprint": [2, 2]}, "recipe": {"in": {"wood": 1}, "out": {"planks": 2}, "time": 8, "buffer": 2}}, "farm": {"structure": {"footprint": [3, 3]}, "recipe": {"out": {"grain": 1}, "time": 12}}, "serf": {"move": {"speed": 3}, "carrier": {"capacity": 1}}, "soldier": {"trainFrom": "recruit", "cost": {"sword": 1, "armor": 1, "time": 6}, "needs": {"hunger": {"interval": 120, "at": "inn", "time": 3, "cost": {"food": 1}, "starve": 1}}} } With "storage": "buildings" every stock resource that is not global is a good: it lives in building inventories. The player's stock of a good is the sum of its storehouses (storehouse.capacity = total goods); paying takes goods out of storehouses, income and bounties are put into them. Starting goods (resource start, map player resources) go into the first storehouses; map entities can carry "inventory": {"wood": 5}. Recipes: a workplace consumes in from its own inventory and produces out into it every time seconds (productionSpeed stat and power apply); it keeps buffer cycles of inputs and stops when buffer cycles of output are waiting. Raw producers have no in; from + radius deplete the nearest resource node or field cell of that resource (wood from trees, stone from a quarry, fish from water fields). Carriers (carrier.capacity per trip) haul on request, deterministically (every 0.5 s, buildings in entity order): construction sites and workplace inputs first (source: workplace output, else nearest storehouse), then workplace outputs to the nearest storehouse with room. With roadNetwork.required the source and destination must touch the same road network. Construction: goods in a structure's cost are not paid at once; carriers deliver them to the site and building progress can't exceed the delivered share (builders still build). Other resources are paid up front. Roads: map char +, the road command (rect), or the connect command (the sim paves the shortest path from a structure to the road network of an own storehouse). Movement on road cells is speed times faster. Recruits: trainFrom consumes an idle own unit of that type within 15 cells of the producer. Food: needs with "at": "<structure type>" are satisfied at the nearest own structure of that type (cost taken from the stock); starve hp per second is lost while the need is active.

"lanes": {"left": 4, "right": 2, "spacing": 0.35}: for every pair of garrison buildings the sim finds an A* path around obstacles and other buildings, smooths it into a fixed-point Catmull-Rom spline (about two samples per cell) and adds left + right parallel lanes spacing cells apart (pulled back towards the main lane where they would hit an obstacle). Sent units are spread over the lanes round-robin and follow their lane exactly. Lanes are rebuilt when garrison buildings or obstacles change (GameState::lanes, lanesDirty, event kEvLanesChanged).

Hand-authored routes between garrison structures, sends in rows, and a screen-sized play window over a larger map (modules/rts/RtsRoutes*.cpp). Lengths are map cells; every number is a rules / map key the game sets. Map routes (when a map has them they replace the generated lanes and turn lanes on): "routes": [ {"from": "village_1", "to": "base_a", // entity ids (or "#<index>" into "entities"), both garrisons "points": [[13.98, 2.62], [12.44, 2.2], {"at": [2.2, 4.58], "offsets": [0,0,0,0.2,0,0,0,0], "zone": 2, "slowdown": 1.5}, [1.74, 5]], "lines": [[[13.98, 2.62], [11.47, 1.92], ...], ...], // optional raw nodes per line "blockers": ["rock_3"], // the route is closed while any of them is alive "towersCoverage": [{"point": "p7", "distances": [0, 0, 0.5, 1.2, 3.4]}], "flying": false} // uses the fly column padding ] Each route becomes lanes.routes.lines lanes: line k follows its raw nodes when it has at least two, else the control points with the column offset of k on the inner points (even lines left, odd right; 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 columns of columnPadding, plus the per-point offsets[k]); a Catmull-Rom with smooth nodes between points. With trim > 0 nodes within trim of both ends are cut (lines start and end a little off the points). Lanes keep the route direction (Lane::a = from), offsets are -1, +1, -2, +2... in line order (lanesBetween returns line 0 first). Lanes exist for the whole match (stable indices). Sends need an open route: kCmdSend between garrisons without one is ignored; GameCore::canSend / routeLength (line 0) / routeAiLength and Lua game.can_send(a, b) / game.route_length(a, b) tell. A closed route (a blocker alive) only refuses new sends; units already on it keep walking. The built-in AI only sends along routes. Every line is walked at the progress of line 0 (lane speed x length k / length 0), so a row stays abreast in bends. Units on crossing or shared routes do not fight each other by themselves; a skill can make walkers shoot with GameCore::routeWalkerTargets (hostile walkers in an ellipse / forward sector, nearest first) and routeWalkerDistances (walked / left along the line). Walkers are ordinary unit entities with a LaneWalker. A route between entities whose screenGroups (map entity key, list of ints) do not match does not exist: both empty match, one empty does not, else any shared group. zone (game-defined bits, 2 = slowdown) / slowdown per point feed routeAiLength only. towersCoverage (for computer players): per tower entity the route length inside its range, for ranges 0, 1, 2 ... x routes.coverageStep (at most 21 values, the last holds beyond). GameCore::towerCoverage interpolates; towerUnitsDamage / towerDamageBySpline estimate losses of a group passing it. Walkers get a random diagonal offset (routes.jitter, one sim.rng() draw per unit) that fades in over routes.fade from both route ends; the same fade is the unit's opacity in the view (SceneObject::fade, routeAlpha). Flying sends: a garrison with a status carrying the flying flag sends along a straight flying route made on first use for that pair (in / out points routes.inOut from the ends, columns flyColumnPadding), even where no ground route exists or it is closed; rows are flyRowSpacing apart. groups.flyAll: such a send takes the whole garrison; groups.flySingle: one flying group per garrison at a time. GameCore::sendsFlying(from) tells. Rules (all optional, inside "lanes"): key default routes.lines 6 parallel lines per route = units per row (1..8) routes.columnPadding / flyColumnPadding 0.5 / 1.125 distance between columns routes.trim 0.25 cut from both ends of every line routes.smooth 10 spline nodes between control points routes.inOut 2.5 flying routes: straight part at both ends routes.jitter / routes.fade 0.125 / 0.5 walker offset / end fade length routes.coverageStep 1.25 range step of towersCoverage groups off true or {"rowSpacing": 1.75, "flyRowSpacing": 3, "flyAll": false, "flySingle": false} Groups (lanes.groups): a send creates a group (

Effects are the ability effects (any effect except blink; see "Abilities and effects"). Charges rearm one at a time after rearmTime, paying rearmCost. The AI fires them at enemy concentrations.

Everything a skill does is a list of effects (a payload). Effects can carry their own payload ("effects": [...]): a projectile delivers it on impact, an area applies it when it triggers, a chain applies it on every jump, a status ticks it, a weapon applies it on hit. Skills are compositions of these primitives; nothing is coded per skill. All keys below are optional; a game that uses none of them runs exactly as before (bit-identical replays).

{"id": "barrage", "name": "Ракетный залп", "target": "point", "range": 10, "cooldown": 8, "energy": 40, "cost": {"gold": 25}, "initialCooldown": 3, "castTime": 0.5, "backswing": 0.3, "charges": 2, "requires": ["rocketry"], "level": 1, "autocast": true, "smart": "densestEnemy", "delivery": {"type": "projectile", "speed": 10, "arc": true, "arcHeight": 3, "scatter": 1.2}, "effects": [{"type": "damage", "amount": [20, 30], "radius": 1.5, "falloff": 0.5}], "levels": [{"cooldown": 7, "effects": [{"amount": [30, 40]}]}, {"cooldown": 6, "effects": [{"amount": [40, 55]}]}]} key meaning target none, self, unit, point, structure (a structure, e.g. a garrison), group (units sent together, on a lane), player cost resources (besides energy); player abilities use cost only cooldown, initialCooldown seconds; the cooldownRate stat speeds cooldowns up charges unit abilities: N charges, one regenerates per cooldown (player abilities: {"max", "rearmCost", "rearmTime"}) castTime, backswing windup before the effect (event kEvCastStart; stun / silence / a new order cancel it) and the time the caster stays busy after; player abilities: castTime = activation delay requires types / techs that must exist (abilities granted by a tech tree) level hero level needed; levels: a table for levels 2, 3, ... — each entry overrides keys of the ability (effects merge by index). Sides are teams (free-for-all = one player per team; a king-of-the-hill score is shared by the team). block behaviour conquest team: true: a player with nothing left stays in the match while a teammate still has a base (the normal victory otherwise decides per player) domination a point's hold timer restarts on every owner change and runs while it is owned (points owned at the start begin with a running timer). When every domination point is owned (timers out, none neutral; points outside their owner's zone or screen are skipped): holdAny — sides owning none are out; holdAll — one side owning them all wins. auto: holdAny when every team has one player. type / garrison: what the marked points become while the mode is on kingOfTheHill each side starts with score (teamScore when a team has several players) and loses rate per second per king point it owns (inside its zone); the first side at zero wins (lowest score, then lowest team id). Event at alarm timeLimit counts seconds of game time down; at remaining the game speed becomes speed. At zero, by points per side: maxPoints — most wins, a tie of the best is a draw; compare — the only side with points x coefficient > best wins, else a draw. Sides without points take no part suddenDeath at at real seconds: preview (preview s, game speed previewSpeed), then every player gets status (e.g. incomeMult and cooldownRate mods). With end > 0 the side with most points wins end s later (all equal: draw; a tie of some: they win, the others draw — the match result is a draw). counter s before the start / the end ModesState::sdCounter is on (a countdown screen). One of ruleSets is picked with the match RNG and joins timedRules (time slots shifted by zones.suddenDeathDelay) zones each player's zone is the start rect holding its first structure; a rect stays stay s, then morphs linearly into steps[next] over move s (real time). A point outside its owner's current rect turns neutral (and into neutralType; garrison kept). Rects are [x, z, w, h] in cells, half-open Clocks: a tick stays one tick. GameCore::speedScale() (= time limit speed x preview speed) makes Simulation::advance run that many ticks per real tick; game timers

Optional blocks; a game without them plays exactly as before (stances and retreat commands work in any game). "stances": {"defendRadius": 6}, // defensive stance: chase at most this far from where it stood "retreat": {"speed": 1.25, "damageTaken": 0.75}, // the Retreat command (Company of Heroes / Dawn of War II) "types": { "hq": {"retreatPoint": true, ...}, // retreating units run to the nearest own one (else key / producer) "archer": {"stance": "defensive", ...}, // default stance of the type: aggressive | defensive | hold | passive "apc": {"transport": {"slots": 8, "accepts": ["infantry"], "layers": ["ground"], "unloadInterval": 0.5, "killOnDeath": 1}}, "bunker": {"transport": {"slots": 4, "fireFrom": 4, "heal": 2}}, // passengers shoot from inside "town_center": {"transport": {"slots": 15, "damagePerCargo": 0.2, "accepts": ["villager"]}}, // AoE: more arrows per garrisoned unit "ifv": {"transport": {"slots": 1, "weaponFromCargo": true}}, // the passenger's weapon fires (RA2 IFV) "tank": {"cargoSize": 4, ...} // slots a passenger takes (default 1) } Stances (command kCmdStance, param 0 aggressive, 1 defensive, 2 hold, 3 passive): aggressive = default behaviour; defensive = fights enemies within stances.defendRadius of its spot and walks back; hold = never moves on its own (persistent kCmdHold); passive = never attacks on its own (explicit attack orders still work). Retreat (kCmdRetreat, needs a retreat block): the units run to the nearest own retreatPoint (else a key structure, else a producer) with speed x speed and damageTaken x damage, without fighting; any new order ends it. The AI retreats fighters below 30% hp that see an enemy. Transports (transport on units or structures): kCmdLoad (units = passengers, target = transport; a right click on an own transport does the same), kCmdUnload (units = transports; param 1 + point: drive there first). Passengers are off the map (kUnitInCargo): not targetable, not drawn, not pushing; they ride with the carrier. accepts (type tags) and layers filter passengers, fireFrom passengers with weapons shoot from inside at the carrier's position, damagePerCargo raises the carrier's own damage per passenger, heal hp/s inside. When the carrier dies, killOnDeath of the passengers die with it (default 1 for units, 0 for structures) and the rest get out. Events kEvLoaded / kEvUnloaded (a = passenger, b = transport). The AI mans shooting structures (fireFrom: fighters; damagePerCargo: workers) when enemies are within 10 cells and lets workers out when it is safe.

h: Detection, toggles, veterancy, guard / follow, waypoints (agent-mech)
x: "veterancy": {"xp": [100, 300, 700], "perLevel": [{"stat": "damage", "add": 0.1}, {"stat": "armor", "add": 1}], "healOnLevel": true, "fromCost": 1}, "statuses": {"cloak": {"flags": ["invisible"]}, "burrowed": {"flags": ["invisible", "root", "disarm"]}}, "types": { "observer": {"detects": 9, ...}, // reveals invisible enemies within 9 cells (allies share it) "ghost": {"abilities": [{"id": "cloak", "target": "none", "toggle": {"status": "cloak", "drain": 1}}], ...}, "lurker": {"abilities": [{"id": "burrow", "target": "none", "toggle": {"status": "burrowed"}}], ...}, "wall": {"veterancy": false}, // or its own {"xp": [...], "perLevel": [...]} "tank": {"xp": 50, ...} // xp its killer gets (default: its cost x fromCost) } Detection: invisible objects (status flag invisible) can be targeted by a side only when revealed or within detects of one of its (or an ally's) detectors. GameCore::canSee(sim, e, viewer) is the query for the view/UI. Toggle abilities: casting switches the status on (until toggled off) and off; drain energy per second turns it off when energy runs out. Cloak, burrow, submerge, siege mode (a status with mods / flags) are data. Veterancy (ordinary units; heroes keep hero): the unit that dealt the last hit gets the victim's xp; ranks apply perLevel per rank above 1 and heal on rank-up; event kEvLevelUp (value = rank). Guard / follow (kCmdGuard, kCmdFollow, target = unit): follow within ~3 cells; guard also fights enemies within 6 cells of the guarded unit. Rally waypoints: kCmdRally with the queue flag (Shift) adds waypoints after the rally point; new units walk them in order. A plain rally clears them. The order queue itself (kCmdQueue on any command) always existed. Wave routes: map waves take "route": ["gate", [30, 8]] (area names or points), walked before the objective.

h: Combat and economy models (agent-mech keys = aliases of the fidelity blocks)
x: These keys come from agent-mech; they are parsed into the single implementation of each mechanic described in Fidelity mechanics and mean the same there. "armorModel": "percent", // = "armor": {"model": "percent", "negative": "exponential"}; "factor" = perPoint "armorModel": {"type": "subtract", "minFraction": 0.2, "min": 0}, // = "armor": {"model": "subtract", "minShare": 0.2, "minDamage": 0} "armorModel": {"type": "classes", "base": ["melee", "pierce"], "min": 1}, // = "armor": {"model": "classes", "base": [...], "minDamage": 1} "upkeepResources": ["gold"], // = "resources" of every upkeep tier that names none (Warcraft III) "types": { "spearman": {"weapons": [{"damage": 3, "attacks": {"melee": 3, "cavalry": 15}}], "armors": {"melee": 0, "pierce": 0, "infantry": 0}}, "knight": {"armors": {"melee": 2, "pierce": 2, "cavalry": 0}}, "zealot": {"shields": {"max": 50, "regen": 2, "delay": 10, "armor": 0}}, // StarCraft shields "goldmine": {"resourceNode": {"resource": "gold", "amount": 12500, "maxWorkers": 5}} } classes (Age of Empires II): damage = max(min, sum over the weapon's attacks of max(0, attack - armor of that class)); base classes always count (a missing armor is 0, armor upgrades raise them), other classes only against types that list them in armors (bonus damage is added, not multiplied). A weapon without attacks attacks the first base class with its damage. The damage table is not used in this model. Without min / minFraction the classes model floors at 1 and has no share floor. armorModel percent uses the exact Warcraft III curve for negative armor (2 - (1 - k)^-a); "armor" keeps the linear 1 + min(-a·k, 0.71) unless it says "negative": "exponential". type "shields": {"max", "regen", "delay", "armor"} = health.shields / shieldRegen / shieldDelay / shieldArmor (same defaults: regen 2/s, delay 10 s); one shield component (Shield) for both spellings. resourceNode.maxWorkers = resourceNode.maxGatherers: further workers wait next to the node or take a free node of the same resource nearby.

"market": {"currency": "gold", "prices": {"wood": 100, "food": 100, "stone": 130}, "fee": 0.3, "step": 3, "lot": 100}, "tribute": {"fee": 0.3}, "diplomacy": true, "items": {"potion": {"cost": {"gold": 50}, "use": {"heal": 200}, "charges": 1}, "boots": {"cost": {"gold": 100}, "mods": [{"stat": "speed", "add": 1}], "charges": 0, "consumable": false}}, "cycles": [{"id": "day", "length": 480, "phases": [{"id": "day", "until": 0.6}, {"id": "night", "until": 1, "status": "night"}]}, {"id": "season", "length": 1200, "phases": [{"id": "summer", "until": 0.75}, {"id": "winter", "until": 1, "status": "winter"}]}], "hazards": [{"field": "tiberium", "damage": 6, "tags": ["infantry"]}, {"area": "lava", "status": "burning"}], "deck": {"hand": 4, "deployNear": 8, "ownHalf": true}, "types": { "wall": {"wall": true, ...}, // built in a line (kCmdBuildLine) "gate": {"gate": "own" | "allies", ...}, // the owner walks through; enemies are stopped and attack it "bridge": {"bridge": true, ...}, // walkable ground over water while it stands (map-placed) "nydus": {"transport": {"slots": 20}, "tunnel": "nydus"}, // load at one, unload at any tunnel of the network "hovercraft": {"move": {"layer": "amphibious", ...}}, // ground and water "harrier": {"weapons": [{"ammo": 2, ...}]}, // empty: flies to the nearest own dock and rearms "airfield": {"dock": {"slots": 4, "rearmTime": 1}}, "templar": {"mergeInto": {"with": "templar", "result": "archon"}}, "archon": {"splitInto": {"type": "templar", "count": 2}}, "market": {"market": true}, "cart": {"trader": {"rate": 0.5}}, // currency per cell between the two markets per round trip "hero": {"inventory": {"slots": 6}}, "shop": {"shop": {"sells": ["potion", "boots"], "radius": 4}}, "kobold": {"drops": [{"item": "potion", "chance": 0.3}]} } Map players may have "deck": ["card ids..."] (default: every player ability). Commands: kCmdFormation (param 0 line, 1 box, 2 wedge, 3 loose, -1 break; a formation ordered to a point keeps its shape and the pace of its slowest member), kCmdBuildLine, kCmdMerge, kCmdSplit, kCmdTrade (sell / buy one lot; prices move by step and are shared by all), kCmdTradeRoute, kCmdTribute, kCmdDiplomacy (alliances need both sides; war moves the player to a new team), kCmdBuyItem / kCmdUseItem / kCmdDropItem / kCmdPickItem. Cycles apply their phase status to every player and set trigger variable cycle.<id> = phase index (event kEvCyclePhase). Jumps over cliffs, jetpacks and blinks are abilities with the blink effect; teleport networks are area effects with teleportTo. The AI sells surplus / buys shortages, sends idle carts to the farthest market, buys and drinks potions with heroes and merges idle pairs. Through MCP (scenario_run / play_command), trade, tribute and bounty take readable fields instead of the packed param: {"cmd": "trade", "units": [market], "resource": "wood", "sell": true}, {"cmd": "tribute", "resource": "gold", "amount": 100, "to": 2}, {"cmd": "bounty", "target": id, "resource": "gold", "amount": 50}.
Optional blocks; a game without them loads, plays and hashes as before. Tested in tests/tests_mech.inc (mech_tactics, mech_society, mech_rounds, mech_ai_staffing, mech_designs).

h: Cover, suppression, armor arcs (Company of Heroes, Men of War)
x: "cover": {"levels": {"1": 0.75, "2": 0.5}, "tags": ["infantry"]}, "suppression": {"decay": 5, "suppressed": 30, "pinned": 80, "suppressedSpeed": 0.5, "suppressedAttack": 0.5, "tags": ["infantry"]} cover.levels: damage multiplier per cover level 1..9. A unit (with one of tags, all if omitted) takes the level of its cell — map "cover": {"rows": ["0012..", ...]} (digit per cell) — or of a structure with "givesCover": N within half its footprint + 1.5 cells, whichever is higher. Weapon "suppress": 10 adds suppression (0..100) per hit; it decays by decay per second. Above suppressed the unit is slower and attacks slower; above pinned it cannot move. Type "armorArcs": {"side": 0.75, "rear": 0.5}: damage multiplier for hits from the side / rear by the unit's facing. Weapon "turret": {"turnRate": 90} (degrees per second): the weapon only fires once its turret faces the target. Weapon "crater": 1 (or {"radius": 1}): the ground around the hit becomes cover level 1.

h: Crews, crushing, ruins, infection (Z, Men of War, C&C, They Are Billions)
x: Crews are one mechanic with the fidelity crew / crews / killsCrew keys (see Fidelity mechanics): "crew": {"accepts": ["infantry"]} (or true: any mobile unit) is a crewed vehicle that any unit with an accepted tag may man, without "crews": true. Weapon "killsCrew": 1 (chance per non-lethal hit) leaves it empty and neutral (owner 0); a unit that may man it right-clicks it (smart / load), walks up and becomes its crew: the vehicle changes owner, the soldier is removed. "crush": {"damage": 500, "tags": ["infantry"]}: a moving unit damages hostile mobile units with those tags it touches. "ruins": "rubble": a type spawned (neutral) where this one died. Weapon "infect": "zombie": a unit it kills rises as that type for the killer's owner. A structure with "infectable": {"spawns": "zombie", "count": 2} destroyed by such a weapon spawns count of spawns.

h: Staff, growth, power fields (Settlers, Stronghold, StarCraft, Anno)
x: "staff": {"count": 2, "accepts": ["worker"]}: income and production scale with the share of places taken (workers enter with load / smart click; a transport block with count slots is created). The AI sends idle workers. "grows": {"unit": "villager", "interval": 30, "cost": {"food": 20}}: the structure produces the unit every interval seconds while it can pay and has supply. "powerField": 6 (radius) and "needsPower": true: a structure that needs power works and can be placed only inside a finished field of its owner.

"autonomous": true units are not commanded; they pick fights by themselves and prefer targets with a bounty. Command bounty (target, param = resource index | amount << 8) pays the amount, held until the target dies, to the owner of the unit that killed it. MCP: {"cmd": "bounty", "target": id, "resource": "gold", "amount": 100}.

"rounds": {"prepare": 20, "fight": 40, "rounds": 10, "reset": true, "lives": "lives", "damagePerUnit": 1, "income": {"gold": 5}} The game alternates a prepare phase (nobody acquires targets) and a fight phase. At the end of a fight each side loses damagePerUnit of lives per surviving enemy unit; with reset the armies are restored to the snapshot taken at the start of the fight. Everyone gets income per round. After rounds rounds (or when a side runs out of lives) the game ends: the side with most lives wins.

"upgradeGarrison": 10 on the target type of an upgrades entry is an alias of the fidelity key "cost": {"garrison": 10}: the upgrade costs that many units of the building's garrison on top of its resource cost (refused when the garrison is smaller; the units are taken only when the upgrade is queued).

Types can be assembled from a chassis and parts (Master of Orion, Galactic Civilizations, Supreme Commander kits). loadRules expands them into plain type blocks before parsing (expandDesigns), so every other key works as usual; rules_lint lints the expanded copy. "designs": { "chassis": {"light": {"move": {"speed": 4}, "health": {"max": 100}, "cost": {"gold": 50}, "slots": {"weapon": 2, "system": 1}}}, "parts": { "laser": {"slot": "weapon", "weapons": [{"range": 5, "damage": 10, "cooldown": 1}], "cost": {"gold": 20}}, "plating": {"slot": "system", "add": {"health.max": 60, "move.speed": -1}, "cost": {"gold": 30}, "health": {"armor": 2}} } }, "types": {"scout": {"design": {"chassis": "light", "parts": ["laser", "laser", "plating"]}, "sight": 8}} The chassis is copied; parts apply in order: add adds numbers at dotted paths, cost / upkeep add per resource, weapons, tags, abilities, upgrades are appended, other keys are merged (objects) or replaced. slots: a count, or a count per part slot kind; too many parts is a load error. The type's own keys (besides design) are applied last.

h: Morale, rout, fatigue, charge (Total War, Close Combat)
x: "morale": {"max": 100, "regen": 2, "hitLoss": 100, "allyDeath": 6, "allyRadius": 6, "flankSide": 1.5, "flankRear": 2, "waver": 40, "rout": 20, "rally": 60, "routSpeed": 1.25, "waverAttack": 0.85, "tags": ["soldier"], "general": {"tags": ["general"], "radius": 10, "regen": 6, "death": 30}}, "fatigue": {"run": 2, "fight": 4, "recover": 5, "tired": 50, "exhausted": 85, "tiredMul": 0.85, "exhaustedMul": 0.6} Morale (per unit, "morale": 120 on a type overrides max) falls by hitLoss x the share of max hp a hit takes, times flankSide / flankRear when the attacker is beside / behind the unit's facing; by allyDeath when an own unit dies within allyRadius (general.death within twice general.radius when a general dies). It recovers by regen per second, plus general.regen near an own general. Below waver the unit wavers (attack speed x waverAttack); below rout it routs: drops its orders, runs away from the nearest enemy (speed x routSpeed), does not fight and recovers only when no enemy is in sight, until rally. Event morale (value 0 steady, 1 wavering, 2 routing). The AI walks idle generals to its shakiest soldiers. Fatigue 0..100 grows by run per second moving and fight per second shooting, drops by recover when idle; above tired / exhausted speed and attack speed are multiplied by tiredMul / exhaustedMul. "charge": {"bonus": 1.5, "run": 3, "shock": 15, "cooldown": 8} on a type: after running run cells, the first blow deals bonus x damage and costs the target shock morale. MCP state shows morale, moraleState, fatigue, supplied.

h: Supply lines (Rise of Nations, Hearts of Iron)
x: "supply": {"tags": ["soldier"], "attrition": 0.01, "speed": 0.8, "attack": 0.8} and "supplyRadius": 12 on depot types: units farther than that from every finished own or allied depot lose attrition x max hp per second and move and attack slower.

"flowFields": true (or {"minCells": 8, "cache": 16}) is an alias of the one flow-field system (movement.flowField, see Movement): it means {"minGroup": 1, "minCells": 8, "maxFields": 16} — every ground move, attack-move, patrol or right-click order of a unit at least minCells cells from its goal follows the goal area's shared field (an explicit movement.flowField wins). In addition attack-move groups of more than 24 form a block of rows instead of one wide arc (each unit walks to its own row point with its own path). Separation and RVO neighbour lookups always use a one-cell grid (results identical to the spatial-hash version). Benchmark (ARM VM, -O3): 3000 units fighting, about 13 ms per tick.

"belt": {"structure": {"footprint": [1, 1]}, "conveyor": {"speed": 4}}, "drill": {"structure": {"footprint": [2, 2]}, "beltOutput": {"resource": "ore", "amount": 1, "interval": 0.5}}, "smelter": {"structure": {"footprint": [2, 2]}, "craft": {"in": {"ore": 2}, "out": {"plate": 1}, "time": 1}}, "core": {"structure": {"footprint": [2, 2]}, "beltInput": ["plate"]} A conveyor piece carries one packet per cell at speed cells per second in its direction (east, south, west, north): set by build_line (along the line's main axis), map entity "dir": "e", or command rotate ({"cmd": "rotate", "units": [...], "dir": "n"}; without dir it turns clockwise). Producers put a packet on a free adjacent belt that does not point back into them every interval; crafters take their inputs from belts (up to twice a batch), work time seconds (scaled by staff / power) and put outputs on belts. A structure with beltInput (resource list or "any") takes packets into its owner's stock (event delivered). Belts are ordinary structures (blocking, destructible); a packet on a destroyed belt is lost. The AI does not lay belts yet. MCP state: a belt's dir and carries, a crafter's input / output.
Tested in tests/tests_mech.inc (mech_turns, mech_strategic, mech_space_flight).

h: Turn-based mode (Heroes, XCOM, Advance Wars battles)
x: "turns": {"moveSeconds": 4, "attacks": 1, "timeLimit": 0}: players act one after another on the same simulation. During a turn only the active player's units move (at most type speed x moveSeconds cells) and shoot (attacks shots per weapon); the others stand still and don't return fire; commands of other players are ignored. Command end_turn (or timeLimit seconds) passes the turn to the next living player; event turn (player, turn number). Bots send their fighters at the nearest enemy once per turn and end the turn when they stop moving.

h: Strategic map (Total War campaign, Company of Heroes 3, Empire at War)
x: engine/game/Strategic.h: provinces and armies on top of the game's rules.json; battles are auto-resolved (Lanchester square law on hp x dps) or simulated on the RTS simulation with bots, and the survivors return to the map. {"players": [{"name": "Red"}, {"name": "Blue"}], "start": {"gold": 100}, "movesPerTurn": 1, "recruit": {"spear": {}, "archer": {"gold": 40}}, "battle": {"mode": "simulate", "seconds": 240, "size": [48, 32]}, "provinces": [{"id": "a", "owner": 1, "income": {"gold": 40}, "adj": ["b"], "pos": [0, 0], "terrain": {"rows": [...]}}, {"id": "b", "adj": ["c"]}, {"id": "c", "owner": 2}], "armies": [{"owner": 1, "at": "a", "units": {"spear": 12}}, {"owner": 2, "at": "c", "units": {"spear": 6}}]} Adjacency is symmetric. recruit with {} uses the type's cost. Moving into a province with an enemy army fights a battle; an empty enemy or neutral province is taken. Own armies in one province merge. Income of owned provinces comes at the start of the owner's turn; a player with no provinces and no armies is out; the last one standing wins. MCP: strategic_load (file in the project or def), strategic_state, strategic_order (move / recruit / end_turn), strategic_bots (bots play N turns; battle: auto | simulate), strategic_battle_map (the RTS map of a battle, to play by hand), strategic_save.

"altitude": {"min": 0, "max": 30, "climb": 3, "start": 10} on an air type: the unit keeps its own height, climbs or dives to the y of its move orders (MCP {"cmd": "move", "x", "z", "y"}), follows the height of the target it attacks, and weapon ranges to and from it are measured in 3D. Paths and avoidance stay 2D. The view does not draw the altitude yet.

Type keys (all optional; engine/game/Sensors.h). Radii are in cells. "radar_tower": {"radar": 30, "income": {"energy": -20}}, // enemies inside the circle are contacts of its side "sonar_buoy": {"sonar": 25}, // the same for underwater units (radar does not see them) "jammer": {"jammer": 12}, // hides its own side's units inside the circle from enemy radar / sonar "spy": {"stealth": true}, // never a radar contact (still seen in sight) "submarine": {"move": {"layer": "naval"}, "underwater": true, // only weapons with "underwater": true hit it "weapons": [{"range": 6, "damage": 80, "underwater": true, "targets": ["naval"]}]}, // rules "radar": {"targeting": true} // units pick targets beyond their sight, up to weapon range, that their side sees or tracks A contact is an enemy inside the radar (sonar, for underwater units) circle of the viewer or an ally, not inside a jammer circle of its own side and not stealthy. Unpowered (kUnitDisabled), unfinished or carried sources are off. The view draws contacts outside sight as red dots (no model: the viewer does not know the type). Native code: GameCore::sensors()->onRadar(sim, e, viewer), blips(sim, viewer). radar.targeting: artillery and long-range towers fire at what radar or allies see. Without it nothing changes. Bots build one structure with radar once their base runs (ComputerPlayer); contacts feed their long-range guns. No state: contacts are recomputed from the units, so saves and replays carry nothing extra; games without these keys keep their checksums.

Optional blocks for flow-economy wars (engine/game/FieldOps.h; state in the FieldOpsStore resource: hashed, saved). Games without them have no extra system and keep their checksums. // rules "repair": {"cost": 0, "units": true}, // share of the cost for a full repair (default 0.3); mobile units too "reclaim": {"units": true, "refund": 1}, // builders take units apart (own or enemy) for that share of their cost "selfDestruct": {"time": 5}, // kCmdSelfDestruct arms a countdown (again: disarms); death effects apply "ambient": {"wind": {"min": 0, "max": 25, "every": [15, 45]}, "tidal": 18}, // the map's "ambient" overrides key by key // types "con_kbot": {"assist": true, "patrolWork": true}, // guard a factory: adds build power; patrol: repairs / reclaims on the way "wind_gen": {"income": {"energy": 2}, "ambientIncome": {"wind": {"energy": 1}}}, // + wind strength x 1 energy/s "tidal_gen": {"ambientIncome": {"tidal": {"energy": 1}}}, "nuke_silo": {"tags": ["nuke"], "stockpile": {"max": 5, "time": 90, "cost": {"metal": 1000, "energy": 20000}, "abilities": ["launch"]}, "abilities": [{"id": "launch", "target": "point", "range": 200, "effects": [{"type": "projectile", ...}]}]}, "anti_nuke": {"intercept": {"radius": 40, "tags": ["nuke"]}, "stockpile": {"max": 3, "time": 60, "cost": {"metal": 500}}}, "bomber": {"move": {"layer": "air"}, "attackRun": {"overshoot": 5}, "seekRepair": 0.3, "weapons": [{"range": 1.5, "damage": 200, "targets": ["ground"]}]}, "air_pad": {"repairPad": {"heal": 40, "radius": 1.5}} Repair / reclaim: kCmdRepair (target = damaged own or allied unit; structures always, mobile units with repair.units), kCmdReclaim (target = resource node: a gather order; a unit: OrderType::Reclaim, at the builder's buildPower over the target's build time, paying the cost x refund while it shrinks; no wreck, no death blast). Smart click on a damaged own unit repairs it when repair.units is on. Assist: a builder with assist guarding (kCmdGuard) an own producer within 5 cells adds its buildPower to the producer's (step x (1 + sum / producer buildPower)); progressive costs are paid at the faster rate. Patrol work: a patrolWork builder on patrol repairs damaged allies in sight first, then gathers flow resource nodes (wrecks, rocks, trees) it passes; the patrol resumes after each job. Stockpile: charges build one at a time over time seconds (scaled by low power), paying cost as they build and stalling when short; abilities listed in abilities (default: every ability of the type) need and use a charge. The bot uses them through ability autocast + smart targeting. Intercept: hostile projectiles shot by types with any of tags are destroyed inside radius; with a stockpile each interception uses a charge. Event kEvFieldOp (value kFieldOpIntercepted, a = interceptor, b = projectile). Ambient income: the wind changes every every seconds to a random strength in [min, max] (sim RNG); tidal is constant per map. ambientIncome adds strength x amount per second to the owner's income (finished, powered objects). Keep a small fixed income on such types so the bot counts them as income buildings. Attack runs: an attackRun unit flies over its target and overshoot cells past it, then turns for the next pass; its weapons fire while passing (short-range bombs). Repair pads: units standing still within radius of an own or allied repairPad heal heal hp/s for free; seekRepair sends an idle unit below that health share to the nearest own pad. Events kEvFieldOp: value & 0xFF = kFieldOpArmed (data = ticks left) / Disarmed / Stockpiled (data = charges) / Intercepted / Wind (data = strength). Native code: GameCore::fieldOps() (stockpile, selfDestructAt, wind).

Simulation::serialize() returns the whole dynamic state as bytes (versioned, little-endian, identical on every platform: engine/core/Archive.h); deserialize(bytes) loads it into a simulation set up from the same rules, map and seed and checks the state checksum stored in the file. Saved: tick, RNG, players and teams, pending and executed commands (replays continue), the entity allocator, every component pool in dense order and the dynamic part of GameState (per-cell layers run-length encoded). Not saved: rules, triggers, the planet surface (from setup) and derived caches (clearance, HPA*, rebuilt on demand). The computer players keep their own memory, so bots resume from the loaded state with fresh plans. Module side: GameCore::serializeState (engine/game/Save.cpp); a component type missing from its list makes saving fail. aiverse_headless --save F --save-at S / --load F; MCP match_run with saveCheck (seconds). A skirmish match at 90 s is ~150 KB. Since save version 9 the frozen match outcome (MatchOutcome) is saved too: a state from before the end, loaded into a simulation that had already finished, no longer keeps the old result (the computer players stopped and --verify-restore-at windows across the match end desynced on the serialized pass); older saves load with no outcome, latched again on the next tick.

campaign.json in the game folder chains missions; see engine/game/Campaign.h: {"start": "m1", "missions": [ {"id": "m1", "name": "Raid", "map": "maps/m1.json", "briefing": "campaign.m1.briefing", "next": "m2", "carry": {"resources": ["gold"], "tags": ["hero"], "types": ["knight"], "max": 12}}, {"id": "m2", "name": "Siege", "map": "maps/m2.json"}]} Trigger actions for missions: {"type": "objective", "id": "raze", "text": "...", "op": "add" | "done" | "fail", "primary": true}, {"type": "dialog", "speaker": "Captain", "portrait": "ui/captain.png", "voice": "vo/c1.ogg", "text": "...", "duration": 4}, {"type": "camera", "at": [x, z] | "area": "a", "zoom": 1, "duration": 2, "lock": false}, {"type": "endMission", "result": "victory" | "defeat", "next": "m2"}. State in GameState::mech (objectives, dialogs, nextMission, missionResult, saved with the match); events kEvObjective, kEvDialog, kEvCamera, kEvMissionEnd for the HUD (objective list, dialog box, camera moves). Between missions collectCarry (survivors with hp, rank, hero level; resources) -> applyCarry (into the next map, players[0] = campaign player) -> restoreCarry after setup. MCP: campaign_get, campaign_set (validated), campaign_run (bots, mission chain, outcomes, carry).

Optional rules block raid (+ map raid overrides): the match loop of extraction shooters — raiders (types in raiders, carrying loot in their inventory item bags), hold-to-use objects (interact per type, loot tables), objectives (collect / reach / kill / interact / script), extraction points (zones with open / sleep cycles, called helicopters with arrival, channel, contest, leave, interruptOnDamage, requires), match phases and per-player receipts for the meta. Full reference: raid.md; sample: templates/extraction.

Besides the unit commands (GameCore.h): kCmdSurrender (the issuing player is defeated, event value 1), kCmdDig / kCmdPaintRoom (point = first cell, param = rectParam(w, h, extra): dig extra 0 mark / 1 unmark; room extra = room index or -1 erase), kCmdPickUp (units), kCmdDrop (point; units or param = count), kCmdSlap (units), kCmdPossess (units[0]; empty = release), kCmdDirect (point = direction, param bit 0 = fire, optional target), kCmdPlayerAbility (param = index, point), kCmdBuildRoad (rect, extra 1 = remove), kCmdConnectRoad (units = own structures), kCmdTransit (planets: orbit units, param = target body), kCmdStance (param = stance), kCmdRetreat, kCmdLoad (target = transport), kCmdUnload (param 1 = drive to point first), kCmdGuard / kCmdFollow (target = unit). kCmdRepair / kCmdReclaim (builders, target = unit) and kCmdSelfDestruct (units): see "Field operations". kCmdPlayerAbility with a structure / group / player ability takes the clicked object in target (or the nearest one to point).

Event → conditions → actions, evaluated inside the deterministic simulation. {"id": "relic", "once": true, "enabled": true, "forEachPlayer": false, "event": {"type": "enterArea", "area": "relic", "player": 1, "unit": "hero"}, "conditions": [{"type": "count", "player": "triggering", "kind": "structure", ">=": 3}], "actions": [{"type": "message", "text": "Реликвия найдена!"}, {"type": "give", "resource": "gold", "amount": 500}]} Events: start, time (seconds), every (seconds), enterArea / leaveArea (area, unit filter), unitDied, built, trained (unit filter), researched (tech), captured, wave, regionClaimed, playerDefeated, ability, levelUp, resource (resource, comparison: fires when it becomes true), variable (name, comparison). Event player: a slot number, "any" (default), "creeps". Unit filter (events, conditions, actions): "unit": "type", "tags": [...], "kind": "structure"|"unit", "area": "name" or [x,z,w,h]. Comparisons: one of ">=", ">", "<=", "<", "==", "!=" with a number. Conditions: count (objects matching the filter), resource, variable, researched, random (chance), time (seconds), alive, regions (owned count). "not": true negates. Actions: spawn (unit, count, at [x,z] / area, attackMove), give / take (resource, amount), setOwner, kill, remove, damage, heal (amount), buff (stat, add/mul, duration), message (text), setVariable / addVariable (name, value), research (tech), enableType / disableType (unit), victory / defeat, enableTrigger / disableTrigger (trigger), addScore (amount), setRegionOwner (region name), attackMove / move (units matching the filter to at / area), setTickets (amount); Bunker Wars bot triggers (agent-bw-ai): setResource (resource, amount: the stock becomes amount, e.g. morale), resetCooldowns (the players' player abilities are ready), setProduction (amount: production speed coefficient of the matching structures, replacing the previous one), timeScale (amount: game speed, needs match modes / matchStats). Action player: "triggering" (default: the player of the event), "all", "enemies", "allies", "creeps", "neutral", or a slot number. "target": "triggeringUnit" acts on the event's unit.

scenario_run runs a scripted check on a copy of the open map: named spawns, timed commands (keys of play_command), optional bots, checks (pass/fail) and watch / events / trigger logs. Every fired trigger is also a simulation event kEvTriggerFired (value = trigger index: rules triggers first, then map triggers; player = triggering slot) — presentation/tools only, not hashed. rules_lint lists keys the loader never reads; rules_schema with part: "keys" lists every key the loader reads per block, taken from the loader itself.

native_status compares rules.json nativeModules with what the running editor binary has compiled in (required, compiled, missing) and describes the per-project editor build in <project>/Builds/.temp/editor-<host> (editor, headless, built, buildModules, upToDate, ready, why). native_build configures and builds aiverse_editor + aiverse_headless there with -DAIVERSE_CONTENT_DIR=<project> (Release), streaming into the build log (build_status); wait: true blocks until it ends and returns the binary paths. See docs/native-modules.md.

The editor's Build window shows oversized atlas candidates under “Не в атласе”. “Исправить размеры текстур” applies the proposed maximum sizes as exact, first-priority packaging.targets.<platform>.files rules and refreshes the size estimate. This reduces image detail in the built pack; original assets are unchanged. Sprite sheets, tile atlases, and UI @spritesheet sources in RCSS with pixel-based coordinates are never offered this fix. Existing resize rules for these sources are ignored during packaging to preserve their frame coordinates. Other exclusions (repeat wrapping, noAtlas, decode failures, a lone image in a group) require manual decisions. Recalculate a stale report before applying fixes; the button is disabled while settings differ from the report. When a game is packaged (aiversebuild, assetpipe pack --atlas <profile>), small 2D images are packed into atlas pages: fewer texture switches/draw calls, trimmed transparent borders, identical images stored once, and pages compressed by the pack's zstd. Game code keeps using the original paths (units/orc/grunt/walk_0.png); the lookup is transparent at runtime. Loose-folder builds (--no-pack, editor) use the images as they are. The whole block is optional: "atlas": { "enable": true, // false (or aiversebuild --no-atlas): ship images as is "maxPage": { "web": 2048, "android": 2048, "default": 4096 }, // or a single number "pageSize": "mul4", // page sides: multiples of 4 (default) or "pow2" "padding": 2, // empty texels between images "extrude": 1, // edge texels repeated around each image (no filtering seams) "trim": true, // cut fully transparent borders (offsets are kept) "maxTextureSize": 0, // larger images stay standalone; 0 = maxPage / 4 "mipLevels": 2, // groups with "mips": padding/alignment safe down to 2^levels "pageFormat": "rtex", // "rtex" (raw RGBA, zstd in the pack, fastest load) or "png" "groups": { "units": { "rotate": false, "mips": true }, "tiles": { "trim": false } }, "files": { // glob -> settings; `*` also matches '/'; later rules win "ui/splash/*": { "noAtlas": true }, "units/orcs/*": { "group": "orcs" }, "textures/water.png": { "wrap": "repeat" }, "units/*/shadow.png": { "kind": "mask" } } } Profiles are aiversebuild targets (macos, ios, android, web, windows, linux); built-in page limits: 2048 for web/android, 4096 otherwise. Targets with equal settings share one pack. What goes together. An image's group key is usage group + kind (+ opaque/alpha when the group splits by alpha, + mips). Images only share a page with the same key: usage group default folders (first path component, engine/ prefix ignored) defaults ui ui/, icons/, portraits/, cursors/, hud/ trim units sprites/, units/, buildings/, structures/, characters/ trim tiles tiles/, tilesets/, terrain/ no trim (sheet grids stay intact), opaque and alpha tiles on separate pages effects effects/, fx/, vfx/, particles/ trim any name set with "group" (or "atlasGroup") in files as units Other folders (models/, textures/, ...) are not atlased unless a files rule names a group: 3D meshes use UVs outside 0..1 and wrap. Kind is color, normal (*_n, *_nrm, *_normal, normals/) or mask (*_mask) — normal maps and masks are never mixed with colour and never trimmed. Never atlased: noAtlas, "wrap": "repeat" (also *_repeat, *_tiling, *_wrap), images above maxTextureSize (after trimming), and an image that would be alone in its group (one page = no saved texture switch, only padding). Images referenced as a frame-grid sprite sheet anywhere in the game's JSON ("sheet": "sprites/tank.png") are never trimmed or rotated, so frame uvs map linearly onto the atlas region. Inside a group, images of one folder (one unit's frames, one faction) stay on the same page whenever they fit; pages are shrunk to the smallest size that holds them. Per-file keys: group/atlasGroup, noAtlas, wrap, kind, rotate (allow a 90° turn, off by default so facings never rotate), trim, mips, splitAlpha, padding, extrude, mesh, tight, frames, me

h: Icons and splash (game.json icons, splash, optional)
x: Both blocks are read by aiversebuild (every size each platform needs, generated on the host without sips/iconutil — works from Linux), by the client (the splash) and by the editor window Иконки и заставка (opened from Сборка) / MCP branding_get, branding_set, icons_preview, splash_preview. Paths are relative to the game folder. Code: tools/branding (host), engine/splash (runtime), apps/client/ClientSplash.cpp (startup).

"icons": { "default": "branding/icon.png", // master: square, >= 1024 px (old "icon" is the fallback) "background": "#101a28", // for icons that must be opaque (else: the image's edge colour) "padding": 0.0, // artwork inset on opaque squares (fraction of the side) "cornerRadius": 0.0, // rounding of the Android legacy icon (default 0.12) "ios": "branding/icon_ios.png", // path, or {"image", "background", "padding"} "macos": {"margin": 0.098, "cornerRadius": 0.225}, // Big Sur grid by default; 0/0 for pre-shaped art "android": {"legacy": "...", "round": "...", // path or look object "foreground": "branding/icon_foreground.png", // adaptive 108dp layer (centre 72dp visible) "background": "#101a28", // colour or image path "monochrome": "branding/icon_monochrome.png", // Android 13 themed icon (alpha is used) "foregroundPadding": 0.17}, // when the master is used as the foreground "windows": "...", "linux": "...", "web": {"image": "...", "appleTouch": {...}, "maskable": {...}} } A look object (any platform) has image, background, padding (inset of the art inside the icon body), margin (transparent space around the body), cornerRadius (fraction of the body), circle. Warnings (build log, branding_get): master missing, smaller than 1024, not square, iOS image with transparency (it is flattened on background). Platform Generated (aiversebuild) iOS gen/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset: iPhone 40..180, iPad 20..167, App Store 1024 + Contents.json (opaque) macOS gen/AppIcon.iconset (16..512@2x) and gen/AppIcon.icns (written by aiversebuild; iconutil re-packs it on a Mac) Android res/mipmap-{mdpi..xxxhdpi}/ic_launcher.png, ic_launcher_round.png, ic_launcher_foreground.png (+ _background, _monochrome), mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher(_round).xml, values/ic_launcher_background.xml, app/src/main/ic_launcher-playstore.png (512); manifest gets android:roundIcon Windows gen/app.ico (16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64 BMP + 256 PNG) and gen/app.rc (icon resource 1, also the window icon), compiled into the .exe Web favicon.ico (16/32/48), favicon-32.png, apple-touch-icon.png (180, opaque), icons/icon-{192,512}.png, icons/maskable-{192,512}.png, manifest.webmanifest (PWA); links injected into index.html Linux share/icons/hicolor/<n>x<n>/apps/<exe>.png (16..512) and share/applications/<exe>.desktop next to the executable

Every client - game, actor (first / third person, races, battle royale) and voxel projects - shows the same loading screen at startup and on map loads (engine/splash/SplashBoot.h), and the project alone decides what it is: "splash" value Loading screen missing, null, true, "default" the engine's screen (the AIVERSE mark assembling) false, "none", {"enabled": false} none: the game loads, then shows (no logo, no bar, no labels) {"base": "engine", ...} the engine's screen with these keys replaced; objects merge, so {"base": "engine", "progress": {"color": "#00c0ff"}} only recolours the bar, "logos": [...] swaps the art, "minSeconds": 0 leaves as soon as loading is done any other object the project's own screen (format below); background only = {"background": "#000000", "progress": false} "mapLoading" inside the block chooses the screen of later map loads: "same" (default), false (none) or any value from the table. The engine art is found from a package (content/engine) and, in dev runs on a project folder, from the engine's engine/assets (platform::setEngineAssetsDir). Choices: splash::resolveBlock / resolveMapBlock / projectSpec, test splash_choice. "splash": { "background": "#0a0f16", "image": "branding/splash_bg.png", "fit": "cover", "scale": 1, // base layer (optional) "logos": [ {"image": "branding/studio.png", "start": 0, "duration": 2.2, "scale": 0.34, "animation": {"fadeIn": 0.5, "fadeOut": 0.45, "zoom": {"from": 0.85, "duration": 0.8}}}, {"image": "branding/logo.png", "start": 2.0, "scale": 0.55, "anchor": [0.5, 0.46], "animation": [{"t": 0, "opacity": 0, "scale": 0.7}, {"t": 0.6, "opacity": 1, "scale": 1, "ease": "out"}]}, {"sheet": "branding/coin_sheet.png", "frame": [128, 128], "count": 8, "fps": 14, "start": 2.5, "scale": 0.2} ], "minSeconds": 3.5, "maxSeconds": 6, "loop": false, "skippable": true, "fadeOut": 0.5, "waitForContent": false, "progress": {"show": true, "color": "#e8b640", "track": "#ffffff26", "position": "bottom", "width": 0.36, "height": 5, "offset": 0.08}, "native": {"image": "branding/logo.png", "background": "#0a0f16", "scale": 0.35, "androidIcon": "branding/splash_icon.xml"} } Layers (base image first, then logo / logos in order, later on top): a static image, an animation from frames (list of images) or a sprite sheet (frame [w, h], count, frames in rows left to right) played at fps (loopFrames, default true). fit: contain (default for logos), cover (default for the base), center (image pixels × dpi), stretch; scale multiplies the fitted size; anchor is the centre on screen (fractions). start / duration in seconds (duration 0 = until the splash ends). animation: keyframes [{"t", "opacity", "scale", "x", "y", "rotate" (degrees), "ease": linear|in|out|inOut}] (t from the layer start; a property is interpolated between the keys that set it), or effects {"fadeIn", "fadeOut", "fade", "pulse": amount | {"amount", "period"}, "rotate": deg/s, "slide": "bottom" | {"from", "distance", "duration"}, "zoom": from | {"from", "duration"}, "keyframes": [...]} — both combine. Timing: the splash leaves when loading is done and minSeconds have passed (default: the end of the last layer with a duration, so a studio logo → game logo sequence plays once); maxSeconds caps that minimum (never the loading). loop: repeat the sequence while loading takes longer. skippable: a tap / click / key ends the minimum. fadeOut: crossfade to the menu. Progress bar: real loading progress — the client's startup steps (rules, renderer, models and textures of every type, effects, audio, UI), and with waitForContent (split builds) the download of every pack chunk (platform::contentProgress). In-engine splash: drawn through the RHI from the first frame (engine/splash, one textured quad pipeline, GLSL + MSL; images decoded one per frame and capped at 2048 px), so it runs on any GPU. AIVERSE_SPLASH=off loads the old way; with --map the splash only covers loading (AIVERSE_SPLASH=full plays it all). Native launch screen (shown by the OS before

Dune II: spice fields, capped spice with silos storage, terrain: "rock" for structures, sandworm neutral.wander + move.layer: "sand". Total Annihilation: flow metal/energy with income, costModel: "progressive", commander key + victory: keyUnits, extractors structure.on: metal_spot, wreck reclaim; radar / sonar / jammer / stealth + rules radar.targeting, underwater subs and torpedoes, rules repair / reclaim / selfDestruct, assist + patrolWork builders, ambient wind / tidal generators, geothermal vents as structure.on, nuke silos stockpile + anti-nukes intercept, bombers attackRun, air repairPad (templates/metaltide). Age of Empires II: four stock resources, farms with infinite ownerOnly nodes, ages as techs required by types, techs with tag effects. Company of Heroes: squad, capture points with victoryPoint, victory: tickets, income from captured points via triggers or income on point types. They Are Billions: map waves from a waves: true player, victory: survive, buildRadius. Northgard: regions with claimCost and buildOnlyOwned.
