leg on his way: walk, to_stop, at_stop, drive) and the game day (rules traffic.population) game.traffic_kind(h) → "car"\ "bus"\ "emergency"\ nil a vehicle the traffic drives (sirens, HUD) game.var(name) trigger variable (fx) game.data(h), game.has_data(h, key) the entity's own persistent table (view: read-only copy of the table as the simulation scripts hold it now, any unit incl. neutral props) / does it have the key game.orders(h), game.current_order(h) the order queue / its first order: {order, x, z, target, param, state} (order: move attack_move attack patrol gather return build repair enter cast dig claim_cell need haul board unload follow rearm trade pick_item merge) game.target(h), game.idle(h) weapon target (else the current order's target) / no orders, not moving, not fighting, nothing in production game.facing(h) → dx, dz, game.velocity(h) → vx, vz, game.path(h), game.energy(h) → energy, max path: remaining waypoints {{x, z}, ...} ending at the goal game.log(...), print(...) script log Filter: {owner = 2, type = "footman", tag = "mechanical", kind = "unit" | "structure", area = "gate", x = 10, z = 12, radius = 6, has = "morale", sort = "id" | "dist", limit = 5} (all optional; has: the entity's game.data table has that key; sort = "dist": nearest to x, z first, ties by handle). Radius queries use a bucket grid of the living units, built on the first radius query and kept while the script only reads (any action, or C++ running in between, drops it): many game.units{x, z, radius} calls in one handler cost one pass over the units plus the buckets they touch. Results are exactly those of a full scan (same order). Actions (simulation scripts only): function game.give(p, res, amount), game.take(p, res, amount) → taken resources game.spawn(type, owner, x, z) → handle or nil owner 0 = neutral, 255 = hostile creeps game.attack_event(actor, target) emit the standard attack animation/FX/audio cue for scripted combat; no damage, projectile or order; false for invalid/dead handles; simulation only game

Maps with routes / screen (docs/game-format.md § Routes): game.can_send(a, b) (an open route joins the two garrisons; always true without routes), game.route_length(a, b) (line 0, nil without a route), game.screen() -> x, z, w, h of the current screen (nil without one), game.on_screen(x, z), and in simulation scripts game.set_screen(x, z) (moves the screen centre, clamped to its bounds).

Per-cell layers (fire, water, creep, influence...) defined in rules "fields" run as C++ kernels; scripts read and write them: field.get(id, x, z [, player]), field.set / field.add / field.fill_rect / field.fill_circle, field.sum / field.max / field.count / field.find over a rectangle or disc, and on_field_threshold(id, value, fn [, "rise" | "fall"]) hooks. Values are integers (int fields) or fx (fixed). View scripts get the read-only part. Reference: docs/fields.md.

State of the city services (traffic.services, ServiceState.h) and the handles a script uses to take a person, a vehicle or a hero over for a while. Queries work in view scripts too; the actions only in simulation scripts. Query Returns services.custody(player) phase (0 free, 1 cuffed, 2 walked, 3 boarding, 4 driven, 5 delivered), custody vehicle or nil, deliveries services.held_by(e) the custody vehicle holding e, or nil services.stand_in(body) victim handle and victim type id of a stand-in body, or nil services.custody_car(car) / services.carry(car) phase (0: none), prisoner / patient or nil services.carried(car) delivered, x, z of the carry the vehicle ended within the last minute, or nil services.totals() custody deliveries, carry deliveries, calls answered by a vehicle already out services.crossing(e) 0 walking, 1 waiting for a vehicle, 2 peeking past a parked one services.passenger(e) claim, aboard, walk result, walk done services.citizen(id) held, off, journey (nil: no such citizen) Action Effect services.claim(e, claim) take a person over (0 gives him back to the pedestrians) services.board(e, aboard) a claimed person rides inside a vehicle services.walk(e, request, x, z) a claimed person walks to (x, z); passenger answers +request / -request, then done services.signals(vehicle, beacon, siren) >0 on, <0 off, 0 automatic services.door(vehicle, open) 0 closed, -1 / 1 open left / right (presentation) services.hold(car, held) the script runs the crew's work at the scene and their way back in services.set_citizen(id, held, off, journey) held: the schedule leaves him alone; journey 1 to work, 2 home services.control(player, held) the player's stick does not move his hero while held

{"type": "script", "fn": "chain_heal", "jumps": 3, "amount": 60} Ability effect (any effect list: abilities, projectiles, areas, statuses...): fn(ctx) with ctx = {caster, owner, target, x, z, scale, source_type, targets, args} — targets are the handles the effect's filter selected (radius, affects...), args is the effect's JSON. It runs in the scripts phase of the same tick. Trigger action {"type": "script", "fn": "f", ...}: fn(ctx), ctx = {player, unit, x, z, tick, trigger, args}. Trigger condition {"type": "script", "fn": "f", ...}: fn(ctx) returns true / false. Functions named in data that the scripts don't define are reported when the match loads.

These APIs let games implement front lines in Lua without adding game-specific C++ behavior. Simulation arguments use integers or fx; persistent assignments belong in state. API Contract game.territory_at(x,z) Ground cell owner, including neutral 0; nil outside ground. Flat maps only. game.territory_count(player) Number of owned cells; uses the same counters as victory and the HUD. game.frontier(player) Array of unit-length land boundary segments, sorted by cell index then east/south/west/north edge. Each {x,z,nx,nz,owner,cell} has an fx midpoint, integer outward normal, neighbouring owner and zero-based neighbouring cell index. Excludes the sea and map rim. game.order_target(unit) x,z for the first move/attack-move order; otherwise nil. Read this before consuming the order with set_position. game.paint_territory(player,x,z,radius,connected=false) Change ground cells whose centres lie inside the disk, returning the changed count. Radius must be 0..64, player must exist (0 clears ownership), and rules.territory must be enabled. Off-map centre returns 0. With connected=true, candidate cells must touch ownership present before this brush call. Uses normal territory events, counters, room invalidation and save/hash state. game.set_position(unit,x,z) Place a living mobile unit on flat-map ground; returns false for stale handles, structures, water or out-of-map destinations. Stops native movement, clears queued orders and preserves prevPos for frame interpolation. Does not pathfind, avoid other units or test intermediate terrain. The game script chooses legal trajectories. territory_at, frontier, paint_territory and set_position currently reject planet maps with an explicit error. Queries are available in view scripts; the two mutation methods are not. frontier scans the map: cache its result in state and refresh a few times per second, not once per soldier. Read endpoints and distribute slots by length, then match soldiers to nearby free slots in deterministic handle order. Move a bounded distance per tick; paint only after successful placement. User destinations must originate in regular commands, obtainable through order_target. local x,z = game.pos(unit) if game.set_position(unit, x + fx(1,20), z) then game.paint_territory(game.owner(unit), x + fx(1,20), z, fx("0.8"), true) end Use movement.avoidance: "none" to disable both ORCA and body separation for formations; body radii retain their meaning for range queries. Smooth rendering is optional and independent of simulation: game.json → terrain.territory: {smooth:true, transition:0.2, fill:0.4}. Ownership remains deterministic cell data; the view reconstructs a soft contour and animates it. The view never writes ownership or decides victory. Validation for this API: aiverse_tests script_territory_brush_frontier_and_placement checks brush counts, overwriting ownership, the connected-brush restriction, frontier segment counts, invalid placement, overlapping units with avoidance:none, and snapshot replay equivalence. The full macOS suite passed 4967 checks. A 3600-tick project battle replay matched all checkpoints. The 78 template/fixture checksum runs retained current HEAD behavior: the checked-in baseline contains duplicate obsolete lastcolony entries and stale planets sums; all six relevant seed results were reproduced with an independently built unmodified fd300f2. The baseline was not rewritten. Metal visuals were inspected; GL/Android/web were not exercised in this change.

A game defines its own player commands in rules; each becomes a button (with hotkey) on the command card of the client and of the editor play-test, can be sent from view scripts and through MCP (play_command with command: "script"), and arrives in the simulation as one generic command (kCmdScript) that the engine validates before the game's handler sees it. "commands": { "rally_cry": { "label": "Rally cry", "hotkey": "Y", "tip": "+25% damage for 10 s", "targets": ["footman", "archer", "tag:infantry"], "cost": { "gold": 25 }, "cooldown": 30 }, "muster": { "label": "Muster", "hotkey": "U", "targets": ["footman"], "cooldown": 5, "args": [{ "name": "where", "type": "point" }, { "name": "pace", "type": "enum", "values": ["walk", "run"], "default": "run" }, { "name": "count", "type": "int", "min": 1, "max": 20, "default": 5 }] } } function on_command(player, id, args) -- or per command: "fn": "global_function_name" if id == "muster" then game.order(args.units, "move", args.where.x, args.where.z) end -- return false: refused (cost and cooldown are not taken) end key label, icon, hotkey (one letter / digit), tip the button; script hotkeys win over the built-in ones (A, S, H, P) targets unit types / "tag:x" / "any": shown when the selection has such an own unit, and only those units reach the handler (args.units, sorted by handle); without targets the command needs no selection args array [{name, type, ...}] (or an object {name: {type, ...}}): int (min, max, default), enum (values, default), bool, point ({x, z} in the handler), unit (a living unit; own: true = of the sender), entity cost, cooldown resources taken and cooldown (seconds, per player) started when the handler accepts; while unaffordable / cooling down the command is dropped (the card shows the remaining seconds) fn handler function (default on_command) card false: no button and no hotkey on the command card; view scripts (view.send), HUD documents (send('id')) and MCP still send it (a tutorial's "Next", a game's own panels). Default true mapClick true: a plain left click / tap on the map (normal input mode, nothing armed) sends this command with the clicked ground point as its first point argument (on release; a press that moves more than 10 px pans the camera instead, a finger drag pans and two fingers zoom; a press on a script HUD element with the attribute map-drag released over the map also sends it there: drag-to-cast discs whose own data-event-mousedown arms the aim); for games whose input is tapping the map (OpenWar). Needs a point argument and no targets; the first such command (by id) wins. Client and editor Game view; test script_command_map_click The first point / unit / entity argument is what a click picks: the button enters a targeting mode and the next left click fills it in; the other arguments take their defaults (view scripts and MCP pass them by name). Wire format: param = the command's index in id order, args = one integer per value (points: x and z as raw fx), so replays and network play carry them. Invalid input (unknown index, wrong count, out of range, dead or foreign handles, a point off the map) is dropped silently. Each player's handlers have their own instruction budget per tick (rules "commandBudget", default 200000): a player who sends endless loops only burns their own commands. game.commands() lists the definitions, game.command_cooldown(p, id) gives the remaining seconds; view scripts send with view.send("muster", {where = {x = 10, z = 12}, pace = "walk", units = {h1, h2}}).

-- scripts/view/hud.lua (rules: "viewScripts": ["scripts/view/hud.lua"]) view.on("unit_died", function(e) if e.owner == view.player() then view.notice("We lost a " .. e.unit_type) end end) view.on_frame(function(dt) end) -- dt in seconds (float) View scripts are presentation: floats are fine, game.* queries work, actions don't exist. view.screen() tells what the host shows over the match: "playing", "paused" (the pause screen: the simulation does not tick, view scripts keep running, so a game can draw its own pause panel) or "over" (the match has ended). Their outputs are requests the host shows: view.notice(text), view.effect(name, x, z[, y]) (particle effect of fx/), view.sound(name, x, z), and script commands as the local player (view.send(id, args), above). They never change the simulation directly, so they don't need the determinism rules.

h: Sound: the sound table (view scripts and the UI Lua)
x: view.sound(name, x, z) plays a sound of audio.json fire-and-forget. A game that runs its own mixer (voice pools, per-play gain / pan / pitch, fades, ducking — e.g. a port of Unity's AudioSources) uses the sound table instead; the same table exists in view scripts and in the client's UI Lua (ui/*.lua), so one Lua module serves the menus and the battle. Presentation only, never part of the simulation. call meaning sound.play(name, {gain, pan, pitch, variant, at, loop}) → handle \ nil starts a sound of the bank: gain multiplies its volume; pan -1..1 stereo balance; pitch multiplies its random pitch; variant 1-based file of files (default random, never twice in a row); at seconds into the clip; loop true / false overrides the sound's. nil when nothing plays (no audio device, headless, unknown sound, the sound's own cooldown / maxInstances) sound.set(h, {gain, pan, pitch}) changes a playing voice (missing fields stay); pitch is the absolute rate. Call it every frame for fades / ducking: changes ramp over one mix block sound.stop(h [, fade]), sound.pause(h, on), sound.seek(h, seconds) stop (fade seconds, default 0.02); pause holds the voice silent at its place; seek jumps within the clip sound.state(h) → playing, time, paused what the mixer reported last (one audio period behind; a start still queued counts as playing at its start time) sound.variants(name), sound.length(name [, variant]) number of files; length of one in seconds (0 unknown) sound.music(name | nil [, fade]), sound.current_music() plays a playlist of "music" (crossfade fade seconds, default 1.5; a playlist that is still fading out comes back from where it is); nil stops sound.music_gain(g) script level of the music 0..4 (ducking), on top of the bus and the player's setting sound.settings() → {music, sfx, musicOn, sfxOn} the player's volumes 0..1 and on / off switches (client data model music, sfx, musicOn, sfxOn) sound.available(), sound.trace(text) a mixer runs; trace prints audio| text on stdout when AIVERSE_AUDIO_LOG=1 (tools compare a game's sound decisions) One mixer for menus and matches: view.ui_call(name, ...) → ok, results... calls the client UI Lua's global function name (dotted, e.g. "MyAudio.play") synchronously with the arguments copied (nil, booleans, numbers, strings, tables of those; functions / userdata become nil) and copies its results back; false, message without a UI Lua (headless) or when the function is missing or fails. A game keeps its mixer state (voice pools, cooldowns, ducking, the requested music) in the UI Lua, which lives across menu -> match -> menu, and its view scripts play through it (OpenWar: ui/audio/ui_audio.lua). Test: view_script_ui_call; engine side ui::luaCallAcross / ui::luaCopy (engine/ui/UiLua.h). With "scripted": true in audio.json the client never starts or stops music by itself (no menu / match / battle / victory playlists) and starting or leaving a match stops only the sfx bus, so a click on a result screen keeps ringing into the menu. OpenWar ports Unity's GameAudio this way (scripts/openwar/audio/). Tests: audio_voice_handles, audio_scripted_music_and_bus_switches, view_script_sound_table.

h: Script UI (view scripts drive in-match panels)
x:
View scripts own a data model script in the client's RmlUi: they set values, open the game's documents ui/hud/.rml and receive their button events. Simulation state stays read-only: buttons act through script commands (above), which go through the simulation like any input. -- scripts/view/hud.lua ui.open("war", {title = "War report"}) -- ui/hud/war.rml; params -> {{params.title}} ui.on("hide", function(args) ui.close("war") end) -- data-event-click="event('hide', 1)" -> args = {1} view.on_frame(function() local s = view.state() -- read-only copy of the simulation's `state` ui.set("trained", (s.trained or {})[view.player()] or 0) -- {{trained}} end)
{{params.title}}: {{trained}}
view Lua ui.set(key, value) a top-level value of model script (numbers, strings, booleans, fx, tables / arrays); unchanged values are not resent. A document binds its {{names}} when it loads: set every key it uses before (or in the same frame as) its first ui.open ui.open(name [, params]), ui.close(name) show / hide ui/hud/.rml (while the host screen is playing, or one of the screens its lists: a game's own pause / result panels, a HUD under them); params -> {{params.*}} ui.on(event, fn(args)) event('name', ...) in a document; args = the extra values as an array ui.on("back", fn(args)) Esc / Android Back (Back arrives as Escape) during a match (playing or paused). With such a handler the client skips its own pause / resume / tool cancel and leaves the key to the script: args = {screen = "playing" | "paused", platform = "android" | "ios" | "web" | "macos" | "windows" | "linux"}; return true to also cancel the pointer interaction in progress (a map-drag press, a skill drag, a tool mode). Pause / resume from the script with view.ui_call('game.pause') / view.ui_call('game.resume') (client, and the editor's Game window playing as in the client while it has focus) view.state() the simulation scripts' state as of this tick (a copy; writing to it changes nothing) send('id', {...}) in a document sends a script command as the local player (the current selection is added as units unless given). The engine part is engine/ui/lib/scriptui.lua (model, documents) and apps/client/ClientScriptUi.cpp (bridge); the UI documents' general rules (styles, @keys, sandbox) are in docs/ui-scripting.md. Sample: templates/scripted (ui/hud/war.rml). Effect coordinates are world coordinates; optional y is absolute height (default 0.5, preserving existing calls), not an offset from terrain. Coordinates must be finite. Both client and editor play these one-shot requests through the particle system and its quality budgets. View scripts must throttle repeated trail emissions and avoid replaying historical bursts on load; requests are drained once per presentation update.

h: Engine standard library (rule-level mechanics in Lua)
x: Part of the engine's own mechanics is written in Lua: engine/game/lua/*.lua, compiled into the engine (embed.cmake turns them into a header, so every platform loads them without file access) and run by every game, before the game's own scripts, in the same deterministic VM. The C++ core keeps everything hot (ECS, commands, movement, pathfinding, avoidance, targeting and weapons, projectiles, vision, hashing, data parsing) and offers aggregate queries and primitives in the low-level rts table (engine/game/ScriptStd.cpp); Lua decides the rules. module replaces (C++) called victory.lua (std.victory) GameCore::sysVictory "victory" system, every 10 ticks (std.period.victory) waves.lua (std.waves) GameCore::sysWaves (+ wave objective scan, kept as rts.wave_objective) "waves" system, only in games with waves triggers.lua (std.triggers) GameCore::sysTriggers, triggerConditions, runTriggerActions (parsing stays in Triggers.cpp) "triggers" system, only in games with triggers commands.lua (std.auto_build, std.sell) the kCmdAutoBuild and kCmdSell branches of GameCore::applyCommand from applyCommand Every module is bit-identical to the C++ it replaced: same iteration order (ECS order comes from the C++ helpers), the same Fixed operations (fx metamethods call the engine's Fixed), the same RNG calls. tests/checksums/check.sh compares the checksums of every sample game and of the fixtures in tests/checksums/games (seeds 1-3) with baseline.txt, recorded from the C++ implementation; tests/checksums/perf.py compares two builds (wall time, or exact instruction counts with --ir). Modules run without the instruction budget (engine code) and keep their state in the C++ GameState (hashed and rolled back as before), so a game with no scripts of its own has unchanged checksums. A module schedules itself: std.period.<name> = N (every N ticks; 0 = never in this game). Override: a game replaces a module with scripts/std/<name>.lua listed in its rules "scripts" (same contract: define std.<name>). Its changes are then the game's own rules. Kept in C++ after measuring: the per-player economy pass (upkeep, capacity, income) — it runs over all 256 player slots every tick, and the Lua version cost +50% instructions on ironfront.

Window Скрипты lists the files and the script log of the running play-test; script errors also appear in Console. When a .lua file under scripts/ changes on disk, its syntax is checked and a running play-test restarts with the new scripts (the VM is built from the sources when the match starts). MCP: script_api (this reference as JSON), script_list, script_read, script_write {path, text, register} (compiled first — a syntax error or a float literal is returned and nothing is saved; register: true adds it to rules "scripts"), script_check {seconds, seed} (compiles everything and runs a headless bot match, returns errors with file:line). game_file_write checks .lua files the same way. Headless: aiverse_headless --project templates/scripted --seed 3 prints the script log (errors also with --quiet).

engine/game/Script.h (design notes), Script.cpp (VM, sandbox, fx, serialization), ScriptEngine.cpp (handlers, dispatch, state), ScriptApi.cpp (game table and scriptApiReference()), modules/rts/view/RtsViewScript.* (view VM). Loaders call game::embedScripts(rules, map, reader) next to applyTilesToMap: script sources travel inside the rules JSON, so the simulation needs no file access. Lua 5.4.7 is vendored in third_party/lua (compiled as C, without the os / io / package / debug libraries; local changes in README.rts.md).

h: Render textures and paint layers (view scripts)
x: view.render_texture{width,height} creates a persistent mask canvas; view.paint_layer{bounds, texture?,color?,...} displays a canvas over terrain (or creates its own). :stroke(x0,z0,x1,z1, {radius,softness}), :clear() and :destroy() operate on manual canvases. An optional source="territory",owner=N derives the mask from visible ownership. These APIs are presentation-only; see render-texture.md for examples, limits, lifetime and backend conventions.

Optional game.json.scriptHud panels bind localized text, numeric counters and choice indices to game.set_var values. Buttons send ordinary player-ability commands; the simulation validates their effects. Shared client/editor evaluator and schema: Script HUD bindings. This API is presentation-only.

view.targeting() returns {ability, x, z, active, overWorld} for the local UI's current player-ability target. Coordinates are world X/Z floats. This is presentation state only: it is neither replicated nor written into the simulation. Use it for allowed-area masks and cursor previews; authoritative validation remains in the command's simulation handler. Client and editor clear it when targeting ends. In mapClick games a drag that started on a map-drag HUD element (drag-to-cast discs) reports ability = "map-drag" with the pointer's ground point while the drag lasts (overWorld: over the map, not over the UI, where a release taps the map); client and the editor's Game window when it plays as in the client (the same GameClient; its touch device profiles send the left button as a finger, so touch is true there as on a phone). A map-drag also reports touch (the drag is a touch, not the mouse) and sx, sy (the pointer in window points). view.set_map_drag_offset(dx, dy) (window points, reset when a map-drag starts) moves the point the drag aims at: the ground point (x, z) and the release tap are taken at the pointer + (dx, dy), while overWorld and the release over the UI stay the pointer's own — e.g. aim above a finger so the target is not under it. The client data-model callback skill_drag(actionId, progress) starts a point-target HUD drag on mousedown for an enabled action with nonnegative progress (the support button convention). Pair it with support_click(actionId, progress) on click for non-target actions such as rearm. Release over the world submits the command; release over UI, Escape, lost focus, and touch cancellation cancel the gesture. The editor's point-target script HUD buttons use the same press/drag/release flow. paintLayer:set_opacity(value) clamps finite values to 0..1 without clearing its canvas. Two pairs of layers can retain the previous geometry while animating a new network, avoiding destructive clear/repaint flicker. The existing 16-layer budget still applies.

view.camera() returns the host camera {x, z, zoom, pitch, yaw, width, height, ortho}: target on the ground, zoom in the units of game.json "camera" (orthographic: visible view-plane height in world units; perspective: distance), angles in degrees, viewport in framebuffer pixels. view.set_camera{x =, z =, zoom =, pitch =, yaw =} changes any subset after the frame's view scripts (pitch 5..90, zoom > 0, finite values). A game ports its own framing with it (OpenWar: scripts/view/openwar/camera.lua, Unity's ArmyMapView). Presentation only; the client applies it, the editor Game view does not yet. Test: openwar_player_colors_flat_lighting_view_camera.

view.to_screen(x, z [, y]) returns sx, sy, onScreen: the window point (logical points, top-left origin) of a world point (y = height, default 0) through the host camera; onScreen is false behind the camera or outside the window. A view.set_camera earlier in the same frame is already applied, so a script listed after the camera script projects with the frame's final camera. view.draw(verts [, {image = "ui/x.png", layer = 0}]) adds a triangle list in those window points for this frame only: without image each vertex is x, y, rgba, with image it is x, y, u, v, rgba (uv 0..1 over the image, 0, 0 = its top left; atlases work). rgba is an integer 0xRRGGBBAA. Consecutive calls with the same image and layer share one batch; batches are drawn in ascending layer (call order within a layer) after the world, the particles and the overlays, under the UI documents. A call with a partial triangle, a non-finite number or more than 1048576 vertices a frame raises an error and adds nothing. This is how a game ports a 2D vector board drawn over the 3D map (OpenWar: Unity's ArmyBoard VertexHelper meshes, scripts/view/openwar/board.lua). Client only (the editor Game view does not draw it yet); presentation only. Test: view_to_screen_and_draw_canvas. transform = {xx, xy, yx, yy, ox, oy} maps the batch's points on the host side (x' = ox + x*xx + y*yx, y' = oy + x*xy + y*yy, binary64 in that order, then float like any vertex): a script keeps a batch in its own coordinates (e.g. ground coordinates under an orthographic camera, whose ground-to-screen map is affine: three view.to_screen calls give it) and redraws the same table every frame without rebuilding it when only the camera moves — the result equals the same sum written in Lua. OpenWar's nuclear scorch uses it. Test: view_draw_transform. view.draw_ground(verts [, {image = "ui/x.png", layer = 0}]) is the world-space counterpart for marks lying on the map: each vertex is x, y, z, rgba (with image: x, y, z, u, v, rgba) in world units (y up, absolute height — put it a few hundredths above the ground). The triangles are drawn inside the 3D scene after the opaque and translucent meshes, depth tested without depth writes and with a small bias towards the camera, so units and buildings standing on a mark hide it (the screen canvas above draws over them). Batches are sorted by layer, then call order; same image and layer merge; one frame only; the texture alpha below .02 is cut (vertex alpha is free). Same limits and errors as view.draw (1048576 vertices a frame). Client only; presentation only (modules/rts/view/GameGroundCanvas.*). OpenWar draws its ground ability areas, railways and nuclear target rings with it, as Unity's ground canvases under the units. Test: view_draw_ground_world_triangles. A unit type's view can carry a flat ground shadow image drawn through the same ground canvas (layer -1, before the view scripts' draw_ground batches of layer >= 0): "groundShadow": {"image": "ui/shadows/Tank.png", "size": [w, d], "offset": [x, z], "color": [r, g, b, a], "lift": .05, "flip": [u, v]} — size and offset in world units in the model's frame (the drawn model's rotation, without its scale), color multiplies the image (default black at alpha .55), the image's u runs along the model's +x and its top lies towards the model's -z unless flipped. It follows the interpolated position and facing and replaces the default blob of air units. OpenWar ports Unity's footprint sprites (ArmyUnitModelLayer.AttachShadow) with it. Client only (drawn by GameView::drawGround). Test: view_ground_shadow_option.

view.entity_parent(child, parent, {x=0,y=0,z=0,yaw=0}) attaches an entity's presentation to another entity's final rendered frame. Offsets are in cells: +X forward, +Y up, +Z right; yaw is in degrees. Nested attachments inherit translation, rotation, tilt and scale. Cycles and non-finite offsets are rejected. view.entity_parent(child, nil) detaches. Native hosts may provide GameScene::entityFrames for physics-driven chassis after their visual update. Children use that same frame rather than independently interpolated simulation positions. This is a presentation-only hierarchy: collision, ownership and simulation positions do not change. Links are cleared with the view and when either entity dies; rebuild them from saved simulation state in view.on_frame after loading a game. Tests: view_entity_parent_frames and view_entity_parent_api. view.entity_fx(h, fields) overrides how one entity (unit, structure, prop: any handle of game.units) is drawn, on the local machine only: field meaning (default) scale number or {x, y, z}: multiplies the model in its own axes about its ground point (1) lift world units the model is raised along its up (negative: lowered); the ground shadow stays (0) pitch, roll degrees the model tilts on top of its facing, about its origin (lift included): pitch > 0 lowers the nose, roll > 0 raises the right side; applied roll first, then pitch, then the facing (Unity's Euler(pitch, yaw, roll)), so a flyer can dive and bank while game.set_facing / its movement turn it; the sun shadow follows, the groundShadow image does not; 3D models only (0, 0) corpse_age seconds since the death on the script's own clock: the corpse (death clip, fall, sink, corpseFade) shows that moment and stays while it is below the type's corpse (a paused match holds a dying model like Unity's frozen Elapsed); an entity removed without a death event (game.kill(h, true), or a death in a frame that ran several ticks) becomes a corpse when its values carry corpse_age; false: the view's frame clock again (unset) opacity 0..1: below .99 the model is drawn in the blended pass (sorted back to front, no shadow-map casting) and still writes depth, so the ground layers drawn after that pass (paint layers, draw_ground, sprites) stay behind it; 0 draws nothing (1) tint {r, g, b} multiplies the surface colour (1, 1, 1) team_mix {r, g, b, amount}: the team colour moves towards rgb by amount, in display space, before it is applied to the team-coloured surfaces (Unity's Color.Lerp of a _BaseColor) (amount 0) team_glow emission of the team colour on team-coloured surfaces: team * team_glow in display space (0) shadow 0..1: the type's groundShadow image (and the air blob) fades by opacity * shadow (1) shadow_scale number or {x, y, z}: size of the groundShadow image; by default it follows scale; false makes it follow again time, ease seconds to ease from the values drawn now to the new ones (frame time, also while paused; default 0 = at once) and "linear" / "smooth" (smoothstep) Fields left out keep their current target. view.entity_fx(h) returns the values drawn now (scale, tint, team_mix, shadow_scale as arrays) or nil, view.entity_fx(h, nil) removes them (drawn unchanged at once). A call with a bad field raises an error and changes nothing. The values follow the entity's interpolated position and facing, its attachments, effect anchors, selection outline (faded with it) and, when it dies, its corpse (death clip / fall / fade) for up to 10 s after it left the simulation; then they are dropped. They apply on every backend (GL / GLSL and Metal share the model shaders: ModelDraw::tint.w, teamGlow = instance draw.w), on planets, and to 2D sprites (scale x = width, y = height, opacity). Scripts that run per frame can also set values every frame from their own clock (OpenWar computes Unity's per-tick curves from the match time it publishes in state). Presentation only: the simulation and its checksum never see them; the headless server has no view scripts. Store:

view.paint_layer{bounds = {x, z, w, h}, cells = {width = W, height = H}, density = 1..4, smooth = .75..2, borderWidth = 0..2, borderColor = {r, g, b [, a]}, outside = id, opacity, lift, landOnly} creates a raster of one id byte per cell (row-major, z rows) drawn as smooth categorical regions: every pixel takes the id with the largest smoothstep-weighted coverage of its 5x5 texel neighbourhood (smooth = falloff in texels), and a border of borderWidth texels is drawn where the coverage of an id crosses one half (2x2 bilinear coverage on low material quality). layer:set_cells(bytes) takes a Lua string of W * H bytes, layer:set_palette{[id] = {r, g, b [, a]}} sets colours (0..1); outside is the id used beyond the raster edge. transparent = id draws that id fully transparent (an overlay raster over another layer, e.g. OpenWar's capture flashes: id 0 empty, the flashed cells white, layer:set_opacity(v) animated per frame); palette alpha is not used (the texel alpha holds the id). density repeats each cell as density x density texels (smoothing and border widths are in texels). One quad per layer, texelFetch on an RGBA8 texture (rgb colour, a id); presentation only. OpenWar draws its ownership raster with it (ArmyMapWorld look). ground = {scale, strength, flipHeight, team = {min, max}, context = {min, max}, linear, coast = {sea, drop, beach, shallow, earthNear, earthFar, foam}} adds a ground surface (a port of ArmyMapWorld's meadow and coast): land ids in team keep their colour under a world-anchored meadow relief (patches, blots, pale spots; scale = patch size in world units, strength = fine variation), other land ids get the neutral meadow (green / olive / pale), ids in context a faint noise; flipHeight > 0 anchors the noise at y = flipHeight - z (north-up source maps); relief = 1 / 2 replaces the meadow of non-context land with the biome surface (the id colour under broad relief and snow / dune ripples of frequency 8 / 12: ArmyMapWorld ApplyMeadow for ice / desert campaigns), 0 (default) keeps the meadow. With coast, the id sea is water: a static signed shoreline distance (texels, chamfer + 3x3 smoothing, rebuilt only when the sea mask changes) gives a beach rim on land and shallows, a shore shadow, a cliff on the shore facing drop (texture-row direction, -1 = towards -z) and an animated foam line on water (colours 0..1). linear = true runs the surface maths on linear colour (sRGB in and out), as a linear-space Unity project. The value noise uses the desktop sine hash, the mobile hash on low material quality (as the source's ARMY_MOBILE variant). Test: view_paint_layer_ground_options.

game.set_position(unit, x, z) keeps its flat-map, living mobile-unit and in-bounds validation. Air-layer units can be placed over water; other units still require a ground cell. Previous render position is preserved for interpolation, native movement/orders are cleared, and presentation applies the configured flight height. The API does not paint territory or find routes. Covered by script_air_position_over_water, including snapshot replay.

game.seed() returns the configured match seed as a Lua integer (the signed two's-complement representation of the full 64-bit seed). It is available in simulation and view scripts, consumes no RNG values, and is unchanged by rollback. Games can use it for deterministic keyed decisions whose result must not depend on unrelated RNG calls. Store accepted decisions and command identities in state as usual.

game.grid_path(width, height, cells, start, goal [, label]) performs a deterministic native A* query over a custom four-neighbour grid in both sim and view scripts. It does not move units or inspect/change the engine map. Cell IDs are zero-based (z*width+x); cells is a sparse Lua table. Without label, only boolean true is passable. With an integer label, only cells containing exactly that Lua integer are passable (including label 0); missing values are blocked. Metatables are not consulted. The returned one-based array excludes start and includes goal; unreachable or out-of-range endpoints return nil. An in-range start equal to goal returns an empty array. A blocked start is allowed so a unit can escape newly blocked ground; all subsequent cells, including goal, must be passable. Width/height must be integers in 1..4096 and their product at most 262144; malformed dimensions/tables/labels raise a script error. Costs are integer, ties use remaining Manhattan distance then cell ID. No persistent query cache or state is created: changed masks take effect immediately, and scripts store accepted paths in hashed state as usual. Unit radius, diagonals, height and dynamic avoidance remain the caller's responsibility. game.grid_sample_segment(width,height,cells,x,z,tx,tz[,label[,margin[,density]]]) checks a fixed-point segment against the same masks/labels. It returns false for out-of-grid endpoints or any blocked sample. The start is excluded, the destination included, and a zero-length segment samples its single point. There are floor(length*density)+1 evenly spaced samples; density defaults to 8 and must be an integer in 1..16, with a 65536-sample cap. Coordinates/margin are integer or fx; margin defaults to zero (allowed 0..4096). A nonzero margin adds four probes at ±margin on each axis per sample. This is a sampled cross footprint, not continuous collision detection or a swept circle/rectangle: narrow diagonal obstacles can be missed. Use it for steering shortcuts only where that sampling model is appropriate. Out-of-grid margin probes block; malformed arguments raise a script error. The query reads raw table entries, has no cache/mutation, and uses the same integer/fx arithmetic in sim/view; native query work is outside Lua instruction counting, so callers must bound query frequency too.

aiverse_headless --project <dir> --max-seconds 35 --verify-restore-at 15 --verify-restore-ticks 200 captures both SimSnapshot and Simulation::serialize() at 15 seconds, advances 200 ticks, then repeats the same interval after snapshot and serialized restoration in the same live VM, and after serialized restoration into a newly initialized simulation/VM. Every tick's simulation checksum must match, and script errors fail the verification. External C++ bot objects are copied along with the verification baseline so their input decisions repeat; ordinary save-state files do not serialize those external controllers. A plain --load bot match can therefore receive different commands and is not by itself a deterministic save/load comparison. The checker retains normal final state and recording behavior. --record can be replayed normally; verification wall time includes the repeated intervals and is not a normal performance benchmark. Restore ticks must be 1..100000 and fit before the requested match limit. A natural match end shortens the checked interval and the actual count is printed. A match ending before the restore point fails rather than reporting success. Verification cannot be combined with replay/setup-only/path/group benchmark modes. Exit 1 reports failed verification; exit 2 reports invalid configuration or failed setup. tests/check_headless_restore.py <binary> exercises all three restoration paths, tick-zero startup, replay consistency, invalid intervals and a deliberately untracked Lua local that must desynchronize. This checks identical-input continuation, not arbitrary alternate command histories, cross-platform equivalence, UI/visual state, or migration between game versions. Use targeted game tests for those additional requirements.

view.targeting() now also exposes caster, the packed source entity ID (0 for player abilities). The manifest may opt into generic world-anchored entity controls; see Entity action controls. Presentation captures an explicit source, while normal entity commands and game handlers remain authoritative. Source on GitHub: docs/scripting.md

h: Cross-genre C++ gameplay packages: first batch
x: These are reusable deterministic policies for project-native/host code. They compose with engine mechanics; they do not silently replace existing FPS movement, RTS abilities/damage or match rules. Package Implemented API Boundaries character-locomotion MotionConfig/State/Input, stepMotion: ground/air speed, acceleration/braking, gravity, jump buffer, coyote time, bounded extra jumps, ceiling response. LocomotionModes.h (0.2.0): stepLocomotion mode machine Ground/Air/Ledge/Ladder/Swim/Climb/Mantle with slopes, ledge grab/shimmy/climb-up, ladders, buoyant swimming, stamina-limited wall climbing and timed mantle/vault; 0.3.0 adds Dash (air dash count, cooldown), WallSlide, WallRun, Grapple (pull or swing with reel) and one-way platform drop-through Returns velocity, mode and events; collision owner reports grounded/ceiling, ground normal, ledges, ladders, water depth, climbable walls and obstacles, and applies movement. No physics queries, root motion or animation controller. melee-combat AttackSet/State, phase evaluation, input buffering, allowed combo cancels, authorization callback, once-per-swing hit bookkeeping, evade/parry/block outcome Geometry/target validation and actual damage/stamina belong to the existing combat owner. No parallel health/status system. combat-actions Frame-keyed hitboxes + hurtboxes (sphere/capsule/yaw box) with overlap tests, self/team filtering and once-per-swing hits; dodge i-frames + cooldown; directional guard arc + perfect-parry window with re-arm; poise damage/break/recovery and hit/block/parry stun; deterministic lock-on acquire/switch/break Composes melee-combat. Returns contacts/outcomes; damage, stamina, health and statuses stay with the existing combat owner. No per-tick sweep, animation-driven boxes, ragdoll or camera presentation. weapon-policies Deterministic recoil recovery, seeded spread, swept projectiles with gravity, lifetime and bounded ricochets; 0.2.0: material-layer penetration, radial explosions with owner LOS, ammo feeds (magazine/belt/per-shell/energy + overheat), charge tiers, attachment stat stacking, ballistic launch and lead solving (see Weapons and ballistics) Existing FPS ammo/reload/fire cadence remain authoritative for built-in FPS weapons. No automatic replacement of hitscan, no damage/health owner, no presentation. action-bots Melee bot (spacing band, phase-aware openings, hit-confirmed combos, telegraph dodge/parry timing, lock-on), shooter bot (turn-limited aim, seeded aim error, solveIntercept lead, recoil bursts, reload/overheat, cover choice), squad roles + formations, objective choice hook (see Genre bots) Returns player-equivalent inputs only; perception, cover, objectives and navigation come from owners. No pathfinding, match rules, senses or sports/racing/card bots. stealth-senses Sight cones (near/focus/peripheral) with owner light/cover/stance/visibility multipliers and LOS callback, hearing with occlusion callback and noise/query budgets, decaying footprint/scent markers, per observer-target suspicion meters (Unaware/Suspicious/Searching/Alert), delayed ally alerts sharing last known positions, deterministic search points with give-up, disguises, hiding spots (see Stealth and senses) Perception records and events only. Owner supplies poses, multipliers, raycasts/occlusion and search candidates and moves agents. Not RTS fog of war. No sound propagation, navmesh routes or presentation. physical-interactions Pick up/carry (hold point, mass limit, carry speed penalty, drop when blocked), charged throws with an arc preview from the same integrator and swept landing, push/pull (free or grid, friction/mass resistance, cooperative pushing, blocking), XPBD ropes with a fixed iteration count, attach/detach and breaking force, hinged/sliding doors (locks/keys, one-way, timing, auto-reverse), waypoint moving platforms with per-rider carry deltas, breakables (damage types, thresholds, stages, debris requests) (see Physical interactions) Authoritative kinematic polic

One registry for every package that stores state through genre/Persistence.h; a new package reserves the next free block of eight here before using it. Kinds Owner 1..7 genre core (motion, melee, recoil, projectile, match, capture, story) 16..18 weapon-policies (feed, charge, loadout) 20..23 character-locomotion (20 = 0.2.0 locomotion modes, still loads; 21 = 0.3.0 with moves) 32..36 combat-actions 40..47 match-rules objectives 48..55 stealth-senses 56..63 action-bots 64..71 narrative-graphs scenes 72..79 cinematic-gameplay (76 = NarrativeCueQueue bridge) 80..87 physical-interactions 88..95 vehicle-controllers, sports-rules and their bots 96..103 card-games, tactics-grid, cards-turns-bots 104..111 settlement-production, survival-ecology 112..119 puzzle-solvers 120..127 battle-royale (own royaleSave / royaleLoad, genre/royale/Persistence.h) 128..135 vehicle-controllers race sessions (128 RaceSessionState) 136+ free

Include <aiverselib/mechanics/Configured.h>, the needed policy header and genre/Persistence.h. Executable hosts link AIVERSE::mechanics; registered OBJECT modules call aiverse_native_use_mechanics(aiverse_native_<id>) after aiverse_native_module(...). The helper puts collision backend dependencies on the owning aiverse_game target, avoiding object-library linkage cycles. For header-only policies without projectile collision, AIVERSE::gameplay_native is sufficient. See examples/native/libraries/GenreConsumer.cpp for validated settings and NativeState storage. The library_demo native module now initializes these records in setup (module VERSION 7: adds the stage 1-4 genre records, including puzzles, cards/tactics, vehicles/sports and settlement/survival). tests/libraries/genre_tests.cpp runs trajectories, combos, world collision, round transitions, choice transactions and restoration checks. No engine source edit is required in a consuming project. External input must arrive as validated Commands. Use these helpers inside the owning authoritative system/handler, not from presentation. Keep immutable definitions separately from dynamic state. Use integer ticks and Fixed dt. Save every outcome-affecting state and do not update the same controller twice per tick. Motion, melee and match policies reject repeated/backwards ticks. Recoil/projectile steppers are per-step primitives; their owner is responsible for exactly one update per simulation tick.

Scalar defaults are in libraries/spec/gameplay.json (configuration package 0.3.3): sections locomotion, melee, projectile, matchRules. Run generate_gameplay.py after spec changes. Load through readGameplaySettings, then motionConfig, locomotionModeConfig, attackConfig, projectileConfig, matchConfig. The locomotion mode keys are optional (maxSlopeMilliDegrees, ledge*, ladder*, swim*, buoyancyMilli, climb*, mantle*, vault*); relations such as swimExit <= swimEnter <= swimFloat <= swimDive and mantleMin <= vaultMax <= mantleMax are rejected with readable errors. Metres/seconds use integer milli-units in JSON; C++ converts directly to Fixed. Tick durations are literal ticks at the project's tick rate. Existing settings remain optional. examples/libraries/mechanics/settings.json configures a double-jump controller, attack timing, a ricocheting projectile and best-of rounds. Attack definitions are typed AttackSet entries: set stable positive IDs, allowed combo IDs and cancelFrom explicitly. Graph validation rejects unknown combo edges. attackConfig(settings,id) cancels into combos from recovery start by default. RecoilConfig is a typed public settings struct; angles use turns and recovery is per simulation step. Narrative JSON uses readStory and the example examples/libraries/mechanics/story.json. Every node and choice has a localization key. Choice next:0 ends the graph; conditions reference integer fact IDs. Missing facts fail their conditions. Define an explicit ending choice even for a final dialogue node. Unknown fields, duplicate IDs, broken edges and invalid integer values are rejected during loading.

genre/LocomotionModes.h adds LocomotionModeConfig/State/Input/Result and stepLocomotion. It wraps stepMotion for Ground/Air (behaviour is bit-identical on flat ground) and adds modes driven only by LocomotionEnvironment, the per-tick report of the collision owner: Slopes: ground normal with normal.y >= cos(maxSlope) is walkable and the velocity follows the plane; steeper ground slides along the downhill tangent (slideAcceleration, capped at slideSpeed), with no jump. Events SlideStart/SlideEnd. Ledge: while falling (or on grab) next to a reported ledge whose top is ledgeMin..ledgeMax above the feet: hang, shimmy with wish.x along cross(up, normal), jump/up climbs (timed LedgeClimb phase), drop/down releases. A released ledge is ignored for ledgeRegrabTicks. Ladder: grab attaches, vertical*ladderSpeed; ladderTop + up runs a timed exit phase onto the top, ladderBottom/grounded + down exits to Ground; jump pushes off along the ladder normal. Swim: immersion >= swimEnterDepth enters (not while rising), < swimExitDepth leaves. Buoyancy drives the body to floatDepth; vertical input dives/surfaces (Dived/Surfaced at diveDepth); a jump with the head above water leaves the water at waterJumpSpeed. Climb: grab on a climbable wall (climbEnabled); moves along the wall, consumes stamina per tick (built-in counter or the owner's pool through stepLocomotionWithStamina), wall-jumps, reaches a reported ledge at the top or falls with StaminaDepleted. Mantle/vault: jump next to an obstacle mantleMin..mantleMax high starts a timed phase: rise for the first half, move over obstacleDepth for the rest. On the ground, obstacles up to vaultMaxHeight taken at >= vaultMinSpeed vault in vaultTicks and keep momentum. A ceiling during the rise aborts. Dash (0.3.0): dashPressed dashes along wish (or facing when there is no wish) at dashSpeed for dashTicks with no gravity, then leaves at dashEndSpeed. Ground dashes are free; airborne ones use one of airDashes, refilled on landing or touching a wall move. dashCooldownTicks after the dash ends; a wall ahead (wallContact, normal against the dash) stops it with no momentum. Events DashStart/DashEnd. Wall slide (0.3.0): airborne, falling, wallContact reported and wish pushing into the wall: fall speed is capped at wallSlideSpeed; jump wall-jumps (contactNormal*wallJumpPush + jumpSpeed). Stops when grounded, the contact ends or the push stops. Wall run (0.3.0): airborne with wallContact and speed along the wall >= wallRunMinSpeed: runs along the wall tangent at wallRunSpeed (same direction as before), vertical speed starts at max(vy,0) and falls with gravity*wallRunGravityScale, up to wallRunTicks. Ends on ground, lost contact, drop or timeout (then wallRunCooldownTicks before the next run); jump leaves with push + run speed + jumpSpeed. Grapple (0.3.0): the owner aims (raycast) and reports grappleAnchor + grappleOffset (anchor minus body) every tick; grapplePressed attaches when the offset is grappleArrive..grappleMaxLength. Pull (default) flies to the anchor at grappleSpeed and lets go within grappleArrive. Swing (grappleSwing) keeps gravity and light air control, the rope only pulls (outward radial velocity is removed when taut, stretch is corrected at up to grappleSpeed) and vertical reels at grappleReelSpeed. Jump, grappleReleased, a lost anchor or grappleTicks let go. Events GrappleAttach/GrappleRelease. One-way platforms (0.3.0): the owner sets groundOneWay when standing on one; drop on it leaves the ground (DropThrough) and LocomotionResult::ignoreOneWay stays true for oneWayDropTicks so the collision sweep lets the body fall through. oneWaySupports(top, previousFeet, feet, vy, ignoreOneWay) is the owner's landing test: only from above, not while rising, not during drop-through. Glide (0.3.0): airborne, falling, no wall, jumpHeld (a level, not the jump press): fall speed is capped at glideFallSpeed and the body moves at glideForwardSpeed along wish (or facing). Ends on release, ground or a wall. Same wall

Motion: jumpPressed is an input edge, not a held button. The physics owner must provide the actual collision result on the next tick. Walking off a ledge consumes the ground jump once the coyote window expires. A buffered press may fire on landing before expiry. The policy clamps terminal falling speed at 1000 units/second and accepts dt in (0,1]. It does not add extra jumps to the FPS motor automatically. Melee: one active attack owns a sorted list of already-hit target IDs. Use stable packed entity IDs that fit positive int64 (or project-owned IDs). recordMeleeHit records only active-window contacts; call it after the authoritative spatial/team check. stepMelee calls authorization only when an attack can start; make spending atomic in that callback and issue resulting effects through the existing owner. resolveMeleeContact prioritizes invulnerability, then parry, then block, then normal hit. It does not compute another damage formula. Input buffering expires; no hit may be emitted twice for one swing. Weapons: use sim.rng() with sampleSpread; invalid spread consumes no RNG. Sampling uses uniform integer yaw/pitch offsets, not a uniform solid-angle cone. Persist recoil if it changes authoritative aim. Projectile movement uses the world's real swept AABB collision (radius as equal half-extents), avoiding fast-projectile tunneling through boxes. One impact is handled per tick; leftover travel after bounce is discarded. Every impact is returned for the damage/effects owner to process. Lifetime counts completed steps, so lifetime=1 moves once. Projectiles leaving +/-100000 world bounds are clamped and terminated. No physics position, velocity, ammunition or damage is silently copied into the existing FPS actor state. Matches: initialize unique positive team IDs with makeMatch. awardScore accepts nonnegative points only during live/overtime, with strictly increasing event IDs per team. Persist those IDs across rounds; never reuse them while delayed commands can arrive. Step evaluates score/clock transitions. Overtime ends on a sole leader or its limit; tied rounds may draw. Match win uses round wins. Capture points freeze while contested, decay progress by one per empty tick, and commit ownership at the threshold. The caller validates presence and awards associated score/rewards. Presence counts are not trusted input. Narrative: available choices are stable by ID. chooseStory rechecks conditions, applies all fact changes to a copy, rejects integer overflow, commits the next node and records the command ID atomically. One explicit choice produces one transition; loops are allowed without recursive auto-execution. Only project-owned story facts are mutated. For rewards/inventory, use an existing transactional owner and an idempotent event from the committed story transition; do not treat a fact increment as a wallet.

genre::save/load provides version-1 Archive records for MotionState, MeleeState, RecoilState, ProjectileState, MatchState, CaptureState and StoryState. Each subsystem needs its own key; records include a state-type discriminator. Load validates limits and canonical encoding, rejects truncation/trailing data without replacing destination. Bind the exact immutable configuration and definition versions in the project save envelope. storeBytes/loadBytes reuse runtime/NativeBytes.h to bridge records to NativeState arrays. Bot persistence uses the same byte bridge. Run catalog.py check, generate_gameplay.py --check, tests/libraries/run.py and native_consumer.py. Run root aiverse_library_genre_tests and the standalone test under ASan/UBSan. For engine wiring, add real gameplay acceptance and replay/save checks. Current tests exercise the C++ policies and real collision; they are not a claim that a complete platformer/fighting/story UI is shipped. No rendering changes in this batch. Windows, Metal presentation, mobile and web runtime paths remain unverified. The broader proposed scope is in genre-mechanics-roadmap.md.

Header genre/CombatActions.h (+ CombatConfigured.h settings adapters, CombatData.h hitbox JSON). Target AIVERSE::lib_combat_actions (depends on lib_melee_combat, aiverse_engine); native OBJECT modules call aiverse_native_use_libraries(target combat-actions). Skill: skills/gameplay/aiverse-combat-actions. Shapes and hits: Fixed metres; yaw in turns around +Y (yaw 0 faces +Z, +X is right). CombatShape is a sphere (centre a), capsule (segment a..b) or box (centre a, half extents, yaw-only rotation, radius 0). overlaps is exact for sphere/box/box-box (SAT) and uses a deterministic integer ternary search over the segment parameter for capsules; touching counts. HitboxDef{id,from,to,shape} is live for attack ages [from,to) which must lie inside the attack's active window. collectMeleeHits transforms hitboxes by the attacker pose and hurtboxes by each target pose, skips self, same nonzero team (unless friendlyFire) and targets already hit this swing, and records hits through recordMeleeHit. Contacts are sorted by target ID and name the first overlapping hitbox/hurtbox by ascending IDs. Invalid data or duplicate target IDs return nullopt without touching state. Overlaps are sampled per tick (no sweep between ticks). Defense: stepDodge (authorize callback, cooldown counted from the dodge end) and dodgeInvulnerable ([invulnFrom,invulnTo) from the start). stepGuard raises/lowers; raising opens a parryTicks window unless the previous raise was less than rearmTicks ago. insideGuardArc compares the attacker bearing with the defender yaw (halfArc turns each side). resolveCombatContact feeds Melee.h resolveMeleeContact (invulnerable > parry > block > hit); unblockable skips the guard. Poise: integer milli-units. stepPoise once per tick (initializes to maximum, refills recoveryPerTick after recoveryDelay since the last poise damage, resets to full after a break stun). applyPoiseHit on the same tick: Hit drains full damage + hit-stun, Blocked drains blockScaleMilli/1000 block-stun, Parried/Evaded drain nothing. Reaching 0 breaks poise (breakStunTicks); while broken further hits add nothing. applyParryStagger stuns the parried attacker; interruptMelee cancels the swing. Lock-on: lockScore = distance/range*distanceWeight + |angle|/halfAngle*angleWeight; lower wins, ties by smaller ID. stepLockOn: break on missing/untargetable/beyond breakRange; toggle releases or acquires; switch picks the nearest angular neighbour on that side among scorable candidates (no wrap), then distance, then ID. Candidate visibility (targetable) comes from the owner's authorized senses. Settings: optional combat section in libraries/spec/gameplay.json (configuration 0.3.2): dodgeTicks/dodgeInvulnFrom/dodgeInvulnTo/dodgeCooldown, blockHalfArcMilli (milli-turns), parryTicks, parryRearmTicks, poiseMilli, poiseRecoveryMilli, poiseDelayTicks, blockPoiseMilli, hit/block/break/parry stun ticks, lockRangeMilli/lockBreakMilli (milli-metres), lockHalfAngleMilli (milli-turns), lock weights. The loader rejects dodgeInvulnFrom > dodgeInvulnTo, dodgeInvulnTo > dodgeTicks and lockRangeMilli > lockBreakMilli. Hitboxes: readHitboxes(json, attacks), see examples/libraries/mechanics/hitboxes.json; unknown keys/attacks, frames outside the active window, bad shapes and non-ascending IDs fail with path-qualified messages. State: CombatActorState{dodge,guard,poise,lock} and each member are genre::save/load records (kinds 32..36 reserved for this package), canonical and validated on load. combatHash / hashCombatState hash the canonical bytes for the simulation checksum. All steppers reject repeated/backwards ticks. GenreConsumer.cpp runs one swing into a defender, resolves the contact, applies poise and stores genre.combat, genre.combat_swing and genre.combat_hash in NativeState. Verified only with g++ 11 (Linux VM): header syntax checks, aiverse_library_genre_tests sources built by hand (also ASan/UBSan) and the consumer function in a standalone driver. New headers compose Weapons.h without changing it: genre/Ballistics.h (penetration, explosions, aiming), genre/WeaponMods.h (ammo feeds, charge, attachments), genre/WeaponData.h (settings adapters, weapons JSON) and genre/WeaponPersistence.h (save/load, hashing). All math is Fixed/integer; invalid input returns std::nullopt (or false) without calling owner callbacks or mutating state. Penetration. traceLayers(world, start, delta, materialOf) returns every collider crossed by the segment in (entry, collider id) order with geometric thickness (box entry/exit from two swept casts; triangles are zero-thickness sheets). Overlapping colliders are separate layers. resolvePenetration walks the layers with a MaterialTable: each layer costs resistance * thickness power (thickness at least minThickness), damage and speed are multiplied by 1 - falloff * thickness (floored at 0). It stops on unknown/impenetrable material, exhausted power, minDamage, minSpeed or maxLayers, reporting PenetrationStop and per-layer damageIn (damage for that layer's occupant) and exit values. Applying damage to occupants remains the combat owner's job. Explosions. resolveExplosion(config, center, targets, exposure): full effect inside innerRadius, linear falloff to edgeScale at outerRadius, nothing beyond. Distance is to the target's bounding sphere (radius). Targets need unique positive IDs. The owner-supplied exposure(target) (LOS/cover, 1 visible, 0 occluded, clamped) is called once per in-range target in (distance, id) order, never for out-of-range ones, and stops at maxTargets exposed hits. Occluded targets are omitted. Results carry damage, impulse magnitude and direction (up for a coincident target), in the same order regardless of input order. Ammo feeds. stepFeed(config, state, tick, {fire, reload, cancel}, draw) is a per-tick state machine (one call per weapon per tick, strictly increasing ticks). Kinds: Magazine (whole reload, optional longer empty reload), Belt (each shot draws from the owner's reserve), PerShell (one round per shellTicks after reloadStartTicks), Energy (no ammunition). Optional heat on every kind: overheat at heatCapacity, locked at least overheatTicks and until heat <= recoverHeat; cooling coolPerTick per elapsed tick. intervalTicks and spinupTicks (held-trigger ticks before the first shot) are optional cadence rules. draw(n) must atomically remove up to n rounds from the owner's reserve (inventory, meta wallet, ...) and return the granted count; it is only called after validation, so the step always commits. Order per tick: cooling/recovery, reload cancel/interrupt, reload start (explicit or auto on dry fire), reload progress, fire. Firing with rounds left interrupts an interruptible reload: magazine progress is lost, inserted shells stay. These records are separate from modules/fps actor ammo: never mirror one magazine in both owners. Charge modes. stepCharge(config, state, tick, {held, cancel}) (level input, one call per tick). Release before minTicks cancels (or fires tier 0 with fireBelowMin); held ticks are capped at maxTicks; tier counts reached thresholds, fraction is min-to-max progress, scale is the tier's scale (or baseScale). autoReleaseTicks fires automatically and latches until the trigger is released. Attachments. WeaponFrame (stats with base/min/max, allowed slots) + AttachmentSet (one slot each, add/mul modifiers). equipAttachment validates slot/ID and returns the replaced attachment; resolveStats applies base, then every Add, then every Mul (slot id ascending, authored order, sequential Fixed rounding), then clamps. Equip order never changes the result. Intermediates are clamped to +/-1e10 so no data overflows. Aiming. solveLaunch(delta, speed, gravity) returns 0, 1 or 2 launch solutions (low/high arc, gravity along -Y as in ProjectileConfig). It solves for flight time, so the analytic trajectory passes through the target up to Fixed rounding and |velocity| approximates speed; a power-of-two scaled discriminant k

Target AIVERSE::lib_stealth_senses (depends on aiverse_engine); native OBJECT modules call aiverse_native_use_libraries(target stealth-senses). Skill: skills/gameplay/aiverse-stealth-senses. This is a generic per-agent perception policy for guards, monsters and bots; RTS fog of war stays in modules/rts (RtsVision). Long-term memory/threat ranking can compose ai-perception. Tick. stepSenses(config, defs, state, tick, input, los, occlusion) once per authoritative tick, strictly increasing ticks; invalid config/definitions/state/input (duplicate or non-positive IDs, out-of-range multipliers 0..4000, unknown disguise/spot IDs, bad noise radius) or a repeated/backwards tick return nullopt and leave the state untouched. Input lists may arrive in any order; they are processed by ascending ID. Order inside a tick: expire markers, deliver due alerts, disguise equip/blow, hiding exits, sight, hiding entries, hearing, trail detection, marker deposits, suspicion, alert broadcasts, search, records. Observers absent from the input are frozen (no decay, no search progress); alerts addressed to them are dropped (AlertDropped). stepSensesOpen uses always-visible / unoccluded callbacks (tests, open fields). Sight. Fixed metres; yaw in turns around +Y (yaw 0 faces +Z). Eye = position + eyeHeight. Zones: Focus (|bearing| <= halfAngle, distance <= range; strength nearMilli inside nearRange falling linearly to farMilli at range), Near (any bearing within nearRange, nearMilli) and Peripheral (|bearing| <= peripheralHalfAngle, distance <= peripheralRange, peripheralMilli); the strongest applies. Strength is then multiplied by the target's light/cover/stance/visibility and the observer's sightMilli (milli, capped at 1000). Only samples = sight.minMilli reach los(agent, target), called in (observer id, target id) order, at most sight.maxQueries per tick (losSkipped counts the rest). Self and same nonzero team are never sensed. Hearing. NoiseEvent{id, source, team, position, radius, loudnessMilli}; source 0 = anonymous disturbance (capped at Searching). Strength = loudness * (radius - distance)/radius * occlusion/1000 * hearingMilli/1000. At most hearing.maxNoises events per tick are processed, loudest first then smaller ID (NoiseDropped events for the rest). occlusion(agent, noise) (milli 0..1000, clamped) runs in that noise order then listener ID, only for listeners whose unoccluded strength reaches thresholdMilli, at most hearing.maxQueries per tick. Same-team noises are ignored; hidden targets still make noise. Trails. SenseTarget::leaveTrail deposits a marker (strength trailMilli) after this tick's detection. Markers decay linearly to zero over trail.lifetime and are removed then; beyond maxMarkers the oldest goes. Observers sense the strongest marker per owner within trail.range (scaled by distance and trailMilli, = minMilli; ties by smaller marker ID) without LOS. Suspicion. One AwarenessRecord per (observer, target): gain per tick = (sight*sightGain + hearing*hearingGain trail*trailGain)/1000, scaled by an active disguise. Levels: >= alertAt Alert, >= searchingAt Searching, = suspiciousAt Suspicious (1 <= suspiciousAt < searchingAt < alertAt <= maximum). Without stimulus the meter decays by decayPerTick per tick starting decayDelay ticks after the last stimulus (exact across skipped ticks), never below searchingAt for the active search target; records at 0 are dropped. The last known position follows sight > hearing > trail; alerts update it when newer. Alerts. A sensed transition into Alert (or any transition with alert.relay) schedules PendingAlerts to allies of the same nonzero team within alert.radius of the sender that are not already Alert about that target, delivered alert.delay ticks later (bounded by maxPending). Target AIVERSE::lib_action_bots (depends on combat-actions, weapon-policies, configuration); native OBJECT modules call aiverse_native_use_libraries(target action-bots). Skill: skills/ai/aiverse-action-bots. Namespace aiverse::lib::bots; the policies are independent of genre labels. Contract. Each policy is a pure decision step: one call per bot (or squad) per strictly increasing tick (repeated/backwards ticks and invalid input return nullopt with state untouched). It reads an owner-supplied snapshot and returns the same input a player produces; the owner applies it through its ordinary authorization (stepMelee/stepDodge/stepGuard/stepLockOn, stepFeed/stepRecoil, navigation, Commands). Bots never write health, poses, ammunition, cooldowns or match state, and difficulty never changes stats. Run them on the authoritative host only; replays record the resulting commands. Randomness only through the passed Random& (sim.rng() or an RNG saved with the simulation); draws happen only for chances strictly inside (0,1000) and for aim error > 0, so the stream is reproducible. Perception. PerceivedTarget{id,team,position,velocity,yaw,visible,guarding,vulnerable,healthMilli,threat} is the minimal hand-off from the owner's senses (LOS/FOV/hearing). Only visible hostile targets are engaged (same nonzero team and the bot itself are skipped); the current lock/target is kept while visible, else nearest by distance then id. meleeThreat(attacks,meleeState,tick,reach) derives the telegraph (attack id, start, windup, active, reach) from the visible attack phase. A senses package can adapt its output to this struct without changing the policies. Difficulty. BotDifficulty{reactionTicks,decisionTicks,aimError,misreadMilli}; presets difficultyPreset(0..2) (easy 20/8/1/40 turn/600, normal 5/4/1/200/150, hard 2/2/1/2000/0). Reaction delays acting on a newly perceived target and reading a telegraph (counted from the swing start); the decision interval re-plans movement and re-samples aim error; misreads ignore a read swing. Melee bot. stepMeleeBot(config, attacks, dodge, guard, state, tick, self, seen, rng) -> MeleeInput. Spacing band [minRange,maxRange]: approach beyond, retreat inside, strafe within (side flips every strafeTicks; outside attackRange the strafe also closes in). Openings: when idle and within attackRange it requests opener with openMilli chance per tick (avoids mirrored trades), never into a raised guard when respectGuard unless the target is vulnerable (recovery/stagger: always punished). Combos: only after a hit confirm on this swing, requested when age + bufferTicks >= cancelFrom so stepMelee starts the follow-up at the cancel frame. Defense: a swing in reach is read once after the reaction delay; the answer is Dodge (start at activeStart - invulnFrom, so the i-frames cover the first active frames), Guard (raise at activeStart - parryTicks/2, perfect-parry window straddles the first active frame; hold until the swing ends), Ignore (misread) or Retreat (no dodge ready and unblockable). dodgeMilli biases dodge vs guard. Lock-on: toggles to acquire once reacted. Stagger/committed swings hold position. Shooter bot. stepShooterBot(config, feed, state, tick, self, seen, cover, rng) -> ShooterInput. View turns at most turnPerTick per axis towards the solution plus seeded aim error, minus recoilCompensationMilli of the current recoil. Hitscan aims at the reported position; projectile weapons (projectileSpeed > 0) lead through genre::solveIntercept with aim (AimConfig) and do not fire when no solution exists. Fire (held trigger level) only when aligned within fireTolerance, recoil settled under recoilTolerance (burst control), in maxRange, round available and the feed Ready. Modifier pipeline. A perk is one package of ModEffect{stat, op, value, stage, bearer}; well-known stats are perk_stat::IncomingDamage, OutgoingDamage, MoveSpeed, FireInterval, FireCount, AttackRange, MaxHealth, SplashRadius, PickupRadius, PickupXp, CritChance, CritDamage, SummonCharges, SummonCooldown, HealthRegen, games add their own ids in stats (with min/max clamps). evaluateStat(defs, progress, stat, base, slot, bearer, &steps) orders effects by stage (default Set 0, Add 1, Multiply 2; explicit 0..15), then slot-scoped before player-scoped packages, then occurrence id and effect index; Multiply is milli and truncates per step (sequential packages, not a folded product); the result is clamped; steps lists every applied effect with the value after it (explainable builds). Slot-scoped perks reach only queries for that deck slot, player-scoped perks reach every slot; a bearer (owner kind: robot/weapon/bullet/hero...) filters effects. scaleAmount applies damage multipliers with saturation; rescaleHealth keeps the health fraction when max health grows and clamps when it shrinks. Built-in GameCore stats keep their own owner: this pipeline is for native/host games and custom stats. Stacking and selection. maxSelections (0 = unlimited) counts per player or per slot; requires / excludes look at the same slot and the player scope; units restricts slot perks to deck units; minLevel gates by the level being chosen; upgrades makes tier chains (selecting replaces one occurrence of the previous tier; loops rejected). offerable=false perks are only granted (initial abilities). grantPerk applies a perk under the same rules without xp (console, scripted rewards); clearPerks removes selected perks (optionally keeping initial ones); occurrence ids stay monotonic. Experience and offers. xpToNext reads the per-level table (xp.toNext, by current level), past its end adds xpGrowthPerLevel or caps; without a table the linear xp.curve (progression-curves systems::curve) is used; maxLevel caps both. grantXp adds kill/objective xp; with pickupBonus the player's PickupXp stat scales it and keeps the fractional remainder. Levels are banked: availableLevels, levelProgressMilli (HUD ring). openOffer builds the next level's offer from offers.levels[level] or offers.default (variant types recruit, slotPerk, playerPerk, anyPerk; explicit perk picks are reserved first), with the count from the battle deck (choiceCount, else deck.choices by tech level, else the variant count / offerChoices). Candidates are enumerated in ascending slot/perk order, filtered by the rules and an optional PerkHooks::weight hook, then drawn with the state's own PCG32 stream (seedPerks); unavailable positions are skipped without substitutes; an empty offer closes without spending xp. preferNewRecruitAtLevel narrows recruit picks to slots not yet recruited. rerollOffer spends one of offerRerolls, keeps explicit picks and avoids repeating items when alternatives exist. Every change bumps offer.revision; selectOffer(revision, index) re-validates, spends the level's xp, applies the perk (PerkSelected / PerkReplaced events with the perk's hook string, e.g. a Lua function name) or reports a Recruit for the owner to spawn, and opens the next banked offer. closeOffer cancels (stations). botOfferChoice picks the lowest aiPriority (recruits: recruitAiPriority; aiPriorityLowHealth when the bot is low on health).
