Pistol, shotgun and sniper require a new press for each shot. All are hitscan weapons. Weapon changes preserve separate magazine/reserve counts, cancel the current reload, and apply a switch delay. Fire cooldown survives switching. Reload completion transfers only the missing rounds from reserve. Respawn restores the configured loadout. Optional rules.json block (1–4 entries): {"actor": {"weapons":[ {"nameKey":"fps.weapon.pistol","damage":28,"magazine":12,"reserve":72, "automatic":false,"intervalTicks":15,"reloadTicks":75,"switchTicks":15,"range":150}, {"nameKey":"fps.weapon.rifle","damage":25,"magazine":30,"reserve":120, "intervalTicks":6,"reloadTicks":120,"range":400}, {"nameKey":"fps.weapon.shotgun","damage":14,"magazine":8,"reserve":40, "automatic":false,"intervalTicks":54,"reloadTicks":150,"range":60, "pellets":9,"spread":0.006}, {"nameKey":"fps.weapon.sniper","damage":100,"magazine":5,"reserve":25, "automatic":false,"intervalTicks":72,"reloadTicks":160,"range":1500} ]}} This is an excerpt, not a complete rules file. Times are simulation ticks; these values assume 60 Hz. spread is a turn offset in the deterministic pellet grid; damage is per pellet, one shell is consumed for the entire shot. nameKey is a localization key. The legacy actor.weapon block remains supported when weapons is absent. The editor weapon panel edits each loadout entry. Existing projects can add the array in the FPS panel's advanced rules editor and Apply. The client displays a procedural placeholder weapon, flash, cosmetic shot streak, magazine/reserve, reload state and a hit marker. Flash and hit markers follow accepted server shot/hit counters (they may be delayed by network latency). They are not a complete animated weapon asset. Extended mode adds synthesized audio. Damage and ammo are server-owned.

Build aiverse_fps_client, aiverse_fps_server, aiverse_fps_tests, aiverse_headless with CMake. The first three binaries are under <build>/modules/fps/. <build>/modules/fps/aiverse_fps_client --project templates/fps_training <build>/modules/fps/aiverse_fps_client --project templates/fps_arena --listen <build>/modules/fps/aiverse_fps_server --project templates/fps_arena --port 27100 <build>/modules/fps/aiverse_fps_client --project templates/fps_arena --connect udp://127.0.0.1:27100 <build>/modules/fps/aiverse_fps_tests examples/fps/arena <build>/aiverse_headless --project templates/fps_arena --seed 3 --verify-restore-at 1 --verify-restore-ticks 20 Client and server require identical content and protocol. The current FPS save version is 9 (gear and battle royale; versions 3, 6 and 7 still load); earlier experimental FPS saves and older peers are rejected. RTS save/protocol versions are unchanged.

Offline loopback, listen host and dedicated reference server share the authoritative simulation. It has bounded input queues, movement prediction/reconciliation, snapshots, interest filtering and bounded hitscan rewind. UDP latest snapshots use fragmentation; WebSocket uses its reliable transport. Production authentication, matchmaking, admission, reconnect, anti-cheat operations and WAN capacity qualification remain separate work. Snapshots travel as deltas against the newest snapshot the client acknowledged (its input viewTick) through the snapshot-delta package (protocol 5); Server::snapshotStats() reports packets, bytes and the full-snapshot equivalent. A 100-client loopback test is not evidence of production PUBG capacity. Large-world support uses sparse static AABB collision, relative render origins and budgeted loading of presentation box chunks through the generic large-world streamer (multiple observers, local chunk coordinates, load priorities, retry delays and resident resource reservations). Maps with world.async use background terrain/model preparation and streamed box/triangle collision, with a pre-tick authority gate and bounded GPU publication. See examples/world/streamed. Legacy maps retain resident collision. Dynamic-world persistence and streamed navmesh are separate work. Bots aim and strafe; they do not have production navigation/tactics.

Weapons with positive bulletSpeed can opt into the shared flight block: ordered Split, Ricochet, Fly Through and scalar modifiers. This works independently of mechanics.enabled; flight.gravity defaults to bulletGravity. Authoritative 3D sweeps, actor-life hit history, material penetration, save/rollback and existing snapshot presentation are supported. See projectile programs for the JSON schema and trajectory semantics.

actor.royale (mode battleRoyale) runs the battle-royale package on the FPS actors; a map's own royale block replaces the rules block. The JSON is the package format (examples/libraries/mechanics/royale/royale.json): bounds, zone phases, optional flight, drop, bombardment, supplyDrops, standings. actor.crate lists the items a landed supply drop spawns (item IDs as in loot; default armor, two medkits, magazine, ammo). Without the block the legacy linear zone keeps working. templates/fps_survival uses it (rules/royale.json). Piece Behavior Limits Insertion With flight every actor starts in the carrier on a seeded path; Jump leaves (door open after doorOpen ticks, eject at the end), Jump again opens the chute above minDeployHeight, Sprint dives, movement steers; the chute opens itself at autoDeployHeight; landing hands the actor to the motor. Ground height = collision cast down No carrier model / camera; fallback bots jump at seeded points and steer to their spawn Zone Seeded nested circles, wait / shrink, per-phase damage to landed actors outside Damage goes through armor like any hit Bombardment Shells hit landed actors in the blast circle unless collision is above their head (roof) No explosion falloff Supply drops Crates announced inside the next circle; actor.crate items spawn as loot on landing Crate is not a physical object Standings Downs, knocks (mechanics.knockdown), revives and outs are mirrored into the standings each tick; a team with nobody standing has its knocked members finished; the standings decide the winner (or a draw when the last teams fall on the same tick) Kill credit = last enemy who damaged the victim Snapshots carry RoyaleView (current and next circle, stage timer, own skydive phase, carrier position, players and teams left, own placement and kills, bombardment area, up to 8 falling crates); the client keeps the server pose while skydiving. SimEvents: 5 = kill feed (player = actor, value = victim | kind << 8), 6 = zone stage (value = phase | kind << 8, pos = target centre), 7 = supply drop (value = id | kind << 16, pos = point), 8 = shell impact (value = damage). FPS save version 8 stores the run (versions 3, 6 and 7 still load for games without actor.royale / actor.gear); snapshot protocol 5 (older peers are rejected). Test: royale in tests/fps/tests.cpp. The client (apps/fps/RoyaleHud.h) draws the zone wall near the viewer, landed crates, a minimap (current and next circle, bombardment, crates, carrier, own position and facing), the phase timer with players / teams / kills, jump / parachute hints, an outside-the-zone warning, the kill feed (RoyaleView::feed, the last six lines) and the result banner; strings are actor.royale.* in engine/assets/lang. Checked on a screenshot during the flight (Linux, Mesa software GL); the zone wall and the banner have not been looked at on screen yet.

actor.vehicleTypes (requires mechanics.enabled) holds vehicle-controllers definitions (examples/libraries/mechanics/vehicles-sports/vehicles.json format: wheeled / tracked / hover / flight controller, damage zones, seats). A map vehicle with "type": id (and optional "yaw" in turns) drives with that controller: the driver's forward / back become throttle / brake (reverse when stopped), right steers, Jump is the handbrake, pitch drives flight; the ground height under it comes from collision, static walls stop it through the package's collision response, and a hard crash damages it. Interact enters the nearest typed vehicle within 6 m (driver seat first, then the next free seat) and leaves it at the first clear exit point when it is slow enough. Passengers and gunners keep Fire / Aim / Reload / weapon keys; the driver does not shoot. Knocked, killed or thrown-out occupants are ejected; a destroyed vehicle kills everyone inside. Vehicles without type keep the legacy car. Typed vehicles run on the one vehicle system of every host (engine/vehicles, docs/driving.md): the entity carries vehicles::VehicleDrive, actor.vehicleTypes become shared vehicle types (metres, seat lists; a hard crash costs (impact - 8 m/s) x 10 health), and engine/actor/ActorVehicles.cpp is only the metre-map world query (ground cast, box sweep against the triangle world, seat-list glue). An empty typed vehicle at rest sleeps (not stepped) like every parked vehicle. FPS save version 10 stores the shared VehicleDrive record. templates/fps_survival has ten four-seat cars (rules/vehicles.json). Test: typedVehicles in tests/fps/tests.cpp.

A map "race" block makes the typed map vehicles race: the shared race capability of every project, documented in races.md (data, behaviour, HUD). The adapter is the shared vehicles::VehicleRace (engine/vehicles); this module only seats the racers (RaceSeats in engine/actor/ActorVehicles.cpp): player i is seated as the driver of the i-th typed map vehicle (ascending vehicle id); the race decides the round (at the round limit the leader wins). ECS shape: the vehicles::RaceState world resource (racer i = slot i, racers[i - 1] = its car), the cars are Vehicle + vehicles::VehicleDrive entities. FPS save version 10 appends the RaceState record only on maps with a race; snapshots carry the player's lib::mechanics::RaceView (authority protocol 6). The client shows the chase camera (rules / map "camera": {"chase": {...}}, first-person look: "firstPerson"; presets in camera-behaviors.md) and the race HUD at the wheel and hides the weapon UI.

Map buildings lists building-gen houses: {"pos":[x,y,z],"yaw":0..3,"seed":n,"building":{"width":12,"depth":10,"floors":2,...},"loot":[item types]}. At setup each becomes static collision boxes (ids from kBuildingColliderBase; slabs, walls with a door and windows, a partition, switchback stairs, roof) sized for the FPS motor (radius, height, step height), and its loot lies on the generated room spots (requires mechanics.enabled). The client draws them also on chunked maps. templates/fps_survival has 25 houses of one to three floors. Test: buildings in tests/fps/tests.cpp (walk in through the door, climb a floor with the real motor).

actor.bots holds bots-combatant settings ({"preset":"normal","sightRange":120}). Map players with "bot": true then run that controller inside the authoritative tick instead of the reference fallback bot: perception, reaction, bounded aim, reload, retreat and the battle-royale zone (the announced circle). On top of it the module adds goals: wanted loot within 25 m (weapons it lacks, better gear, medkits, ammo) and Interact when in reach, Heal when hurt and out of combat, and a point inside the next circle otherwise. Navigation: one navmesh per generated building (0.5 m cells, built at setup from collision) plus straight steering in the open; a goal inside a building outside the bot's region goes through its door, other floors through the stair flights (the navmesh reaches the flight's hall point, the bot walks the flight straight). Bot state is saved (FPS save version 9) and hashed. templates/fps_survival uses it. Tests: houseBots, upstairsBot, houseNavigation.

A map collider with "yaw" (turns) is {"id","center","half","yaw"}: a box turned about +Y, stored as its 12 surface triangles (engine/world/OrientedBox.h), so casts, the motor and hits use the exact turned box. Its collision ids are allocated from kRotatedColliderBase; the navmesh treats it by its bounding box. Test: rotatedColliders.

actor.gear (requires mechanics.enabled) is a gear-tiers catalog: pieces with id 1..55, slot, tier, durability, reduction / wear (milli), zones (1 = head shots, 2 = every other hit) and capacity (extra inventory stacks, up to 24 in total). Loot type 200 + id is a gear piece (map loot, actor.crate); Interact equips it and the replaced piece takes its place on the ground with its durability. With a catalog the gear replaces the legacy flat armor absorption. Broken pieces emit SimEvent 9 (player = wearer, value = slot); dying drops every worn piece. The own loadout travels in snapshots (Snapshot::gear); FPS save version 10 stores loadouts. templates/fps_survival ships three helmet, vest and backpack levels (rules/gear.json) spread near the spawns and in supply crates.

A locomotion block (top level of the rules, or rules.actor.locomotion) moves characters through the shared character-locomotion mode machine (engine/mechanics/LocomotionModes.h) instead of the plain motor. Keys are the locomotion.* settings of docs/gameplay-settings.md (milli-units and ticks, same ranges and relations; {} = defaults); the motor's speed / sprintSpeed / jumpSpeed / gravity and stances still apply. Rules without the block behave and hash exactly as before: no locomotion state, no save or network bytes. Move Input How the host reports the world Dash Dash press (desktop K, pad RB): along the move direction, else the view wall ahead from the side probes ends it Wall slide / wall run hold the move key into a wall / run along it after a jump short side probes around the body: wall normal and collider id (same-wall reattach rule) Grapple (pull or swing) hold Grapple (middle mouse, J, pad LB); release lets go the view ray up to grappleMaxLengthMilli; the hit point is kept while attached Glide hold Glide (Space held, pad A) while falling — Slopes, coyote time, jump buffer as before ground normal of the sweep The server sends each player its own locomotion state (snapshot-delta record kind 5); the client predicts the modes with the same motor and reconciles them with the rest of the pose. Saves (version 10) append the per-character state only with the block; the checksum includes it only with the block. Not reported by this host yet: ledges, ladders, climbable walls, water and one-way colliders (the map format has no tags for them), so those modes stay idle here. Tests: aiverse_fps_tests (locomotionModes: dash, wall run, grapple, save mid-dash, client prediction).

actor.melee.enabled: true adds an authoritative melee strike, guard, parry and lock-on. It is independent of actor.mechanics; rules without the block behave as before. Swing timing, input buffering, chaining and one-hit-per-target-per-swing come from the shared melee-combat library (engine/mechanics/Melee.h). Behavior Implementation Current limits Strike Windup, active and recovery ticks; the blade tip is swept from its previous position each active tick against actor bounds widened by radius One attack type, no combos or weapon-specific swings; no skinned animation Guard Held Block negates hits whose attacker is within guardTurns of the facing direction; Block also stops firing No stamina or guard break Parry Pressing Block opens a parryTicks window; a strike landing in it deals no damage and staggers the attacker Parry gives no riposte bonus Stagger A landed hit staggers the target and a parry staggers the attacker for staggerTicks; staggered actors cannot strike or fire — Lock-on Holding LockOn selects the nearest living enemy within lockRange; strikes aim at the locked target until it dies or moves out of twice the range Camera does not follow the lock Data: actor.melee accepts enabled, damage, windupTicks, activeTicks, recoveryTicks, bufferTicks, parryTicks, staggerTicks (ticks; defaults scale with tick rate), range, radius, lockRange (world units) and guardTurns (half-angle in turns, at most 0.25). Simulation events: 3 = swing started, 4 = contact (value = target slot | contact << 8, where contact is hit 0 / blocked 1 / parried 2). Melee state is saved from FPS save version 7 and hashed when the block is enabled. Desktop client controls when enabled: Z strike, hold Left Alt guard (press to parry), hold T lock-on. The client has no melee viewmodel or hit sounds yet; check it live before treating the feel as finished.

actor.mechanics.enabled: true enables the extended authoritative systems. Existing rules without this block retain their single-round behavior. The bundled training, arena, survival and tactical templates enable this block. System Implemented behavior Current limits Aiming and recoil RMB zoom/sensitivity, reduced ADS spread, movement spread, server recoil and recovery Procedural viewmodel, no skinned arms or authored animations Damage Height-based head/body/leg regions, head and limb multipliers, consumable armor Regions of the actor AABB, not skeletal hitboxes Penetration Opt-in collider penetration cost, decreasing damage and a bounded per-projectile penetrated-collider list Material cost, not thickness/ricochet simulation Ballistics Swept bullet segments, speed, gravity, range and lifetime Projectile hits use current state, not hitscan rewind Grenades Frag radial damage with cover; bouncing smoke and flash grenades; smoke lifetime; view-direction-dependent flash duration Smoke is a box volume placeholder; no fluid simulation Inventory Bounded stacks using the shared inventory library, pickups, weapon drop/pickup retaining ammo and attachments Fixed item catalog; no drag-and-drop inventory UI Attachments Scope, suppressor, extended magazine, with actual accuracy/audio/capacity effects Three fixed attachment types Medical Delayed consumable healing, movement/fire/damage cancellation, teammate knockdown, bleeding and revive Knockdown requires a living teammate Tactical rounds Freeze/buy phase, spawn buy zone, money, plant/defuse timers, dropped bomb recovery, score, round restart Team 1 attacks; team 2 defends; no halftime or overtime; loadout resets each round Movement Prone with ceiling clearance, explicit ladder regions, checked short-obstacle vault Axis-aligned collision; vault is a discrete move, not a root-motion animation Vehicles Legacy: driver admission, exclusive control, steering, swept static collision, safe exit and weapon damage. Typed (actor.vehicleTypes, below): package controllers, seats with passengers and gunners Legacy car: single seat on flat ground. Typed: no suspension geometry, no vehicle-vehicle collisions Audio Synthesized original shot/reload/footstep sounds through the engine audio service; remote shot attenuation and simple cover volume reduction Placeholder sound design; own-player footsteps only fps_tactical / Breach Protocol is a separate bomb-mode example. Existing copied projects are not upgraded automatically. The default standalone FPS client opens fps_training and resolves engine assets independently of its launch directory.

Input Action RMB Aim / scope G / X / C Frag / smoke / flash grenade H Heal E Nearby pickup, revive, enter/exit vehicle, ladder, or defuse Q Drop equipped weapon V / F Toggle prone / vault P Plant bomb while carrying it inside a site 1–4 then B Buy the selected weapon in the buy zone and equip it F1 / F2 / F3 Install carried scope / suppressor / magazine Hold Tab Inventory list

Weapon entries additionally accept hipSpread, moveSpread, recoil (turns), bulletSpeed (zero = hitscan), bulletGravity, penetration, headMultiplier, limbMultiplier, and price. Defaults preserve legacy accuracy and hitscan behavior. actor.mechanics accepts knockdown, startArmor, startMoney, killReward, winReward, lossReward, healTicks, reviveTicks, bleedTicks, freezeTicks, buyTicks, plantTicks, defuseTicks, bombTicks, roundsToWin, grenadeFuse, smokeTicks, flashTicks, interactRange, blastRadius, smokeRadius, flashRadius. Timing defaults scale with tick rate. Distances use world units. Map arrays: loot (pos, type, count), vehicles (pos, optional speed), ladders and bombSites (min, max). Collider penetration is an optional positive cost; absent means impenetrable. Item IDs: 1 medkit, 2 armor, 3 frag, 4 smoke, 5 flash, 6 scope, 7 suppressor, 8 magazine, 9 ammo; 100–103 are weapons. Bounds: 256 projectiles, 256 loot objects, 32 vehicles, 12 inventory stacks. Snapshots carry at most 128 nearby projectiles and loot objects, plus 32 vehicles; latest-message transport is bounded to 128 KiB. Snapshots are delta-compressed (above); interest filtering still decides what is sent. All new outcome-affecting fields, objects and timers are saved and hashed. tests/fps/systems.inc covers inventory, attachments, cancellation, vehicles, ladders, prone, grenade effects, hit regions, penetration, ballistics, revival, restoration, buying, planting/defusing, round reset and vaulting. The current client HUD/viewmodel/smoke and audio changes require a successful live visual/audio check. The automated GUI launch was interrupted; do not treat a compiled client or the headless scenarios as proof of visual quality. Windows, web and mobile integration of these new controls has not been verified.

The reference FPS client now supports an optional character model without changing authoritative FPS simulation, saves, or network protocol: { "actor": { "visual": { "model": "models/hero.glb", "scale": 1.0, "heightOffset": 0.0 } } } Place the model under the FPS project directory. An optional actor.visual.animationGraph object uses the existing AnimationGraph JSON format; otherwise, the client builds a basic Idle/Walk or Idle/Run blend graph from recognized clip names. Input parameters projected from snapshots: speed, moving, dead, grounded, reloading. The reference client runs a separate presentation ECS World, not a gameplay world, and computes remote actor poses per render frame. Invalid model/graph assets retain the previous box rendering fallback. The procedural first-person weapon remains unchanged. This path requires a real model and visual testing.

Set actor.visual.bakedCrowd: true with a skinned actor.visual.model and no custom actor.visual.animationGraph. The FPS client then bakes the model's clips into a joint-matrix texture, drives per-entity Idle/Walk/Run/Death through the shared AnimationCrowdComponent, and submits Renderer3D::ModelDraw::baked for GPU instancing. If a bake is unavailable, it uses the existing palette graph or box fallback. Complex avatars with IK, upper-body layers, and imported controllers stay in palette mode. The palette path now uses the shared AnimationSignificanceComponent / assignAnimationBudgets rather than hard-coded per-distance pose sampling.

Optional actor.visual.graphFile: "animations/hero.json" loads a project-relative AnimationGraph file instead of the generated Idle/Walk/Run graph. The client polls for changed file timestamps on its presentation thread (every 30 rendered frames), recompiles transactionally, retains the last good graph after an invalid edit, and swaps immutable graph pointers on existing presentation entities. Game/network simulation is unchanged. Changing a graph restarts its visual state machine. This file is resolved inside the current project; it must not contain parent-path traversal.

Under actor.visual, optional animationMode is "auto" (default), "cpu", or "gpu". Existing bakedCrowd: true remains equivalent to forcing "gpu" when a suitable animation can be baked. Custom animationGraph or graphFile, native callbacks, IK and layered rigs remain on the CPU graph path. In auto mode, the client chooses GPU baked instanced skinning for simple imported clips at gpuEnterActors living remote characters (24 by default). It switches back to full CPU graph below or at gpuExitActors (12 by default), with hysteresis to reduce mode thrashing. Backend changes recreate presentation-only animation entities; simulation actor state, game networking and saves are not touched. A missing GPU bake retains CPU fallback. CPU graph animation automatically uses the host-owned persistent MotionWeave scheduler when 16 or more remote presentation actors exist. Its cost-aware worker jobs avoid custom callback/rig operations, which execute on the submitting thread after a barrier. Set actor.visual.animationStats: true to see CPU/GPU path, worker count, work estimates, jobs, and CPU timings in the FPS HUD. This is presentation profiling, not deterministic simulation state.

h: MotionWeave cosmetic Montages from replicated FPS actions
x: Optional project-local JSON assets can be authored in the editor (animations/montage/) or through Workspace/MCP: {"actor": {"visual":{ "model":"models/hero.glb", "montages":{ "shot":"animations/montage/fire.json", "reload":"animations/montage/reload.json", "death":"animations/montage/death.json" } }}} Montage files reference imported clip names, sections, optional masks, blend-in/out and cosmetic notifies. Missing or invalid files are logged and skipped; no crash or authoritative gameplay action is generated. While a death Montage is active the dead actor may still render until its visual section completes. Replicated shot count, reload deadline and health/life transitions are used for one-shot visual triggers; stale/duplicate snapshots never replay the same Montage. A newly visible actor doesn't invent a shot. The FPS game server, hit detection, ammo, damage and reloading remain authoritative. When any valid Montage is configured, the backend stays on the CPU Graph path so its upper-body mask/sections can be evaluated. When switching between simple CPU Graph and GPU Baked Animation, MotionWeave now captures each remote actor's normalized idle/walk clip phase and seeds the new presentation player. This avoids the previous forced restart at clip time zero. MotionWeave preserves confirmed replicated animation-action history across backend changes, so shot/reload/death cosmetics do not replay. The transition still cannot preserve arbitrary controller blends or motion-matching state and remains limited to simple clips.

h: Engine View for models and primitives
x: The FPS reference client maps both animated models and ordinary scene meshes (cube fallback actors, collider debug shapes, world boxes) to the shared genre-independent aiverse::View. The renderer still receives the same world transforms, color and draw flags: View::submitOne for ModelDraw and View::submitMesh for simple Mesh packets. No FPS state is ever read by the core View, and a missing animated character continues to fall back to the visible cube. For groups of independent world objects, the host now collects view::MeshObject records into view::ScenePacketBatch and submits them through View::submitPackets. The draw command sequence for loot, vehicles, projectiles and planted objects is unchanged. A deliberate batch boundary before the royale-zone wall preserves the previous wall/crate ordering. Only generic geometry enters View; game-specific rules stay in the FPS host. ScenePacketBatch does not replace Renderer3D's existing material/mesh batching logic. Source on GitHub: docs/fps.md

The reusable aiverse::meta::Service adds friends/clans, instance items, entitlements and ranked tournament groups to the existing economy, leaderboard and chat policies. engine/meta/Service.h is public to both engine and external native C++ hosts. No Lua, GPU, network library or running RTS match is required.

cmake -S tests/meta -B build/.temp/meta -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug cmake --build build/.temp/meta -j 4 ctest --test-dir build/.temp/meta --output-on-failure python3 tools/meta/scaffold.py --preset full --with-ui --out /path/to/game python3 tools/meta/compose.py --project /path/to/game --validator build/.temp/meta/aiverse_meta_validate python3 tools/meta/server.py --db /path/to/game/meta.sqlite user player1 # Copy the printed player token into the browser sign-in form. python3 tools/meta/server.py --db /path/to/game/meta.sqlite serve \ --binary build/.temp/meta/aiverse_meta_service \ --config /path/to/game/meta/service.generated.json --ui /path/to/game/ui/meta # Open http://127.0.0.1:8765 economy.json, boards.json, chats.json and extensions.json are editable sources. compose.py validates before replacing service.generated.json; never hand-edit that output. The generator refuses to overwrite definitions or UI. full adds all new policies; minimal/mobile/competitive retain their narrower presets. Remove optional extension sections to disable features. Restart the reference host after changing configuration. Keep configuration versioned while orders/tournaments are pending. The browser UI is a working reference client with shop, quests/daily/energy, leaderboards, global chat, friends/clans, item collection, inbox and tournaments. Text is inserted with textContent; RU/EN labels are in ui/lang.json; colors/layout are CSS variables. No framework or CDN. It is not automatically mounted in RmlUi. For a native UI use the same view projection and RPC actions with the host's localization and existing RmlUi components. Real-money offers show a store handoff; the reference browser does not initiate native platform payments.

#include "engine/meta/Service.h" using namespace aiverse::meta; auto definitions = ServiceConfig::parse(json); Service service(definitions, savedSnapshot, atomicCompareAndSwap); ServiceRequest request{"friends", "request", "stable-request-id", args}; auto reply = service.execute(authenticatedPrincipal, request, trustedUtcSeconds); auto presentation = service.view(authenticatedPrincipal.player, trustedUtcSeconds); Link aiverse::meta; registered game modules use aiverse_native_use_meta(aiverse_native_ID). Keep the service in the native UI/service host, never in simulation tick callbacks. Use engine commands for any validated meta snapshot that affects the match. RemoteBackend accepts a host transport function and delivers callbacks during pump. The host owns HTTPS, session acquisition, timeout/retry and response decoding. All completion and pump calls occur on the owning thread; the adapter does not create threads. Late callbacks after adapter destruction drop into an unobserved queue safely.

A Principal comes from the host, not client JSON. Ordinary players may create their own profile once, spend their own balances, claim earned rewards, send messages and manage permitted social actions. Only authority=true may grant rewards/items, record progression, submit scores, settle tournaments, fulfill/cancel purchases, moderate messages or deliver entitlement provider events. This flag is not a receipt validator: the host must first verify the platform event or authoritative match result. The server snapshot owns all profiles, extra state, social relations, clans, boards, chats, tournaments and receipts. A command mutates a copy, then performs one Commit(expectedRevision, wholeSnapshot) and publishes on success. Failed operations and failed commits leave the prior state unchanged. The reference host holds SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE across native dispatch and snapshot replacement. This serializes cross-profile transfers and season rewards, including across host processes. Operation IDs are scoped to authenticated player, with service/action/arguments and privilege in their canonical fingerprint. Identical retries return Duplicate with the original result. Changed payloads return Conflict. JSON object key order does not change the fingerprint. Account age is derived from the persisted profile creation time; ordinary clients cannot supply it. Other targeting metrics come from authoritative progress events. UTC is read by the host; mutating calls reject backward clock jumps. Dedupe receipts must not be pruned without an explicit retry-retention protocol. The snapshot constructor accepts trusted server storage, not uploaded saves. view exposes only the current profile (without operation receipts), the player's friend requests, own clan, visible channels and public scores. The full aggregate snapshot is never returned by the HTTP host. Pending order IDs and receipt tokens are server-only; the reference view strips payment order records.

All mutations need a nonempty operation (up to 128 bytes), service, action and object arguments. IDs are nonempty strings of at most 128 bytes. Amounts/times are integers in 0..10^12. Errors use Code: Ok=0, Duplicate=1, Invalid=2, Missing=3, Unavailable=4, Insufficient=5, Limit=6, Conflict=7, Denied=8, Unsupported=9. Service Actions Arguments / semantics meta view no arguments; read-only projection profile create no arguments; configured initial balances, once economy buy, daily, energy, mail, reserve id; reserve returns stable server order ID economy claim id, zero-based tier economy event authority: metric, nonnegative amount economy grant authority: reward bundle economy deliver authority: id, reward, expires (0 = none) economy fulfill, cancel authority: order, token for fulfill; globally unique verified payment token friends request, accept, reject, remove, block, unblock target; symmetric friendship, directional block clan create, join, leave id; join requires unexpired invitation clan invite, kick, transfer id, target; owner/officer authorization clan role owner only: id, target, role = member/officer clan donate id, asset, positive amount; atomic debit + cumulative bank clan goal id, goal; member claims once when bank threshold reached items grant authority: instance id, definition type items redeem new instance id, definition type; atomically consumes one configured asset items upgrade, salvage, unequip instance id items equip instance id, compatible slot; occupied slots reject items merge surviving instance id, inputs = other distinct instance IDs entitlement grant, revoke authority: id, unique provider event, increasing sequence, start, end board submit authority: id, score tournament join id; server allocates cohort by league and arrival order tournament submit authority: id, score, enrolled player tournament settle authority: id, at/after end, all groups in one transaction chat send id, text, optional kind chat read, report, delete id, sequence; delete requires authority chat block, unblock id, target chat mute authority: id, target, until

See examples/meta/service.json for a complete, validated definition. initial: starting balance bundle. Only profile creation applies it. friends: maxFriends/maxRequests (default 100 each, bounded 1..10000). clans: maxMembers (50), inviteSeconds (86400), createCost, named goals. Goal = asset/amount/reward. Donations are cumulative contributions, not a withdrawable wallet. Owner transfer is required before the owner of a nonempty clan leaves. Officers invite/kick regular members; only the owner promotes/kicks officers. Each player can belong to one clan. New members may claim completed shared goals. items: named definitions with optional asset, slots, upgradeCosts (per next level), salvage bundle, optional mergeCount/mergeTo, metadata. Instances have stable ID/type/level; merge requires equal types and levels, consumes exactly mergeCount instances, retains the selected ID and resets its level to zero on the target type. Equipped items cannot be consumed. Upgrade/salvage and balance changes commit together. The optional asset maps shop/quest/mail balance rewards to instance creation via items.redeem; the browser collection offers that conversion when the asset exists. This is persistent instance inventory, not the simulation's stacked inventory. entitlements: named tag/metadata definitions. Verified provider events replace the entitlement's authoritative interval. End=0 means permanent; end is exclusive. Sequence must increase, and event IDs cannot be reused across players. Renewals use a new provider event and updated interval; refunds revoke. For restore, replay the original operation or send a newer authoritative snapshot event. Multiple provider purchases for one entitlement must be reconciled by the provider adapter. tournaments: each ID is an immutable season: start/end, groupSize (2..10000), promote/demote counts, maxLeague, per-rank rewards and ordinary board policy. Groups fill in enrollment order within league; ties use board rules and player ID. Promotion/demotion uses ordered position (unique), rewards use displayed rank. Small groups allocate promotion first. New season = new ID. Enrollment records group membership without inventing a score. Only verified score submitters receive ranks/rewards or league changes; non-submitters retain their league. Settlement writes results, league and reward mail once; inbox avoids losing payouts to an inventory cap at settlement. Settled season results do not change when claims are retried.

h: HTTP reference host and operational limits
x: server.py is a real local HTTP endpoint backed by SQLite and the C++ executable. It stores SHA-256 hashes of random bearer tokens, checks expiration, rejects unknown request fields, caps body size and strips complete state from replies. user PLAYER provisions a token for an already identified player; revoke PLAYER revokes sessions. user PLAYER --authority creates a trusted server credential; do not put it in the player UI. A game authentication provider must exchange verified identity for sessions. No OAuth account linking or password database is included. It deliberately binds 127.0.0.1. Internet deployment requires TLS/reverse proxy, rate/connection limits, identity provisioning, observability and backups. Set --public-origin https://game.example to the exact browser origin when behind a TLS proxy; forwarded scheme headers are not trusted. None has been deployed by this change. The host starts one native subprocess per request and stores one aggregate snapshot: suitable for integration/reference and small projects, not an MMO database architecture. Read views contain the first 50 leaderboard/chat rows; the underlying Leaderboard/Chat APIs expose pages and cursors for native hosts. Configured reference chat channels are global. Private/clan scopes must use the underlying Chat authorization callback in a project host; do not label global channels as private based on their names. Tournament grouping is ranked cohorts, not brackets or latency-aware matchmaking. State migration and expired-season archival remain explicit host responsibilities. Do not delete or mutate pending-season definitions.

h: Battle networking for mobile PvP / PvE (hosted battles)
x: Drone Fall-style battles (direct-control heroes, PvP and PvE, phones on Wi-Fi / LTE) run on the engine's own server and rollback stack. No compatibility with Drone Fall's LiteNetLib / ME.BECS protocol is kept; the behaviour it needs is reproduced: input rollback with hash sync, ping and server time, interpolation of corrections, reconnect / late join with a world catch-up, a startup payload per player (SpawnWanderData) and a compatibility key that splits incompatible builds. Piece Where What Crypto engine/net/Crypto.*, third_party/monocypher (4.0.2, BSD-2/CC0) XChaCha20-Poly1305, keyed BLAKE2b, OS entropy Match tickets engine/net/MatchTicket.* sealed per-player tickets, compatibilityKey() Secure transport engine/net/SecureUdp.*, Datagram.h encrypted UDP with handshake, replay window, NAT rebinding, battle ping Mobile link simulator engine/net/SimNet.* loss, bursts, latency, jitter, duplicates, rebinding, app suspend on a virtual clock Loss tolerance ReliableChannel::setRedundancy (engine/net/Reliable.*) repeats small unacked messages at a growing interval Hero input engine/net/HeroInput.h the one hero wire format: kCmdHeroInput = RTS kCmdTopDown, kCmdHeroAbility = kCmdTopDownAbility Correction smoothing engine/net/Smoothing.h, RollbackSession::setRollbackHook blends rollback corrections in presentation Hosted battles engine/net/server/ServerHosted.cpp, BattleProtocol.* allocation, seating by ticket, start payload, result consensus, reports Control plane engine/net/server/BattleControl.* signed JSON over TCP: allocate / release / status / reports Client lifecycle NetClient::suspend / resume / matchPayload / setResultReporter background / foreground, payload, result blob Tools apps/battle (aiverse_battle), aiverse_server --battle-port ... keys, tickets, control client, ping, headless load test RTS battles apps/battle/RtsBattle.* a top-down GameCore project (topdown_arena, extraction, Drone Fall) on the load harness Tests tests/net_mobile/battle_tests.cpp (aiverse_battle_tests) everything above

The client pings every battle server it was told about (sendBattlePing / readBattlePong, 32-byte request, 10-byte answer with the server's load) and sends the pings plus its compatibility key "<appVersion>|protocol:<n>|map:<mapId>" to matchmaking (Drone Fall's GetCompatibilityKey format). Matchmaking (the meta backend, out of the engine) groups players, picks a server and calls its control port: allocate with match id, game id, compatibility key, map, seed, players (player id, slot, team, name, loadout bytes), game data, join timeout and time limit. Matchmaking issues one ticket per player with the server key it shares with the battle servers (issueTicket, or aiverse_battle ticket) and sends it to the player over its own TLS channel. The client connects: connectSecure(ClientTicket) and hands the connection to NetClient. The server seats the player by the ticket's player id and slot. It never trusts names, slots or ids that the client sends. When every allocated human is there, or the join timeout passes with at least one player, the match starts. Each client gets MatchPayload first, then MatchStart (matchReady()), builds the simulation from the payload, and calls attach(). Players who are not there join late and receive the whole confirmed history. Players who never come are counted as gone after the reconnect grace. When the match result is confirmed, every client sends its result blob (setResultReporter) and its result. The server compares the blobs. MatchReport (callback onMatchReport, queue takeReports(), control op reports) carries the result, per-player join / leave / connected state, filtered command counts, the agreed blob, consensus, desync, abort and replay path.

A handshake works like netcode.io connect tokens, with its own wire format: Request: 0xA1, version, the ticket's sealed part, zero-padded to 1000 bytes. The server opens it with the server key. It checks the expiry against its unix clock, then checks that it hosts that match, player, slot and compatibility hash (Server::admits). Challenge: 0xA2, session id, random nonce, then a salt and cookie encrypted with the ticket's s2c key. Session keys are derived per handshake (BLAKE2b(ticketKey, label | sid | salt)), so 64-bit sequence nonces never repeat under one key, even after many reconnects with one ticket. Response: 0xA3, the cookie encrypted with the derived c2s key. This proves the client holds the ticket keys and receives at its source address. A stolen sealed part is useless without the keys. Data: 0xA4, session id, sequence number, then an XChaCha20-Poly1305 payload. The 13-byte header is authenticated. The payload carries the existing ReliableChannel or LatestChannel bytes, or bye / accept. A 256-packet replay window drops duplicates and replays. NAT and handover: only the client initiates. Keepalives every 250 ms hold the NAT mapping. When an authenticated packet with a newer sequence number arrives from a new address, the session moves there (Wi-Fi to LTE, carrier NAT rebinding). Without path validation, an on-path attacker who races a fresh packet can redirect traffic until the real client sends its next packet. The attacker cannot read or forge that traffic. No amplification: requests are 1000 bytes. Challenges (77 bytes) and pongs (10 bytes) are smaller. Rejected tickets get no answer: the client times out, and nothing becomes an oracle. Half-open handshakes are limited to 256, expire after 5 s, and the oldest is dropped first. Sessions are limited to maxSessions. Keys stay off the command line: servers read them from files (--server-key-file, --control-key-file, create them with aiverse_battle keygen, mode 0600). Tickets are secrets for the client. The game never sees session keys: SecureAccepted::claims has them wiped. Web builds have no UDP. A browser battle client would need a WebSocket-over-TLS gateway. That gateway does not exist yet.

h: Loss and latency on mobile links
x: SecureLinkConfig::redundancyMs (default 30) makes the reliable channel repeat unacknowledged messages of 256 bytes or less (input frames, tick batches, checksums). It repeats them in the first datagram of a flush after 30, 60, 90, ... ms, without waiting for an RTO. The test secure_stream_tolerates_mobile_loss measures a 20 Hz stream of input frames over 150 ms RTT, 40 ms jitter and 1% loss bursts of 4 packets: independent loss p95 one-way delivery, with redundancy without (plain RTO resends) 10% 160 ms 570 ms 20% 260 ms 2940 ms Every message arrived in order in both cases. The base one-way delay is 75 ms plus up to 40 ms of jitter. Plain connectUdp keeps the old behaviour (redundancy off).

h: Rollback and prediction for a direct-control hero
x: The existing RollbackSession (server-confirmed input, client prediction, snapshots, re-simulation) drives the battle. Hero input travels as sticky state (HeroInput.h). There is one scheme: the RTS module's top-down heroes (docs/topdown.md) use the engine-reserved ids, so games, the server's command filter, the load test and the tools all speak it. kCmdHeroInput (0xF100) = kCmdTopDown: topdown::pack(Input) in Command::param: move angle in binary turns (0 = +z, 16384 = +x) and magnitude (per mille), aim angle and the aim / fire bits. The simulation keeps it until the next one and re-quantizes it to its rules (Drone Fall: 45 sectors, full speed or nothing). HeroInputQuantizer (or the client's TopDownControls) sends a command only when the quantized state changes, as Drone Fall's HandleMovement does. When a remote player sends nothing, the session predicts "no command". With sticky state, that means "same input as before", so remote heroes keep moving and shooting. A misprediction only happens when a remote player changes input, and costs a short rollback. kCmdHeroAbility (0xF101) = kCmdTopDownAbility: one button event, topdown::abilityParam(Ability): ability index (255 = escape), phase (tap, press, release, cancel), optionally the button's stick direction and distance; Command::point for a cursor / preview point. A bare index (stage-1 clients) is a tap. net::kCmdHeroAction is kept as an alias of kCmdHeroAbility. The simulation decodes with topdown::unpack / unpackAbility and the fixed-point moveVector, aimVector, directionXZ. Hostile bit patterns are clamped or rejected. Hosted allocations restrict a match to these types (allowedCommands = {kCmdHeroInput, kCmdHeroAbility}) and to maxCommandsPerTick per player. Anything else is dropped on the server and counted in the report. battleSettings(tickRate) gives the mobile room settings: input delay 1, rollback window max(8, 0.6 s) (12 at 20 Hz), lag tolerance 250 ms, a checksum every second, no spectators. Drone Fall runs its logic at 10 Hz with input lag 0. The engine's 20 Hz with delay 1 gives the same 50 ms local response at twice the simulation resolution. Presentation: RollbackSession::setRollbackHook(fn) calls fn(true) right before a rollback and fn(false) after the re-simulation, both at the same tick. Read hero positions in both calls and pass the difference to CorrectionSmoother::correct(). Draw at the interpolated sim position plus offset(), and call advance(dtMs) once per frame. The offset halves every 50 ms. Corrections over 4 units snap. The game client does this for heroes and squad members (TopDownPrediction, ClientTopDown.cpp), and the load test does it for every bot client, reporting corrections and the largest per-frame jump of the sim position versus the drawn position. Local visual prediction: the client draws its own hero where the input already in flight takes it (input delay plus interpolation lag), render only (docs/topdown.md § Network). Desync: checksums every checksumInterval ticks are compared on the server. Desync reaches every client (NetEvent::Kind::Desync), and the report has desync = true and no consensus. The game must freeze outcome state once result() is non-zero, as HeroDuel does. Every client's result blob is then the same, however far past the result tick it has predicted. GameCore does this for every RTS game: the outcome system latches the first result and its blob (outcomeBlob()); see docs/topdown.md § Outcome.

h: Reconnect, late join and app suspend
x: NetClient::setReconnect(...) with a lambda that calls connectSecure(ticket) again. After a drop, the client handshakes again with the same ticket. The ticket's expiry bounds this, so give it the match's time limit plus the grace period. The server moves the player's record to the new link. If the client still has the match running, it resumes with a delta: only the input confirmed since its last confirmed tick. Otherwise it gets a full MatchStart with the history and re-simulates. Mobile lifecycle: call net.suspend(now) on FocusLost (iOS applicationWillResignActive, Android APP_CMD_LOST_FOCUS). It sends Away, so the server stops waiting for this player's input and the others do not stall. Call net.resume(now) on FocusGained. After more than 3 s away (the OS has probably killed the socket or the NAT mapping has expired), it reconnects right away instead of waiting for the 10 s silence timeout. The session then fast-forwards within catchUpBudgetMs per frame.

The game client joins a hosted battle from UI Lua with the ticket text its matchmaker returned (ClientTicket::encode(), the server address is inside): local ok, why = game.joinBattle(ticketText, {name = profile.name, compatKey = "1.2.3|protocol:3|map:square"}) game.on("battleFailed", function(e) show_error(e.reason, e.text) end) -- connect, disconnected, compat, error, ... net::joinBattle (engine/net/BattleJoin.h) decodes the ticket, refuses an expired one ("expired") or one issued for another build ("compat": the ticket's compatibility hash against compatKey), connects with connectSecure(ticket) and gives NetClient a reconnect with the same ticket. The match then starts like any network match: when MatchPayload + MatchStart arrive the client checks the payload's compatibility key (battleCompatible), builds the map with applyBattlePayload — a seat's loadout that is a JSON object is merged into players[slot - 1] of the map (for example {"deck": {...}}, progression.md), match-wide gameData that is a JSON object becomes the map's "battle" key — and attaches the simulation. The result reporter sends GameCore::outcomeBlob(). On phones the client calls suspend / resume on focus loss / gain. A failed connect (rejected tickets get no answer: the 10 s connect timeout), a lost battle after the reconnect window or a payload for another build ends the battle, goes back to the menu and emits battleFailed {reason, text}. Web builds return "unsupported" (no UDP). Test: battle_join_by_ticket_payload_and_compat (aiverse_battle_tests). net::ServerConfig cfg; cfg.hostedOnly = true; cfg.udpPort = cfg.wsPort = 0; cfg.onMatchReport = [](const net::MatchReport& r) { /* send to meta */ }; net::Server srv(cfg); srv.listenSecure(27017, serverKey); net::MatchAllocation a; /* matchId, gameId, compatKey, map, seed, players + loadouts, gameData */ srv.allocateMatch(a, &error); for (;;) srv.update(net::nowMs()); MatchPayloadMsg gives every client the same bytes: match id, compatibility key, map id, game data, and each slot's team, kind, name and loadout. These replace Drone Fall's SpawnWanderData startup packets. Build the simulation from them in setup, not through commands. In-match progression (rules progression, progression.md) reads each seat's battle deck (units per slot, unlock flags, initial perks, tech level) from the map's players[i].deck: decode the seat's loadout into that entry when building the match map, so every client builds the same decks. releaseMatch(id) aborts a match. hostedMatches() lists matches. Hosted matches skip the server's Elo, because ratings belong to meta. Lobby rooms, queues, the RTS relay and their protocol are unchanged (kProtocolVersion is still 3). The new messages are additive: Away and ResultReport from the client, MatchPayload from the server.

aiverse_battle keygen > server.key; aiverse_battle keygen > control.key; chmod 600 *.key aiverse_server --udp-port 0 --ws-port 0 --hosted-only --battle-port 27017 --server-key-file server.key \ --control-port 27018 --control-key-file control.key --max-matches 64 --public-address play-eu1.example.com:27017 aiverse_battle control --key-file control.key --address 10.0.0.5:27018 allocate match.json # see BattleControl.h aiverse_battle control --key-file control.key --address 10.0.0.5:27018 status | reports | release 42 aiverse_battle ticket --key-file server.key --match 42 --player u1 --slot 1 --compat "1.2.3|protocol:14|map:square" aiverse_battle ping play-eu1.example.com:27017 Each control line is <hex BLAKE2b-mac> <json>. A request carries ts (within 30 s of the server's clock) and a unique nonce. Responses are signed the same way. The channel carries no secrets, but keep it on a private network or loopback. Capacity is --max-matches, and allocate fails when the server is full. The orchestrator spreads matches over processes and machines using status (capacity, running, clients). It sends each player to the server with the best pings (the pong carries the load). It collects reports and calls release for matches it wants gone. There is no fleet autoscaler or cross-region directory. Both are backend work.

aiverse_battle load --matches 50 --players 2 --seconds 30 --profile bad [--suspend] [--rebind] [--json] This runs one hosted battle server with N HeroDuel matches (apps/battle/HeroDuel.h, a stand-in top-down shooter with heroes, projectiles, dashes and loadouts, speaking the same hero commands), or with --project DIR [--map FILE] [--rules-patch JSON] N matches of an RTS top-down project (apps/battle/RtsBattle.h: GameCore simulations, heroes steered by the computer pilot, ability taps, the frozen outcome blob as the report). Every player is a bot client with its own simulation, connected over the secure transport through the simulated mobile network, all on a virtual clock in one process. It reports finished matches, agreed results, desyncs, rollbacks, how far clients run ahead of confirmation, server update time (p50 / p99 / max), server CPU share and bytes per player. Profiles: lan, wifi, 4g, 3g, bad (20% loss + bursts, 150 ms RTT, 40 ms jitter, 1% duplicates). Override them with --loss, --rtt and --jitter. Measured in the Linux VM (aarch64, gcc Release) with --matches 50 --players 2 --seconds 30 --profile bad: all 50 matches finished, all 50 result reports agreed, 0 desyncs. Clients ran on average 4.5 ticks (max 12, the window) ahead of confirmation. Server update time: p50 0.19 ms, p99 0.34 ms, max 2.2 ms, about 1.9% of one core for 100 players. Traffic per player, packet headers included: about 4.9 KB/s up and 9.3 KB/s down. The whole run took 1.3 s of wall time. Clients and server share one process and the network is simulated: these numbers show what the relay costs. They are not a WAN capacity figure. For the HeroDuel stand-in, most traffic is commands (about one per player per tick, because the bots re-aim constantly) and their redundant copies.

h: Visibility and anti-cheat: what this does and does not do
x: Identity is server-side: slot and player come from the ticket, names come from the allocation, and a ticket is bound to one match, one slot and one compatibility hash. Input is limited: a player can only command its own slots, command types are allowed per match, and commands per tick are capped. Results need every reporting client to agree on the blob, plus the existing checksum desync detection and server arbiter re-simulation (ServerConfig::arbiter) for disputed or abandoned matches. Not solved: lockstep / rollback gives every client the whole simulation state, so map hacks (seeing through fog, enemy loadouts) cannot be prevented by the transport. Interest management needs server-authoritative snapshots, which is the FPS authority path (engine/net/authority), not this one. A PvE match with a single human has nobody to disagree with: run the arbiter on a sample of reports, or on all reports that grant valuable loot. No TLS for the control channel (it is MAC-authenticated only), no key rotation, no DDoS scrubbing, no fleet orchestration service. These belong to deployment. Source on GitHub: docs/battle-net.md

Prefer the theme's colours (ImGui::GetStyle().Colors, ui::accentColor(), ed.theme().palette()) over hard-coded RGB, so both themes stay readable. Icons: Lucide font merged into the UI font, constants in apps/editor/EditorIcons.h (ImGui::Button(ICON_PLAY " Играть")). a window with nothing to show draws ui::emptyStateHere with what to do; results of actions go to a callout in the window (and ed.status for the status bar); quote other windows by their Russian title in «ёлочках» («Сцена», «Консоль»).

If the window adds an action an agent should be able to do, register an operation (in the window's constructor is too early; do it in update() once, or in EditorAgent.cpp): ed.ws().registerOp({"balance_report", "Damage per cost of every unit type.", Json::parse("{}"), [&ed](const Json&) { Json r = Json::object(); /* ... */ return r; }, true}); Operations appear in MCP tools/list for agents connected through aiversemcp (the tool list is the Workspace registry; GUI-only operations have guiOnly = true and fail politely without the editor window).

The Game play-test renders ui/hud.rml and ui/howto.rml through RmlUi into its viewport after the scene. Missing documents, styles and images fall back to engine/assets/ui; game fonts (fonts/ui.ttf, fonts/title.ttf) follow the client. The editor selects the game language with the same saved-choice/system-language rules. Restart the play-test after editing RML, RCSS or fonts to reload them. apps/client/UiModel.h owns the shared game model schema and change-only updates. apps/editor/GameHud adapts the editor simulation to that model: resource/status panels, script HUD cards, support actions and region ratios. Buttons issue Commands; pause/restart/stop operate on the editor play-test. Pointer coordinates are local to the viewport; RmlUi layout and projection use its framebuffer size and device density. World-space region markers remain editor overlays. This is an embedded play-test HUD, not a second GameClient: client lobby/menu flow, UI Lua game APIs, audio playback and the client's full standard RTS command card/minimap are not hosted by the editor adapter. For those use Play as in the client below.

The Game window can also run the game exactly as AiverseGame does: the same GameClient (apps/client/GameClient*.cpp, Client*.cpp; AiverseGame's main.cpp adds only the entry point) hosted by apps/editor/ClientHost and rendered into the window's offscreen target, inside the device simulator frame. Everything is the client's: the game's menus / meta screens (ui/main.lua, ui.screen / ui.popup), launch parameters, battle -> result -> meta flow, view scripts (draw, camera, HUD documents, view.ui_call), script UI, input (rules mapClick tap on release, left-drag pan, wheel zoom, map-drag HUD elements, RmlUi clicks, keys), the pause screen and audio. The editor's own play-test tools (bots vs bots, player pick, speed, pause, stats) stay for the map play-test; the two never run at once. Start: the gamepad button of the Game toolbar, «Как в клиенте» under the empty Game window, the play popup of the top bar, menu Логика → Тест, MCP play_start {"client": true}; F5 and the top-bar Play button start it for games with their own screens (ui/main.lua). Stop / restart in the Game toolbar, F5, play_stop; the game's own Quit stops it too. «В отдельном окне клиента» (external-link button): the project in a separate AiverseGame window (AIVERSE_CONTENT = project), the one built next to this editor first (same C++ modules). The project's C++ modules (rules nativeModules) must be in the editor binary, as for the play-test (the banner offers the per-project editor build). Hosting: while the host calls into the client it sets platform::setHostedView (logical size of the device screen, framebuffer size, scale, safe area of the device preset, touch, content root = project, engine/... -> the engine assets; requestQuit / fullscreen are recorded, the window title is left alone) and restores the editor's ImGui context afterwards (every ImGuiLayer owns its context). Pointer events inside the device screen (or captured by a press inside) and keys while the Game window has focus are mapped into screen points and forwarded. Profiles / saves go to the editor's user data dir (AIVERSE_UI_SAVE_DIR overrides, as in the client). Command line (automated checks): aiverse_editor --project <dir> --play-client --device iphone-se:portrait --window game. Source on GitHub: docs/editor-windows.md

h: TerraWeave — procedural terrain, biomes and vegetation (AIVERSE)
x: Status (2026-11-19): Core + Arbor/Flora, Horizon HLOD, async forest/terrain scene adapters, authored near/far Q16 stitching and Stage 22 diagnostics implemented in source. GPU, editor, integration and performance verification remain pending; see the Draft PR and handoff for exact test status. Implementation: engine/world/TerraWeave.h. Test: tests/terraweave_test.cpp. Handoff: docs/terrain/AGENT_HANDOFF.md.

AIVERSE already has chunked RTS heightfield rendering, editor sculpt/paint operations, MapGrid heightfield simulation, modules/rts/gen/GenNoise.* and water/roads. Do not duplicate or replace these. TerraWeave supplies genre-independent, pure CPU world-generation outputs. Genre adapters consume them without changing legacy project, save, replay or networking contracts. The existing RTS terrain uses map corners in 1/16 map units; TerraWeave uses integer world centimetres. The adapter must explicitly convert units and coordinate handedness/axis orientation, then update dirty chunks through the existing surface API. Never silently cast centimetres into old map units.

Namespace: aiverse::terraweave. heightAtCm(TerrainSettings, worldXcm, worldZcm) -> int32_t: signed terrain elevation in cm. climateAt(TerrainSettings, BiomeSettings, xCm, zCm) -> ClimateSample: temperature, humidity in [0,1000], and one categorical Biome. generateChunk(TerrainSettings, BiomeSettings, ChunkKey, resolution, spacingCm) returns TerrainChunk with (resolution+1)^2 signed heights and biome ids. Coordinates are absolute; adjacent chunk borders are identical. scatter(TerrainSettings, BiomeSettings, ScatterSettings, RectCm worldBounds, vector<FoliageSpecies>, vector<RectCm> exclusions) returns stable sorted row-major foliage instances. Prototype ids are uint32 and unique within the invocation. Candidate selection is anchored to a global lattice; chunk partitioning and prototype order cannot change the result. slopePermilleAt estimates local max-axis slope from signed height differences. TerrainChunkComponent, VegetationPatchComponent are small ECS-ready descriptors; these are not yet registered into an ECS scheduler. FoliageInstance::key is the stable hash of global lattice coordinates and scatter seed. Persist removals/harvests by key and world-generation revision, not by GPU buffer index. Sample (C++20; no renderer or RTS dependency): #include "engine/world/TerraWeave.h" using namespace aiverse::terraweave; TerrainSettings terrain; BiomeSettings climate; auto tile = generateChunk(terrain, climate, {0, 0}, 32, 100); FoliageSpecies oak; oak.id = 1001; oak.biomeMask = biomeBit(Biome::Forest) | biomeBit(Biome::Grassland); auto trees = scatter(terrain, climate, {}, {0, 0, 3200, 3200}, {oak}, {{1000, 1000, 1600, 1600}}); // building exclusion

All phase 1 outputs are integer-only, seeded and independent of call order. No rand(), platform time, global mutable state, or float. Helpers use stable 64-bit mixing and signed floor-division for negative world coordinates. Pure generators can be called concurrently. The host job system schedules them; the ECS main-thread/guarded commit order must remain deterministic. CPU outputs are authoritative; GPU placement or rendering must not affect gameplay RNG or collision. Changes to generator parameters, coordinate transforms or hashing are world-format version changes, requiring migration or explicit revision. Use one ECS entity per terrain/vegetation patch or interactive tree, not per grass blade. Render-only millions of blades belong in instance buffers. Decorative foliage may not have gameplay state. Harvestable foliage must have a stable removal record, replicated and hashed by the game's simulation owner.

Height: 2D multi-octave signed value noise (Q16) in integer centimetres. No erosion, caves, stamps or mesh triangulation yet. Biomes: deterministic temperature/moisture samples with simple threshold classification, including Ocean/Tundra/Desert/Grassland/Forest/Wetland/Alpine. Not yet physical climate simulation or biome blend weights. Scatter: jittered one-candidate-per-world-lattice-cell placement; deterministic density/weighted species selection, biomes, height, slope, world-space rectangular exclusions and scale/yaw variance. It is not exact Bridson Poisson-disk, nor does it currently guarantee separation of full tree crowns. Limits: nonempty region up to 1,000,000 lattice cells per scatter call, max 1024 terrain quads per tile. Do not feed untrusted arbitrary 64-bit coordinates; future validation should enforce a supported world extent. No automatic spawn into ECS, GPU buffers, RHI draws, editor UI, road/water subscriptions, tree meshing, streaming residency, erosion, virtual textures, physics collisions, terrain navmesh updates or season/wind simulation yet. These are future phases, not features of the phase 1 header.

A world config selects TerraWeave seed/settings and an explicit generator version. Visible-world streaming chooses chunk keys; workers call pure generateChunk. An adapter maps centimetres to the existing heightfield MapGrid/editor document or to a generic terrain mesh; changes go through the existing dirty-chunk pipeline, never a second competing terrain renderer. Query roads, buildings, waterways and designer overrides as exclusion/stamp sources before scattering. scatter returns instance descriptors for prototype render groups; only interactable objects become separate ECS entities. All rendering uploads and GPU work go through gfx::Device, using GLSL+MSL parity and quality tiers; no direct graphics backend calls in generation.

cmake -S . -B build/terraweave-test -DAIVERSE_BUILD_TESTS=ON cmake --build build/terraweave-test --target aiverse_terraweave_test -j ctest --test-dir build/terraweave-test --output-on-failure -R '^terraweave$' The test covers adjacent tile edges, negative tile coordinates, stable seed, partition-independent foliage, prototype input reordering, world exclusions, invalid configs and worker-thread purity. When terrain is mapped into the sim, also run the existing full determinism, headless, replay and editor view suites per AGENTS.md.

TerraWeave Terrain: existing heightfield adapters, geomorph LOD, stamps, erosion, SDF/voxel overlays. TerraWeave Biome: climate layers, transition masks, species ecologies. TerraWeave Arbor: procedural trees / parameterized archetypes, branch/crown meshing, LOD and impostors. TerraWeave Flora: species asset registry, batches, GPU placement/culling. TerraWeave Eco: growth, wind, seasons, harvesting and gameplay systems. TerraWeave Stream: bounded streaming residency, chunk jobs and persistence. See the handoff file for exact priorities and integration hazards.

Added engine/world/TerraWeaveArbor.h (integer-authoritative tree skeleton) and engine/world/TerraWeaveArborMesh.h (render-only CPU tessellation). This is independent of any genre, and a native C++ module can include it. #include "engine/world/TerraWeaveArborMesh.h" using namespace aiverse::terraweave; TreeProfile oak; oak.speciesId = 1001; oak.shape = CrownShape::Broadleaf; oak.primaryBranches = 22; const TreeSkeleton skeleton = generateTree(oak, instance.key, TreeLOD::High); const ArborMesh renderGeometry = buildArborMesh(skeleton, {6, true}); // Upload through gfx::Device (not implemented in this stage). TreeProfile defines tree height range, trunk radius, crown start, primary branches, branch reach/rise, leaf-cluster radius and broadleaf/conifer/columnar shape. Tree seed is derived from stable foliage instance key + species ID; the same inputs yield the same integer local-space structure regardless of worker thread or scene partition. TreeLOD High/Medium/Low reduce branch counts and leaf clusters. Impostor returns bounds only; actual billboard atlas baking is not implemented. TreeSkeleton contains a root trunk, child branch segments with parent indices, leaf clusters and conservative height/crown radius bounds. buildArborMesh converts branches to cylindrical bark tubes and clusters to crossed alpha-card quads with UVs, normals and a bark/leaf material discriminator. The returned mesh uses float only for presentation, not gameplay state. Meshes have no tangents or GPU material binding yet. The first visual pass is simple card foliage, not photorealistic SpeedTree-equivalent geometry. The mesh is local-space in centimetres. Instance translation, rotation and scale are supplied by FoliageInstance externally. If gameplay needs tree collision/hitboxes, derive deterministic proxies from TreeSkeleton, not from float render vertices. View LOD selection and GPU uploads must live in a renderer adapter and not in lockstep ECS simulation. Test source: tests/terraweave_arbor_test.cpp. CTest name: terraweave_arbor. Check seeded determinism, all crown archetypes, branch parent validity, LOD topology, independent parallel evaluation, render geometry index validity, and invalid profiles. Compilation/CTest results are tracked in docs/terrain/AGENT_HANDOFF.md.

h: Stage 2b: Flora CPU visibility and instancing prep
x: engine/world/TerraWeaveFlora.h contains a presentation-only draw-list organizer that does not add one ECS entity per grass blade or tree. #include "engine/world/TerraWeaveFlora.h" using namespace aiverse::terraweave; FloraView view; view.cameraXcm = cameraXcm; view.cameraZcm = cameraZcm; auto batches = buildFloraBatches(placements, view); for (const FloraBatch& batch : batches) { // Resolve species prototype + TreeLOD, pack instance transforms. // Upload/submit via gfx::Device in a future renderer adapter. } FloraView selects radial ranges for High/Medium/Low/Impostor mesh tiers, a hard culling radius, and stable seeded far-density thinning. FloraBatch groups copies of FoliageInstance by (speciesId, lod). Ordering is canonical regardless of worker/chunk completion order, and overlapping identical placements are deduplicated within the resulting group. This is draw-list preparation only, not GPU instancing/culling/indirect drawing, frustum/Hi-Z occlusion or crossfade. Screen-space LOD, camera-frustum culling and distance-field shadows remain future stages. Never feed visibility decisions back into authoritative ECS state or network simulation; gameplay placement continues to use scatter. Test source: tests/terraweave_flora_test.cpp; CTest terraweave_flora.

Core generator explicitly supports world positions [-1,000,000,000, +1,000,000,000] centimetres on X/Z. heightAtCm, generateChunk, slopePermilleAt and scatter validate inputs before coordinate multiplication/offset sampling. Chunk keys that would leave this world box are rejected, as are scatter bounds that fall within the 100-cm boundary margin required by slope sampling. This is intended to fail cleanly on malformed/extreme world coordinates, not to impose a practical memory-residency or render-distance budget. Do not remove these guards when introducing a streamed world. Large-world support additionally needs camera-relative rendering, origin rebasing and bounded chunk residency, which are not yet implemented.

engine/render/TerraWeaveModelAdapter.h is a thin render-only adapter into the pre-existing render::Model and its prepareModelUpload / uploadModel(gfx::Device&, Model&) path: #include "engine/render/TerraWeaveModelAdapter.h" auto tree = aiverse::terraweave::makeArborModel(profile, instance.key); // On the render-owning thread: aiverse::render::prepareModelUpload(*tree); aiverse::render::uploadModel(device, *tree); The adapter builds explicit High/Medium/Low mesh variants in a single render::Model, with mesh-0 LOD switches at 128 and 32 projected pixels. It uses standard render::ModelVertex, Primitive, Material, Node and Model::finalize(); positions convert from integer cm to floating-point metres. Existing model renderer infrastructure owns the shaders, LOD fade, frustum culling, backend upload and instanced draws. The default bark and leaf materials have simple untextured PBR colours. Leaf cards are opaque rectangles until a caller binds a real alpha-cutout foliage texture and sets AlphaMode::Mask; do not misrepresent this as production-quality foliage. Billboard atlas generation, material/texture registry, wind deformation and actual scene draw submission remain unfinished. tests/terraweave_model_test.cpp checks three LOD meshes, range/index correctness, bounds, and stable topology. It links aiverse_models; the target aiverse_terraweave_model_test and CTest terraweave_model are registered in CMake. All four TerraWeave test targets explicitly undefine NDEBUG on GCC/Clang so their assertions execute in Release builds. Important: using makeArborModel per individual tree is not the final scalable forest strategy. Generate a bounded catalogue of species/variant prototypes and reuse meshes across instance transforms. buildFloraBatches already groups placement data; the next renderer adapter must submit these groups through existing model instancing.

h: Stage 2f: baking TerraWeave into existing editor MapDoc heightfields
x: engine/world/TerraWeaveHeightmap.h provides a pure generateLegacyCorners(TerrainSettings, widthCells, heightCells, LegacyHeightfieldOptions) adapter. Inputs use centimetres; output is the existing MapData signed-int16 corner format, 1/16 map metre per sample. Coordinates and output ranges are validated; overflow/saturation throws instead of corrupting map heights. Offset/spacing can be configured. apps/editor/core/TerraWeaveMapAdapter.h provides: #include "apps/editor/core/TerraWeaveMapAdapter.h" aiverse::editor::bakeTerraWeaveTerrain( mapDoc, terrainSettings, {0, 0, 100}); // For intentional regeneration replacing authored corner data: aiverse::editor::bakeTerraWeaveTerrain( mapDoc, terrainSettings, {0, 0, 100}, aiverse::editor::TerraWeaveExistingTerrain::ReplaceExplicitly); The editor adapter writes through MapDoc::beginEdit() and MapDoc::touched() after constructing all generated heights, preserving undo and the existing view-revision notification. It never silently overwrites manual sculpting, never changes rules.terrain.model, and rejects planet maps (separate cube-sphere adapter needed). This is one-shot baking API, not yet an editor button, regeneration graph, streaming terrain or painted override stack. Source test: tests/terraweave_heightmap_test.cpp (CTest terraweave_heightmap) verifies signed heights, seam continuity, legacy overflow rejection and invalid inputs. The inline MapDoc helper is not yet exercised end-to-end in a running editor.

h: Stage 2f — shared forest model submission adapter (CPU / RHI bridge)
x: engine/render/TerraWeaveForestAdapter.h exposes aiverse::terraweave::ArborForestAdapter. It bridges deterministic FloraBatch instances to the existing render::Renderer3D::drawModel path. It does not own or replace Renderer3D, ECS, streaming or shaders. addPrototype(TreeProfile, meshSeed, ArborMeshSettings) builds one render::Model per species. Duplicate/zero species IDs are rejected. Changing the tree's mesh on every instance defeats batching; only transform, yaw and scale vary by FoliageInstance. All nodes use existing model projected-size LODs. prototype(speciesId) gives the stable shared model pointer, valid while the adapter lives. uploadModels(gfx::Device&) and releaseModels(gfx::Device&) MUST run on the GPU-owning render thread. Release GPU resources before destroying the device or the adapter. forEachDraw(batches, ForestRenderOriginCm, callback) is a GPU-free inspection/submission primitive, and submit(Renderer3D&, batches, origin) forwards directly to Renderer3D::drawModel. Call submit between beginScene and render, only after model upload. ForestRenderOriginCm is signed world centimetres, with fields x,y,z. For X/Z, subtract origin using int64 BEFORE float metre conversion, to preserve precision in large worlds. Camera and renderer must use the same rebased coordinate frame; model draw transforms are metres. ModelDraw::persistentId is a namespaced stable hash of FoliageInstance::key and species, independent of the draw index. Draw flags are kDrawStatic. An Impostor Flora batch now selects a separate camera-facing alpha-mask tree billboard model (one quad and one procedural RGBA silhouette), not the lowest geometry mesh. This is a single-view silhouette, not a multi-angle atlas. Minimal native / host render integration sketch: #include "engine/render/TerraWeaveForestAdapter.h" using namespace aiverse::terraweave; ArborForestAdapter forest; TreeProfile pine; pine.speciesId = 21; pine.shape = CrownShape::Conifer; forest.addPrototype(pine, 0x5678); // CPU / setup stage forest.uploadModels(device); // render thread, check bool auto batches = buildFloraBatches(placements, view); renderer.beginScene(camera, width, height); forest.submit(renderer, batches, {originXcm, originYcm, originZcm}); // ... other scene draws and renderer.render(pass) forest.releaseModels(device); // render thread at shutdown The adapter does not register with WorldScene or the editor yet. It does not provide per-tree geometry variation, guaranteed indirect draw counts, actual impostors, material cutout textures, scene screenshots, GPU validation, or an opt-in manifest format. Existing projects remain untouched. Validation is added to tests/terraweave_model_test.cpp; see AGENT_HANDOFF.md for observed test results and next task.

The new engine/world/TerraWeaveBranchLod.h and makeArborBranchLodModel(profile, seed, BranchLodSettings) in engine/render/TerraWeaveModelAdapter.h build a reusable native render::Model containing one render node per tree branch. Each node retains TreeBranch::parent and has its own three MeshDef variants. Renderer3D already chooses a node's LOD by its projected size using its existing selectModelLod path, considering camera and shadow views. This allows, e.g., a large near-side trunk to remain fully detailed while individual smaller background branches switch to their cheapest shape. There is no whole-tree mesh switch for these three geometric tiers. Per-branch geometry levels: BranchDetail::Full: full radial bark mesh, local foliage clusters with crossed leaf cards. BranchDetail::Reduced: about half the bark radial segments, one distal local foliage cluster, crossed cards. BranchDetail::Minimal: three bark radial sides, one distal cluster represented by one card plane. BranchLodSettings::reducedPixels (default 96) and minimalPixels (default 30) set independent projected screen-diameter thresholds. The renderer's own LOD fade settings control transition blending. LeafCluster::parentBranch is the original high-detail structural branch index (new metadata). It is used by buildArborBranchMesh(tree, branchIndex, BranchDetail, ArborMeshSettings). No branch is dropped, and tree skeleton generation/gameplay remains deterministic; branch geometry and resolution choices are presentation only.
