A single prototype is shared by all instances of a species; do not create a distinct render::Model for each tree. Tree silhouette geometry still uses the existing opaque leaf material if no project alpha-cutout texture is assigned.

makeArborTreeLodModel(profile, seed, TreeLodSettings) builds the same branch geometry as BranchLOD, but merges every branch of a detail tier into ONE mesh: one node, three MeshDefs (Full -> Reduced -> Minimal via MeshDef::lods), each with exactly two primitives (bark, foliage). All trees of one species share these primitives, so Renderer3D instancing draws a whole species tier with one draw per material (per instance-limit chunk) instead of one draw per branch node. vertexOwners keep the structural branch per vertex, so GPU hierarchical wind masks (docs/wind-masks.md) still bend each branch. The tier comes from Terra's own FloraView distance ranges: ArborForestAdapter sets ModelDraw::lodLevel (High=Full, Medium=Reduced, Low=Minimal; Impostor stays the atlas card). ModelDraw::lodLevel is a general renderer feature: a host-chosen level of every node's LOD chain, skipping projected-size selection. The renderer's projected-size metric is conservative (nearest box corner, divided by w*(w-size)) and kept whole 20 m trees at Full inside the near range. ArborForestAdapter::setTreeGeometry(ArborTreeGeometry, TreeLodSettings) (before the first addPrototype): PerBranch = classic BranchLOD (needed for CPU per-branch wind poses), Merged, or Auto (default): Merged when enableHierarchicalWind() is on, else PerBranch. ForestSceneSettings::treeGeometry / manifest world.terraweaveForest.treeGeometry: "auto" | "merged" | "perBranch". Renderer fixes found on the way (Renderer3DModels.cpp): LOD selection no longer adds the vertex-offset (wind) culling margin to the projected size. With wind on, a 2 m branch plus a multi-metre margin pinned every node at LOD0, so BranchLOD never switched. Rigged trees in calm air declare a 1 cm maxVertexOffsetMetres. Zero means "unbounded displacement" and turned off culling and LOD. Measured in the editor (Mac Release, 192x192 TerraWeave map, 5 botanical species, wind 12 m/s, tools/editor/terra_forest_perf.py, 4 cameras): scene draw calls camera triangles GPU frame PerBranch (with the LOD fix) 6006-6496 366k-504k 2.4-3.3 ms Merged + FloraView tiers 110-177 348k-473k 1.2-2.4 ms PerBranch before the LOD fix: ~3400 draws, every node at LOD0.

h: Far impostors baked from the near tree
x: bakeArborImpostorFromModel(atlas, nearModel) re-bakes the azimuth atlas by CPU rasterization of the near tree itself (every node's base mesh, with the material base-colour textures and alpha cutout), 2x2 supersampled, simple wrap lighting, colour bled into transparent texels against mip halos. Bark and foliage keep separate pages (winter bark-only still works). The card is resized to the mesh's real extent. ArborForestAdapter does this by default right after the prototype decorator (textures) and before GPU upload; setImpostorFromNearModel(false) keeps the legacy skeleton disk/line silhouette. Deterministic: the same model gives the same bytes.

engine/render/TerraWeaveArborBillboard.h provides makeArborBillboardModel(TreeProfile, seed, ArborBillboardSettings). It projects the procedural bark/leaf silhouette to an RGBA8 image (default 128x256), creates a full-tree XY quad, and assigns the image to a standard render::Material with AlphaMode::Mask. Transparent pixels are genuine alpha holes, not a green rectangle; no new GLSL, MSL or custom rendering backend is required. ArborForestAdapter now caches two models per species: a hierarchical near model via prototype(speciesId), and a full-tree far quad via billboardPrototype(speciesId). uploadModels(device) and releaseModels(device) manage both through the engine's existing GPU model uploader. forEachDraw selects the billboard model only for FloraBatch::lod == TreeLOD::Impostor, while near/medium/low batches use the per-branch LOD chain. The far quad's rotation faces the horizontal camera direction; the native submit path reads Renderer3D::cameraPos(). For CPU draw-list tests / custom callers, pass ForestCameraCm to the optional fourth argument of forEachDraw(batches, origin, callback, camera). Billboard and near representations retain the same stable instance ID. The billboard image is intentionally a single-view, deterministic silhouette, not yet a high-quality baked 8/16-view albedo+normal/depth impostor atlas. Near-to-far switching presently follows FloraView distance buckets and has no whole-tree temporal crossfade; the per-branch transitions are handled independently by Renderer3D. The billboard currently disables cast shadows to avoid fake flat shadows. Test screen-space pop, alpha halo/mipmaps and multi-angle visual quality on actual GPUs before claiming production readiness. Tests added but not confirmed executed: tests/terraweave_model_test.cpp now verifies branch counts, parent graph, three independent geometry tiers, index bounds, deterministic mesh and silhouette image, material cutout, transparent/bark/leaf pixels, model switching, camera orientation and stable identity. Isolated CI contains this target. See docs/terrain/AGENT_HANDOFF.md for commands and exact verification status.

h: Stage 3a — editor and MCP integration (opt-in heightfield baking)
x: The legacy RTS TerrainWindow now has a TerraWeave section with seed, average height, relief, noise period and octaves. It exposes two actions using the same Workspace::call operations as agents: terraweave_preview: returns an integer-cm 9×9 height sample grid plus minCm and maxCm; does not edit the map. terraweave_generate: explicitly bakes a full heightfield into the existing MapDoc::corners, creates an undo snapshot, calls MapDoc::touched(), queues a Change::Map invalidation and writes sanitized generator metadata into map.extra.terraweave (version 1). Both operations are registered in apps/editor/core/TerraWeaveOps.h via registerTerrainOps and are reachable through the existing editor/MCP registry. Example: { "seed": 42, "baseHeightCm": 0, "reliefCm": 5000, "basePeriodCm": 6400, "octaves": 5, "originXcm": 0, "originZcm": 0, "cellSizeCm": 100, "overwrite": false } Safety/compatibility: Without explicit overwrite: true, the adapter refuses to replace either an existing corner heightfield or an authored detail surface. With explicit replacement, the previous detail layer (including splat/file/scale) is cleared after recording the undo snapshot so it cannot mask the new corners in the renderer. Planet and FPS maps are rejected by this legacy MapDoc adapter; TerraWeave's generic C++ world generator and ForestAdapter still work independently of genre. The operation does not silently change rules.terrain.model; game authors choose whether corners influence simulation. No project changes occur until the user calls Generate. Limitations: preview is a 9×9 numeric sample, not a live 3D preview. Generation is a one-shot bake, not procedural streaming, a persistent non-destructive graph or a paintable biome editor. The terraweave map block records generator inputs but is not yet automatically re-evaluated on load. Testing: tests/terraweave_ops_test.cpp checks param defaults, bounds rejection, versioned metadata and deterministic preview. The test does not construct a live Workspace or render screenshots; an end-to-end editor/GUI/MCP regression remains mandatory.

engine/render/TerraWeaveImpostorAtlas.h adds ArborImpostorAtlasSettings, ArborImpostorAtlas, makeArborImpostorAtlas(profile, seed, settings) and selectArborImpostorAzimuth(instanceYawMilliDegrees, treeXcm, treeZcm, cameraXcm, cameraZcm, views). The CPU baker uses one deterministic tree skeleton to render 4, 8 (default) or 16 azimuth silhouettes into one RGBA8 horizontal atlas (default 8 × 128 × 256). One render::Model and one atlas image are reused across all trees of a species. Each of the views std::vector<render::Material> overrides references the same baseTex but has a different uvOffset/uvScale with a half-texel inset. Renderer3D already handles those overrides via render::ModelDraw::materials; no new shader or GPU API is added. ArborForestAdapter now caches near BranchLOD geometry, a far atlas model and per-view material overrides per species. billboardAzimuthCount(speciesId) returns the atlas view count. forEachDraw(..., ForestCameraCm) selects the nearest tree-local azimuth (camera world heading minus each instance's own yaw), and submit(renderer, ...) uses the real renderer camera position. Storage for the material override vectors must outlive the frame until Renderer3D::render() returns. The billboard is camera-facing but depicts the corresponding view of the tree, avoiding a fixed flat silhouette during orbit. The older single-view makeArborBillboardModel API remains intact. The new atlas is silhouette/albedo only: no depth, normal or parallax impostor, no interpolation between adjacent views, and no whole-tree temporal alpha transition. The source assertions have been updated for later execution; CMake/CTest and GPU verification have not been run by request.

h: Stage 3c — stable spatial transition to impostor
x: FloraView::impostorBlendWidthCm (default 0, preserving legacy hard-ring selection) spreads the TreeLOD::Low → TreeLOD::Impostor threshold over a bounded interval around FloraView::lowRangeCm. Each FoliageInstance selects a stable threshold based on its persistent key and species ID. The same tree does not flicker when camera position changes within the band, and all trees no longer swap on one circular boundary. The interval is validated to stay between mediumRangeCm and cullRangeCm. Example: view.lowRangeCm = 18000; view.impostorBlendWidthCm = 4000; distributes transitions over 160–200 metres. Because thresholds are stable, this is population dithering, not a true per-object temporal or alpha crossfade. No additional draw calls or extra transparent meshes are required. tests/terraweave_flora_test.cpp has deferred assertions; test execution is intentionally postponed.

h: Stage 3d — opt-in streaming forest host and WorldScene manifest
x: engine/world/TerraWeaveForestScene.h introduces the reusable, genre-independent native C++ TerraWeaveForestScene and ForestSceneSettings. The scene owns: per-species shared near BranchLOD and far impostor atlas prototypes through ArborForestAdapter; integer-centimetre, globally keyed foliage placements and stable IDs; an explicitly bounded maxResidentChunks patch cache; streamAt(ForestCameraCm): generate nearest resident chunks and release patches outside the current budget/radius; setExclusions(vector<RectCm>): regenerate for road/building/clearing rectangles, with cache revision invalidation; visibleBatches(): per-view Flora LOD/culling, including staggered impostor transition; uploadModels(gfx::Device&), submit(Renderer3D&, ForestRenderOriginCm) and releaseModels(gfx::Device&) for the existing RHI lifecycle; stats(): number of resident chunks, placements, prototypes and generation revision (not actual GPU draw counters). Native projects can instantiate it independently of an RTS/FPS module. addSpecies(TreeProfile, FoliageSpecies, prototypeSeed) must be called before streaming/upload. streamAt is currently synchronous CPU generation, bounded by the cache limits and current scatter settings. Do not invoke it concurrently with submit, setExclusions or releaseModels. Worker-stage streaming, cancellation and generation revision commit validation are future work. engine/world/TerraWeaveForestManifest.h implements an optional JSON adapter, world::forestSceneFromManifest, and WorldScene owns/updates/submits/shuts down the forest only when terraweaveForest exists at manifest root. No existing WorldScene manifest without this key is changed. The opt-in host uses the first observer from WorldScene::update; it does not currently union multiple observer budgets. Example root manifest fragment (all coordinates in cm inside the terraweaveForest object; existing world mesh/camera coordinates outside this block still use WorldScene's normal metre units): { "terraweaveForest": { "terrainSeed": 42, "biomeSeed": 143, "scatterSeed": 55, "baseHeightCm": 0, "reliefCm": 6000, "basePeriodCm": 6400, "octaves": 5, "spacingCm": 450, "densityPermille": 650, "chunkSizeCm": 6400, "radiusChunks": 4, "maxResidentChunks": 64, "highRangeCm": 3000, "mediumRangeCm": 9000, "lowRangeCm": 12000, "cullRangeCm": 24000, "impostorBlendWidthCm": 3000, "species": [ { "id": 1, "shape": "broadleaf", "minHeightCm": 900, "maxHeightCm": 1400, "branches": 24, "weight": 4, "prototypeSeed": 1001 }, { "id": 2, "shape": "conifer", "minHeightCm": 1100, "maxHeightCm": 2100, "branches": 32, "weight": 2, "prototypeSeed": 2002 } ], "exclusions": [[0, 0, 1200, 1500]] } } The fragment is added to an otherwise valid existing WorldScene root manifest with async, assets, and chunks populated according to docs/large-worlds.md. No new world format is implied for legacy RTS MapDoc maps; their editor generator is in TerraWeaveOps.h and separate. The forest here is render-only: it does not create authoritative colliders, navmesh obstacles, harvested resource entities or changed RTS/FPS simulation checksums. Terrain heights derive from the TerraWeave procedural seed; until a heightmap provider adapter is implemented, they may not match an independently authored terrain surface. WorldScene releases the forest's models through its existing shutdown(device) path. GPU upload is on the same update thread as the other world-model uploads. Status: code committed but no local compiler, CTest, real WorldScene launch or GPU screenshot executed, in accordance with the request to defer tests. Do not treat this as a production-ready asynchronous forest streaming subsystem. Future work: worker jobs with revision checks, explicit camera/observer streaming priorities, sampled-world-terrain alignment, collision/navmesh, editor scene preview and GPU resource/performance validation.

h: Stage 4 — opt-in forest Scene overlay and authored-map exclusions
x: Scene integration: apps/editor/TerraWeaveForestPreview.h owns a persistent ArborForestAdapter. The existing Editor::renderScene calls it after the normal terrain/objects draw but before Renderer3D::render (no extra render pass). TerrainWindow has a checkbox to show the generated forest; it is off by default, and enabled only when MapDoc::extra.terraweave.version == 1. The Game window and simulation remain unchanged. Preview generates a bounded 5×5 window of 32-metre source tiles around the camera; placements are global-lattice deterministic even across tile boundaries. They are regenerated when the active camera tile, MapDoc revision or saved TerraWeave recipe changes. Two procedural tree species are preconfigured (broadleaf + conifer) and generated only once per editor preview lifetime; both geometry and multi-view impostors are shared via ArborForestAdapter. The renderer chooses actual per-branch LOD and reuses existing GPU instancing/batching/shadows. Coordinate space: procedural scatter uses absolute world cm (e.g. optional generator originXcm), but the editor/renderer uses map-relative metres. The overlay subtracts the recipe origin BEFORE building draw transforms and samples the current editor heightfield so subsequent sculpt/undo operations move tree roots with the terrain. It changes no map data or gameplay entities. Authored map exclusions: apps/editor/TerraWeavePlacementMask.h rejects placements on water/rock/block/road map cells, within a configurable rectangular clearance around MapData::entities, and within a segment-distance clearance around legacy MapData::roads. Mask is presentation-only: long-double distance arithmetic is allowed here but must not be used for authoritative network/lockstep placement. It currently does NOT parse roadNetwork splines, building footprints, waterNetwork, or the dynamic collider/navmesh world; those need real provider adapters. Resource lifecycle: an explicit unchecked preview releases GPU tree prototypes through the existing RHI. Project/map changes or editor shutdown release preview resources. Browser/mobile runtime and production world streaming are not part of this editor-only feature. Testing: tests/terraweave_preview_test.cpp smoke-compiles the preview header, checks opt-in toggle and authored placement masks. The isolated GCC/Clang workflow also builds terraweave_preview. No evidence of a passing editor build, renderer screenshot or measured GPU performance exists at this stage; maintain PR #24 as Draft.

h: Stage 5 — authored terrain and placement providers for generic forests
x: engine/world/TerraWeaveForestScene.h now supports two optional host callbacks, independent of RTS, FPS and the actual terrain storage: TerraWeaveForestScene forest(settings); forest.addSpecies(profile, species, prototypeSeed); // A snapshot from a project/engine physics terrain provider, integer cm: forest.setHeightSource([&surface](int64_t xCm, int64_t zCm) -> int32_t { return surface.heightAtCm(xCm, zCm); }); // Exclusion/footprint/water provider; evaluated after height sampling: forest.setPlacementFilter([&surface](const FoliageInstance& tree) -> bool { return surface.allowTree(tree.xCm, tree.zCm, tree.heightCm); }); forest.streamAt({cameraXcm, cameraZcm}); Providers are invoked only during streamAt() on the owning CPU work phase. Any replacement automatically invalidates resident patches and increments the host revision. The deterministic placement IDs do not change when elevation or filtering changes; only final heightCm and presence can change. An invalid returned height outside the supported forest world extent throws before GPU submission. Important: callbacks must read an immutable terrain/collision snapshot for the duration of a regeneration. Do not capture mutable ECS data and race it against asynchronous workers. The current host is still synchronous, and these callbacks are presentation-only. They do not change the biome/slope evaluation in the underlying scatter(): if a project has independently authored very steep or underwater terrain, its PlacementFilter must reject unsuitable candidates. A later core API can support complete terrain-surface sampling for both selection and final height. Tests: tests/terraweave_forest_scene_test.cpp and CTest target terraweave_forest_scene (height override, stable keys, filter, revision invalidation, invalid height). Tests have been authored, but are not claimed to have executed.

h: Stage 6 — actual WorldScene terrain heights and footprint placement
x: The opt-in WorldScene path now uses a typed, immutable bridge from loaded world::ChunkCollision::terrain to TerraWeave forest placement. engine/world/TerraWeaveWorldHeightSource.h contains AuthoredHeightTileCm and AuthoredWorldHeightSnapshot. The snapshot's sample(worldXcm, worldZcm) returns an optional signed centimetre elevation from loaded terrain tiles. It uses WorldAssets::cellSize and negative-safe global floor division, then piecewise triangular interpolation matching the exact readChunkCollision triangles (a,c,b) / (a,d,c), not bilinear smoothing across the diagonal. Source height samples are converted from world::Fixed metres to integer centimetres at the worker preparation boundary. The difference from the underlying Fixed collision surface is at most centimetre-scale sampling/rounding, and the operation is presentation-only. WorldScene::Prepared caches authored height samples and collision box footprints only when terraweaveForest was explicitly enabled. On terrain/footprint-bearing chunk publish or unload, WorldScene::update assembles one immutable snapshot from all resident tiles, plus an exclusion mask from resident collision-box X/Z footprints. It calls the new TerraWeaveForestScene::setLandscapeSources(heightSource, mask) exactly once per update: one generation revision invalidation, with old snapshots safely held by any in-flight asynchronous work. The forest's own revision-safe async publisher discards stale results. For areas with no currently loaded authored height tile, the adapter falls back to TerraWeave's configured deterministic heightAtCm. This can create a seam between authored and procedural terrain when loading/unloading tiles; it is not a full world terrain replacement or a solution for arbitrary physics triangle meshes. The footprint mask conservatively excludes the X/Z projections of all resident collision boxes, regardless of altitude. WorldSpace kWorldLimitCm checks and explicit chunk CPU reservation accounting remain in effect. Legacy scenes without terraweaveForest keep the original code path and do not allocate these snapshots. FoliageExclusionMask now buckets building rectangles into 64 m spatial buckets for per-candidate checks. Large rectangles (>256 buckets) use a bounded per-shape overflow path rather than being duplicated across tens of thousands of buckets. Road and polygon queries preserve their prior behaviour.

h: Stage 6b — stable removal/restore state for interactive trees
x: TerraWeaveForestScene also exposes ForestTreeIdentity {key, speciesId} and removeTree(id), restoreTree(id), setRemovedTrees(vector<ForestTreeIdentity>), and removedTrees(). It tracks a bounded sorted set of identities (up to 1,000,000) separately from deterministic scatter outputs. visibleBatches() excludes removed trees immediately; residency eviction/regeneration does not resurrect them. ForestSceneStats adds removed. This allows a native game to serialize stable tree removal state with its own save format or map an interactive tree to a gameplay ECS entity without allocating ECS entities for all decorative foliage. The removed-tree identity is meaningful only under the matching generator seed/version/species configuration. The host still owns actual game save/load, authoritative harvesting, inventory, network replication and collision/navmesh updates. This visual filter alone does not implement those gameplay systems. Verification: this stage was committed through the repository connector; source inspection only. Builds, CTest, live GPU launch and screenshots remain explicitly not run, per user request.

h: TerraWeave Horizon — kilometre-scale landscape and forest HLOD
x: engine/world/TerraWeaveHorizon.h generates a coarse forest landscape snapshot without expanding distant trees to individual objects. engine/render/TerraWeaveHorizonModel.h packs the entire snapshot into one standard AIVERSE render::Model with two materials/primitives: (1) a very low resolution far-terrain heightfield, with biome vertex colours and slope normals, and (2) hundreds of cluster-level crossed billboards sharing one RGBA8 silhouette atlas. Renderer3D therefore does not submit one draw per tree, nor one draw per 128/512-metre forest cluster. Shadow casting is disabled on far impostors. Unlike near tree LODs, the cluster silhouettes are generated directly from low-frequency climate/heightfield samples; individual trees are never generated at this tier. This makes the cost bounded by the terrain grid and number of cluster tiles, not the number of simulated or visually implied trees.

Approximate distance Representation 0–250 m Existing detailed trees and per-tree impostors (ForestScene) 250–1,000 m 128-metre cluster silhouettes 1–6 km (roughly 8 km at diagonal) 512-metre cluster silhouettes Beyond 1,100 m terrain One 48×48-quad geometry patch with a near cutout The ranges are adjustable through HorizonSettings. The nearest range is coordinated with ForestSceneSettings.view.cullRangeCm (default 240 m) to avoid duplicate detailed trees. The single large proxy is not a substitute for collision, walkable ground, pathfinding, close-up rocks or detailed tree meshes.

h: Approximate upper bounds, not measured GPU performance
x: Default estimateHorizonBudget(HorizonSettings{}): 832 possible forest cluster slots in total (16×16 middle + 24×24 distant). One 1392×1392 RGBA8 texture, 7,750,656 bytes before mipmaps. At most 9,253 vertices and 8,320 triangles (including outer skirts and two crossed quads per forest cluster; many clusters skipped in sparse biomes). One Model with at most two material primitives. Actual main-pass draw count varies by renderer/backends/visibility; shadows, reflections, render passes and hardware have not been benchmarked. This is much cheaper geometrically than distant individual foliage but not literally free: alpha overdraw, one-time CPU bake, texture upload, memory and shadow/atmospheric composition still cost resources.

{ "terraweaveHorizon": { "terrainSeed": 1, "biomeSeed": 2, "middleTileCm": 12800, "middleTilesPerSide": 16, "distantTileCm": 51200, "distantTilesPerSide": 24, "closeForestEndCm": 25000, "middleForestEndCm": 100000, "terrainBeginCm": 110000, "terrainSkirtDepthCm": 1200, "terrainResolution": 48, "atlasTilePixels": 48, "canopyHeightCm": 1800, "distantTerrain": true } } No terraweaveHorizon block means no additional memory, GPU work or change to the existing world. If terraweaveForest is also in the manifest, Horizon inherits the near forest's terrain/biome seeds unless explicitly overridden. Use matching seeds and elevation conventions to avoid near/far colour and silhouette mismatches. distantTerrain: false draws only cluster forests, useful when an existing world terrain renderer already covers far ground. engine/render/TerraWeaveHorizonScene.h reuses AsyncChunkStream: one queued/cancelable CPU region bake, bounded staging memory, stale region rejection, render-thread RHI upload. The previous uploaded proxy remains visible until the new region is fully published. Region position snaps to a 128m camera grid so no atlas is regenerated every frame. WorldScene::update/draw/shutdown owns this automatically for an opted-in manifest.

Cluster textures are procedural silhouette/colour approximations, not full multiview photographic or normal/depth-accurate atlases. Two crossed ribbons are a cheap all-azimuth fallback; a future offline baker should capture real forest materials and directional lighting, with atlas paging and mips/alpha coverage preservation. Mid-to-far transitions use distance ranges but not yet full alpha/dither crossfade. First GPU visual proof is required to identify popping and vegetation/ground colour discrepancies. Far terrain is a coarse mesh with a central hole (to avoid z-fight with nearby authored geometry), not a depth-aware mountain panorama. It must be disabled or coordinated with independently authored far-terrain patches to prevent overlap/double rendering. Rebuilding the atlas when the camera crosses a 128m cell runs on the existing background worker but is still CPU work; pack/cache prebaked assets for entirely static game worlds and profile the upload latency. The renderer and WorldScene still need screenshots and actual GPU measurements. Tests added: tests/terraweave_horizon_test.cpp (aiverse_terraweave_horizon_test, CTest terraweave_horizon). Tests cover deterministic baking, atlas contents, card/terrain mesh bounds, topology and budget, invalid settings, and constructing the async host without an initialized GPU. Tests are authored but not confirmed passing. See docs/terrain/AGENT_HANDOFF.md.

h: Stage 8 — layered cluster crowns, stable transition bands and atlas quality tiers
x: TerraWeaveHorizon.h now rasterizes a cluster as a deterministic overlapping canopy instead of a row of vertical green strips. Each texture tile contains hashed broadleaf ellipses, occasional tapered conifer crowns, variable heights/colours, gentle alpha-test edge coverage and sparse exposed trunks. This is intentionally a stylized procedural approximation of a forest silhouette, not a render of real 3D foliage assets. The GPU still sees the same two crossed cluster cards and one shared atlas. HorizonSettings has these optional quality and LOD properties: C++ / JSON field Default Purpose crownDetail 2 1–3: CPU-only canopy silhouette complexity; no extra GPU cards orientationViews 1 1: use the same atlas frame for both crossed cards; 2: bake separate X/Z projections nearBlendCm 6000 (60m) Spread spatial HLOD entrance into the final 60m of detailed forest tierBlendCm 16000 (160m) Stagger 128m→512m cluster coverage around the 1km boundary The band logic uses deterministic spatial stochastic alpha masking. A cluster's canopy coverage ramps in/out through hashed pixel thresholds based on distance to the snapped bake camera. The near-to-mid layer starts partially visible before individual trees stop, and mid/far clusters overlap at reduced coverage rather than switching all cards at once. This has no additional per-cluster draw calls or new GL/Metal shader. It is not a continuous per-frame alpha crossfade: the atlas is still recomputed only when the background Horizon region is updated. Camera movement across a region boundary may cause residual small pops; only actual orbit/zoom screenshot tests can establish perceived continuity. When both opt-in terraweaveForest and terraweaveHorizon blocks exist, the default closeForestEndCm is inherited from the detailed forest's FloraView::cullRangeCm unless explicitly overridden. This avoids the former 240m vs 250m gap in the default near/far ownership. If Horizon is used alone, it retains its 250m close boundary. Existing scenes with no Horizon block do not change. orientationViews=2 stores independent azimuth-orthogonal projections of each cluster and uses a different UV subrectangle for the corresponding crossed card. It still uses one shared image and one model with two primitives, exactly the same card geometry and draw submission topology. High-quality mode costs more atlas memory/CPU bake work, but not more triangles. orientationViews=1 remains the mobile/low-memory default. Approximate maximum atlas bytes, before mipmaps and image staging: 1 view: 1392×1392 RGBA8 = 7,750,656 bytes (~7.39 MiB). 2 views: 1968×1968 RGBA8 = 15,492,096 bytes (~14.77 MiB). estimateHorizonBudget validates both options within the 16 MiB packed-atlas cap. For real performance use TerraWeaveHorizonScene::runtimeStats() (cluster count, uploaded atlas bytes, vertices, triangles, CPU preparation milliseconds, render-thread upload milliseconds, pending/canceled async tasks). These are measurements captured by the running host only once a scene is actually executed, not benchmark results supplied by this document. Example opt-in quality settings within terraweaveHorizon: { "crownDetail": 3, "orientationViews": 2, "nearBlendCm": 6000, "tierBlendCm": 16000 } Tradeoffs / unverified: The spatial mask can create gaps or partially doubled canopy in its overlap bands; better complementary per-pixel fade and material-driven frame transitions require GPU screenshots, alpha coverage testing and perhaps a dedicated shader pass. Differing near forest density, custom species, authored roads and nonprocedural landscape still need production integration. The CPU image baker runs on existing background work threads and the atlas memory cap is an analytic bound. Neither GPU timings nor frame stability nor image quality has been verified on Metal, Vulkan or GLES in this stage.

h: Stage 9a — authored landscape inputs for Horizon
x: bakeHorizon(..., const HorizonSurfaceSources* source = nullptr) now accepts optional immutable host-provided functions: heightAtCm(x,z), biomeAt(x,z) and allowsCanopyAt(x,z). The old overload remains source-compatible and uses procedural TerraWeave noise whenever a callback is absent. This resolves the previous pure-noise-only limitation at the CPU bake boundary: independently authored worlds can supply their heightfield tiles, biome masks and road/shore/structure clearings. A disallowed canopy sample is skipped before rasterization; it does not require another draw call or an individual-tree entity. Both forest/terrain vertex colours and their heights sample the same source snapshot, so distant ground can be made consistent with nearby collision/terrain. The input pointer is borrowed during a single bake; asynchronous hosts must hold a shared_ptr<const HorizonSurfaceSources> or equivalent immutable snapshot while worker jobs are running. Do not capture mutable ECS world objects in worker callbacks. Callback source values and GPU visual agreement have not been verified by tests or screenshots in this stage.

TerraWeaveHorizonScene::setSurfaceSources( std::shared_ptr<const HorizonSurfaceSources>) accepts an immutable sampling snapshot from the owner thread. Internally the worker copies the shared pointer before invoking bakeHorizon. Replacing a snapshot cancels the selected asynchronous cell and queues a new revision on the next update(); the last successfully uploaded model remains available until a replacement succeeds. WorldScene now populates authored AuthoredWorldHeightSnapshot and FoliageExclusionMask whenever either an opt-in near forest or an opt-in Horizon renderer is active. It supplies resident height tiles to the far-terrain sampler and uses resident collision-box footprints to clear canopy. It does not modify source collision, gameplay ECS or deterministic placement IDs. Unloaded terrain tiles fall back to the Horizon procedural height seed; this is not yet a guarantee of seamless authored terrain beyond the resident world. Do not call setSurfaceSources once per frame: it invalidates the current pending region and would cause repeated CPU bakes. Only publish an updated snapshot when the underlying authored terrain/obstacle residency changes, as WorldScene currently does.

HorizonSettings::maxCachedRegions (default 2, range 0–4) enables a bounded CPU-side LRU cache of immutable baked Horizon regions. Re-entering a recently visited camera region reuses its already rasterized forest/terrain snapshot, while a new GPU model is still uploaded through the existing Renderer3D RHI path. This saves CPU canopy baking, not GPU upload work. 0 disables retention for constrained devices. A new authored landscape setSurfaceSources() revision invalidates cached regions and cancels the current pending publication. Old worker snapshots continue to exist only as long as jobs need them. HorizonSettings::regionHysteresisCm (default 3200 cm) holds the selected 128-metre camera cell until the observer moves a further 32 metres past its previous boundary, reducing repeated streaming near grid edges. It must be less than half the middleTileCm cell side. Both fields are configurable through terraweaveHorizon JSON. TerraWeaveHorizonScene::runtimeStats() now returns cachedRegions and cacheHits in addition to previous CPU/GPU/geometry stats. The default cache can retain two packed RGBA atlases in addition to the current render model, so memory grows predictably; cache capacity is not a hard ceiling for all temporary worker/upload staging allocations. No disk cache or runtime skip-GPU-upload was implemented by this stage. Benchmarks and cache-key/invalidation/camera-boundary tests are explicitly delegated to a separate test agent.

Native C++ projects can call horizonSettingsForQuality(HorizonQualityPreset::Minimal|Mobile|Balanced|High) to receive validated, genre-independent Horizon settings. The opt-in WorldScene terraweaveHorizon block accepts "quality": "minimal" | "mobile" | "balanced" | "high" (default balanced); individual JSON fields override the preset without another rendering path or a shader fork. Preset Atlas tile Terrain grid Crown detail Atlas views CPU regions cached minimal 16 px 16×16 1 1 0 mobile 24 px 24×24 1 1 0 balanced 48 px 48×48 2 1 2 high 48 px 64×64 3 2 2 The same ~832 potential cluster slots apply; the atlas resolution changes rather than the number of forest cluster cards. Minimal and mobile deliberately avoid retaining additional CPU atlases. The two-view high preset increases the texture budget to about 14.77 MiB before mipmaps, requiring real-device profiling before being a recommended default. These are intended presets, not measured FPS or validated platform quality settings.

Static worlds may avoid the expensive canopy rasterization across game restarts by preparing a region offline and shipping a .twh asset. engine/world/TerraWeaveHorizonArchive.h provides pure portable C++20 APIs (no filesystem, OS or rendering dependencies): const uint64_t fingerprint = terraweave::horizonArchiveFingerprint(terrain, biomes, settings); auto bake = terraweave::bakeHorizon(terrain, biomes, settings, regionCenterXcm, regionCenterZcm); std::vector<uint8_t> bytes = terraweave::encodeHorizonArchive(bake, fingerprint); // The game/editor build tool writes bytes into its own asset pack. // At runtime, given the *same* settings and matching world content: terraweave::HorizonBake decoded = terraweave::decodeHorizonArchive(bytes, fingerprint); Archive wire format is currently versioned TWH3, explicit little-endian integer fields, packed RGBA atlas, terrain vertices and cluster metadata, with a 64-bit FNV payload checksum and 20 MiB maximum serialized size. It is intended for trusted application assets; the checksum is not cryptographic authentication. Decoder checks version, fingerprint, sizes, atlas frame bounds, payload integrity and trailing bytes before returning any bake. TerraWeaveHorizonScene::setArchiveStore(...) accepts an optional shared HorizonArchiveStore with read and/or write callbacks and an optional stable authoredContentHash. Configure it before the first update(), because callbacks are then invoked by the bounded worker. The worker checks the in-memory LRU first, then a prebaked archive, then falls back to a fresh procedural bake. Failed/corrupt/stale archive reads and write failures are best-effort cache misses, not fatal. The runtime keeps only one uploaded Horizon GPU model, regardless of how many CPU archives are available. runtimeStats().archiveHits counts successful archive restores. For WorldScene game manifests, optionally add: { "terraweaveHorizon": { "quality": "balanced", "archivePrefix": "world/horizon-cache" } } It looks for world/horizon-cache/<cellX>_<cellZ>.twh, where X/Z are signed middle-Horizon camera-grid keys, through the normal game AssetReader. No configured prefix means no asset lookups. The WorldScene adapter is read-only; the build pipeline is responsible for producing and packing the blobs. Important for authored terrain/roads: if the async Horizon has an external HorizonSurfaceSources snapshot, disk archive reuse is disabled unless the caller provides a nonzero stable content fingerprint via HorizonArchiveStore::authoredContentHash (or manifest archiveContentHash). That value must change whenever surface heights, biome paints, road/water/structure masks or other region-affecting authored data change. This avoids silently loading a stale canopy/terrain snapshot. Without an external authored source, a zero hash denotes a purely procedural world and archive lookup remains available. Verification explicitly delegated: portability (AppleClang/Clang/GCC/MSVC), archive round-trip, corrupt/truncated bytes, stale fingerprints, missing pack asset fallback, alpha atlas GPU upload and races with source invalidation. The authoring agent has NOT built or run tests for this code.

h: Stage 10 — bulk asset baking and selective Horizon regeneration

x: The reusable engine/world/TerraWeaveHorizonBatch.h declares HorizonBatchBounds, HorizonBatchOptions, HorizonBatchStorage (game-supplied read/write/cancel callbacks), HorizonBatchProgress and bakeHorizonBatch(...). It generates deterministic signed camera region keys in z-major, x-minor order, using the same grid and fingerprints as runtime HorizonScene. Up to 4,096 regions are allowed by default. Existing valid TWH2 archives are skipped; wrong settings/version/CRC/missing assets are regenerated. The tool never accesses the GPU or authoritative ECS. aiverse_horizon_bake is a host-only CMake target built with AIVERSE_BUILD_TOOLS=ON, disabled for Emscripten. Example: aiverse_horizon_bake \ --manifest content/world.json \ --out content/world/horizon-cache \ --cells -4 -4 4 4 Each region produces <x>_<z>.twh in that output folder. Pack the files as normal content and configure the same terraweaveHorizon.archivePrefix in the runtime manifest. --force bypasses skip-existing; --max-regions N limits work. The executable builds procedural Horizon surfaces only. Projects with authored collisions/roads/water instead use bakeHorizonBatch directly with their immutable HorizonSurfaceSources snapshot and a nonzero authoredContentHash.

h: Stable atlas slots and partial CPU updates
x: Before partial regeneration each cluster receives a stable atlas slot independent of visible cluster count: (layerBase + row*rowCount + col) * orientationViews. Changes to road/shore mask, terrain height or biome in one region do not move unrelated cluster UV subrectangles. This atlas-layout change advanced the archive format to TWH2/version 2; previous TWH1 blobs must be regenerated. bakeHorizon(..., source, previous, editedRegions) can reuse an immutable previous HorizonBake when its snapped camera, atlas dimensions, terrain grid and region origin match and editedRegions is nonempty. It copies the previous atlas, reuses unchanged cluster records and their pixels, clears only affected stable atlas tiles, redraws affected canopy pixels, and recalculates only edited terrain vertices. A conservative cluster-width margin captures affected neighbouring canopy/slope samples. Incompatible previous bakes or empty change bounds perform a full bake. TerraWeaveHorizonScene::setSurfaceSources(source, editedRegions) now captures old CPU bake and an immutable source generation snapshot for the background job. The GPU model remains visible during regeneration. Regions not intersecting the currently displayed Horizon footprint do not need an immediate rebake. On mobile/minimal configurations with maxCachedRegions=0, the full-regeneration path avoids retaining an extra CPU Horizon bake. Authored source changes bypass stale static archives rather than silently restoring old foliage. WorldScene::update records touched loaded/unloaded authored height/obstacle cells as world-centimetre RectCm bounds and passes them only to the Horizon snapshot adapter. The near forest maintains its separate revision-safe streaming model; no gameplay collision, navmesh or ECS entities are modified. Scope limit: partial updates reduce CPU atlas rasterization but still rebuild and upload the combined GPU model/atlas. There is no partial GPU texture update and no dynamic material-driven temporal crossfade in this stage. Both require actual backend quality/performance validation. Verification: These are implemented source APIs only. The separate testing agent is responsible for builds, CTest, archive round trips, moving-camera snapshots, memory and GPU captures. None were executed by the feature agent.

h: Stage 11b — incremental GPU atlas subregion uploads
x: Horizon can now skip replacing an entire GPU render::Model for atlas-only changes that preserve every terrain vertex (including colour), camera-clipped near terrain topology, forest cluster positions, heights, sizes and UV slots. This is a conservative optimization, not a new shading backend: engine/render/TerraWeaveHorizonGpuPatch.h: horizonCanReuseModelGeometry(oldBake,newBake), planHorizonAtlasUpload(oldBake,newBake,atlasTilePixels), applyHorizonAtlasUpload(gfx::Device&,Model&,newBake,plan). The pure CPU planner identifies changed fixed atlas slots, coalesces horizontally adjacent/vertically equal runs, and defaults to at most six rectangle updates totalling at most 25% of the current atlas RGBA bytes. Larger updates, invalid resident atlas textures or any changed geometry use the existing full uploadModel path. On the GPU owner thread, gfx::Device::updateTexture updates RGBA8 subregions. The engine's existing GL/Metal/ Vulkan implementations regenerate mipmaps as required. No new graphics backend calls or per-tree draw calls. TerraWeaveHorizonScene::runtimeStats() exposes atlasPatchCount, atlasPatchBytes, atlasPatchRegions and fullUploadCount. The counters are meaningful only when an actual scene runs; no frame-rate claims have been made. Only atlas pixels are patched; changes to cluster count, geometry, base colour, far terrain vertices or authored heightfield force a full model swap. This stage does not provide partial GPU vertex buffers, continuous per-frame crossfade, or eliminate the CPU worker's model preparation. The user assigned validation to another agent: test partial uploads including mips/row-pitch on Metal, GL, Vulkan and real mobile/desktop workloads before marking production-ready.

h: Stage 12 — GPU terrain vertex subrange updates (geometry-safe)
x: Horizon may now commit small terrain height/normal/vertex-colour edits directly into the existing GPU vertex buffer, instead of reuploading an entire distant forest/terrain Model. This uses the same cross-genre RHI: render::Model::batching.allowGeometryPool is a generic bool, default true. TerraWeaveHorizonModel sets it to false to guarantee a dedicated GPU vertex/index allocation. Never blindly call updateBuffer with model-relative offsets when model.geometryPoolPage is present: the pooled VB can contain several unrelated models with nonzero base offsets. TerraWeaveHorizonGpuPatch.h has horizonCanReuseHorizonLayout(): preserves source camera region, terrain X/Z positions, atlas footprint, all cluster crosscard/UV geometry and index topology while allowing changes in terrain height/colour/normal. TerraWeaveHorizonVertexPatch.h exports the pure CPU planHorizonVertexUpload(), and owner-thread horizonCanApplyVertexUpload() / applyHorizonVertexUpload(). Planning requires exact unchanged index data, node and primitive topology, unchanged crossed-card vertex bytes, and new computed model/primitive bounds contained in the resident conservative bounds. Other changes trigger the existing full RHI model upload. The default vertex patch budget is at most 20 contiguous ranges and 35% of terrain vertices. A successful patch issues gfx::Device::updateBuffer on the same owning thread that publishes the CPU forest atlas and renders models; changed atlas tiles can be patched in the same publication. The previous CPU ModelVertex and index snapshots are captured after prepareModelUpload, before uploadModel discards its CPU arrays. They are retained only with an enabled Horizon CPU cache (maxCachedRegions>0). This avoids keeping an extra 7–15 MiB atlas CPU copy inside the resident GPU Model. Minimal and mobile presets keep full-upload fallback to minimize memory. HorizonRuntimeStats adds vertexPatchCount, vertexPatchBytes, and vertexPatchRanges alongside atlas patch/full upload counters. Important safety limits: gfx::Device::updateBuffer is a void/nontransactional device API; a backend or GPU device loss cannot provide a partial-patch success guarantee. All geometry/data/range validation happens before issuing GPU writes, but true rollback requires general RHI device-loss recovery. Renderer culling bound expansion is deliberately NOT part of this optimization; edits that would grow any draw bounds use the full upload. This is a correctness-first fast path. GPU/device/CTest testing is owned by another agent and has not been executed in this development stage.

h: Stage 13 — bounded GPU residency for Horizon regions
x: TerraWeaveHorizonScene now reuses previously uploaded region render::Model resources after the observer returns to an earlier camera cell. This GPU residency is distinct from the existing CPU maxCachedRegions atlas LRU and from the streaming/staging worker budget. engine/render/TerraWeaveHorizonGpuCache.h implements render-thread-only HorizonGpuRegionCache. An inactive entry owns its uploaded RHI Model, matching immutable CPU bake when available, optional terrain CPU vertex/index data for incremental updates, camera coordinates, model bounds-related metadata and a source-generation tag. take transfers model ownership without copying or reuploading geometry; retain can evict LRU entries by count and estimated GPU bytes; prune rejects authored-terrain revisions, and clear(device) explicitly destroys cached buffers and textures. Configurable terraweaveHorizon manifest properties: maxCachedGpuRegions: 0–3 additional GPU region models (Balanced default 1; Minimal/Mobile 0, High requests 2). gpuCacheBudgetMiB: 8–96 MiB for the additional cached regions (default 32 MiB). The current visible model and async upload staging are separate, bounded through their existing contracts. Approximate byte accounting includes vertex/index buffers, atlas RGBA8 and 4/3 mip allowance, but not exact driver overhead. Navigation A→B retains the visible A model while B is prepared. On successful B publication, A can enter the bounded GPU cache. On B→A cache hit, A becomes active immediately with no new CPU region bake and no full GPU model upload; meanwhile canceled background jobs are still drained to release staging reservations. Source revisions invalidate all stale cache entries and reject late CPU results from old landscape snapshots. TerraWeaveHorizonScene::runtimeStats() now reports gpuCachedRegions, gpuCachedBytes (estimated extra GPU use), and gpuCacheHits. These are instrumented counters, not measured FPS. Lifecycle and correctness: all GPU resource retirement goes through render::releaseModel(device) on the owning RHI thread and explicit shutdown(device). No per-tree ECS entities, separate renderer, backend-specific calls, or unbounded GPU caching. A disabled/opt-out Horizon creates no new caches. Quality presets and native projects can opt out by setting maxCachedGpuRegions=0. Status: source code was committed, but builds, CTest, platform GPU screenshots, GPU memory tracking, and frame-time measurements are the separate validation agent's responsibility. Runtime GPU reuse and lifecycle are not yet verified. The GPU residency counters additionally include gpuCacheEvictions, counting models explicitly released from the inactive LRU due to count/byte limits or stale terrain revisions. This excludes active-region replacement when no cache could retain the old model and does not measure GPU driver allocations or frame time.

h: Stage 14 — temporal transition between GPU Horizon regions
x: Horizon now has an optional neighbor-only temporal crossfade when the camera crosses a 128m-region key and the next proxy has been uploaded (or found in the GPU residency LRU). HorizonSettings::regionTransitionMs is a bounded 0..1000 milliseconds, default 240. It can be overridden through terraweaveHorizon.regionTransitionMs. 0 disables the fade for all platforms. The Minimal and Mobile quality presets choose 0 automatically to conserve GPU memory and avoid alpha-overdraw costs. During the bounded transition only, the renderer draws the outgoing and incoming already-uploaded render::Model proxies with complementary smoothstep alpha using existing Renderer3D::ModelDraw.tint.w and kDrawTransparent rendering flags. Both are non-shadow-casting during the effect. The normal single, opaque, static model draw path resumes immediately afterwards. There is no new shader, per-tree foliage model, framebuffer or RHI backend. The outgoing model occupies ONE of the existing inactive GPU residency slots and is subject to maxCachedGpuRegions and gpuCacheBudgetMiB. HorizonGpuRegionCache::reserveTransient evicts inactive LRU models as necessary. On completion, the outgoing model is stored back into that GPU LRU when the authored source revision still matches; otherwise it is explicitly freed using render::releaseModel(device). Camera changes across more than one grid cell, updates to terrain/ water/road masks or insufficient GPU budget skip temporal blending to avoid stale/outlandish visuals. New diagnostics: HorizonRuntimeStats::transitionStarts, transitioning and transitionProgressPermille. Important: Conventional alpha blending can produce sorting/depth artifacts when two terrain rings overlap or when crossed forest billboards intersect. This is a short, bounded visual transition, not order-independent transparency or a depth-aware geomorph. It is unverified on real render backends. The user assigned all CMake/CTest, GPU screenshots and performance testing to a separate agent.

h: Stage 15 — opaque far-ground ownership during Horizon transitions
x: The previous Horizon crossfade blended two entire combined terrain+canopy models. On overlapping coarse ground grids this could cause semi-transparent terrain to double-composite, incorrect depth ordering or Z-fighting. Now render::ModelDraw::primitiveMaterialFilter is an optional engine-generic source material selector (-1 default, 0 only source material 0, 1 only source material 1). The standard Renderer3D::drawModel skips unrelated Primitive entries, disabling aggregate material/shadow batches and static-cache acceleration only for these filtered calls. All ordinary unfiltered model submissions keep their existing batching, LOD and shadow logic. The new field is placed at the end of ModelDraw to preserve source compatibility with positional aggregate initializers. Horizon has two established material slots in one GPU model: 0 = distant terrain, 1 = canopy cluster cards. During short regionTransitionMs crossfades: Submit incoming terrain only, opaque, once, with primitiveMaterialFilter=0. It writes the depth surface. Submit outgoing canopy material 1 at alpha 1 - t through the existing transparent pass. Submit incoming canopy material 1 at alpha t through that same pass. Once the fade is over, go back to one full combined model draw with filter -1. The GPU model is not copied or split into multiple GPU allocations; draw calls reuse its existing buffers and texture atlas. Temporarily drawing two forest materials costs two transparent model submissions plus one opaque ground submission. Shadow/light-bake capture is skipped for partial transient draws. This is still alpha blending and may show canopy sorting artifacts, but it prevents simultaneous semi-transparent far-ground meshes. Navigation also supports direct A→B→A reversal during the fade: the old region is reclaimed from its temporary transition slot rather than being evicted by an over-subscribed LRU. When camera teleporting far outside the current region's safe footprint, an obsolete proxy is not submitted while the async worker prepares the replacement, even on low-memory devices whose maxCachedRegions=0. Remaining functional/visual caveats: Far terrain changes instantly (instead of crossfading its geometry). Large mountain skyline changes may still pop at a region boundary. Transparent canopy cards may intersect/sort poorly; real Metal/GL/Vulkan recordings are needed to decide whether shared shader-driven dither is worthwhile. The safe-footprint teleport gate may temporarily leave no horizon when a new region is not ready. This is preferable to drawing a distant proxy around a camera tens of kilometres away. All compilation, CTest, GPU validation and FPS measurements belong to the separate test agent; code is currently NOT RUN / UNVERIFIED.

h: Stage 16 — globally aligned Horizon terrain and edge skirts
x: Horizon terrain vertices now lie on a globally anchored, signed rational world lattice, using floorDiv(gridIndex * regionSide, terrainResolution). Adjacent camera regions therefore sample the same terrain positions even at High 64×64 or custom resolutions where the 512m camera-region shift is not divisible by the coarse grid spacing. Negative world coordinates remain stable. Each HorizonTerrainVertex stores slopeXPermille and slopeZPermille. Normals are obtained from height samples one global grid step on either side of the vertex, including outside the current region. Authoring a small terrain edit also marks the surrounding one-grid-step normal footprint dirty for partial CPU re-baking. This avoids the old region-dependent one-sided lighting normals. terrainSkirtDepthCm is an optional downward, outer-edge skirt on the coarse terrain material, from 0 to 5000cm. It preserves sampled top heights and adds no new material primitive or separate draw call. Default Balanced/High 1200cm, Mobile 600cm and Minimal off. From a high vantage point, downward geometry can be visible and should be tuned with atmospheric fog; it is not terrain geomorphing. With default 48×48 terrain and 832 possible forest clusters, analytic worst-case geometry is 9,253 vertices and 8,320 triangles, including 196 outer-skirt vertices and 384 skirt triangles. The 1392×1392 shared one-view RGBA atlas still uses 7,750,656 bytes before mipmaps. Top terrain and forest remain in the same standard GPU Model. Archive format: TWH3 (version/magic 3) stores both global slopes and skirt depth; its fingerprint also changes to reflect the new lattice. Previous TWH1/TWH2 binaries are deliberately rejected. Use aiverse_horizon_bake to rebuild static-world .twh assets or rely on the existing runtime regeneration fallback. Earlier TWH1/TWH2 references in this document describe historical stages, not the current on-disk format. Limitations: matching border geometry requires the same immutable source heightfield in the overlapping area. Authored terrain streaming changes may still require incremental re-baking; a source swap can visibly change the true landform. The skirt hides small outer-edge cracks, not abrupt skyline changes or inner near-terrain cutout mismatches. GPU screenshots, builds, CTest and platform performance have not been run by this agent; testing belongs to the dedicated validation agent. See Stage 16 handoff.

makeHorizonTerrainLattice(settings,cameraXcm,cameraZcm) is a reusable, genre-independent helper for third-party native terrain producers and offline tools. The returned HorizonTerrainLattice provides worldX(i) and worldZ(i) for vertex indices 0..terrainResolution (and ghost indices -1, N+1) plus the nominal grid step. The Horizon CPU baker calls that same API. It avoids reimplementing camera-local rounding in other engine/world modules. All API and rendering tests are delegated to the separate test agent.

h: Stage 17 — near-ground ownership, inner seam and stable outer skyline
x: HorizonSurfaceSources exposes an optional ownsNearTerrainRect(minXcm,minZcm,maxXcm,maxZcm) callback. It must return true only when a full half-open coarse world rectangle is covered by live near-terrain geometry. WorldScene supplies it from AuthoredWorldHeightSnapshot::coversRect, which checks all resident near ground tiles and returns false if any are absent. The generator stores a HorizonBake::nearOwnedQuads byte map (terrainResolution × terrainResolution). During makeHorizonModel, far-ground quads are omitted where the near mesh owns the whole coarse cell. With a callback present, this replaces the old uniform radial cutout, so a missing/unloaded near tile is filled by far Horizon ground instead of exposing sky. Without any callback, existing procedural Horizon settings continue to use the legacy radial terrainBeginCm cutout. The optional innerTerrainLipCm (default 40cm, valid 0–200cm) makes a tiny downward seam along near-owned/far-owned quad boundaries. At most 512 segments are generated. Each segment adds 2 bottom vertices and 2 triangles, using existing material 0; above that cap the inner lip is omitted without losing the near ownership mask. This is not exact polygon clipping: far quads overlapping only part of an authored near tile remain rendered and may still exhibit coplanar depth overlaps. terrainGridSnapSteps (1..16; default 4) stabilizes mountain silhouettes. Terrain sample positions snap to the nearest coarse global lattice anchor. Forest atlases can still stream on their 128m keys without moving the distant terrain grid every time. Minimal preset uses 1, Mobile 2 and Balanced/High 4. When distant terrain is on, the outer forest radius is conservatively limited to the region still guaranteed to have distant ground at any allowed snap offset, typically 5+ kilometres; without distant ground, forest keeps its original far radius. New analytic default worst-case with outer skirt and maximum optional inner seam: 10,277 vertices / 9,344 triangles across terrain and up to 832 cluster cards. This includes the conservative 512-segment inner seam cap. A procedural scene with no near ownership needs fewer vertices and has no inner seam. One shared forest atlas and at most two material primitives remain.

Current TerraWeaveHorizonArchive.h is TWH4, version/magic 4. Its wire payload adds innerTerrainLipCm and the optional byte-per-cell near-ground ownership map; its fingerprint includes terrainGridSnapSteps and inner lip depth. Old TWH1, TWH2 and TWH3 files are not compatible; rebuild with aiverse_horizon_bake or allow the existing runtime worker fallback. Older sections of this document describing TWH1–TWH3 reflect past implementation phases. For full migration in a native project with authored terrain, bake assets with the same ownsNearTerrainRect, height snapshot and stable authored-content hash used at runtime. The generic batch CLI still supports procedural-only content and cannot invent independently authored near-terrain masks. Not verified: zero Z-fighting, truly seamless mountain skyline, TWH4 decode or GPU performance. Real builds/CTest and captures are assigned to the separate test agent. See Stage 17 of the handoff.

h: Stage 18 — precise partial near-ground tile clipping (TWH5)
x: Stage 17 omitted a far-ground whole coarse quad only when every portion was owned by resident authored near terrain. The gap-free fallback avoided missing geometry but a partially covered 256m cell could still render an overlapping distant triangle. The new optional HorizonSurfaceSources::collectNearTerrainRects returns at most 1024 immutable, world-centimetre, half-open resident near-ground rectangles for the currently prepared Horizon footprint. AuthoredWorldHeightSnapshot::coveredRectsIn exposes this directly to WorldScene, using deterministic geometric ordering. The CPU HorizonBake stores these rectangles in nearClipRects alongside the existing full-quad nearOwnedQuads mask. engine/render/TerraWeaveHorizonClip.h implements planHorizonNearGroundClipping(bake): Each affected coarse far-ground cell is split into the same two original triangles. Subtract overlapping near-tile rectangles using convex half-plane polygons; retain only regions not owned by near terrain. Convert them back into bounded triangles with their original winding and source-triangle plane. Reconstruct clipped vertex positions, normals, UVs and RGBA8 colors through barycentric interpolation of the original far-terrain triangle, so the new mesh does not invent a second, divergent far-ground surface. Keep all terrain triangles in the same material 0 primitive and existing shared GPU model. No new shader, per-tile draw calls, FPS/RTS module or parallel renderer is introduced. Enforce a global per-region cap; on excessive geometric fragmentation, the planner returns no plan, and the entire bake falls back to conservative Stage 17 full-quad ownership. Invalid or unbounded near input never produces an unbounded GPU mesh. HorizonSettings::maxNearClipTriangles controls the maximum new clipped triangles (0=disabled, 0–8192 accepted). Default presets are: Preset Near clipped triangles Minimal 0 Mobile 512 Balanced 2048 High 4096 With default Balanced, the worst-case analytic bound becomes 16,421 vertices and 11,392 triangles, including the prior outer skirt, inner 512-segment lip cap and the extra 2,048 clipped triangles. Actual forests typically use substantially fewer. The shared atlas budget, additional GPU cache limits and usual RHI path do not change. Diagnostic fields HorizonRuntimeStats::nearClipQuads, nearClipTriangles and nearClipFallback identify how many coarse cells were partially clipped, resulting triangles, and whether the safe budget fallback was triggered. Values persist through GPU-region caching. Archive migration: TerraWeaveHorizonArchive.h is now TWH5, not TWH4. The wire format stores bounded nearClipRects and maxNearClipTriangles; the generator fingerprint includes clip triangle budget and archive version. Existing TWH1–TWH4 assets must be regenerated with the offline aiverse_horizon_bake or the existing asynchronous runtime fallback. Limits: This is precise horizontal X/Z coverage against axis-aligned near terrain tile rectangles, NOT vertical geomorphing. If the authored near terrain lies higher/lower than its coarse distant representation, the clipped boundary may still have a vertical crack. The previously existing 40cm inner lip covers only whole coarse ownership boundaries, not every new partial cut edge. Real GPU visual acceptance and any height-aware stitching remain separate work. Tests, compilation, Metal/GL/Vulkan screenshots, archive roundtrips and performance runs have NOT RUN in this functional implementation stage; a different agent owns them.

h: Stage 19 — near/far terrain height-welded clip boundaries (TWH6)
x: Following Stage 18's exact 2D subtraction of authored near-tile rectangles from distant Horizon triangles, the clipped perimeter can now be snapped to the actual authored near-terrain height, leaving the triangle interior on the existing far-ground surface. This removes a vertical boundary height gap when the source terrain is resident and the optional sampler is supplied. HorizonSurfaceSources::nearGroundHeightAtCm(worldXcm,worldZcm) returns optional<int32_t> (near height in signed centimetres); WorldScene connects it to the same immutable resident AuthoredWorldHeightSnapshot used for near coverage rectangles and terrain sampling. The CPU helper populateHorizonNearSeamSamples(HorizonBake&,source) finds clipped polygon vertices along near-tile boundaries, deduplicates them in world-centimetre Q16 space (fractional positions preserved) and samples at most 4096 unique near-ground heights. A half-open tile's high edge is sampled at most 1cm inside that already resident tile to avoid reading an unloaded neighbor. If a required point cannot be sampled, the entire seam-height table is withheld and the prior Stage 18 exact horizontal clipping remains available without half-welded geometry. HorizonBake::nearSeamSamples is an immutable, serialized list of {xQ16cm,zQ16cm,nearHeightCm}. During makeHorizonModel, only clipped-edge position.y is replaced with the matching authored near-surface height. Far-interior vertices stay on their coarse parent triangle. No new GPU vertex topology, material, draw call, graphics backend, gameplay ECS entity or collision modification is introduced by welding. Both the runtime CPU worker (TerraWeaveHorizonScene) and native bakeHorizonBatch offline API populate these samples before storing/serializing the immutable HorizonBake. Reading an archive or GPU model cache restores the same data without consulting the mutable current WorldScene from the renderer. New diagnostics: HorizonModelBuildStats::weldedVertices/maxWeldHeightDeltaCm, HorizonRuntimeStats::weldedNearVertices/maxNearWeldDeltaCm. They survive GPU-cache region restoration. The maximum delta measures the absolute Y correction applied to a clipped vertex in centimetres. No measured GPU timings or screenshot-quality guarantees are implied.

TWH6 is now the current .twh wire format and generator fingerprint. TWH6 includes a bounded count and Q16 X/Z + i32 near height per sample (20 bytes each; up to 4096 samples, ~80KiB before in-memory container overhead). Existing TWH1–TWH5 files are incompatible and must be regenerated using aiverse_horizon_bake or the worker fallback. The earlier TWH1–TWH5 sections in this document are retained as historical implementation phases, not current format guidance. The height-aware weld reduces vertical cracks, not necessarily all visual artifacts: large height differences may produce a steep sloped polygon near the cut; near-terrain normals can differ from interpolated coarse normals, and neither fog nor temporal geomorphing is changed. The default forest atlas and GPU geometry limits remain unchanged. To verify perceptual quality, test the actual authored scene with steep terrain, negative coordinates, tile boundaries and GPU draw sorting. Tests/build/GPU visual runs were not performed by the functionality agent; another agent owns them.

h: Stage 20 — slope-safe height welding and shared seam normals (TWH7)
x: Stage 19 welded the exact near/far clipped-edge Y to the authored near terrain. This could create a nearly vertical far triangle if the coarse original height differed sharply across a tiny clipped polygon. A normal-map fix alone cannot change the actual steep wedge. Now HorizonSettings exposes two bounded, optional C++/manifest settings: maxNearWeldSlopePermille (0–8000; default 2500). 0 disables the slope guard. The CPU seam sampler preflights each proposed welded triangle using its actual barycentric original far heights and near-boundary heights. A newly induced triangle gradient above the limit rejects the ENTIRE optional height weld for that Horizon bake, retaining the exact Stage 18 X/Z clipping and setting nearWeldSlopeFallback=true. Existing naturally steep far terrain is not flattened. This deliberately can leave a vertical seam; no algorithm can simultaneously keep an arbitrarily high near edge, an unchanged nearby far vertex, zero additional horizontal distance and a strict slope cap. Avoid lying about a perfectly seamless result. nearSeamNormalBlendPercent (0–100; default 65). While constructing an already existing partial near-clip triangle mesh, makeHorizonModel computes upward-facing, area-weighted geometric face normals after any valid near-height weld. It groups shared clipped corners by signed Q16 world X/Z and height to average adjacent face normals. Near-edge vertices blend 65% of the repaired normal, interior near-border vertices blend 16.25% by default. 0 leaves the original far-grid interpolated normals. This changes only the CPU-built existing ModelVertex normal attributes: no extra geometry, shader, material, GPU buffer or draw call. The CPU worker, offline bake and runtime Model all consume the exact same immutable seam-height snapshots as in Stage 19. HorizonRuntimeStats adds smoothedNearNormals and nearWeldSlopeFallback; these metrics are also preserved when the GPU LRU restores a previously uploaded region.

TerraWeaveHorizonArchive.h is now TWH7, version/magic 7. It adds the seam slope limit, normal blend percentage and per-bake slope-fallback flag to the binary payload. The fingerprint includes both configuration settings. Earlier TWH1–TWH6 .twh files are intentionally rejected and must be regenerated by aiverse_horizon_bake or the existing runtime fallback. Known limits: the default 2500 permille is a guard for new weld-induced slopes, not an upper bound on all terrain gradients. On extremely narrow clip polygons the guard may reject a weld for the full region, preserving accurate X/Z ground ownership but allowing a vertical height mismatch. Normals are smoothed only on clipped triangles, not on the authoritative near mesh; this is not shared tessellation or true normal-field matching. Captured GPU images and geometry regression tests are REQUIRED before claiming the terrain is visually seamless. Implementation stages and exact commit hashes are in docs/terrain/AGENT_HANDOFF.md Stage 20a/b. No CMake, CTest, platform screenshots or CPU/GPU performance tests were executed by the feature agent; a separate agent owns those validations.

h: Stage 21 — precise Q16 seam sampling and authored near normals (TWH8)
x: Stage 20 already implemented an all-or-none welded-slope guard and area-weighted geometric normal smoothing. The current stage improves the precision and source agreement of the underlying near terrain data. AuthoredWorldHeightSnapshot::sampleQ16(xQ16cm,zQ16cm) samples the same immutable authored two-triangle height tiles as the existing integer-centimetre sample method, but at signed fractional world-centimetre Q16 coordinates. Integral inputs retain the exact old integer-height result. Fractional points use bounded fixed-point barycentric weights, not floating GPU interpolation. HorizonSurfaceSources::nearGroundHeightAtQ16Cm is optional. WorldScene supplies it from the same immutable near-ground snapshot that provides collectNearTerrainRects and ownsNearTerrainRect. A native authored provider may omit it and retain the legacy whole-centimetre height path. During populateHorizonNearSeamSamples, exact clipped polygon coordinates are sampled at Q16 precision. At the high side of a half-open tile the query moves only one Q16 unit (1/65536 cm) into the already resident tile, rather than shifting by up to 1 cm. A bounded +/-200cm stencil entirely inside the same tile derives near-surface slopeXPermille and slopeZPermille. Missing derivative data merely marks the normal unavailable; missing height still disables the entire seam height weld for that region. Each baked NearSeamSample now contains: xQ16cm, zQ16cm (the same seam identity as Stage 19); nearHeightCm (exact authored Q16-sampled near height, rounded to signed centimetres); nearSlopeXPermille, nearSlopeZPermille, plus nearNormalValid. makeHorizonModel continues using the existing bounded clipped far triangles. At a welded point with nearNormalValid=true, lighting normals blend toward the authored near-source normal, under the existing nearSeamNormalBlendPercent setting. Interior clipped far triangles retain the Stage 20 area-weighted face-normal blending. Neither clipping topology, vertex/triangle counts, materials nor draw submissions increase. HorizonRuntimeStats::matchedAuthoredNearNormals counts the clipped render vertices where an authored Q16 surface normal was actually blended. Existing smoothedNearNormals includes the geometric normal path. Both counters survive GPU LRU restoration. The strict atlas-only patch planner refuses modified seam heights/gradients; safe index-compatible edits can still use the combined partial vertex upload or full-model fallback. Current archive: TWH8. The .twh payload now stores 32 bytes per near-seam point (Q16 X/Z, height, two slopes and encoded validity). The bounded 4096-point table adds at most 48KiB of normal metadata compared to TWH7; no new GPU memory allocation is required beyond existing model vertex attributes. TWH1–TWH7 archives are intentionally stale and should be rebaked with aiverse_horizon_bake or regenerated through the existing worker fallback. Old version sections below/above are historical only. Not yet validated: compiled native targets, TWH8 roundtrip, 0/65/100% normal interpolation, device-specific lighting captures, cross-compiler Q16 rounding or GPU performance. All are owned by the dedicated testing agent; the feature source has been committed but testing is NOT RUN.

h: Stage 22 — neighbor-aware seam normals and live Horizon diagnostics
x: This section describes the current source contract for feature/terraweave (PR #24); earlier TWH6/TWH7 descriptions in this file are historical. The current .twh archive version is TWH8.
