h: Seam sampling across resident authored terrain tiles
x: AuthoredWorldHeightSnapshot::continuousSlopeQ16(xQ16cm,zQ16cm, radiusCm=200,toleranceCm=1) returns std::optional<std::pair<int32_t,int32_t>> with signed X/Z slopes in permille (-dY/dX, -dY/dZ), or nullopt if a neighboring tile is unavailable or the crossed tile-edge heights disagree. Input X/Z is signed Q16 world centimetres (multiply whole centimetres by 65536). The bounded stencil radius accepts 1–4096cm; discontinuity tolerance is 0–100cm (default 1cm). The snapshot probes the original authored two-triangle heightfields, including negative world tile coordinates, and never changes collision or authoritative terrain. HorizonSurfaceSources::nearGroundContinuousSlopeAtQ16Cm is an optional CPU-bake callback supplied by WorldScene from the same immutable AuthoredWorldHeightSnapshot used for authored near-ground heights. Native projects may provide this callback alongside nearGroundHeightAtQ16Cm; omit it to keep the existing local normal algorithm. During populateHorizonNearSeamSamples, the worker prefers a continuous neighbor-aware slope for each unique Q16 clipped perimeter point. When that query returns nullopt it falls back to the previous tile-local +/-200cm derivative when that data is available. If neither yields a valid normal, nearNormalValid remains false and the existing area-weighted clipped-face normal path is used. This affects render shading only. The Stage 20 all-or-none maxNearWeldSlopePermille height-weld guard, near X/Z clipping, TWH8 NearSeamSample layout and existing atlas/VB/full model patch selection remain in effect. The normal stencil must not smooth a genuine cliff across independently authored tiles.

After updating the scene on its owning thread, a native host/editor can read TerraWeaveHorizonScene::runtimeStats(): const auto h = horizon.runtimeStats(); if (h.requestedRegionPending) { // A requested region is not yet resolved at the current source revision. // h.preparing is a separate worker status; "pending" != "CPU is running". } if (h.activeRegionResolved && h.activeRegionEmpty) { // Accepted bake for the active cell, intentionally no drawable GPU model. } if (h.staleProxy) { // Active resolved cell is from an older authored source revision. } if (h.nearNormalProvenanceAvailable) { // Counts are unique sampled seam points, NOT vertices or draw calls. auto neighbor = h.continuousNearNormalSamples; auto local = h.localFallbackNearNormalSamples; (void)neighbor; (void)local; } // Only inspect requestedCellX/Z if requestedRegionPresent is true. // Only inspect activeCellX/Z if activeRegionResolved is true. Field Contract sourceRevision / activeRevision Current immutable source revision / accepted active-region revision. requestedRegionPresent, requestedCellX/Z A camera-selected target exists; coordinates are middle-tile grid indices, not centimetres; camera hysteresis applies. activeRegionResolved, activeCellX/Z A region result was accepted (including an intentionally empty result); active coordinates are defined only when resolved. activeRegionPresent Accepted region currently has a drawable GPU model; false does not imply pending. activeRegionEmpty A resolved region intentionally has no GPU model (e.g. empty ocean Horizon). requestedRegionPending Target exists and is unresolved, differs from active cell, or active revision is stale. An empty resolved same-cell/same-revision region is not pending. staleProxy Active resolved region revision differs from sourceRevision; it can also describe a stale empty region. Wrong-camera-cell status without source edits belongs to requestedRegionPending, not this flag. preparing / discarded Async stream state; check independently of requestedRegionPending. continuousNearNormalSamples Unique Q16 near-seam samples with valid neighbor-aware slopes in the CPU bake. localFallbackNearNormalSamples Unique Q16 near-seam samples using the local-height derivative because neighbor-aware results were unavailable/invalid. nearNormalProvenanceAvailable Counts above have a known CPU sampling origin. When false, treat both counts as unknown, even if numerically zero. matchedAuthoredNearNormals Number of render vertices matched to an authored near-source normal; do not add to sample counts. Archive behavior: TWH8 stores the near-seam height, slope and normal-valid bit but not the provenance counters or availability flag. A disk archive cache hit can legitimately report nearNormalProvenanceAvailable=false and zero provenance counts even when stored normals are valid; this is unknown, not measured zero. A fresh bake can report valid zero counts when no seam sample qualifies. All-or-none weld fallback may discard samples and zero counters while the CPU sampling-path availability flag remains true. Lifecycle: shutdown(device) clears current region, requested region, geometry metadata and diagnostic counters. GPU-cache retirement/restoration carries provenance counts and their availability. A source revision update can temporarily keep an older GPU proxy until an updated bake succeeds. activeRegionPresent only reports model existence, while requestedRegionPending reports unresolved selection. A large teleport may be hidden by the separate camera coverage check in submit(); this is not encoded by staleProxy. Validation delegated to another agent: compile with C++20 on target platforms; check adjacent positive/negative tiles, sloped and discontinuous boundaries, missing neighbors, Q16 corner rounding, all-or-none slope fallback, empty region and shutdown, GPU LRU restore, source revision invalidation, archive hit/miss, and atlas/vertex patch safety. h: Stage 24 — sparse deterministic forest regrowth and presentation ticks
x: Status: native C++ source committed, runtime/compiler/CTest/GPU verification intentionally deferred until the separate testing phase. This feature extends the already-existing persisted ForestTreeIdentity removals; it does not introduce per-tree ECS entities, a new shader, another RHI backend, a new save file format, or a second GPU forest model. A TerraWeaveForestScene now supports ForestRegrowthSchedule, a sparse value type: struct ForestRegrowthSchedule { ForestTreeIdentity tree; // {key, speciesId}: stable across chunks uint64_t regrowAtTick; // hidden before this tick uint64_t matureAtTick; // full generator scale at/after this tick uint32_t initialScalePermille; // 1..1000, defaults to 150 }; Use the game's own deterministic simulation tick — not wall-clock time — with setPresentationTick(uint64_t). scheduleRegrowth(schedule) removes the tree from the persistent removedTrees set and hides it before regrowAtTick. For ticks between appearance and maturity, visibleBatches() modifies the presentation copy of FoliageInstance::scalePermille using bounded integer interpolation, from initialScalePermille to 1000 permille of its original generated scale. matureAtTick == regrowAtTick means instant restoration. Nothing changes in the authoritative scatter keys, heights, seed, collision, navmesh or GPU prototype models. On later camera movement/re-streaming the same identity gets the same scale for the same tick. #include "engine/world/TerraWeaveForestScene.h" using namespace aiverse::terraweave; // Use an existing configured scene and a stable ID obtained from foliage. ForestTreeIdentity oak{stableTreeKey, 1001}; forest.removeTree(oak); // optional gameplay-driven harvest forest.scheduleRegrowth({oak, 6000, 12000, 120}); forest.setPresentationTick(gameplayTick); const auto batches = forest.visibleBatches(); // Host still calls uploadModels()/submit() on the renderer owner thread. // Persist forest.removedTrees() and forest.regrowthSchedules() in game saves. Here stableTreeKey and gameplayTick are native-game values, not engine globals. setRegrowthSchedules(...) atomically validates and replaces a saved sorted list; regrowthSchedules() exposes a stable sorted snapshot for persistence/replication. cancelRegrowth(id) cancels a schedule without automatically hiding or removing the tree. removeTree(id) cancels any pending regrowth and hides the tree; restoreTree(id) clears both hidden and scheduled states; setRemovedTrees(...) clears any overlapping regrowth schedules so explicitly removed trees remain hidden. Use the caller's save/network authority for lifecycle decisions. The implementation limits regrowth to at most 1,000,000 sparse records, rejects zero species, duplicate replacement keys, initialScalePermille outside 1..1000, backward schedules, and maturity intervals greater than 1e12 ticks. These bounds keep elapsed * (1000 - minScale) within signed/unsigned 64-bit integer range without platform-specific 128-bit arithmetic. Even with asynchronous forest generation, tick changes are evaluated at presentation time and do not cancel/rebuild chunk workers. ForestSceneStats exposes the additional trailing fields scheduledRegrowth and presentationTick, without breaking earlier aggregate uses of its existing members.

An opt-in world::WorldScene exposes terraweave::TerraWeaveForestScene* forestScene() noexcept (and the const overload). It returns null if the world manifest does not enable terraweaveForest. Native games can include both engine/world/WorldScene.h and engine/world/TerraWeaveForestScene.h and feed game time or saved lifecycle records directly without any genre-specific API: if (auto* forest = worldScene.forestScene()) { forest->setPresentationTick(gameplayTick); forest->scheduleRegrowth({oak, 6000, 12000, 120}); } Ownership and limitations: this is cosmetic presentation only. An authoritative game layer is responsible for deciding when harvests occur and for modifying collision/navmesh/resources, save versioning, replay/network replication and any wider ecosystem simulation. Harvesting a single tree does not yet punch an individual hole in the far Horizon HLOD cluster silhouettes; coordinate harvested-area masks with Horizon in a later stage to avoid near/far inconsistencies. The implementation has not been built or visually tested in this feature-first phase.

h: Stage 25 — runtime forest clearings shared by near Flora and Horizon HLOD
x: Source implemented, tests deferred at user request. A native world::WorldScene now exposes: void setVegetationClearings(std::vector<terraweave::RectCm> clearings); const std::vector<terraweave::RectCm>& vegetationClearings() const; Clearings are signed world-centimetre half-open X/Z rectangles, not RTS map-grid units. A game can use them to clear whole construction areas, timber harvest zones, or landscape patches (unlike the individual per-tree ForestRegrowthSchedule in Stage 24). All input rectangles must be nonempty and inside TerraWeave's +/-kWorldLimitCm extent; at most 4096 are accepted. The setter normalizes order and removes exact duplicates; passing an identical canonical set is a no-op. The returned list is suitable for caller-owned save/replication; the engine does not create authoritative gameplay events, collision edits, or a new save schema. using aiverse::terraweave::RectCm; worldScene.setVegetationClearings({ RectCm{siteX0cm,siteZ0cm,siteX1cm,siteZ1cm} }); // Call worldScene.update(device, observers, radius) from the owner thread. // Later: worldScene.setVegetationClearings({}) to restore the area. The site*cm values in this example are game-provided coordinates. The next WorldScene::update captures one immutable FoliageExclusionMask containing both active clearing rectangles and resident authored object/terrain footprints. The same snapshot is shared with: TerraWeaveForestScene::setLandscapeSources for near Flora placement. Its bounded async patches are invalidated by a single source revision and rebuilt safely after their captured callbacks are released. HorizonSurfaceSources::allowsCanopyAt for distant forest silhouette atlas sampling. It suppresses crowns at masked positions during the normal bounded CPU region bake and reuses the existing Horizon async/GPU update path. Existing terrain mesh and near/far height welding remain unchanged. Clearing updates mark both previous and new rectangles as edited, so moving or removing a clearing restores vegetation in the old location rather than preserving stale distant silhouettes. Multiple setter calls before a scene update retain only the first pre-update clearing state and the final replacement; intermediate states never become published. Large edited lists take the Horizon full-rebake fallback rather than unbounded incremental work. Unlike per-tree regrowth, this area mask does affect the far HLOD canopy, while not adding a new shader, draw pass, GPU buffer layout or component type. Caveats: The mask suppresses individual CPU canopy samples and may leave empty far cluster cards if all samples in that cluster are excluded; this is a rendering efficiency follow-up. An authored forest/city streaming update can also trigger shared mask republishing, independent of gameplay clearings. No shape rotation, polygon harvesting, sector replication, authoritative resource/collision modifications, or weather/season coupling is included yet. Runtime re-bake, cross-boundary exclusions, visual transitions and performance budgets have NOT been verified; another agent owns those tests.

h: Stage 26 — resident tree spatial queries for native gameplay
x: TerraWeave now supports presentation-resident tree selection without forcing every decorative tree into ECS: // TerraWeaveForestScene forest already configured / streamed. const auto closest=forest.nearestTreeAt(playerXcm,playerZcm,500); if(closest) { forest.removeTree({closest->key,closest->speciesId}); // The authoritative game must still update lumber, collider and save. } const auto trees=forest.treesInRect( {plotMinXcm,plotMinZcm,plotMaxXcm,plotMaxZcm},1024); The coordinates above are game-provided signed world centimetres. nearestTreeAt(xCm,zCm,radiusCm=500) -> optional<FoliageInstance>: searches resident CPU scatter patches, using an AABB precheck and circle distance. Radius must be in 1..10,000,000cm; out-of-world centres are rejected. Equal-distance ties select the lowest stable ForestTreeIdentity{speciesId,key}, independently of map iteration order. It is not camera/frustum/LOD dependent. treesInRect(RectCm,size_t maxResults=1024) -> vector<FoliageInstance>: checks only resident patches intersecting a nonempty half-open rectangle, excludes removed/pending-regrowth trees and sorts results by species ID, key then X/Z. The result budget is 1..100,000; overflow throws std::length_error instead of silently returning an arbitrary truncated set. Both use the exact same presentationInstance lifecycle filter as visibleBatches(); harvested trees are invisible to queries; a scheduled tree is hidden until its regrowAtTick, and returned growing trees carry the current visual scale. Queries never re-scatter terrain, modify the GPU, sample external game physics or use a platform clock. Results cover only loaded forest patches. An unloaded tree or a tree outside the configured residency area cannot be found through this presentation-only API; collision, harvesting at long range and persistent jobs remain responsibilities of the authoritative gameplay/world systems. The generic WorldScene::forestScene() accessor from Stage 24 gives native projects access to these methods for opt-in worlds. For huge worlds, if frequent queries become hot, consider an optional per-chunk spatial index after profiling; no claimed performance benchmarks or compiler/CTest/GPU validation have been performed in this features-first stage.

h: Stage 27 — shared canopy phenology for Flora and Horizon
x: Source committed; compilation, CTest, screenshots and GPU benchmarks intentionally deferred. The engine now accepts a host-owned seasonal appearance state, not a built-in calendar or weather simulation. PHYSIS and game-specific time-of-year systems can supply the same small POD via a genre-independent bridge: #include "engine/world/TerraWeavePhenology.h" // A non-default fall/autumn profile; choose values in the host. aiverse::terraweave::CanopyPhenology autumn; autumn.broadleafCoverPermille = 480; autumn.evergreenCoverPermille = 960; autumn.tintRPermille = 1350; autumn.tintGPermille = 810; autumn.tintBPermille = 580; worldScene.setVegetationPhenology(autumn); The above values are an example, not a baked climate forecast. Each cover value is in 0..1000; RGB tint multipliers are integer permille 0..2000; 1000 = identity. validateCanopyPhenology, canopyCoverPermille and tintCanopyChannel are pure C++20 helpers in engine/world/TerraWeavePhenology.h. They do not include PHYSIS, RTS, FPS, GPU or platform timing. The caller owns climate, seasonal chronology, persistence and replication. The opt-in world::WorldScene::setVegetationPhenology(state) stores the canonical policy, forwards it to TerraWeaveForestScene::setPhenology, and queues a Horizon source revision for the next WorldScene::update. Unchanged state is a no-op. Near Flora updates shared per-species material overrides in ArborForestAdapter without rescatters or async worker cancellation. Conifer prototypes use the evergreen coverage; other shapes use broadleaf coverage. Bark material stays intact, while the leaf material receives RGB tint and optional blended alpha when canopy cover is below full. Overrides must not be changed after submitting draws to Renderer3D but before that frame is rendered, because ModelDraw::materials stores a borrowed pointer. For near azimuth impostors, the same policy updates the existing shared per-view billboard material overrides; the source atlas includes bark and foliage on one quad, so coverage alpha fades the entire billboard rather than just its leaves. This is a known LOD-parity limitation, not a leaf-only billboard mask or per-pixel seasonal foliage solution. It adds no atlas, mesh or extra draw pass by design. Partially transparent canopy may incur standard blended-render overdraw; benchmark in the later test phase. Far Horizon uses the same immutable CanopyPhenology captured in HorizonSurfaceSources::phenology: each procedural broadleaf/conifer canopy crown is deterministically thinned by the corresponding cover value, and resulting leaf RGB pixels are tinted before writing the existing shared RGBA atlas. Occasional exposed trunks remain untouched. Heightfields, terrain geometry, physics, material count, triangle budgets and near-seam welding do not change. HorizonSurfaceSources appends the policy to its existing optional callbacks; native projects that do not supply it retain default summer-like output. Seasonal changes request a bounded worker re-bake; old GPU proxy stays visible until replacement succeeds. TWH8 cache safety: the current static archive format/fingerprint does not serialize the season. The Horizon worker therefore deliberately disables static disk atlas read/write while a non-default phenology is active, avoiding false summer archive hits. Default state retains the existing TWH8 path. No archive version/layout migration occurs. Native projects wanting prebaked multiple seasons would need an explicit future archive key and asset naming policy. Remaining limitations: Per-tree ForestRegrowthSchedule still controls individual growth scale, independent from seasonal leaf cover. Spring/autumn transitions are immediate material/atlas policy changes rather than continuous blended dual-atlas animations; near impostor cards fade trunk as well as canopy; distant HLOD crown types are procedural/bio-climate approximations, not identities of actual nearby species. Individual harvested trees remain near-only until far HLOD supports

h: Stage 28 — genre-neutral wind presentation for Arbor forest
x: Code committed, tests intentionally deferred. The wind motion API is a presentation-only adapter: games or PHYSIS supply wind vectors and simulation ticks; TerraWeave does not run its own weather, physics forces, collision, ECS or platform-time timers. The new engine/world/TerraWeaveWind.h defines: struct ForestWindState { int32_t xCmPerSec = 0, zCmPerSec = 0; uint32_t gustPermille = 350; uint32_t cycleTicks = 120; uint32_t maxLeanMilliDegrees = 1500; }; ForestLeanMilliDegrees forestTreeLean( const ForestWindState& state, uint64_t tick, uint64_t stableTreeKey); Both wind components use signed world X/Z centimetres per second. A state is valid when the horizontal magnitude is no more than 5000cm/s (50m/s), gustPermille in 0..1000, cycleTicks in 8..4096 and maxLeanMilliDegrees in 0..3000. The helper computes a bounded integer triangle-wave phase using mix64(stableTreeKey); each tree has a stable offset instead of the entire forest tilting in lockstep. The zero-wind default preserves identical model transforms. aiverse::terraweave::ForestWindState wind; wind.xCmPerSec = 900; // 9 m/s toward +X wind.zCmPerSec = -300; worldScene.setVegetationWind(wind); worldScene.setVegetationPresentationTick(gameplayTick); WorldScene forwards those values to its optional TerraWeaveForestScene; native projects using the forest independently may call forest.setWind(wind) and forest.setPresentationTick(tick) directly. For an opt-in renderer, the ArborForestAdapter computes a small world-space lean about the base of the model, before the tree's local yaw, then uses existing Renderer3D::drawModel. Stable tree identity, origin-rebased centimetres, per-species LOD, shared meshes and billboard atlas remain unchanged. Per-tree phases and angles are computed on the presentation side; changes to wind/tick do not rescatters, restart workers, or force Horizon atlas uploads. Important limitations: this is a low-cost root/whole-tree sway approximation, not branch/leaf skinning or vertex-shader wind deformation. Distant Horizon HLOD remains static (moving 12km forest atlases per tick would be excessive); the very far treeline therefore does not individually sway. Billboard impostors lean as one quad. The final float transform is cosmetic and not guaranteed bit-for-bit identical between rendering backends; authoritative physics or harvest logic must never use it. PHYSIS can map its velocity field into this POD from the owning game host without linking the TerraWeave engine to PHYSIS. Performance and correctness: no new model geometry or draw calls are introduced; however CPU transform math is performed per submitted tree when wind is nonzero, so actual frame cost and visual quality still require the separately scheduled benchmarking and GPU test phase. A future optional vertex deformation shader could preserve stable roots while bending crowns more naturally. Neither compiler nor GPU/CTest has been run during this features-first stage.

Code committed; no build/CTest/GPU validation yet per the feature-first instruction. This stage replaces the combined all-season RGBA impostor image produced by makeArborImpostorAtlas. A near Arbor tree and its billboard can now lose leaves while retaining an intact bark silhouette.

engine/render/TerraWeaveImpostorAtlas.h generates one GPU RGBA8 texture per species with two horizontal sets of equal-sized view tiles: The first azimuthViews tiles contain bark/trunk/branch strokes only. The following azimuthViews tiles contain foliage/leaf-cluster strokes only. Both sets are projected from the same stable TreeSkeleton for each view angle and retain per-tile gutters. The atlas is 2 * tile.width * azimuthViews pixels wide by tile.height high (maximum width 8192, hence previously accepted ultra-wide combinations may now be rejected). Default 8-view, 128x256 atlas becomes 2048x256 RGBA8 instead of 1024x256, doubling raw atlas bytes but still using ONE texture object. The common render::Model contains one node, one mesh, 8 vertices, 12 indices and two alpha-masked primitives (Primitive.material=0 bark, =1 foliage). The foliage quad is offset +2cm toward its camera-facing model +Z to avoid depth fighting. Both material slots reference the same baseTex=0 with independent per-view UV transforms; ArborImpostorAtlas::viewMaterials is still indexed by azimuth but now contains exactly two materials for each view, in bark/foliage order. No new shader, RHI backend, ECS components, model per instance, or separate atlas upload pass.

ArborForestAdapter::rebuildPhenologyMaterials() copies per-species near and impostor material variants only on policy changes. Material 0 (bark) remains untouched; only material 1 (foliage) gets tint and alpha. canopyCoverPermille chooses evergreen versus broadleaf by the registered profile. At zero canopy cover, existing ModelDraw::primitiveMaterialFilter=0 submits bark primitives only for near BranchLOD and impostors, skipping invisible leaf draws. At partial cover, foliage uses the existing alpha-blend material policy; bark remains alpha-masked and fully opaque. Existing wind lean and root-anchored camera-facing orientation are shared by both impostor layers. Cost/quality caveats: full-canopy impostors now have two primitives instead of one, so draw submissions/material batching and texture bandwidth can increase. Cutout bark and blended foliage may differ slightly in ordering/coverage from the previous single-layer approximation. Far Horizon still uses its separate aggregated silhouette atlas and is unaffected by this near-impostor format. Partial transparency is a simplified seasonal representation, not deterministic individual leaf shedding; GPU/backend captures are needed to confirm blend order, shadow behavior, LOD transition quality and precise visual parity. Backward compatibility: makeArborBillboardModel (the standalone single-view utility) retains its original one-quad format. Only the multi-azimuth makeArborImpostorAtlas output changes shape; any native consumer assuming 4 vertices, 6 indices, single material or original atlas width must migrate. Existing tests/terraweave_model_test.cpp has expectations for that old layout and is intentionally not updated or executed in this features-first phase. The later testing agent must revise these assertions to the two-layer contract, then run GCC/Clang CTest, GPU screenshot and benchmark checks. No TWH8 distant-Horizon disk archive version change is needed because its format is unrelated to this near-impostor atlas.

h: Stage 30 — bounded hierarchical BranchLOD wind motion
x: Functional source committed, independent testing deferred. This stage extends Stage 28's PHYSIS-neutral root lean into more organic, articulated wind motion for near Arbor BranchLOD trees, without reskinning meshes or requiring a new render shader. ForestWindState appends branchFlexPermille (default 600, bounded 0..1000); 0 preserves the exact previous low-cost whole-tree tilt. ArborForestAdapter regenerates the already-deterministic high-detail skeleton ONCE at prototype registration to cache per-branch root pivots (metres relative to original tree root). It then uses the existing branch node hierarchy and Renderer3D's ModelDraw::nodeWorld rigid-model transform path to compute a per-visible-tree vector of cumulative model-space rotations around each branch's own start pivot. The trunk node itself remains at its original pose while global ModelDraw::world supplies the original whole-tree sway. Children inherit parent movement and have a stable per-node phase derived from the tree key, species and branch index. No tree ECS entities, animation clips, skinned matrices, GPU mesh mutation, shader variants, atlas rebuilds or extra draw passes are added. The original Arbor mesh geometry, TreeProfile, branch LOD simplification and canonical procedural tree seeds remain unchanged. View-distance tiers attenuate additional branch sway (High 100%, Medium 65%, Low 25%, Impostor 0%) to limit near-to-billboard discontinuity. Distant statistical Horizon remains static as previously documented; it is intentionally NOT rebuilt per wind tick. The private temporary pose arena is a std::deque<std::vector<render::mat4>> so references in ModelDraw::nodeWorld remain stable during a forEachDraw call; the arena is cleared at the next forEachDraw. Renderer3D::drawModel reads node transforms synchronously and copies them into render items. Native callbacks collecting ModelDraws may only use their nodeWorld pointers until the next forEachDraw invocation, and must not use the forest adapter concurrently on multiple threads. ArborForestAdapter::setBranchPoseBudgetBytes(bytes) (forwarded through TerraWeaveForestScene) accepts 0..8MiB and defaults to 4MiB. A draw whose node matrix snapshot would exceed the remaining budget uses root-only sway instead. The budget is for CPU temporary matrices, not new GPU residency. Example (on the owning host/update thread): if(auto* forest = worldScene.forestScene()) { forest->setBranchPoseBudgetBytes(4u * 1024u * 1024u); } aiverse::terraweave::ForestWindState wind; wind.xCmPerSec=700; wind.gustPermille=450; wind.branchFlexPermille=850; // optional, 0 = whole-tree-only worldScene.setVegetationWind(wind); worldScene.setVegetationPresentationTick(gameplayTick); A real PHYSIS solver may supply the world X/Z velocity components; this bridge does not require PHYSIS headers, does not alter collision/navmesh/authoritative physics and does not put wind in an ECS component. WorldScene continues forwarding the same validated wind state and tick, so native code uses the existing public methods. Limitations/QA debt: Branches are rigidly rotated at their joints rather than continuously bent as a skinned elastic curve. At high winds thin joints can show gaps. The source uses integer hashed wind phases but converts degrees to float matrices in renderer presentation; bitwise cross-GPU determinism is not promised. Very dense near forests can hit the CPU pose budget and switch to root-only motion. Source forEachDraw collectors must respect pose borrowing lifetime. No CMake, CTest, GPU screenshot, per-frame CPU benchmark or cross-platform rendering check has been executed. Dedicated test agent should validate hierarchy/pivot continuity, season + wind, LOD transitions, budget fallback, material/draw pointers and native PHYSIS integration before marking production ready.

h: Stage 31 — shared GPU crown wind for near Arbor and Horizon
x: Source implementation committed in feature/terraweave; independent compilation/CTest/GPU QA NOT RUN. Stage 31 extends Stage 28/30's existing root and rigid-branch sway with an optional GPU vertex-layer. It uses Renderer3D's existing Material Shader Graph vertexOffset hooks for GLSL and MSL, with no compute jobs, new render backend, separate shaders pipeline, GPU vertex buffers, extra atlas or re-bake-per-tick.

h: First-party vertex graph and instance payload
x: The new engine/render/TerraWeaveVertexWind.h provides canopyWindGraph(), one immutable engine-authored render::graph::Program containing both GLSL and Metal vertex code, plus canopyWindVertexParameters(wind,tick,yaw,strength). The graph preserves the fragment's original material/shading (outputs["color"]="sg_input") and emits bounded vertexOffset: wind vector * squared 0..1 height weight * low-frequency, spatially staggered sine wave with bounded higher-frequency gust. Crown roots remain fixed. It uses I.anim, already present in rigid model instance uniform U0, instead of allocating a new uniform buffer. The phase derives from the host's setVegetationPresentationTick (tick modulo ForestWindState::cycleTicks), not uncontrolled wall-clock shader time. X/Z velocities come from the same PHYSIS-neutral ForestWindState as CPU root sway; near instance yaw is inverted before passing the local vector, so wind remains oriented in world space. This is a trusted engine-generated program, not a user-authored shader source injection API. canopyWindGraph() returns a shared, immutable program to avoid creating a new shader-pipeline identity every tick or every tree. A zero wind vector or zero branch-flex/amplitude leaves the feature disabled and preserves existing materials. render::ModelDraw appends generic useVertexParameters, vertexParameters (float4) and maxVertexOffsetMetres. Renderer3D::drawModel places those four parameters in U0 Inst.anim only for eligible rigid, non-baked, non-lightmapped instances whose material has a graph. Baked animations and lightmap UV transforms retain priority; no U0 binary layout change was made. Other graph-using native projects may reuse the generic contract, but callers must not request the same U0 payload for baked skin/lightmapped models. Unknown/unbounded shader vertex offsets retain the renderer's conservative no-cull behavior; finite positive explicit bounds allow normal model/node frustum rejection and per-node LOD, with expanded geometry bounds. The TerraWeave graph sets a conservative 0.65m local-space maximum offset.

makeArborBranchLodModel encodes each foliage vertex's source height relative to the procedural tree skeleton as a normalized RGBA8 alpha wind weight. Foliage Material::vertexColors=false keeps this auxiliary weight from accidentally tinting/cutting out the leaf texture. Bark geometry/materials remain static under this vertex shader; wind still rotates the tree root and optional rigid branch nodes via the earlier Stage 28–30 paths. ArborForestAdapter applies the single graph only to foliage material slot 1 in shared per-species and per-azimuth override vectors. The shared program is attached when nonzero validated wind, branchFlexPermille>0 and maxLeanMilliDegrees>0; changing numerical wind/tick values updates per-instance parameters without creating another graph program. GPU flutter amplitude diminishes by LOD (High 100%, Medium 75%, Low 50%, Impostor 35%). If foliage cover is 0 during winter, the old bark-only primitive filter remains active; no hidden leaf vertex pass is submitted. Stage 29's split impostor geometry encodes zero weight at its lower foliage vertices and full weight at the top, so its root is anchored.

makeHorizonModel keeps one combined model, the original terrain primitive and shared forest-cluster primitive/atlas. Forest billboard vertex alpha now encodes a weight of 0 at the base and 1 at the canopy top; the forest material ignores vertex alpha in fragment shading so it cannot accidentally erase half the forest. Only its canopy material slot 1 opts into the same graph. TerraWeaveHorizonScene::setWind and setPresentationTick accept the same POD/tick as near Arbor. x: Feature source committed, build and tests deferred per the project owner's feature-first priority. Native games/PHYSIS can publish one bounded, immutable spatial wind snapshot for near Arbor trees and far Horizon, without linking PHYSIS to the forest renderer. The new engine/world/TerraWeaveWindField.h defines ForestWindField as a regular X/Z lattice of ForestWindSample {xCmPerSec,zCmPerSec,gustPermille}, all in signed world centimetres and cm/sec. The caller owns sampling from its actual PHYSIS wind/weather field; TerraWeave performs only the render-side interpolation: using namespace aiverse::terraweave; auto mutableField=std::make_shared<ForestWindField>(); mutableField->originXcm=-12800; mutableField->originZcm=-12800; mutableField->spacingCm=6400; mutableField->columns=5; mutableField->rows=5; mutableField->samples.assign(25,{800,0,400}); // Optionally fill specific nodes with different PHYSIS velocities. mutableField->samples[12]={-100,550,750}; mutableField->validate(); // reject invalid geometry/oversized winds std::shared_ptr<const ForestWindField> published=mutableField; worldScene.setVegetationWindField(published); worldScene.setVegetationPresentationTick(gameplayTick); // Publish a NEW immutable object when the weather field changes: worldScene.setVegetationWindField({}); Do not mutate a field after publishing it, even if a mutable shared pointer alias still exists. Limits: either empty/default field or 2..64 nodes per axis, at most 4096 node samples; spacing 100..10,000,000cm; all node coordinates within +/-kWorldLimitCm. Each node is validated using validateForestWind (horizontal magnitude <=5000cm/s; gust 0..1000). Invalid input fails before replacing the active world snapshot. sampleForestWindField(field,xCm,zCm,fallback) uses Q16 bilinear interpolation in absolute signed world centimetres, including negative positions. Outside the lattice it returns fallback; a half-node-spacing interior feather blends border values back to the fallback to prevent sudden direction/speed jumps at the field edge. No shader texture, RHI buffer, global mutable state or wall-time dependency. blendForestWind(local,macro,macroPermille) is a bounded integer interpolation of velocity and gust. Branch flex, period and lean maximum remain those of the fallback source. The near ArborForestAdapter samples the immutable field at each resident tree's stable world position. The forest scene configures these boundaries once; an unchanged/no-field setup retains its old execution path. The far TerraWeaveHorizonScene takes one observer-space macro wind sample in submit, shared by active and outgoing region draws during crossfade. This prevents a wind-vector discontinuity when the Horizon region changes and keeps HLOD geometry/atlas batched. WorldScene::setVegetationWindField forwards the same shared_ptr<const ForestWindField> to its optional forest and Horizon modules, with no terrain worker invalidation or TWH8 archive changes. Repeated pointer identity is a no-op; passing null clears the field so only uniform wind remains. Performance/ownership: the spatial field adds a handful of bounded CPU integer interpolations per submitted near-tree, not per ECS entity or terrain scatter candidate. Horizon performs one sample per submission rather than one per billboard cluster. Live weather updates need a new bounded field snapshot but do not allocate new vertex/texture buffers or recompile ShaderGraph programs. The sampler assumes the caller has validated the immutable field on publication; direct native callers MUST invoke field.validate() before sampling, rather than mutating the structure concurrently. h: Stage 33 — smoothly varying far-Horizon forest-cluster wind
x: Source code committed; build/CTest/real GPU checks are deferred. The far Horizon no longer needs to use one visually identical wind vector for every forest card in a multi-kilometre region. Each baked cluster receives a smooth, signed-world-coordinate variation in direction, gust strength and phase without adding draw calls, atlas textures, per-cluster ECS entities, or per-tick GPU uploads.

engine/render/TerraWeaveVertexWind.h adds horizonSpatialWindVertexColor(worldXcm,worldZcm,terrainSeed,canopyTop) and horizonSpatialWindGraph(). The former evaluates three deterministic 2.4 km wavelength world-space noise channels at a cluster's fixed X/Z centre and packs them into RGB8 in the already-existing render::ModelVertex::color. Alpha still holds the Stage 31 crown-weight: zero at the bottom edge, 255 at the top. Each pair of crossed silhouette cards for a cluster uses the same RGB wind sample, so the cards cannot diverge. The sampling is independent of observer cell and of how the Horizon region is streamed, including negative world coordinates and transitions between GPU-resident regions. No additional ModelVertex fields or static archive changes. At runtime, the first-party GLSL + Metal horizonSpatialWindGraph() uses the same inherited I.anim instance data as the Stage 31 crown graph. One shared macro wind vector (from the existing ForestWindField sampled at the observer location, or the fallback uniform wind) is rotated by at most 30 degrees per cluster, scaled between 0.75 and 1.25, and given a coherent but cluster-dependent phase offset. The exact per-cluster coefficients are fixed by the baked vertex RGB metadata and never require new CPU atlas work when the wind tick changes. Roots stay fixed because alpha is still zero at the card bottom. Direction, amplitude and phase vary smoothly across neighbouring clusters in world space rather than jumping between camera tiles. makeHorizonModel writes this metadata only to the distant forest vertices, not authored/coarse terrain. The far forest material already has vertexColors=false, ensuring these packed RGB8 values do not unexpectedly tint the foliage or modify opacity. No changes were made to near authored terrain, clipping, Q16 height welding, canopy atlas pixels or TWH8 serialized data.

// Already supported PHYSIS/game wind setup: worldScene.setVegetationWind(baseWind); worldScene.setVegetationWindField(immutableSpatialWind); worldScene.setVegetationPresentationTick(gameplayTick); // New optional comparison/quality switch. True by default: worldScene.setVegetationHorizonSpatialWind(true); // Return to Stage 31's identical macro wind for every far card: worldScene.setVegetationHorizonSpatialWind(false); Standalone TerraWeaveHorizonScene::setSpatialWindVariation(bool) and spatialWindVariation() expose the same switch, while WorldScene::vegetationHorizonSpatialWind() returns the current choice. The setting is presentation-only and should be set on the render/update owner thread before calling submit(); toggling changes only the shared ShaderGraph program selection, not the mesh, atlas, CPU bake or source revision. First use of a variant may incur the renderer's existing pipeline warm-up cost, not shader recompilation every simulation tick. The default is enabled; if zero wind is configured, neither the old nor new wind graph is active. Important scope distinction: The Stage 32 field is sampled exactly at the near individual tree and at the Horizon observer. Stage 33's independent far cluster variation is procedural, applied to that sampled macro vector. It is not a direct sample of the upstream PHYSIS field at every far cluster, and therefore is designed to make a 1–12 km treeline feel alive, not to simulate exact kilometre-scale weather boundaries or tornado trajectories. Exact per-cluster PHYSIS fields would require dynamic vertex metadata updates or an extra bounded GPU wind-grid resource, both outside this no-extra-resources mode. Bounded visual effect: The base Horizon GPU crown displacement strength remains 30% of the near-tree graph; the per-cluster amplitude is at most 1.25 and the graph's sine/gust multiplier is bounded. The current ModelDraw::maxVertexOffsetMetres = 0.65f remains conservative for the validated host wind bounds. GPU cost is extra vertex shader ALU and shared shader variant, not an additional draw or material per cluster. Real performance, frustum bounds, visual appearance in moving cameras, GLSL/Metal shader compilation and accurate material batching have not been tested yet. Future work: A dedicated QA agent must test this against Stage 31 default/no-wind parity, near-to-far velocity continuity, camera origin rebasing, negative coordinates, region crossfades, seasonal forest alpha cutout, Vulkan/GL/Metal render captures and batching. h: Stage 35 — sparse dirty-cluster GPU wind range updates
x: Functional source committed; compilation, CTest and GPU execution deferred by request. Stage 34 introduced exact per-cluster spatial wind samples from the host's immutable PHYSIS/game ForestWindField, but transmitted the entire forest-card vertex range to the RHI whenever even one sampled cluster changed. Stage 35 keeps the same public world and Horizon APIs and GPU format, while replacing that coarse update with a bounded sparse dirty-run planner.

engine/render/TerraWeaveHorizonWindPatch.h now provides the pure C++ planner: std::optional<HorizonForestWindUploadPlan> planHorizonForestWindUpload( std::span<const render::ModelVertex> oldVertices, std::span<const render::ModelVertex> newVertices, size_t maxRanges = 8, uint32_t fullFallbackPercent = 70); It compares only the vertex colour attributes of each eight-vertex forest cluster (two crossed cards), because weather updates never change position, normal, UV, indices, or material assignment. Adjacent dirty clusters are coalesced into one contiguous HorizonForestWindUploadRange{firstVertex,vertexCount}. With at most eight separate dirty runs and under 70% of clusters changed, only those ranges are transferred to the existing render::Model::vb by gfx::Device::updateBuffer; there is no GPU allocation, shader permutation or additional render pass. If more than eight disjoint runs are dirty, or at least 70% of clusters changed, the planner falls back to one complete forest suffix upload. The maximum resident CPU shadow is still 2 MiB per model and the scene's aggregate render-owner update budget remains 2 MiB per update() across both active and outgoing crossfade regions. If the chosen sparse or full plan would exceed the remaining budget or canUpdateSharedBuffers() is false, all writes for that model are deferred and the old safe rendering mode remains. No RHI write occurs before every selected range has been validated; the CPU copy and field revision are committed only after the planned sequence of writes is issued. Like Stage34, the backend's updateBuffer returns void, so a mid-sequence device failure cannot be detected here; engine-level device-loss recovery is still required. Important consequence: a small changed area can now be updated even when the full forest suffix is larger than the frame's remaining upload budget. For example, after the active region has consumed some budget, an outgoing region with one modified cluster may still be refreshed through one 8-vertex write instead of being repeatedly deferred. The planner reports an empty plan when the new quantized RGB8 values equal the existing values; this advances the applied weather-field revision with zero GPU traffic. A field snapshot can therefore change with no visual or RHI cost if all cluster samples quantize identically. HorizonForestWindPatchResult now reports ranges, changedClusters, and fullRangeFallback alongside readiness and uploaded byte count. The existing runtime count windOverlayPatchWrites counts region update batches, not individual RHI calls; windOverlayPatchBytes continues recording actual summed bytes. Added HorizonRuntimeStats::windOverlayPatchRanges, windOverlayChangedClusters, windOverlayFullRangeFallbacks, and windOverlayNoopRevisions to distinguish range traffic, changed cluster groups, dense/fragmented fallback, and no-change field revisions.

The algorithm operates on the same already-uploaded Horizon forest primitive, signed world-centimetre PHYSIS sample centres and quantized RG8/B8+A8 wind metadata as Stage34. No changes to WorldScene::setVegetationWindField, setVegetationHorizonExactWindField, season policy, terrain height/near weld/clip geometry, shared atlas or TWH8 format. HorizonGpuRegion still owns its matching compact vertex shadow through LRU and crossfade. Camera ticks alone do not trigger vertex uploads. CPU work still visits/samples all resident clusters to detect which quantized colours changed; only the GPU transfer is sparse. A pathological checkerboard of changed clusters intentionally uses the full-range fallback rather than issuing hundreds of RHI updates. Validation intentionally deferred: source commits and source inspection only; the new planner and RHI code have not been compiled, CTest has not run, and no Metal/Vulkan/GL backend or PHYSIS integration screenshots/performance data have been obtained. A later tester must verify one dirty cluster, adjacent clusters, eight vs nine disjoint runs, the 70% threshold, negative world coordinates, identical quantized samples, reduced bandwidth, active/outgoing combined budgets, disabled buffer updates, old cached GPU-region reactivation, and full-fallback correctness before release. Stage29's outdated impostor tests also remain pending.

h: Stage 36 — configurable far-Horizon wind upload quality policy
x: engine/world/TerraWeaveWindUploadPolicy.h exposes a small, genre-neutral HorizonWindUploadPolicy for C++ games. Default values retain Stage35 behavior: maxBytesPerUpdate=2*1024*1024 (one combined RHI bandwidth budget for active + outgoing crossfade GPU regions), maxSparseRanges=8 and fullFallbackPercent=70. Set it from the WorldScene owner/render update thread or directly on the optional TerraWeaveHorizonScene: aiverse::terraweave::HorizonWindUploadPolicy policy; policy.maxBytesPerUpdate = 256u * 1024u; // e.g. mobile: 256 KiB/update policy.maxSparseRanges = 4; // <= 4 runs per region policy.fullFallbackPercent = 85; // full range if >=85% dirty worldScene.setVegetationHorizonWindUploadPolicy(policy); auto applied = worldScene.vegetationHorizonWindUploadPolicy(); The Horizon native API is setWindUploadPolicy(policy) / windUploadPolicy(). validateHorizonWindUploadPolicy rejects uploads larger than 2 MiB, ranges outside [1,8] or density outside [1,100] before changing the live policy. Upload bytes may be zero: this explicitly pauses changed GPU wind metadata while allowing zero-byte identical-quantization revisions to advance. Raising it later retries the pending revision; no terrain or forest rebake is required. applyHorizonForestWindOverlay retains its backward-compatible default policy argument after remainingUploadBytes. It now passes the policy's range/density settings to the existing pure planHorizonForestWindUpload and enforces both the caller's remaining budget and the policy's own maximum before any RHI write. The TerraWeaveHorizonScene::refreshForestWindGpu owner-thread updater starts from the configured budget and consumes it across active and outgoing models, active first. A plan that does not fit is deferred as a complete region revision, with the existing macro wind shader fallback. This is a GPU traffic / update scheduling policy, not a CPU-cache quality selector: each GPU-resident model may still keep up to 2 MiB of forest vertex CPU shadow, and active/cached model residency remains controlled by the existing Horizon settings. There is no new vertex/index/texture allocation, HLOD topology change, shader, PHYSIS dependency, ECS/gameplay data, atlas format or TWH8 archive version. The host must not set the policy concurrently with update/submit. Limitations: A too-small budget can permanently defer a dense full-suffix update, leaving the safe macro presentation. Fragmentation thresholds and actual RHI cost must be tuned after GPU measurement; gfx::Device::updateBuffer remains void-returning, so multi-range writes have no device-loss atomicity guarantee. h: Stage 37 — bounded inactive Horizon wind CPU shadow cache
x: A Horizon GPU cache hit normally preserves its matching per-region CPU wind overlay (up to 2 MiB of forest vertex data plus cluster centres). The overlay is necessary for Stage35's sparse wind RGB patch planner: the GPU may already contain exact PHYSIS metadata rather than baked procedural colours. Discarding the overlay alone would make future colour comparisons wrong, and there is no guaranteed cross-backend RHI vertex-buffer readback. Stage37 adds a separate inactive cache CPU budget via <engine/world/TerraWeaveWindShadowCachePolicy.h>: aiverse::terraweave::HorizonWindShadowCachePolicy cpuPolicy{}; cpuPolicy.maxCachedShadowBytes=1u*1024u*1024u; worldScene.setVegetationHorizonWindShadowCachePolicy(cpuPolicy); auto configured=worldScene.vegetationHorizonWindShadowCachePolicy(); Direct scene use: TerraWeaveHorizonScene::setWindShadowCachePolicy(cpuPolicy) and windShadowCachePolicy(). The default is 16 MiB, above the maximum expected three cached wind overlays so pre-Stage37 default residency is preserved. The setting is bounded to 0..16 MiB and validated before publication. 0 prevents inactive GPU cache entries from retaining any CPU wind overlay; it does not disable the active or outgoing transition wind animation, nor does it change Stage36's per-update GPU transfer budget. This budget measures actual vector capacities of forestWind.vertices and forestWind.centersCm, not merely the current logical vector lengths. HorizonGpuRegionCache::trimWindShadowBytes(device,budget) runs only on the graphics owner thread. When the cached wind shadow capacity exceeds the budget, it retires the whole least-recently-used shadow-bearing cached GPU region, releasing its matching vertex/index/atlas resources through the normal RHI owner path and the associated CPU wind shadow together. It never removes a shadow from a retained GPU model, never touches the active model or current outgoing fade, and does not evict unrelated zero-shadow entries solely to meet this policy. The CPU budget is enforced immediately on retain() and again at the next update(device) after changes to policy or terrain-source revisions. It does not require a new GPU allocation, RHI readback, shader, asset format or CPU worker. When a camera returns to a region whose entire GPU cache entry was evicted under this budget, the existing AsyncChunkStream prepare/upload path restores the HLOD model and captures a coherent new wind shadow before uploading. It can reuse a matching CPU Horizon bake/asset archive if enabled; otherwise it re-bakes. The old visible proxy is retained while streaming. No stale GPU colour bytes are ever mistaken for a fresh CPU shadow. If the cache entry was not evicted, it retains both GPU and CPU metadata and remains an ordinary instant cache hit. A tight budget trades GPU cache hit rate/re-upload work for bounded dormant CPU shadow memory. HorizonRuntimeStats::gpuCachedWindShadowBytes reports the current capacity of inactive cached wind metadata, and gpuWindShadowBudgetEvictions cumulatively counts whole GPU cache entries evicted specifically because of this CPU budget (such evictions also increment the preexisting general GPU cache eviction count). Active and outgoing data, general CPU HorizonBake archives, regular vertex patch references, model upload staging and GPU memory are not included in the reported byte count; the feature is intentionally narrow. Ownership and compatibility: PHYSIS/game still publishes an immutable ForestWindField; no new field sampling, mesh, terrain seams, extra ECS entities, GPU shaders/passes or TWH8 archive version. No genre dependency. Invoke setters on the owning WorldScene/Horizon update thread; a setter cannot safely release RHI buffers itself and applies trimming during the next update(device). Existing HorizonGpuRegionCache::retain calls remain source-compatible via its defaulted final wind-shadow budget. h: Stage 38 — lossless dormant Horizon GPU wind-shadow compression
x: Stage37 had to evict a complete GPU cache entry whenever its inactive CPU wind shadow exceeded the configured budget. Stage38 optionally saves dormant CPU memory without evicting the matching GPU region. The wind field, PHYSIS owner, procedural map, material shader and existing RHI GPU buffers remain unchanged. Use the public Stage37 policy from a native project: aiverse::terraweave::HorizonWindShadowCachePolicy policy; policy.maxCachedShadowBytes=2u*1024u*1024u; policy.compressCachedShadows=true; // Stage38 optional; default false worldScene.setVegetationHorizonWindShadowCachePolicy(policy); This setter stays on the WorldScene owner thread. The optional TerraWeaveHorizonScene::setWindShadowCachePolicy accepts the same POD. The per-update GPU upload policy is separate (HorizonWindUploadPolicy). All default API values preserve Stage37 behavior (compression disabled unless explicitly enabled). The current 0..16 MiB inactive CPU-shadow budget remains valid and unchanged. Lossless storage: TerraWeaveHorizonWindCompression.h provides packHorizonWindVertexBytes and unpackHorizonWindVertexBytes with a simple bounded bytewise zero-run/literal codec (1..128 bytes per token). It stores raw ModelVertex bytes, including all 32-bit float fields, RGBA wind metadata and joint/weight fields; it never rescales or recomputes geometry or a PHYSIS wind sample. This is memory-only storage inside the process, not a persistent file format. Before packing, the HorizonForestWindOverlay must be intact and already paired with its GPU-resident model. A compressed overlay keeps its signed world-centimetre centersCm, the exact applied wind revision and first vertex offset, and stores packedVertices plus packedVertexCount instead of a full vertex array. It compresses already-cached entries when the policy is enabled during a live scene, at the next update(device) before budget trimming. windCompressionAttempted prevents repeatedly scanning incompressible entries every frame. The dormant CPU budget now counts the actual capacities of raw vertices, packed bytes and cluster centres. Only if compressed/raw capacity still exceeds the budget will Stage37's whole-region LRU eviction run. There is no GPU upload, new buffer, atlas rebuild or geometry regeneration when a shadow is packed. On a camera return, HorizonGpuRegionCache::take decodes compressed data to a fresh std::vector<render::ModelVertex> before transferring the already-uploaded GPU model into active ownership. Decode validates token boundaries, exact output byte count, cluster count and the existing 2 MiB forest-vertex limit, publishes only on full success, and leaves GPU bytes untouched. appliedRevision remains unchanged, so Stage35 can compare the exact last-uploaded RGB values if a newer wind snapshot is pending. A malformed stream is handled by the device-aware cache take overload: release the entire corrupted GPU cache entry and use the normal async re-prepare/re-upload path; never present a bogus exact-field shader. Allocation failures are not suppressed and must follow normal host memory-error handling. The Stage37 gpuCachedWindShadowBytes now includes packed byte vector capacities and resident cluster centres. These are accounting counters, not measured GPU speedups. h: Stage 40 — opt-in host-fed adaptive Horizon presentation quality
x: Stage40 adds a bounded runtime presentation controller in engine/world/TerraWeaveHorizonAdaptiveQuality.h. It composes only the four Stage39 profiles (BatterySaver, Mobile, Balanced, Desktop) and the existing Stage33–38 wind shader/bandwidth/CPU-cache policy. The terrain/forest geometry, near seam, atlas, PHYSIS field, native ECS state, GPU resource topology and TWH8 archive remain untouched. The controller is disabled by default and never starts timing a frame by itself.

The game or platform host already responsible for framing/presentation supplies measured CPU and/or completed GPU frame times in microseconds, with a monotonically increasing frame index: using namespace aiverse::terraweave; HorizonAdaptiveQualityConfig adaptive; adaptive.enabled=true; adaptive.minimum=HorizonPresentationQualityPreset::Mobile; adaptive.maximum=HorizonPresentationQualityPreset::Desktop; adaptive.initial=HorizonPresentationQualityPreset::Balanced; adaptive.targetFrameUs=16667; // 60 Hz frame budget, not a GPU benchmark worldScene.setVegetationHorizonAdaptiveQualityConfig(adaptive); // On the scene owner thread, after the host has a frame measurement: const HorizonFrameTimingSample timing{ .frameId=completedFrameId, .cpuFrameUs=measuredCpuFrameUs, .gpuFrameUs=measuredCompletedGpuFrameUs // 0 when unavailable }; const bool switched=worldScene.submitVegetationHorizonFrameTiming(timing); auto state=worldScene.vegetationHorizonAdaptiveQualityState(); Direct scene API: TerraWeaveHorizonScene::setAdaptiveQualityConfig(config), adaptiveQualityConfig(), adaptiveQualityState(), submitAdaptiveFrameTiming(timing). A native WorldScene with no Horizon module returns false for submissions. setVegetationHorizonAdaptiveQualityConfig applies the initial profile immediately only when enabling adaptation. Disabling keeps the current profile. Explicit manual calls to the Stage39 whole-policy setter or any of the four existing individual presentation setters disable adaptation rather than fighting the developer's choice. Wind-field publication, normal simulation ticks and camera updates do not count as manual overrides. Re-enabling starts a fresh history. The engine's gfx Device::gpuFrameMs() can report a backend's last completed GPU duration, but this is not universally implemented and may be delayed. The host must distinguish real completed timing samples from unavailable/stale values and may submit zero for missing GPU or CPU. Stage40 does not synthesize GPU time or equate its own HorizonRuntimeStats::gpuUploadMs with the whole-frame render duration. At least one nonzero actual CPU/GPU frame duration is required; a frame with no measurements is ignored. An individual sample of more than 10 seconds, an out-of-order/duplicate frame index, or disabled adaptation is ignored. Missing frame IDs break continuous streaks, so occasional metrics must not masquerade as sustained FPS degradation. CPU and GPU together use the worst available duration. This is global frame quality control, not evidence that TerraWeave itself caused all CPU/GPU work.

HorizonAdaptiveQualityConfig defaults: minimum=Mobile, maximum=Desktop, initial=Balanced, targetFrameUs=16667, downgradePercent=115, upgradePercent=80, downgradeFrames=30, upgradeFrames=240, cooldownFrames=240. Consecutive valid frame IDs more than 15% above the target trigger a one-level downgrade after 30 samples. Consecutive samples at least 20% under the target trigger a one-level upgrade after 240 samples. The neutral band clears both streaks. No further switch occurs until at least 240 frame IDs have elapsed since the previous change; neither direction can pass the configured min/max. No elapsed-wall-clock timers or nondeterministic thread callbacks are involved. Validation rejects quality ranks outside [0,3], reversed bounds, initial outside bounds, target outside 4–100 ms, downgrade threshold outside 101–200%, upgrade outside 25–99%, downgrade streak outside 2–600 frames, upgrade streak outside 2–3600, and cooldown above 36,000 frames. The controller is purely presentation state driven by host measurements and does not belong in authoritative ECS save/replay. advanceHorizonAdaptiveQuality(config,state,sample) is a backend-free deterministic state step for later unit tests.

{ "terraweaveHorizon": { "quality": "high", "presentationQuality": "balanced", "adaptiveQuality": { "enabled": true, "minimum": "mobile", "maximum": "desktop", "initial": "balanced", "targetFrameUs": 16667, "downgradePercent": 115, "upgradePercent": 80, "downgradeFrames": 30, "upgradeFrames": 240, "cooldownFrames": 240 } } } quality still controls the immutable Stage39-era geometry bake. presentationQuality optionally sets the original runtime profile; adaptiveQuality only opts into automatic presentation changes. It remains OFF without "adaptiveQuality":{"enabled":true}. If initial is missing, it inherits the optional static presentationQuality (otherwise Balanced). The default minimum is Mobile, or BatterySaver if the initial static profile is battery-saver; projects can override bounds explicitly. All levels use battery-saver|mobile|balanced|desktop, and invalid names/types/bounds fail manifest parsing instead of silently accepting an unsafe policy. The manifest does not install a frame timing provider; the host must still feed the per-frame measurements.

HorizonRuntimeStats now includes adaptiveQualityEnabled, adaptiveQualityLevel, adaptiveQualitySamples, adaptiveQualitySwitches, adaptiveQualityDowngrades, adaptiveQualityUpgrades, and adaptiveQualityLastFrameUs. Existing effective Stage39 policy diagnostics indicate the currently applied bandwidth/cache options after an adaptive change. WorldScene synchronizes its public policy getters after each automatic switch. Diagnostics are not GPU performance benchmarks. Adaptive control may respond to frame costs from completely unrelated systems; the host should opt in only when this behavior is desired. A Stage39 low-bandwidth profile can postpone dense wind vertex updates and safely show the macro field until later; automatic quality selection does not bypass Stage36 safety checks. Configure appropriate frame sampling and GPU completion handling for each native platform. Feature-first verification: code committed and source re-read via GitHub only. Native C++ compilation, CMake/CTest, frame time instrumentation, Metal/Vulkan/OpenGL visual parity and actual FPS gains NOT RUN. The separate QA agent must test reset-on-gap, duplicates and malformed samples, exact threshold boundaries, 30/240 sample streaks, cooldown, min/max clamp, manifest precedence, enable/disable/manual override, missing GPU data, stale field revisions, crossfade GPU residency, and renderer safety before PR #24 may merge.

h: Stage 41 — automatic native RTS/FPS frame timing bridge for Horizon adaptive quality
x: Stage40 exposed an opt-in, host-fed adaptive Horizon presentation controller, but it did not connect any real game-frame source. Stage41 connects the two existing native game clients to the AIVERSE graphics measurement APIs while respecting async GPU completion and keeping terrain/PHYSIS/ECS independent. The new reusable header engine/world/TerraWeaveHorizonFrameTimingBridge.h defines terraweave::HorizonFrameTimingBridge. Its begin(gfx::Device&,world::WorldScene*) and finish(WorldScene*,Clock::time_point) are called once around an actual native client frame. begin is only active when worldScene->vegetationHorizonAdaptiveQualityConfig().enabled is true; otherwise it returns false, drops pending samples, and makes no GPU timing requests. It records a monotonically increasing frame ID, requests gfx::Device::timeGpuFrame(tag) after the backend has begun a frame, and polls takeGpuTimings() on following frame callbacks. The signed GPU completion is associated with its ORIGINAL frame ID using a reserved tag prefix, not misreported as the current frame. The adapter also measures real std::chrono::steady_clock CPU callback elapsed time, not simulation dt, game tick duration, gpuUploadMs or the displayed FPS estimate. The bridge buffers at most a small bounded number of pending frames (eight GPU-lag frames plus the current submission); frames are delivered to WorldScene::submitVegetationHorizonFrameTiming in increasing frame-ID order, after the matching GPU timestamp arrives or its eight-frame wait expires. Unsupported/non-ready/invalid GPU queries automatically submit the real CPU-only sample, with gpuFrameUs=0. Missing/invalid CPU measurements are likewise zero; never invent a nonzero metric. The controller's existing consecutive-frame and hysteresis policies apply to the delivered samples. No glFinish, waitUntilCompleted, new RHI API, CPU/GPU synchronization stall or new per-frame GPU buffer is introduced. deliveredGpuFrames(), deliveredCpuOnlyFrames(), pendingFrames() and lastFrameId() are lightweight adapter diagnostics. All methods run on the owning game/render thread. Actual game paths now integrated: RTS / composable strategy client: apps/client/GameClient.h/.cpp owns a bridge beside the streamed worldScene_. During an actual streamed-world game frame, after the platform beginFrame but before Horizon scene update/draw, it requests a tagged GPU interval; immediately after the client's UI/render submission it delivers measured CPU work. It discards pending submissions on map loading, world teardown/new match and planet/no streamed-world paths. No network, RTS simulation, camera or UI data model change. FPS client: apps/fps/client.cpp owns the same bridge beside streamedScene. It calls begin just after its existing device.beginFrame, and finish after its existing endPass/endFrame, measuring its entire native FPS callback from entry. Shutdown discards pending samples. No FPS weapon/network/prediction, server tick, collision, terrain or renderer backend change. These calls are automatically dormant for worlds without Horizon or without an explicit adaptiveQuality.enabled=true in the manifest (or native API setting). No CLI switches or external memory allocations at startup are necessary for the disabled case. Backend timing ownership: AIVERSE already exposes gfx::Device::timeGpuFrame(tag) and takeGpuTimings(); Metal records a tagged command buffer and returns its asynchronously completed GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime interval, while supported GL may use GL_TIME_ELAPSED around its active interval. These report different GPU scope semantics by backend (Metal whole command buffer, GL from query start until end-frame), NOT isolated TerraWeave render time. Unsupported backends return false and the adapter uses CPU-only data. The takeGpuTimings() API destructively drains all ready device timing tags, so the adapter must be the one timing consumer for these game-client Device instances, or future integrations must introduce a shared device timing

h: Stage 42 — generic per-device GPU timing fan-out
x: Stage41's RTS/FPS HorizonFrameTimingBridge previously drained the entire gfx::Device::takeGpuTimings() queue. This was incompatible with an editor benchmark or any future Prisma/SpectraFX/VFX timing consumer using the same graphics Device. Stage42 moves all known non-backend GPU query consumers to a shared, genre-independent RHI service: gfx::Device::gpuTimingRouter(), implemented in engine/gfx/GpuTimingRouter.h and described in docs/render/GPU_TIMING_ROUTER.md. The router registers an independent subscriber for each subsystem, assigns a private GPU raw query tag, maps it back to the consumer's original frame tag at asynchronous completion, and delivers results into isolated bounded subscriber queues. A subscriber's take(subscriber) cannot remove another subscriber's data. Only the router polls the backend's destructive takeGpuTimings(). Unsupported or busy backends can still reject a query; the Stage41 Horizon bridge retains its measured CPU fallback. For native games no new manifest key is required. Stage41's bridge now uses device.gpuTimingRouter().subscribe/request/poll/take/cancel and unsubscribes at RTS/FPS shutdown. It cancels its own metadata for a GPU frame that exceeded the Stage41 eight-frame timeout. Stage40's adaptive hysteresis and Stage39 profiles are unchanged; CPU/GPU measurements remain asynchronous and backend scoped. This is not an isolated Horizon GPU render-pass timer. The shared Device router also serves the editor Scene batching benchmark, RenderBench, GeometryBench and the instancing GPU validation preview. These consumers keep original tag semantics but no longer drain one another's completed GPU results. A subsystem may submit its own custom tag or obtain a new subscriber without creating a new graphics Device, render pass, shader or GPU buffer. Public limits: up to 32 subscribers, 64 pending GPU requests across subscribers, and 64 queued completed samples per subscriber. Rejected GPU requests should degrade gracefully to CPU-only timing or no timing; no synchronous fence waits are added. Every caller uses the graphics Device owner thread. Important backend limit: GL currently supports only one active GL_TIME_ELAPSED request per frame. Independent routing does not imply simultaneous exclusive GPU time measurements; a second request can fail. Metal may return the same whole command-buffer GPU duration under multiple subscribers' tags. Do not interpret these as the independent GPU costs of two rendering features or promise performance gains. Use actual backend device measurements and diagnostics before drawing conclusions. Feature-first validation: GitHub source read/writes verified; Clang/GCC, CTest, native editor/RTS/FPS/bench runs, Metal/GL/Vulkan concurrency and GPU timings NOT RUN. The independent testing agent must verify interleaved same-device subscribers, tag ownership, cancel/unsubscribe, queue overflow/rejection, GL busy fallback, Metal completion ordering, device recreation, and teardown. Keep PR #24 Draft. See Stage42 handoff.

h: Native alpine source: optional ridged massifs
x: TerraWeaveAlpine.h accepts an appended AlpinePeak::morphology field. LegacyCone remains the default: existing six-field initializers and old landscape recipes retain their exact old source. RidgedMassif combines a zero-slope elliptical support, seeded domain warp and five ridged octaves with feedback. Samples use signed integer centimetres and Q16 arithmetic. It is a stateless generation profile, not a hydraulic erosion or rock-physics solver. Peak support, shear, height and valley protection retain their existing bounds. The native aiverse_terraweave_landscape exporter accepts each peak's "morphology":"ridged_massif", "cragged_massif" or "legacy". Unknown names reject. CraggedMassif retains the same bounded support while moving modest relief to one-third-radius scales with .42 octave amplitude rolloff and a higher broad carrier. Existing legacy/ridged samples stay exact; it is cosmetic relief, not physical hydraulic erosion. The alpine valley recipe places its broad mountain range behind the forest area, with 128 terrain tiles and an explicit NEREID river. Export to a new directory on the external build drive: aiverse_terraweave_landscape --recipe examples/terraweave/alpine-valley.json \ --out NEW_PACK --materials "$(python3 tools/pkg/aiverse_pkg.py fetch terrain-pbr)/textures" python3 tests/terrain/check_landscape_export.py NEW_PACK The export audit compares actual neighbouring glTF edge heights/normals and checks render vertices against the shared integer planting-height grid. Rebake material masks and vegetation from the new ground.json; retain planted root depth when moving existing trees/rocks to the new surface. A static export is not the live erosion/fall host. The example's full visual acceptance and renderer budget remain separate from source/seam correctness.

engine/render/TerraWeaveTerrainLod.h provides appendTerrainPatchLods(model, patch, targetErrorPixels=1.5f) for a CPU model before upload. The native landscape exporter calls it after world-space normal smoothing and tangent generation. The live mutable makeEarthworksTerrainModel path retains its original full-resolution surface and collision by default. Input must be the complete original patch triangulation on a power-of-two grid (8..128 cells), with matching heights and consistent shared normals/UVs/colors. Skins, animation, morphs, baked-lightmap UVs, uploaded buffers and existing LODs reject. Invalid source input preserves model values. LOD0 vertices/attributes/indices stay exact; three appended alternatives use strides 2, 4 and 8. Each retains all original outer edge segments, so neighbouring tiers join without skirts or edge cracks. For a 129-sample tile the four triangle counts are 32768/8952/2680/1080. Only used vertices are appended for each tier; this adds CPU/GPU asset storage. Each tier measures maximum vertical deviation against the original piecewise linear surface, including coarse edges crossing fine-grid X, Z and diagonal edges. Its maximum pixel threshold targets the requested error through the shared renderer's conservative projected-size metric, with descending caps 512/256/128. This is a presentation budget, not a collision simplification or a universal guarantee for vertex-displaced geometry. The existing renderer owns camera/shadow selection and opaque spatial crossfade. Both meshes render inside a crossfade band; waiting more frames does not remove that spatial overlap. Exports retain the existing glTF rtsLods representation and independent shadow LOD policy; catalog tile entries append lods (stride/triangles/errorMetres/ maxPixels). Old readers can ignore these fields. Check terraweave_model, the shared-height export audit, actual per-frame submitted triangles and near/far pixel comparisons. Metal fixture verification does not establish mobile/Vulkan parity or an FPS gain. CPU visual picking/deformed object parity remains a separate editor acceptance task.
