InstallOptions::workerThreads / map "physis.workerThreads" (1 = serial default, 0 = hardware, N lanes). Atmosphere, surface and the disaster read/compute/commit passes split their cell ranges over a persistent thread pool; flood transfer is gathered per receiving cell, so results are bit-identical to serial for every lane count (test physis_parallel; serial checksum A/B against the previous sources is equal). Custom providers passed to advanceWith while lanes are active must only read the World. Measured on the user's Mac (Release, 28 logical cores, other builds running, load ≈24), 1024×768 grid with storms + disasters, 10 ticks, 3 runs: 1 lane 161.6–162.5 ms/tick; 2 lanes ×1.92–1.95; 4 lanes ×3.69–3.73; 6 lanes ×5.33–5.40; 8 lanes ×6.62–7.00. Linux VM (Debug, 4 cores): ×3.54 on 4 lanes.

"physis.streaming": {"chunkCells": 32} splits the grid into chunks. Any entity with an ActivityAnchor (position + radius; players, cameras, vehicles, scripted regions) keeps chunks within its radius simulated; other chunks are dormant (weather, surface, fire, flood frozen; dormant cells are walls for flood transfer and never ignite). The mask (ActiveChunks) and anchors are persistent, hashed ECS data recomputed by the physis.streaming system at the start of every tick. No anchors = whole grid. Static anchors can be listed in "physis.anchors". This is simulation streaming (what is updated); cell data stays resident — no disk paging. Test physis_streaming; bench aiverse_physis_streaming_test bench 1024 10.

.github/workflows/physis.yml builds the aggregate CMake target aiverse_physis_tests (every aiverse_physis_*_test(s) target, plus aiversemcp when present) and runs ctest -R ^physis_ on Linux x64, Linux arm64, macOS and Windows MSVC, and builds the core tests with Emscripten and runs them in Node. Before this, the hand-written target list missed physis_nature_presentation / physis_nature_cues, and the workflow failed on main with ctest exit 8 (run 44956413363).

A tornado is simulation, not a visual: a StormEvent (kind Tornado) plus a TornadoTrack on the same entity. Every PHYSIS wind reader already sees the vortex through windWithStormsAt (tangential swirl, radial inflow, updraft): forces, nature contacts / stress (trees fracture), sampleNatureField, the presentation frame. The system physis.tornadoes runs once per tick right after the climate/storm/disaster pass and before forces: Part Rule Path drift (StormEvent driftPerTick), wander (heading + random turn from the track's own RNG state, reflected inside bounds or the PHYSIS grid), waypoints (constant speed, optional loop) Life startTick/durationTicks of the storm + rampTicks spin-up/decay; TornadoTrack::intensity 0..1 scales tangential wind, updraft and inflow Fire (enableDisasters) cells under the core lose fire.suppression of their fire per second (blown out); burning cells with fuel in the ring grow by fire.fanning per second (fanned) Debris debris.perSecond pieces torn up in the core (up to debris.max per tornado), carried by the same wind with quadratic drag + PHYSIS gravity, land on the cell elevation, expire after lifeSeconds or 3 s on the ground. Stored in the TornadoDebrisField resource — no entities, so other modules' entity allocation is unchanged Carried objects host entities with Transform + NatureCarriable (mass, area, drag, liftWindSpeed) are lifted when the horizontal wind exceeds the lift speed and carried until they land. Not for Box3D bodies (use applyPhysisToBody) Damage entities with a Transform within damageRadiusMeters (full in the core, linear to 0 at the radius) get damagePerSecond × intensity through GameModule::environmentDamage(sim, target, amount, tornado); the module applies its own health/armour rules. RTS: pure damage via dealDamage (invulnerable types such as trees and units off the map are skipped). Default implementation: no damage Vegetation trees/structures with NatureStressReceiverComponent (forces + nature contacts + stress enabled) load from the vortex wind and fracture through the existing outbox → TerraWeave fall bridge. RTS tree units are invulnerable in the sample rules Determinism: Fixed-point only, tornadoes and carried objects in entity-index order, debris in creation order, explicit RNG in the track. Persistent + hashed: physis.tornado_track, physis.nature_carriable, physis.tornado_debris (registered only when tornadoes are enabled, so maps without them keep the old save manifest and checksums).

A non-empty "tornadoes" array turns the feature on (and storms with it). Per-second values are converted with the simulation tick rate; startSeconds/durationSeconds/rampSeconds may replace the ...Ticks keys. The same parser (PhysisTornadoAssets.h) backs MCP physis_validate / physis_set, so authoring and runtime accept the same documents. "physis": { "grid": { "originX": 0, "originZ": 0, "width": 16, "height": 12, "cellSizeMeters": 4, "seed": 11 }, "climate": { "baseTemperature": 21, "baseHumidity": 0.55 }, "tornadoes": [{ "id": "valley_twister", "center": [16, 9], "coreRadiusMeters": 2.5, "outerRadiusMeters": 12, "heightMeters": 45, "tangentialWind": 42, "updraft": 16, "radialInflow": 6, "clockwise": false, "startSeconds": 2, "durationSeconds": 150, "rampSeconds": 4, "path": { "mode": "waypoints", "speed": 1.4, "loop": true, "points": [[24, 16], [32, 22], [40, 30]] }, "damagePerSecond": 6, "damageRadiusMeters": 5, "fire": { "suppression": 0.8, "fanning": 0.5 }, "debris": { "max": 40, "perSecond": 8, "massKg": 0.4, "areaSqMeters": 0.06, "lifeSeconds": 14 } }] } Wander instead: "path": {"mode": "wander", "speed": 2, "turnDegreesPerSecond": 30, "seed": 3, "heading": 0, "bounds": [minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ]}. Sample map: templates/skirmish/maps/tornado_valley.json ("Tornado Valley", map index 2). C++ hosts: InstallOptions::enableTornadoes = true (persistence), then spawnTornado(world, storm, track) at runtime; advanceTornadoes(world, hooks) is the pure pass for custom schedulers. No Lua API yet.

buildNaturePresentation now samples windWithStormsAt (vegetation wind lattice and particle wind include storms) and fills frame.tornadoes / frame.debris. PhysisNatureRuntime drives: SpectraFX funnel (physis_tornado: rising, widening dust spiral, ground skirt, dark specks; local space, moved every frame with extrapolation between ticks; scale = core radius) and one physis_tornado_debris chunk per airborne piece. Projects may override both in fx/. Sound: positional physis_tornado_loop roar (synth fallback added by addPhysisTornadoSounds). TerraWeave: the vortex shows in the spatial vegetation wind lattice (windFieldNodes). NEREID: within 3 outer radii of a tornado the water wind takes the swirl speed at the camera focus. Switch: "presentation": {"tornado": false} (funnel/debris effects off; simulation unchanged). Tests: physis_tornado (paths, envelope, wind, fire, debris, carried objects, host damage, map install, save/load/continue checksums, parser errors), physis_tornado_cues (frame, FX/audio planners, built-in effects and sound parse). Limits: no Lua API; debris is a point cloud (no collisions with units/buildings); damage reaches only entities with Transform; vortex is an authored analytic field, not CFD; the editor nature preview does not draw funnels yet.

h: Fire whirls, water and ground (2026-11-22) — engine/physis/PhysisTornadoNature.h
x: Every map tornado carries a TornadoNature next to its TornadoTrack (C++: the spawnTornado(world, storm, track, nature) overload, defaults from defaultTornadoNature(tickRate)). A tornado without it keeps exactly the rules above. Part Rule Fire drawn in Each tick the vortex takes fire.intake (share per second) × intensity × ring weight of the fire of every PHYSIS cell under its core and ring (1 in the core, linear to 0 at the outer radius). The drawn fire (in burning m²) is added to heat, which loses fire.decay per second. fireness = heat / (heat + fire.halfHeat) (0..1): it grows with the amount and strength of the fire, a small fire gives a weak whirl, without fire it fades. Blow-out vs. fire whirl Core blow-out is fire.suppression × (1 − fireness): a dust tornado still snuffs fire in its core, a fire whirl no longer does. Ring fanning is multiplied by 1 + fireness. Ignition Every fuel cell under the vortex (not over water) catches fire with chance fire.ignite × fireness × intensity × weight per second, strength fire.igniteStrength × fireness. Random numbers come from the tornado's own RNG state (TornadoNature::rng), in grid order. Embers fire.embersPerSecond × fireness burning embers are thrown from the ring (up to fire.maxEmbers), carried by the vortex wind like debris (TornadoEmberField), burn out after fire.emberLifeSeconds, and set a fuel cell on fire with chance fire.emberIgnite where they land. Heat damage Entities with a Transform inside the outer radius take fire.heatDamagePerSecond × fireness × intensity (full in the core, linear to 0 at the outer radius) through GameModule::environmentDamage, in addition to the wind damage. Water Open water comes from GameModule::environmentWaterDepth(sim, x, z) (new, default 0; the generic game core returns 2 m for ~ cells and 0.3 m for = fords) or the PHYSIS local flood depth. The vortex is over water when 3 of 5 samples (centre + 4 on the core ring) are deeper than surface.waterThresholdMeters. Land tornado over water Loses surface.waterDecay vigor per second, recovers surface.recover on land; at 0 it dissipates (intensity 0, storm disabled). Heat is quenched by fire.quench per second, no ignition, no embers. Waterspout surface: "auto" decides at the first active tick: born over water = waterspout ("water" / "land" force it). Its wind is surface.spoutStrength × the authored wind, it raises spray (presentation) and loses surface.spoutLandDecay vigor per second on land, so it breaks up within seconds ashore. Ground scour On land the core (out to 1.5 core radii) removes erosion.rate × intensity² metres per second from GroundScourField cells (physis.scourCellMeters, default 1 m, sparse, at most 65536 cells) down to erosion.maxDepthMeters; the soil (up to erosion.capacityCubicMeters) is carried and dropped (erosion.deposit share per second) in a band 1.5–2.5 core radii around the centre. Over water the carried soil sinks. groundScourAt(world, x, z) gives the change in metres (negative = scoured). Map data (inside a tornado; all values per second, all optional): "fire": { "suppression": 0.8, "fanning": 0.5, "intake": 0.6, "decay": 0.2, "halfHeat": 50, "quench": 1.5, "ignite": 0.4, "igniteStrength": 0.6, "embersPerSecond": 6, "maxEmbers": 48, "emberLifeSeconds": 8, "emberIgnite": 0.5, "heatDamagePerSecond": 3 }, // "whirl": false = old blow-out only "surface": { "kind": "auto", "waterThresholdMeters": 0.2, "waterDecay": 0.08, "recover": 0.1, "spoutStrength": 0.55, "spoutLandDecay": 0.6 }, // or "auto" / "land" / "water" "erosion": { "rate": 0.04, "maxDepthMeters": 0.6, "deposit": 0.25, "capacityCubicMeters": 40 } // or false Defaults: intake 0.5, decay 0.2, halfHeat 60 m², quench 1.5, ignite 0.4, igniteStrength 0.6, embers 6/s (max 48, 8 s, ignite 0.5), heat damage 4/s, waterDecay 0.08, recover 0.1, spoutStrength 0.55, spoutLandDecay 0.6, erosion 0.04 m/s, max 0.6 m, deposit 0.25, capacity 40 m³. New physis keys for fire scenes: "ignitions": [{"center": [x, z], "radiusMeters": 6, "streng

PHYSIS owns climate/weather, natural event fields and environmental force/gravity policies, but never Box3D rigid-body integration itself. NEREID (Water agent, draft PR #23) owns water-body geometry, flow, contacts and buoyancy; TerraWeave (Terra agent, draft PR #24) owns terrain, biomes, vegetation and land rendering. Use the opt-in host integration plan and precise metre/centimetre conversion in physis-nereid-terraweave-integration.md. The existing PHYSIS shallow-flood prototype is not an authoritative replacement for NEREID water. When a host uses NEREID as the water authority, set InstallOptions::floodMode = FloodMode::ExternalAuthority: PHYSIS continues to update fire and quake but clears/skips its local shallow-flood depth. This opt-in switch is authored and covered by tests; cross-module NEREID/Terra integration and real build/CTest verification remain pending. This is a design contract only. Terra/NEREID integration, rendering and cross-system tests remain NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT RUN on this branch.

h: Wind, gravity, storms and optional Box3D usage
x: #include "engine/physis/PhysisIntegration.h" #include "engine/physics/PhysisBox3D.h" // link AIVERSE::physics, if enabled // During GameModule::setup: aiverse::physis::InstallOptions options; options.enableStorms = true; options.enableForces = true; // only if generic ECS force outputs are required aiverse::physis::install(sim, options); aiverse::physis::StormEvent tornado; tornado.kind = aiverse::physis::StormKind::Tornado; tornado.center = {10_fx, 0_fx, 10_fx}; tornado.eyeRadiusMeters = 20_fx; tornado.outerRadiusMeters = 150_fx; tornado.heightMeters = 500_fx; sim.world().add<aiverse::physis::StormEvent>(sim.world().create(), tornado); // Physics owner: after the authoritative PHYSIS tick, just before Box3D Scene::step: for (aiverse::physics::BodyHandle body : optedInBodies) aiverse::physics::applyPhysisToBody(box3dScene, sim.world(), body); box3dScene.step(); PHYSIS authoritative types are Fixed ECS data. The external Box3D bridge converts from/to Box3D floats only at this boundary. Box3D already applies scene gravity; the adapter applies delta gravity and wind drag via Scene::applyForce, not a second gravity force. Do not also apply ForceResult::totalForce to the same Box3D body. Opt-in kinematic character controllers need a separate locomotion integration; neither hardcoded scalar CharacterParams::gravity nor native Body motion is overridden here. Physics is opt-in. Run ./run-tests.sh --filter '^physis_' and, with -DAIVERSE_ENABLE_PHYSICS=ON, run CTest physis_box3d and the existing physics_runtime / physics_scene. These tests are authored but NOT RUN. There are no physically accurate Navier–Stokes hurricanes, tornado debris destruction, N-body orbital solvers, Terra foliage wind deform or water surge in the current implementation.

h: Read-only combined sampling (for Terra, VFX, Physics and tools)
x: #include "engine/physis/PhysisPresentation.h" aiverse::physis::NatureFieldSample nature; if (aiverse::physis::sampleNatureField(sim.world(), queryPosition, nature)) { const auto wind = nature.windVelocity; // 3D Fixed metres per second const auto gravity = nature.gravityAcceleration; // m/s squared if (nature.hasAtmosphere) { const auto rain = nature.environment.rain; // normalized, not water volume const auto snow = nature.environment.snowpack; } if (nature.hasHazards) { const auto fire = nature.hazards.fire; } } sampleNatureField is immutable and returns true when PHYSIS is initialized, including outside the climate grid; hasAtmosphere/hasHazards indicate which grid data is present. It does not depend on TerraWeave/NEREID/Box3D headers. Terra should consume this as a read-only environment overlay and sample NEREID's canonical waterline separately. No production Terra/NEREID adapter or render scene is linked yet. Save compatibility: Simulation::PersistentEcsRegistry stores a strict list of schema IDs. Therefore PHYSIS does not register the new optional wind/gravity/storm/force component types by default. Set InstallOptions.enableWindZones when persisting WindZone/WindShelter, enableGravityFields for GravityField/GravitySettings, enableStorms for StormEvent, and enableForces for ForceReceiver/ForceOutput. Existing Stage 1–5 save registry remains unchanged when these switches are off. Switching flags on an existing saved game changes the manifest and is not an automatic save migration. Save and load must use the same feature flags. Tests are authored, not run.

#include "engine/physis/PhysisDiagnostics.h" aiverse::physis::DiagnosticRequest query; query.originX = -16; query.originZ = -16; query.width = 32; query.height = 32; query.stride = 1; query.layer = aiverse::physis::DiagnosticLayer::WindSpeedMetersPerSecond; aiverse::physis::DiagnosticRaster raster; if (aiverse::physis::sampleDiagnosticRaster(sim.world(), query, raster)) { // raster.rawValues = Fixed::raw data; raster.valid = inside PHYSIS grid // diagnosticNormalized(raster, i) = 0..65535 for view/shader coloring } The diagnostic API is CPU-only and read-only: it does not render an overlay in Scene, change physics, mutate the authoritative World, or sample NEREID water. It is capped at 65,536 cells per query; missing climate/hazard cells are marked invalid, not replaced with misleading zeros. Only PHYSIS standalone shallow flooding is displayed by LocalFloodMeters (NEREID remains canonical water authority). A future editor adapter may upload/use the returned raster as a heatmap, with no PHYSIS dependency on the renderer. Tests are authored but not yet confirmed by native CTest/CI.

h: Indexed reads for large diagnostic or editor sampling sessions
x: The default windAt, gravityAt, stormsAt, sampleNatureField, and sampleDiagnosticRaster remain available and do not require an index. For repeated queries against one committed ECS snapshot, use the opt-in spatial accelerator: #include "engine/physis/PhysisSpatialIndex.h" #include "engine/physis/PhysisDiagnostics.h" aiverse::physis::FieldSpatialIndex index(sim.world(), {.tileSizeMeters = 256, .maxTilesPerVolume = 1024}); // Stable values pinned to the index's original COW world snapshot: aiverse::physis::NatureFieldSample nature; if (index.sample(queryPosition, nature)) { const auto wind = nature.windVelocity; const auto gravity = nature.gravityAcceleration; } // Optional accelerated debug raster for vector field layers: aiverse::physis::DiagnosticRequest request; request.layer = aiverse::physis::DiagnosticLayer::WindSpeedMetersPerSecond; aiverse::physis::DiagnosticRaster image; aiverse::physis::sampleDiagnosticRasterIndexed(index, request, image); The transient index groups bounded wind zones, shelters, gravity fields and storm volumes into X/Z world-metre tiles; final 3D range/timing checks remain in the canonical PHYSIS policy. Global gravity and very large volumes use a bounded fallback list; candidate traversal preserves ECS insertion/pool order for Fixed-point accumulation and gravity-priority tie-breaks. Build once after an authoritative committed tick, use for many queries and rebuild after an ECS change, rollback or climate/storm movement. It is not persistent state, not a spatial index for climate WeatherFront/QuakeEvent simulation, and not a world streaming/job scheduler. The index holds a copy-on-write World snapshot; keeping many historical indexes resident may retain COW pages and increase memory. No native benchmark or compiler success has been observed yet; tests are source-only until CTest runs.

The editor now discovers apps/editor/windows/PhysisWindow.cpp automatically through its existing AIVERSE_EDITOR_WINDOW registry and CMake glob. Open Мир → PHYSIS · Природа. The panel is closed by default. When the active Editor::sim() has PHYSIS initialized, it displays a read-only raster of live PHYSIS ECS climate, surface, wind, gravity, fire, earthquake or standalone local flood state. The panel does not call Simulation::step on the game's World, does not edit game.json, map documents or Box3D, and does not inject genre-specific scene entities. When the current game does not initialize PHYSIS, the user can explicitly create a separate PHYSIS demo World in the panel, with wind, a tornado, local gravity, a climate gradient and a fire. Demo step controls advance only that independent World; they do not mutate the current project. Layers, palette, sample stride, window size (8..64 PHYSIS cells) and X/Z centre can be adjusted. Clicking a cell displays the fixed-point value, climate cell coordinates, 3D wind and gravity. The panel outlines active wind zones (W), storm radii (T/H) and gravity volumes (G). Scalar weather/hazard layers read ECS directly; wind/gravity layers use the transient FieldSpatialIndex. Refresh occurs on source change, new tick or explicit Обновить данные. Edits/rollback that retain the exact tick require manual refresh until the editor gains revision tokens. PhysisDebugPalette.h exposes DebugColor, DebugPalette, debugGradient and diagnosticColor for native CPU tools. This is presentation-only; colour values are never fed back into simulation. Not yet implemented: world-space overlay projected into the Scene camera, a live PHYSIS agent Inspector for editing component data, general project game.json PHYSIS auto-install, GPU textures and particle/VFX integration. The window is an actual editor GUI implementation, but native editor compilation, UI screenshot and manual clicking have NOT been verified. Use ./run-tests.sh --filter '^physis_' and build/test the editor on macOS before claiming it works end-to-end.

h: Stage 18 — real Scene viewport overlay and Inspector map authoring
x: After the main merge 810feba70f01cdc35003ac80ea8486f39dc16049, the editor Scene adds an opt-in transparent heatmap drawn in the actual 3D view, projected through the existing Camera::worldToScreen, plus world-space rings for WindZone, StormEvent and GravityField. The toolbar controls live under Мир → PHYSIS · Природа; toggle Показать 3D-оверлей в «Сцене». This is an ImGui presentation overlay (not shaded 3D geometry or Box3D collision) and uses the same read-only DiagnosticRaster and bounded FieldSpatialIndex. It only reads a live simulation that already has PHYSIS; it does not install or tick the active world. The shared Inspector under Свойства карты now includes a PHYSIS section: Создать PHYSIS, Настроить PHYSIS, Удалить PHYSIS. The edit dialog has structured controls for grid origin/dimensions, seed, temperature, humidity, wind/gravity/storm/disaster/force opt-in and NEREID external-water authority, plus an extended JSON tab. Применить validates the complete draft and calls MapDoc::beginEdit only once; existing Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z Undo/Redo is shared with other map edits. Invalid JSON/settings are rejected without changing the map. Both regular and FPS map formats are supported via apps/editor/PhysisAuthoring.h; no genre-specific ECS logic is added. Authored data is stored under the map-level "physis" JSON key. It is a declaration, not automatic live ECS writeback. Any native project can opt in from its generic GameModule::setup: #include "engine/physis/PhysisProjectConfig.h" void MyGame::setup(aiverse::Simulation& sim, const aiverse::Json& rules, const aiverse::Json& map) { aiverse::physis::installFromMap(sim, map); } installFromMap returns false for absent/disabled configuration; otherwise it strictly reads grid/climate parameters and flags, registers persistence and one fixed-tick PHYSIS system, and returns true. It does not install itself into RTS, FPS or other genre modules automatically. As of Stage 19, validated individual windZones, storms and gravityFields arrays are spawned deterministically when explicitly installed via installFromMap. Each asset requires a stable unique id; the native importer sorts IDs before creating ECS entities, including across field types. Unknown extra keys are preserved by the editor but are not interpreted by the importer. Runtime IDs are authoritative ECS entities; the authored JSON ID is not itself a persisted component. Validation: stage 18 source tests physis_scene_geometry, physis_project_config, and physis_authoring were written and registered in CTest. The last one needs aiverse_editor_core and runs in the editor / unified build; the PHYSIS-focused headless CI compiles the other two. Studio validation was updated to build/run all three and compile the editor. As of this commit, C++ build, CTest, CI PASS, editor interaction and screenshot are NOT RUN / UNVERIFIED. See the separate Stage 18 handoff.

h: Stage 19 — individually authored WindZone, StormEvent and GravityField
x: Open Мир → PHYSIS · Природа. The section PHYSIS — объекты и Gizmo can create, list, select and remove wind zones, tornadoes/hurricanes and local gravitational fields even while the game is not running. Existing MapProps Inspector shows the selected PHYSIS field's position, radius and type-dependent properties. The advanced field JSON editor preserves unknown extra properties but rejects invalid typed values. Turn on Редактировать маркеры мышью and click a W/S/G marker in Scene: drag in the X/Z plane; hold Shift to change Y. The first effective movement calls MapDoc::beginEdit and subsequent movements call MapDoc::touched; one whole drag equals one Undo/Redo operation. When the marker editor is off, normal genre-independent Scene mouse selection works as before. A PHYSIS marker is a map document asset, not a fake live ECS selection or a Box3D body. An active game World is not mutated. Map example: { "physis": { "enabled": true, "grid": {"originX": -4, "originZ": -4, "width": 8, "height": 8, "cellSizeMeters": 100, "seed": 8}, "climate": {"baseTemperature": 15, "baseHumidity": 0.5}, "enableStorms": true, "enableWindZones": true, "enableGravityFields": true, "floodMode": "ExternalAuthority", "windZones": [ {"id": "wind-1", "center": [0,0,0], "radiusMeters": 120, "velocity": [15,0,0], "gustAmplitude": 3} ], "storms": [ {"id": "storm-1", "kind": "Tornado", "center": [50,0,25], "eyeRadiusMeters": 20, "outerRadiusMeters": 150, "heightMeters": 300, "tangentialWind": 45, "updraft": 25} ], "gravityFields": [ {"id": "gravity-1", "mode": "Uniform", "center": [0,0,0], "radiusMeters": 200, "acceleration": [0,-2,0], "overrideBaseline": true} ] } } The generic native installFromMap(sim, map) validates all assets before changing PHYSIS World state and spawns components in lexicographic stable-ID order; corresponding enableWindZones, enableStorms, enableGravityFields flags are required for nonempty arrays so persistence schemas match. Stable IDs are authoring keys and are not added to the persistent ECS component schema; deterministic spawn order and unchanged map/save manifest are required for consistent replay. Edits to authored map JSON do not hot-reload live PHYSIS or rebind existing ECS entities. The core library contains no editor/genre/Box3D/NEREID/TerraWeave dependency. Water remains NEREID-owned; setting ExternalAuthority disables PHYSIS's separate shallow flood. Box3D dynamics are still an optional independent consumer of PHYSIS forces. Source tests added: physis_field_assets and (editor_core only) physis_field_authoring, plus expanded physis_project_config persistence fixture. Registered in focused Linux/macOS PHYSIS and Studio CI. Native compilation, CTest and graphical drag QA NOT RUN / NOT VERIFIED.

h: Stage 20 — Scene field radius gizmos and metre-grid snapping
x: The shared PHYSIS field panel now offers Move and Radius tools. When the radius tool is active, select a W/S/G map field and drag its world-projected radius handle (on the +X perimeter). The Scene draws the selected field's outer X/Z perimeter. Storm radius editing changes outerRadiusMeters, never the eye radius; the canonical native validator rejects invalid eye/outer pairs. The gizmo uses the editor camera's ground-plane ray at the field's current Y; it does not modify 3D height or perform full 3D volumetric rotation. Snap to grid is opt-in and has a configurable step of 0.25..1000 metres. Move snaps X/Y/Z to the world origin grid; radius snapping is applied before validated bounds. Negative coordinates use symmetric rounding. Height dragging keeps an unsnapped accumulator to avoid losing sub-grid mouse motion. The snap settings are editor-session preferences, not additional map/ECS schema fields. Each successful move/resize drag remains one MapDoc Undo/Redo transaction. No live PHYSIS World, Box3D body, NEREID water, or game genre state is edited. The existing tests/physis_field_authoring_test.cpp has new source fixtures for radius Undo/Redo, invalid radii, no-op edits and negative-coordinate snap. h: Stage 23 — opt-in authoritative field reconciliation and command replay
x: The new engine/physis/PhysisFieldRuntime.h connects the existing pure PhysisFieldChangePlan with an explicit, rollback-owned ECS field identity registry. Unlike static startup-only installFromMap, this optional path supports replacing a set of authored WindZone, StormEvent and GravityField sources at the Simulation command boundary. It is intentionally generic and has NO dependency on FPS, RTS, Box3D, NEREID, TerraWeave or the editor. Host integration example (choose a unique command ID in your own module): constexpr uint16_t kPhysisEdit = 53123; void MyGame::setup(Simulation& sim, const Json& rules, const Json& map) { if (!physis::installEditableFromMap(sim, map)) return; // PHYSIS absent or disabled } void MyGame::applyCommand(Simulation& sim, const Command& cmd) { if (cmd.type == kPhysisEdit) { // The authoritative server MUST authorize system player=0. std::string error; (void)physis::applyFieldEditCommand(sim, cmd, kPhysisEdit, &error); return; } // Other genre-independent gameplay commands ... } // Trusted editor/server-side action; NEVER apply World edits in Scene. uint32_t scheduledTick = 0; std::string error; const bool queued = physis::submitEditableFieldsFromMap( sim, editedMap, kPhysisEdit, scheduledTick, &error); This queued result only means the command was accepted for submission; the authorizing host can reject it later on expected-revision mismatch. Simulation::submit and CommandSink provide the existing command transport. The host must reserve a command ID, reject spoofed system commands at the network ingress, and implement the applyCommand dispatch above. A client cannot gain authority simply by using Command.player=0. The runtime registry is a new opt-in persistent World resource named physis.field_runtime (version 1). It contains monotonic edit revision, stable authored ID -> (Entity, kind, canonical serialized fingerprint). A snapshot and native file save therefore retain the same identity and revision; rollback restores both. Unchanged fields retain dynamic runtime state (including a drifting storm); edited fields of the same kind keep the same Entity handle; removed sources are destroyed; type changes cause Remove+Add with a fresh Entity generation. Changes are staged on a copy of World and committed together, so validation/plan failures leave it untouched. A no-op command still consumes one edit revision. The new optional install enables persistent component schemas for ALL three field kinds so they can be added/retyped while a session is running. This deliberately changes the strict save manifest; it must be enabled on both save and load. Existing installFromMap and saves remain unchanged. No implicit save migration has been implemented. The edit wire payload is a field-wise binary snapshot with a protocol ID, expected revision, sorted unique sources and a size bound. It packs into the standard Simulation Command.args, so the payload must fit within 4096 total int64 words (up to 32760 bytes, one word reserved for length). Larger replacement sets are rejected; atomic multi-command chunking is NOT implemented. The actual maximum number of fields depends on encoded source properties, not the standalone 2048-field parser limit. Because the full source set is transmitted, edits with obsolete revisions reject rather than overwriting concurrent changes. Only authored field collections are editable at this stage. Changes to climate grid settings are rejected by submitEditableFieldsFromMap, and changes to the overall flood/disaster policy are NOT hot-reloaded. There is no automatic map Inspector -> active GameModule command registration, network authorization layer or GUI acknowledgement yet; a native host must opt in and use its existing command system explicitly. CTest target physis_field_runtime has source fixtures for encoding and network Command wire roundtrip, identity-preserving updates, add/remove, type replacement, replay, SimSnapshot rollback, persistent save/load, revision conflict, invalid network

The panel reports: Unavailable, Idle, Queued, Applied, Conflict or Rejected. Queued is NOT Applied. Applied requires the expected ECS registry revision and matching stable authored fingerprints; the status is invalidated when another edit supersedes the values or a rollback restores earlier state. A dropped handler or conflicting revision is reported, not hidden. For REMOTE servers, physis::admitAuthorizedFieldEdit is a generic server- only admission hook. A server transport supplies a principal derived from its authenticated connection and an ACL callback, validates the untrusted request and re-encodes a new player-0 system Command through Simulation:: submit. Files: apps/editor/PhysisLiveEdit.h (no ImGui; capability + status), apps/editor/windows/PhysisWindow.cpp (panel), engine/physis/PhysisFieldRuntime.h (trusted admission policy), and engine/sim/Simulation.h (const module accessor). PHYSIS has a separate, versioned admin protocol over existing net::Conn (reliable UDP, WebSocket or loopback). It is NOT the ordinary player InputFrame or a shortcut around AIVERSE networking authorization. Runtime protocol files: engine/physis/PhysisRemoteProtocol.h, PhysisRemoteServer.h and PhysisRemoteClient.h. The client uses unique instance/request IDs, bounded retries, Query-before-resend on reconnect, and explicit Unknown/Queued/Applied/Rejected/Conflict/Denied receipts. The server stores a bounded idempotent receipt cache by authenticated principal+client instance+request ID and rejects ID reuse with changed payload. Only one new PHYSIS edit can be queued at once. Applied is reported ONLY after scheduled Simulation tick and matching ECS FieldRuntimeState revision plus source fingerprints. Queued != Applied. The server host must run ServerGateway::poll on a separately AUTHENTICATED admin/editor net::Conn, supply a trusted connection principal and ACL callbacks, then call ServerGateway::observe after authoritative Simulation ticks. It must reserve a PHYSIS command type and dispatch Stage 23 applyFieldEditCommand in GameModule::applyCommand. No client-controlled player=0 command is trusted. apps/editor/PhysisRemoteEdit.h::EditorLink accepts only a host-attached already authenticated connection. The PHYSIS window shows remote status, confirmed revision, request ID, and refresh/send/retry controls. A host must provide actual transport authentication/credentials; the editor does not open an anonymous privileged socket. The Stage 24 local play-test route remains separate. Wire bounds: 40 KiB protocol frame and Stage 23 32760-byte typed Command.args payload. Large multi-part atomic uploads are NOT yet implemented. The server cache is IN-MEMORY, so after server restart an old receipt can become Unknown and client may see Conflict. Revision checks prevent duplicate effects but a crash-durable exactly-once ACK requires a persistent journal. Outstanding client requests can be exported/restored, including original IDs, but the host must persist request counters or rotate the client instance. The separate opt-in PhysisRuntimeFields.h/TrackedFromMap registry from another agent does not replace this Stage 23 FieldRuntimeState runtime. Do not install both. No change to legacy installFromMap, FPS/RTS authority, NEREID Water, TerraWeave or Box3D. h: Stage 26 — durable admin journal and authenticated loopback endpoint
x: PHYSIS remote editing now includes a file-backed write-ahead receipt journal and an opt-in, native loopback-only admin WebSocket listener. The existing FieldRuntimeState / installEditableFromMap / GameModule::applyCommand / applyFieldEditCommand remains the canonical editor authority. The separate RuntimeFieldRegistry / FieldCommandHost path introduced concurrently by other agents is NOT connected to this editor and must not be enabled at the same time. New generic engine files: engine/physis/PhysisRemoteJournal.h: FileJournal stores a bounded checksummed snapshot of the server's request/receipt cache in an operator-owned private directory. Entries include trusted principal, client instance and request ID, exact original edit bytes, typed authored fingerprints, expected revision, scheduled tick and status. It uses unpredictable exclusive temporary file creation, write flush/ fsync, atomic rename/replacement and POSIX directory sync. A bad checksum or missing permission rejects startup rather than silently dropping history. Only ONE server process may own a journal path. engine/physis/PhysisAdminAuth.h: versioned admin challenge/proof handshake using a new random nonce and keyed BLAKE2b. The shared secret is not sent. Principal string is tied to proof, checked against a host-supplied key lookup, followed by server ACL and reserved PHYSIS command type. Client-supplied player=0 / instance tokens never grant rights. engine/physis/PhysisAdminEndpoint.h: LoopbackAdminEndpoint owns a real net::WsListener listening at 127.0.0.1 ONLY, and admits authenticated connections to the Stage 25 ServerGateway. It requires a nonzero host-reserved PHYSIS command ID, ACL callbacks and a private journal file. LoopbackAdminConnector can authenticate a native editor connecting over local ws://127.0.0.1. The PHYSIS window uses its EditorLink bridge to poll this connection and show pending/status. apps/editor/PhysisRemoteEdit.h: EditorLink::connectLocalAdmin accepts host-supplied principal, secret from secure storage, nonzero instance ID, assigned slot and command type. It does not auto-generate secrets, open anonymous network connections or grant admin rights. Example native setup: aiverse::physis::remote::admin::LoopbackAdminEndpoint endpoint( privateJournalFile); endpoint.open(localPort, reservedFieldCommandType, serverKeyLookup, canRead, canWrite, &error); // Restore matching Simulation checkpoint BEFORE opening endpoint. // In host event loop: endpoint.poll(sim, monotonicMs); sim.step(); endpoint.afterTick(sim); Credential lookup, key rotation and ACL are host-owned. The admin port is never allowed to bind publicly from this API. IMPORTANT: the current native AIVERSE WebSocket client supports ws:// but NOT wss://; this handshake alone is not transport encryption. For off-machine admin access, use an already encrypted authenticated tunnel to local loopback or implement real native TLS/WSS. Never expose plain remote ws:// and call it secure. Crash recovery: Persist the original edit intent BEFORE scheduling the Simulation command. A failed journal write prevents any new admission. Persist Queued and later Applied/Rejected/Conflict receipts. Restored Unknown intents may be reconciled against saved ECS revision+fingerprints; same original packet can be re-admitted only after ACL and revision checks. Duplicated packet IDs cannot apply twice. On restart, restore the matching Simulation World/checkpoint and pending command state first, then attach the file journal, and only then accept authenticated admin connections. The journal and the Simulation checkpoint are two separate stores, not a single atomic DB transaction. A power failure between writing them can leave an ambiguous outcome. Receipt recovery must report Unknown/Conflict rather than inventing Applied. This is more robust than Stage 25's volatile-only receipt cache, but it is not a blanket guarantee of crash-atomic exactly-once acknowledgment. No changes to default PHYSIS save manifest or NEREI

h: Stage 26 crash-recovery correction — persisted Queued != pending command
x: During Stage 26 hardening, ServerGateway::restoreJournal was changed to restore every persisted Queued receipt as Unknown and clear the old scheduledTick. The previous server's in-memory Simulation command queue may have vanished on restart, even when the sidecar journal still says Queued. A loaded Queued receipt is not proof of execution. After the host restores its matching ECS World/checkpoint, observe() reconciles Unknown against FieldRuntimeState and authored fingerprints. If already committed, the request is Applied. If revision advanced incompatibly, it is Conflict. If unchanged, keep Unknown; the EXACT original authenticated Submit can be re-admitted with the same ID after ACL and revision checks. No new PHYSIS permission or public listener is created by this fix. New source fixtures in physis_admin_journal test both crash before the queued command executes and crash after its ECS effect but before the Applied sidecar flush. These tests are AUTHORED, NOT RUN. The journal and Simulation save remain separate durability domains: this is safe resubmission/reconciliation, NOT full cross-file crash-atomic exactly-once commit. Stage-specific handoff: docs/agent-handoffs/physis-stage26-queued-recovery-2026-11-19.md.

h: Stage 26 crash-recovery fix for durable field receipts
x: An authenticated PHYSIS editor request may be persisted in the file journal as Queued before the authoritative Simulation step. If the process crashes, its pending in-memory command queue may be gone even though the journal still says Queued. Recovery now converts Queued to Unknown, then compares the restored ECS state: matching revision + fingerprints proves Applied; a still-current revision permits the original authenticated request to be resubmitted once. This prevents premature Rejected or incorrect Applied reports after restart. Test fixtures in tests/physis_admin_journal_test.cpp cover both crash-before-commit and crash-after-commit-before-receipt; native CTest has NOT RUN. See docs/agent-handoffs/physis-stage26-queued-recovery-2026-11-19.md.

h: Stage 64 — ignore stale remote ACK after Apply
x: RemoteClient enforces monotonic receipt handling on an active connection: an accepted terminal receipt cannot be overwritten by late Queued/Unknown/etc. When an Applied operation is checked after reconnect, a Query for the original ID must actually be sent before accepting its reply; a pre-query response and stale Queued are ignored. An Unknown during Applied verification is Uncertain: never automatically replay a formerly acknowledged Submit. Manual retry() after a verification timeout is a Query-only operation, and begin() rejects uncertain/in-progress verification. No wire format, ECS schema, NEREID Water, TerraWeave or Box3D changes. V1 has no per-Query correlation nonce, so arrival after a Query is not cryptographic proof that a delayed Applied packet was generated for that Query. A future protocol version should add correlation and server generation. Source fixtures are authored, but native engine CTest has NOT RUN. See docs/agent-handoffs/physis-stage64-monotonic-ack-2026-11-19.md.

h: AIVERSE NEREID — architecture and integration contract
x: NEREID is the universal, genre-independent water framework of AIVERSE. It is not a fork of RTS water nor a renderer-only material. Existing legacy water remains active until explicit, tested migration.

modules/rts/view/RtsWater.{h,cpp}: spline networks, shores, geometry, water cells. modules/rts/view/GameShoreView.{h,cpp}: shores, props and foam rendering. apps/editor/core/WaterOps.{h,cpp}: editor bake and water operations. apps/editor/windows/WaterWindow.cpp: water editing UI. tests/tests_water.inc: existing water/shore/map behavior. docs/water.md: existing scene/map representation. The previous waterNetwork is baked into map tiles and the RTS simulation consumes these tiles, not the source water body splines. Do not change baked tile semantics, game saves, terrain generation or shore placement by introducing NEREID.

Public C++ headers: "engine/world/nereid/NereidWater.h" "engine/world/nereid/NereidWaterSystems.h" Package: AIVERSE::lib_nereid_water from libraries/catalog.json. Namespace: aiverse::lib::nereid. ECS component contract: WaterBodyComponent: authoritative definition, fixed-point coordinates (X/Z horizontal, Y up), kind (Ocean/Lake/River/Pool/Puddle), footprint (Infinite/Box/Disc), surface/bottom Y, flow, overlap priority, enabled. WaterProbeComponent: authoritative query point provided by host input, physics, transform sync or game-specific policy. WaterContactComponent: ECS-owned sampled result and tick; not kept as independent FPS/RTS vector state. WaterSample: selected generation-safe body Entity, kind, surface/bottom, clamped immersion depth, flow, priority and found/submerged bits. Only point-in-footprint sampling is implemented at this stage. A water kind does not automatically supply a spline, hydrodynamics or waves.

Host input/movement/physics writes Transform or WaterProbeComponent. Optional addWaterProbeFromTransformSystem(sim,name) copies the shared Transform::pos into probes; it is not needed for custom probe producers. addWaterSamplingSystem(sim,name) scans water bodies and updates WaterContactComponent. Higher priority wins; same priority takes higher surface, then lowest packed Entity ID. Query does not depend on pool order. Game-specific swim, buoyancy, currents and damage stages consume contact. Renderer may consume presentation snapshots and add GPU-only detail. This is O(body count * probe count); spatial acceleration is planned. No bodies or probes are structurally changed during the sampling pass.

Authoritative values use aiverse::Fixed / integer, never floats or GPU wave samples. No RNG or genre branches in NEREID core. Register registerNereidWaterPersistence(sim) during the host module's setup, before stepping/sealing, to add versioned native ECS schemas: nereid.water_body, nereid.water_probe, nereid.water_contact. World-native snapshots, hashes and serialization are host-integration concerns: do not add a second mutable mirror. The host must also persist any independent Transform/movement state affecting future probes. Add water to an arbitrary native game's public target by linking AIVERSE::lib_nereid_water. Do not link FPS/RTS for the library. tests/ecs_nereid_water_test.cpp exercises two unrelated hosts, rollback, COW, native save/load and checksum for NEREID components. These are authored tests, not yet executed in the current implementation.

Stage 2: shared water-body geometry adapters (legacy waterNetwork, spline river, closed lake polygon), explicit world position/terrain height contract, accelerated spatial queries; test old water editor/bake parity. Stage 3: render backend with low/medium/high profiles, depth/shore foam, SSR/planar reflection fallback, LOD and underwater view. Stage 4: composable water mechanics (buoyancy, swimming, drag, currents, wakes, impulses, waterfalls), deterministic CPU game state + GPU visual layering. Stage 5: editor UX, auto-shores, weather coupling, serialization upgrades, native and existing FPS/RTS adoption, platform performance/CI. Do not claim stage 3/4 features exist because corresponding WaterKind values are present in the enum.

"engine/world/nereid/NereidBuoyancySystems.h" exposes the optional AIVERSE::lib_nereid_buoyancy package. It runs only when Entities have WaterBuoyancyComponent, WaterVelocityInputComponent, WaterContactComponent and WaterForceComponent. computeWaterForces uses fixed-point immersion fraction = clamp(contact.depth / immersionHeight, 0, 1). Output water acceleration = up * buoyancyAcceleration * fraction - (velocity - waterFlow) * linearDrag * fraction. This excludes ordinary gravity and does not integrate movement or alter contacts. A host's canonical physics owns all velocity and spatial updates. Stage order must sample water BEFORE buoyancy and integrate AFTER. Missing component or sample from another tick => zero output. WaterVelocityInput is a per-tick view of host canonical physics state; if the host retains velocity in an existing ECS component, copy it once immediately before buoyancy rather than inventing a persistent second velocity owner. Register registerNereidBuoyancyPersistence in setup when enabled. ecs_nereid_buoyancy_test is authored and not yet run.

NereidGeometry.h defines WaterGeometryComponent as an optional per-body footprint override: a closed simple polygon (lakes, pools), or a variable-half-width X/Z polyline (rivers, canals). Geometry has a maximum of 256 nodes for bounded ECS save and replay. Polygon banks and spline bank edges are included in queries. Self-intersecting polygons and holes are not a supported contract. The shared sampleWater queries the optional component on each water body Entity. If the component is absent or disabled, original v1 Infinite/Box/Disc footprints continue to work. An invalid enabled geometry covers nothing; it cannot silently expand to a larger fallback. Body height, flow, priorities and stable ID tie-breaks are unchanged. Geometry is independent from RTS/editor waterNetwork; no implicit migration. To opt in: call registerNereidGeometryPersistence(sim) in native setup before the registry seals, and attach WaterGeometryComponent to WaterBodyComponent entities. This adds the separate nereid.geometry v1 schema, leaving the water-body v1 wire format alone. AIVERSE::lib_nereid_water is still the native link target. This is a pure deterministic CPU footprint policy. It has no spatial index or geometry mesh generation, waves, shoreline features, VFX or editor adapter. Geometry component storage, snapshot and rollback are ECS owned. Test: ecs_nereid_geometry_test (authored but NOT RUN).

h: Stage 4 — transient water spatial broadphase (authored, not built)
x: NereidQueryIndex.h provides an optional acceleration adapter. It builds a deterministic AABB hierarchy from WaterBodyComponent and optional WaterGeometryComponent data and samples it with the same considerWaterCandidate selection as the reference sampleWater. Finite Box/Disc/Polygon/RiverSpline volumes are indexed by conservative horizontal bounds. Infinite oceans stay outside the tree. Both check coversWaterBody before yielding a sampled contact. Bodies with invalid enabled geometry are excluded rather than falling back to box/ocean. Register either addIndexedWaterSamplingSystem or addWaterSamplingSystem; both consume a probe and overwrite WaterContactComponent with the same tick. The index is constructed on each simulation tick and discarded before the tick ends. It stores a reference to the World and must not be reused after World writes, structural changes, restoring a snapshot or loading a native save. Nothing about the indexed data itself is authoritative or persistent. No changes to NEREID persistence schemas, renderer, RTS/editor waterNetwork or existing save streams. Two-host indexed/reference parity test: ecs_nereid_query_index_test (author-written, NOT RUN yet).

h: Stage 5 — read-only adoption of legacy baked-water raster
x: The legacy waterNetwork stores editor-side Catmull-Rom splines and sea shorelines in cells, with variable river width in metres. Its waterCells function adds a 0.75-cell edge tolerance, interpolates sea frontiers and supports headland/shore features. Consequently, interpreting its original control points directly as NEREID straight spline segments would not preserve existing wet cells. Instead, NereidRasterImport.h implements a deterministic pure converter from a generic binary raster to disjoint WaterBodyComponent rectangles. Row-run compression also merges identical spans in adjacent rows. This represents the baked water mask exactly at cell centres, not an equivalent continuous shoreline. Coordinates are X/Z world metres, cellMeters is explicitly Fixed, and body heights are provided by the caller. There is no change to existing NEREID schemas. engine/view/game/NereidLegacyWaterAdapter.h is the only legacy-dependent header: importWaterNetworkToNereid uses the untouched legacy buildGeometry + waterCells rasterizer, and is appropriate for map source previews/baking. importBakedWaterCellsToNereid consumes the actual canonical game map cells (~ by default), including post-bake changes; prefer this for native gameplay migration. The adapter returns data without altering the input map or automatically registering a game system. A native host opts in by creating entities, registering registerNereidWaterPersistence, adding probes and choosing one contact-sampling stage. No old RTS/editor save protocol, shore/bank geometry or navigation is migrated automatically. Baked cell masks lose per-body sea/river provenance, so callers specify a common WaterKind and an explicit water surface/depth. To support multiple semantic water levels, source distinct masks explicitly. Fixture: ecs_nereid_legacy_raster_test (authored, NOT RUN) compares all centres of an 80x64 legacy river/sea/strait map against both NEREID sampling policies and verifies native save/COW/rollback.

h: Stage 6 — native pipeline and adaptive sampling
x: The new NereidAdaptiveWater.h is an optional deterministic selection policy. addAdaptiveWaterSamplingSystem evaluates ECS water-body and contact-pool counts each tick; it uses reference scanning below minWaterBodies or minProbes, or the transient stage-4 BVH otherwise. This choice is not driven by elapsed time or presentation frame rate, and both paths write identical WaterContactComponent data under the same overlap/tick semantics. It introduces no persistence schema. Only one contact-sampling system may be scheduled. NereidNativeWater.h composes the existing reusable components and systems from any native GameModule::setup without RTS/FPS/renderer dependencies: registerNativeWaterPipeline(sim,prefix,cfg). Optional switches enable geometry persistence, buoyancy persistence and force calculation, and transform-probe synchronization; the adaptive sampler is the one contact stage. Physics integration remains the host's responsibility. spawnNativeWaterBodies(world,bodies) creates water body Entities deterministically; it deliberately does not invent an independently writable water map. Attach probe/contact to any Entity irrespective of genre. CTest ecs_nereid_native_pipeline_test checks two unrelated hosts, forced linear/indexed equivalent results, native save/load and COW rollback. The ECS experimental shell runner now also compiles and executes all six NEREID tests, including the legacy raster bridge. All results remain unverified until CI actually runs.

tests/ecs_nereid_sampling_bench.cpp is an optional measurement program (not a correctness-gated CTest). It uses steady_clock only in the diagnostic process, never within simulation. It times a 3x3 matrix of body and probe counts, including the per-tick rebuild of the transient stage-4 AABB tree, and compares the resulting deterministic sample signatures with the linear reference. Invoke CMake target aiverse_ecs_nereid_sampling_bench or tests/run_ecs_experiment_suite.sh --bench. Results are NOT YET available; default adaptive thresholds remain heuristics.

h: Stage 7B — reusable presentation geometry, not gameplay authority
x: "engine/world/nereid/NereidWaterSurfaceMesh.h" provides independent CPU mesh creation for NEREID water bodies using only generic ECS water data: rectangles/discs, bounded infinite-ocean patches, simple concave polygons and variable-width river ribbons. LOD controls tessellation rather than entity/genre semantics. UVs and shoreline proximity (WaterSurfaceVertex.shore) are outputs for rendering only. WaterSurfaceStyle describes tint/foam/specular/alpha, without imposing a backend. Invalid shapes are rejected rather than silently rendered with an alternate footprint. This is a read-only presentation projection of authoritative WaterBodyComponent/WaterGeometryComponent, never persisted, hashed, networked or read back into sim. Existing RTS/editor water surfaces, shader effects, baked cells and shoreline models remain untouched. New test ecs_nereid_surface_mesh_test was authored but NOT RUN.

h: Stage 7C — renderer opt-in bridge and material identity
x: engine/render/NereidWaterRenderer.h is a small adapter from the stage-7B pure WaterSurfaceMesh to the existing RHI-independent Renderer3D::MeshBuilder and scene queue. It uploads vertices with fixed upward normals and per-vertex foam/deep tint, draws a translucent highly specular surface, and provides a matching releaseNereidWaterSurface GPU lifetime helper. Nothing auto- instantiates or caches an ECS water entity: scene/game owns upload and draw. Geometry/LOD needs explicit rebuild when it changes. The new Renderer3D::kDrawWaterSurface flag (256) is encoded in existing draw U0 params.x as a negative sentinel. GLSL/MSL lit shaders recognize it to run the existing animated open-water normal shader at any water surface elevation, plus SSR where trace-tier inputs exist, without misclassifying unrelated shiny meshes. Mixing with the unlit channel clamps the sentinel to 0..1; old lit/unlit/debug modes remain unchanged when unflagged. No extra GPU uniform block, texture slot or genre-specific renderer is introduced. Known GPU limitation: the existing planar reflection renderer selects a single water plane per pass. Multiple simultaneous NEREID surface levels need a future multi-plane solution or selective SSR/environment fallback. No actual hardware rendering, shader cross-compilation or C++ tests have yet been executed in this stage.

Renderer3DReflect.cpp renders at most one planar-water reflection per frame and records its selected world-space Y only when the render target successfully begins. Renderer3D resets that derived state each scene. The pure NereidWaterReflectionPolicy.h helper compares world Y using a finite, 0.025-unit tolerance. The opt-in kDrawWaterSurface flag now maps to existing U0.params.x: -1 for water using the selected planar reflection, -2 for water at another Y when a reflection pass exists. Both select the existing open-water six-train wave shader and remain eligible for trace-tier SSR; GLSL and MSL suppress only the invalid planar waterReflect lookup for -2. Other materials and old unflagged water behavior remain unchanged. The reflection-plane flag is presentation-only derived state, never a WaterBody ECS source. Multiple simultaneous planar reflection passes are still unsupported; secondary surfaces fall back to SSR (when available) or lighting.

Per-water-surface presentation style now has rapidFoamR/G/B (normalized, default 0.84/0.93/0.94), read from scene JSON key style.rapidFoamColor: [r,g,b]. The value travels through the existing NEREID draw path to a new shared U0 waterRapidColor float4, at the end of the water uniform sequence in C++, GLSL and Metal. This only colours Stage 38 current-driven rapid foam when enabled; no ECS schema, water flow physics, additional GPU texture or pass is involved. Reflection uniforms use the same extended U0 layout. Built/shader-compiled validation not yet performed; see docs/nereid/stage-39-rapid-foam-color.md.

h: Stage 40 — quality policy for current-driven whitewater
x: WaterSurfaceStyle::rapidDetail uses WaterRapidDetail::Low/Medium/High (Medium default), configured by scene JSON style.rapidDetail: "low"|"medium"|"high". It is presentation-only and encoded in the previously unused alpha of waterRapidColor. Low uses fewer waves and no whitewater-normal detail; Medium preserves the Stage 39 formula; High adds secondary cross-flow filaments. GLSL and MSL shader changes remain uncompiled and unbenchmarked. See docs/nereid/stage-40-whitewater-quality.md.

WaterConfluenceComponent is a distinct persistent junction entity linking 2–4 generation-safe upstream water bodies and one outlet. The source is validated in Fixed and sampled only near its explicitly authored mouth. applyWaterConfluenceFlow is a shared post-sampling policy in both linear and indexed paths, BEFORE cascade mouth transfer. WaterSample.flow changes locally, never source WaterBody.flow; no mass conservation, erosion, physics integration or geometry modification. Register through NativeWaterPipelineConfig::enableConfluences (false default) or registerNereidConfluencePersistence. Presentation scene parity is deferred to Stage 42. Neither compilation nor test execution has been performed. See docs/nereid/stage-41-confluence-ecs.md.

h: Stage 42 — immutable scene confluence flow projection
x: NereidConfluenceScene is a read-only value snapshot adapter. snapshotNereidEcsConfluences(world) maps generation-safe ECS junction and water-body IDs to scene IDs (packed()+1). Publish via WorldScene::setNereidConfluences(...) at the same ECS read barrier as setNereidSurfaces(...). Both visual ripple advection and per-tile rapid foam apply flowForWater (shared Fixed confluence kernel) followed by cascade flow, mirroring ECS sampling. Missing/invalid input snapshots suppress contribution. Scene has no new fluid solver, GPU buffer, geometry modification or persistence. C++/GPU/tests NOT RUN; see docs/nereid/stage-42-confluence-scene.md.

h: Stage 43 — GPU mesh residency independent of draw-only style
x: NEREID source mesh revision depends only on body geometry, LOD and vertex tint fields (deep RGB, shoreline foam RGB/strength). Shader-only changes use NereidSurfaceResident::setDrawStyle, avoiding VB/IB uploads while preserving full style equality for external callers. sameNereidSurfaceUploadKey controls mesh residency and async staging acceptance; pending workers remain bound to immutable geometry revision. This changes no ECS data or GPU uniform layouts. Source-reviewed and committed, but C++/shader/GPU tests have not run. See docs/nereid/stage-43-material-residency.md.

h: Stage 44 — explicit static JSON confluence source IDs
x: parseNereidConfluenceManifest(root,water.surfaces) parses nereidConfluences.sources from a WorldScene JSON manifest. It requires referenced water surfaces to have explicit IDs, and validates X/Z footprint coverage at the mouth. Scene links are NOT ECS Entity handles; the numeric validWaterConfluenceFlowPolicy is used by shared flow kernel and scene, whereas validWaterConfluence retains full authoritative ECS link validation. WorldScene construction supplies this manifest to its read-only NereidConfluenceScene, and later ECS snapshots may override it explicitly. No ECS schemas, scene GPU resources or hydraulic simulation added. Validation NOT RUN; see docs/nereid/stage-44-confluence-manifest.md.

Strata is a genre-independent presentation system for rigid, opaque geometry. It must not own ECS worlds, physics/terrain simulation, game logic or materials. It does not replace GeometryScene, existing GeometryCluster, AutoLOD, GlobalGeometryPool, Metal batching, or the existing RHI. Strata is an optional geometry representation consumed by the shared renderer. It prepares selections and index/indirect data; Renderer3D remains the single draw owner, with the original geometry/material ownership and Legacy fallback.

engine/render/StrataGeometry.h: ClusterNode, SelectionInput, SelectionOutput, validate(), CPU reference select(). engine/render/StrataBuilder.h: BuildInput, BuildOptions, Meshlet, ClusterBounds, Asset, build(). engine/render/StrataModelAdapter.h: ModelAsset, ModelPrimitiveAsset, ModelPrimitiveSkip, buildModelAsset(). This is a read-only, opt-in adapter for CPU Model assets, not a renderer hook. Link aiverse_strata_builder or aiverse_strata_model_adapter in project CMake when AIVERSE_BUILD_STRATA=ON (ON by default). Both reuse the pinned aiverse_meshoptimizer_lod dependency. Runtime integration uses the separate aiverse_strata_view, aiverse_strata_portable, aiverse_strata_gpu_scene, aiverse_strata_gpu_culling and aiverse_strata_render_routing targets. build() accepts one material partition per invocation; vertex positions begin with three floats and may be interleaved. Source indices and positions are borrowed during the call only. On failure, output stays unchanged. Output is a CPU-owned asset independent of gfx::Device. Meshlet is a leaf with compact local uint8 triangle indices and a map to original global vertex indices. Defaults: max 64 vertices, max 124 triangles. Original global indices are retained for indexed fallback. ClusterNode is a drawable group in the current schema; interior nodes are not guaranteed to fit a single hardware meshlet. firstIndex and indexCount reference the asset's flat index array. Children are contiguous and listed after parents (breadth-first reordering). Asset::bounds aligns one-to-one with Asset::nodes. Parent clusters use meshopt_simplify (position-only inputs) or meshopt_simplifyWithAttributes (optional 1..32 weighted float attributes), with meshopt_SimplifyLockBorder | meshopt_SimplifyErrorAbsolute. The parent's geometric error is conservatively accumulated from its children. A group with under 10% reduction stays unmerged; multiple roots are permitted. Max levels, target ratio and relative error are configurable. Error in ClusterNode is in object units; the caller must project it to pixels using the correct pass and transform. select() requires all roots resident. A missing child prevents refinement of its parent; budget pressure retains the parent. The caller supplies a valid projected error for every node. The implementation is a CPU reference selector, not GPU culling or residency. buildModelAsset() projects 15 attribute components per vertex from Model (normal xyz, UV0, tangent xyzw, vertex RGBA, packed lightmap UV1), with weighted seam-aware simplification. It does not mutate source Model or LOD0. It skips mutable nodes, skinned/morphed, already uploaded, meshes with existing authored/generated LODs, material variants and alpha/custom-shader materials. It returns explicit skip reasons and fails transactionally on invalid eligible geometry. GeometryScene staging consumes these assets; the adapter itself does not submit draws or take ownership from Renderer3D. This is still experimental; the limited verified scenarios are listed above. Do not automatically route displaced surfaces here. Importers should preserve existing meshes and exact LOD0 as a fallback.

h: Stage 4 — optional CPU staging in GeometryScene
x: GeometryScene remains the source-of-truth for scene instances, model ownership, existing HLOD, visibility and draw submission. New APIs: render::GeometryScene scene; scene.setStrataStagingEnabled(true); // Before load/loadPrepared, default OFF scene.loadPrepared(device, sceneJson, std::move(models)); // Scene draws through the existing Renderer3D exactly as before. const auto& counters = scene.stats(); // strataSources, strataNodes, // strataMeshlets, strataIndexBytes, strataSkippedSources, // strataSkippedPrimitives, strataFailures const auto* cpuAsset = scene.strataAsset("models/stone.glb"); // cpuAsset is nullptr when unavailable or the key is not staged. scene.shutdown(device); // invalidates cpuAsset and all staging handles Staging is compiled only when AIVERSE_BUILD_STRATA=ON, and is inert unless setStrataStagingEnabled(true) is called before loading a scene. strataStagingSupported() reports compile-time availability. The method returns false on builds where Strata was disabled. Scene staging is configured by native API, not via scene JSON, so no existing saved scene is affected. There are no additional draw calls and no GPU-resident Strata buffers. The CPU SceneStaging object is in engine/render/StrataModelAdapter.h and can also be used by tools without creating a scene or renderer. It stores at most one copy per unique source key. It preserves the source Model, reports skip/failure diagnostics and has configurable default caps of 250k vertices and 750k indices per source. These are per-source preparation bounds, not global Strata/VRAM limits. All staged data is released with GeometryScene::shutdown and re-created on subsequent loads. Source proxies and generated HLOD proxies are deliberately excluded. Models ineligible for Strata continue through the existing renderer unchanged. A failed staging operation must never fail the scene's legacy upload. The strataIndexBytes counter measures only auxiliary Strata flat index storage (not total Strata CPU heap usage); do not report it as resident VRAM. All counters are diagnostics and are not part of a public save/network schema. Not yet active: GPU scene buffers, meshlet culling, GPU residency, GPU-encoded indirect draws, software rasterization, per-pass Strata selection, actual Strata render submission, or terrain/foliage integration.

engine/render/StrataView.h/.cpp introduces a CPU-only per-pass reference selector. The selected geometry uses Asset-local index ranges; ranges are not GPU draw commands and MUST NOT be passed to gfx::Device::drawIndexedIndirect without first arranging the auxiliary index stream through the shared geometry residency/allocator and correct material/instance grouping. #include "engine/render/StrataView.h" render::strata::ViewConfig pass{}; pass.objectToClip = cameraViewProj * instanceWorld * bindNodeWorld; pass.width = renderTargetWidth; pass.height = renderTargetHeight; pass.clipDepthZeroToOne = device.info().clipDepthZeroToOne; pass.errorThresholdPixels = 1.0f; pass.maxSelectedNodes = 65536; render::strata::ViewPlan selected; std::string error; bool ok = scene.planStrataView( "models/stone.glb", /* mesh */ 0, /* primitive */ 0, pass, selected, &error); // Existing Renderer3D remains the sole draw issuer regardless of 'ok'. planStrataView resolves the already-staged source once and calls the independent strata::planView(asset, pass, result, error). The caller must supply the correct mesh-to-clip matrix for each node and pass. The API does not silently reuse the main view for shadows, reflections, portals or stereo. strata::planView validates bounds, index ranges, matrix and viewport; projects the existing per-cluster geometric error with geometryErrorPixels, runs the resident-parent fallback selector, then conservatively rejects offscreen selected nodes through geometryBoxVisible. Errors leave prior output unchanged. The resulting ranges identify node ID, firstIndex, indexCount and material group in their individual strata::Asset index stream; stats include tested/cut nodes, triangles, residency misses and budget pressure. The planner is packaged as aiverse_strata_view, using the existing aiverse_models geometry helpers. The CTest target is aiverse_strata_view_tests / strata_view. Neither test execution nor Metal/Vulkan validation has been claimed. The implementation remains a CPU reference path to compare eventual compute culling against; there is no GPU scene buffer, RHI command upload or Strata draw path yet.

h: Stage 7A — experimental GPU cluster metadata (not geometry residency)
x: engine/render/StrataGpuScene.h/.cpp supplies a versioned, fixed-layout storage buffer for CPU-prepared cluster records, primitive mappings and hierarchy root indices. It is optional, off by default, and requires the source Model to have been uploaded into the existing GlobalGeometryPool. It does not create or own geometry VB/IB pages. The CPU packer strata::packGpuMetadata(ModelAsset, bytes, error) is pure, transactional and validates unique primitive keys, all cluster hierarchies, bounds, materials, source-local index ranges and u32 offsets. Layout version 1: GPU metadata record Size Purpose GpuMetadataHeader 32 B Version, counts, byte offsets GpuPrimitive 32 B Model mesh/primitive IDs, global node/root spans GpuNode 64 B AABB, global child ID, source-local index span, error/flags Root IDs 4 B each Global root IDs, padded to 16-byte total length The compact arrays are stored in one RHI BufferType::Storage buffer per eligible source (not per instance). Default bounds: 1 MiB per source, 8 MiB per scene for metadata. Experimental upload is restricted to Metal and Vulkan devices reporting compute support and a matching existing Model::geometryPoolPage, shared VB/IB and nonempty pooled extents. Noneligible sources do not abort scene loading and continue normal rendering. Model::geometryRevision, source identity and source GPU handles are checked when retrieving metadata; stale source records are never silently reused. Native integration is explicit: render::GeometryScene scene; scene.setStrataStagingEnabled(true); scene.setStrataGpuMetadataEnabled(true); // both OFF by default scene.loadPrepared(dev, sceneJson, std::move(models)); auto gpuBuffer = scene.strataGpuMetadataBuffer("models/stone.glb"); auto stats = scene.stats(); // strataGpuMetadataSources, strataGpuMetadataDeclined, // strataGpuMetadataFailures, strataGpuMetadataBytes scene.shutdown(dev); // call before destroying gfx::Device The metadata buffer is read-only for future compute code; it is not a GPU scene draw list and no compute shader consumes it yet. GpuNode::resident is a snapshot of the CPU cluster flag, NOT proof of GPU-resident Strata geometry. Most importantly, GpuNode::sourceFirstIndex references the auxiliary CPU strata::Asset::indices, not the Model::ib index stream or any pooled GPU allocation. Until the shared pool gains safe, versioned auxiliary Strata index-stream allocations, do not emit indexed or indirect draws from these metadata offsets. Existing GeometryCluster preparation can make Model::geometry non-null and intentionally exclude that model from the current rigid shared geometry pool. Such a source will decline experimental GPU metadata staging. Resolve the pool's admission/ownership policy explicitly; do not bypass its safety guards. This stage leaves GlobalGeometryPool.cpp, active Renderer3D batching, all render passes, ECS and saved scene formats unmodified. aiverse_strata_gpu_scene builds the metadata and shared-page sidecar layer; CTest strata_gpu_scene checks CPU binary layout, multi-primitive global offsets, source flags, malformed ranges and transactional failure. Native compilation and GPU/CTest execution have not been verified.

h: Stage 7B — shared-page auxiliary Strata index residency
x: Status: code committed; native/GPU validation NOT RUN. All data remains experimental and the draw path remains the existing Renderer3D. GlobalGeometryPool.h/.cpp now offers the following opt-in source-attached API. It does not introduce a second GPU geometry allocator: render::GeometryPoolIndexSpan lease; if (render::uploadAuxiliaryGeometryIndices( device, sourceModel, strataIndices.data(), strataIndices.size(), lease)) { // lease.buffer == sourceModel.ib == sourceModel.vb (same page). // lease.firstIndex is an absolute uint32 GPU index element offset. // lease.indexCount counts only uploaded indices in the sidecar stream. // Indices remain relative to sourceModel.gpuBaseVertex. assert(render::auxiliaryGeometryIndicesValidFor(lease, sourceModel)); } // Explicitly retire before destroying device / source GPU objects: render::releaseAuxiliaryGeometryIndices(device, lease); The function accepts only models already uploaded into the existing GlobalGeometryPool, valid shared VB/IB handles, a complete checked shared-buffer write, and source-relative indices that fit the reserved vertex slice. It never creates a new page for Strata indices. If the page's remaining vertex-to-index gap is too small, the caller keeps the existing legacy renderer. No change is committed to the allocator if the RHI write fails; all previous model and sidecar byte ranges remain reserved. x: Updated: 2026-11-21. Current integration: main; P2 work on feature/aiv20261121_lens_p2. View camera bodies (overhead, follow, chase, first person), the ECS rig modes that share their math and the named presets: camera-behaviors.md.

LENS now includes ECS camera assets, scheduling and dependency checks, managed color/depth targets, camera rigs, per-camera temporal state, capture/readback, PNG output and the Studio camera authoring window. The native client replays one prepared presentation frame into secondary cameras without updating simulation, animation or visual events again. Generic camera infrastructure remains independent of RTS/FPS modules. Captured RTS frames prepare Terrain, GroundFX, Roads, Shores and Fog privately. MotionWeave/View state, Sprite/tile uploads, lighting and world-overlay state join the final publication boundary. A preparation failure clears queued packets and restores animation/event clocks and published surface resources. Topology candidates supply temporary height queries during preparation. Mesh metadata in camera snapshots is owned; GPU resources remain governed by the host's completion-token retirement queues. Poll retirement at the host frame boundary and use confirmed GPU-idle shutdown. The integration compiles on macOS Debug. The native Metal fixture compares primary/prepared replay pixels, verifies a distinct secondary-camera image and checks that replay preserves the source epoch. Fault fixtures exercise private GPU allocation failures and topology retry. Exact executed commands, commits, results and logs are maintained in the native validation handoff. Run the native acceptance with AIVERSE_LENS_METAL_VALIDATE=1; without it, lens_metal_frame explicitly skips rather than claiming GPU validation. This boundary covers preparation, not rollback of already submitted GPU work. Legacy material-paint and field-visual caches are host providers outside that transaction. The ordinary noncapture host path is preserved. Vulkan/GLES runtime parity, broad genre acceptance and camera-count performance stress must be verified on their target platforms before making those claims. LENS P2 (2026-11-21, branch feature/aiv20261121_lens_p2) adds: a physical lens that drives per-camera PRISMA manual exposure and defocus (CameraLensPhysics.h, CameraLensComponent::driveExposure/driveDepthOfField), cinematic rails with centripetal Catmull-Rom, closed loops, constant speed and ease, seeded noise shake on six axes (CameraRailPath.h), and linear HDR EXR frame sequences from RGBA16F targets (CameraExr.h, CameraHdrFrameRecorder). The lens, rail and shake blocks are part of cameras.json. Exposure is relative to the default lens (f/2.8, 1/60 s, ISO 100), because AIVERSE scenes are not photometrically calibrated. Every view camera in AIVERSE comes from one set of camera bodies (CameraSphereOrbit.h holds the sphere orbit) in engine/render/CameraBehavior.h, and the ECS camera rig (CameraRigComponent, engine/render/CameraRig.h) runs the same math. A project picks a body by the camera block it writes and starts from a named preset; there are no per-game camera classes. Body Block What it does overhead game.json "camera" Free map camera: projection, pitch, yaw, lens, zoom limits, pixel-perfect ortho zoom follow game.json topDown.camera, a map's "camera" Keeps a focus point in frame: smoothing, look-ahead along the move and the aim, speed zoom, velocity lead, map bounds, lens and clip planes chase rules / map "camera": {"chase": {...}} Behind and above a heading (vehicles): distance, height, pitch, lead, lens first person rules / map "camera": {"firstPerson": {...}} Eyes with mouse look: sensitivity (and while aiming), pitch limit, lens sphere orbit planet maps (engine/render/CameraSphereOrbit.h) Orbit over a sphere's surface, zooming out to the whole sphere and the system; parallel-transported heading (no poles), smooth focus changes, a view frame with the focus at the origin

CameraRigComponent::mode: Static, LookAt, Follow, Orbit, Rail, Chase, FirstPerson. Chase uses distance, pitch, offset.y (height), offset.z (lead) and yaw (turn around the heading); FirstPerson puts the eye at the target plus offset (turning with the target) and looks along the target's +Z with yaw / pitch added. A Follow rig with a CameraFollowComponent (cameras.json "follow" block, presets allowed, "bounds": [minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ]) runs the follow body itself: angle, distance, smoothing, velocity lead, speed zoom, lens and bounds, the same code as the game follow camera.
