h: Stage 42 — opt-in HDR temporalResolve (full-resolution history reprojection)
x: This feature extends the existing canonical Prisma pipeline, not the historical PrismaScreenLighting wrapper. The normal postfx catalog now supports a temporalResolve effect, with four editor/MCP/volume-configurable parameters. Existing effect IDs, postfx JSON roots, saved panel ID, and PostFx compatibility headers remain unchanged. To activate, the host must use HDR/High and opt in explicitly with AIVERSE_PRISMA_TEMPORAL=1, in addition to an authored effect: { "postfx": { "effects": [ { "type": "temporalResolve", "minQuality": "high", "historyWeight": 0.86, "depthThreshold": 0.0075, "motionScale": 0.04, "reactiveStrength": 0.95 } ] } } Prisma::resolve() now reuses a single full-resolution signed velocity pass for both Temporal Resolve and Motion Blur, if requested. Velocity is current-minus-previous normalized UV and includes camera reprojection and optional Renderer3D object/deformation velocity (RGBA16F, B presence bit); invalid provider metadata falls back to camera velocity. The current-frame RGBA8 reactive coverage is borrowed from Renderer3D/particle callbacks and never retained as temporal history. Each viewId owns two full-resolution RGBA16F linear HDR textures, with color in RGB and prior hardware depth in alpha. The temporal shader reprojects by signed motion vectors, explicitly reconstructs four previous texel taps (nearest GPU sampling, separate depth checks), clamps accepted history against a 3×3 current-color neighborhood in a compressed HDR domain, then adjusts history weight by motion magnitude and reactive coverage. Missing/invalid history writes the current unblurred scene and seeds the next frame. Disoccluded pixels reject stale depth rather than using an interpolated history alpha. HDR tone mapping, Bloom, LUT, and HUD happen after the resolve. If opt-in Motion Blur is also active, it uses the temporally resolved source. HDR FXAA is skipped when temporal resolve ran: do not stack both AA approaches in one frame. Automatic invalidation applies on resolution change and a large camera translation (>12 presentation-world units between frames); explicit Prisma::resetMotionHistory(viewId) also invalidates temporal history on camera cuts and profile switches. Prisma::retireView(viewId) moves owned history handles into the existing GPU-fenced retirement queue. Resource diagnostics report per-camera temporal history texture counts and lower-bound resident bytes, without charging them to the shared size-keyed render target cache. What Stage 42 is not: it does not implement dynamic-resolution rendering, jittered subpixel supersampling, native TSR/FSR/DLSS upscaling, optical-flow motion estimation, a history confidence/rejection G-buffer, or proof of parity with the historical optional PrismaScreenLighting TAA. This is an opt-in, full-resolution temporal color stabilization pass. Sky pixels with no reconstructed surface depth are not accumulated, and moving silhouettes can still need more robust velocity dilation/occlusion masks. At 1080p, two RGBA16F histories plus one RGBA16F velocity target consume at least ~47 MiB of raw base-level GPU memory per active resolution plus shared depth/scratch targets; physical allocation can be higher. Dual-camera views have separate histories even if target sizes match. Verification: GitHub source readback and static wiring review only. NOT RUN: CMake/C++/Metal build, CTest, GLES/Vulkan shader compile, GPU screenshots, silhouette/transparent parity, VRAM profiling, camera cut/resize runtime, mobile GPU benchmarks or CI. No shipping-readiness or pixel-quality PASS is claimed. Full handoff: docs/handoffs/prisma-stage-42.md.

h: Stage 43 — optional subpixel jitter and confidence-aware temporal AA
x: Stage 43 builds on Stage 42's canonical PRISMA temporalResolve without introducing a second TAA subsystem or rewriting stable postfx/MCP identifiers. The native-resolution history remains two per-camera HDR RGBA16F targets; no lower-resolution render target or temporal upscaler is introduced. The effect adds two optional float parameters: jitterPixels: 0..0.5 (default 0.5) controls the maximum subpixel projection offset. Jitter additionally requires AIVERSE_PRISMA_JITTER=1 and the original AIVERSE_PRISMA_TEMPORAL=1, with HDR + High quality and an authored enabled temporalResolve effect. Existing games are unmodified without both explicit environment flags. historyConfidence: 0..1 (default 0.65) controls how aggressively previous HDR color is rejected near sharp luma/depth changes, in addition to the Stage 42 disocclusion depth/velocity/reactive rules. C++ camera contract: Call setViewId(id), then applyCameraVolumes(stack, camera.eye()), then RTSCamera renderCamera = prisma.jitteredCamera(camera,w,h) immediately before renderer.beginScene(renderCamera,w,h). jitteredCamera returns a copy and never mutates camera itself: keep the original RTSCamera for mouse picking, editor gizmos, UI, and touch input. The standard GameClient, Editor Scene and Editor Game rendering paths have been updated to follow this sequence. ShaderGraph, FX and native preview owners may opt in separately. The real render projection uses RTSCamera::jitter, and the renderer's shadow-camera strips jitter already, avoiding artificial shadow-map projection shifts. Shader behavior: Each view ID maintains its own 8-step Halton (2,3) sequence. Jitter is expressed in NDC by the camera; the temporal shader receives the current/previous jitter in unflipped normalized UV. Each stable output pixel samples the current HDR color/depth/velocity at pixel + currentJitter, then samples the prior history at reprojectedInputUV - previousJitter. This removes projection jitter from the history-addressing and from physical-motion confidence while retaining distinct subpixel samples for accumulation. GLSL and Metal use the same shader body, with the render-target Y flip applied only by the existing TUV macro. A 3×3 current compressed-HDR color neighborhood yields local mean/variance and bounds; the shader uses independently depth-validated previous taps, color disagreement and current depth-edge contrast as confidence multipliers. Moving silhouettes and reactive particles therefore receive lower history weight than smooth static surfaces. On explicit camera cuts, projection type/FOV/near/far discontinuities, history changes, jitter mode/amplitude switches or viewport size changes, the temporal history restarts instead of blending incompatible pixels. The existing camera-position cutoff still applies. PrismaStats reports whether the last frame resolved temporal color, whether jitter was active, and the applied offsets in pixels; the PRISMA — Постобработка panel displays the values. This is native-resolution temporal antialiasing, not jittered temporal upscaling, DLSS/FSR/TSR, optical flow or dynamic-resolution rendering. Transparent surfaces and screenspace effects may still alias if their producers do not supply suitable reactive or motion masks. PrismaScreenLighting contains an older optional independent TAA; do not activate both histories at once. The history and GPU-referenced resources remain subject to GPU-fence retirement from Stages 35–42. Verification: GitHub source inspection and structural readback only. CMake/native C++ and GLSL/MSL shader compilation, CTest, GL/Metal/Vulkan/Android GLES runtime, camera/UI parity, multiple viewports, memory profiling and screenshots are NOT RUN by the ongoing features-first direction. No measurable image-quality improvement or production-readiness is claimed until those tests. The exact source commits, APIs and next steps are recorded in docs/handoffs/prisma-stage-43.md.

h: Stage 44 — explicit internal render resolution and temporal upscaling
x: Stage 44 extends the canonical opt-in temporalResolve / Halton TAA path with a true internal 3D render resolution that may differ from the final output target. It adds two catalog parameters to the existing postfx.effects[{type:"temporalResolve"}] payload: renderScale (0.5..1, default 1): fraction of the output width and height used by 3D, depth and motion-vector passes. The chosen scale is quantized to 1/16 steps; actual pixel counts are rounded, bounded to 32px minimum and require at least 64px output dimensions. reconstructionSharpness (0..0.5, default 0.15): mild color reconstruction/sharpening within the compressed-HDR current-frame neighborhood before confidence-weighted history accumulation. The feature is disabled unless all three flags are explicitly set: AIVERSE_PRISMA_TEMPORAL=1, AIVERSE_PRISMA_JITTER=1 and AIVERSE_PRISMA_UPSCALE=1. An enabled temporalResolve authored in the normal game/map postfx catalog, HDR support, High quality, historyWeight>0, jitterPixels>0 and renderScale<1 are also required. Existing projects and low/medium/mobile quality tiers retain 1:1 rendering by default. Host call order: after setViewId(id) and applyCameraVolumes(stack,camera.eye()), call auto [renderW,renderH] = prisma.renderSizeForOutput(outputW,outputH) and then prisma.jitteredCamera(camera,renderW,renderH). Pass this camera and the smaller dimensions to Renderer3D::beginScene but give Renderer3D::render the unchanged full-resolution destination pass. Draw 3D and particle reactive/motion contributions at the smaller size. Renderer3D::resolvePrisma sends the current viewProjection and internal dimensions to Prisma, which reads final output dimensions from the RHI output texture, the host's per-view size declaration, or the swapchain framebuffer. Draw HUD, labels, picking/gizmos and UI using the original camera/full output dimensions. Both Editor Scene/Game and GameClient now use these calls. The main HDR path now performs shutter blur, DoF and other internal scene effects at the low render resolution; Bloom and sun-shaft buffers remain low-resolution inputs. The temporal pass runs immediately before final color composite and writes a viewId-private output-resolution RGBA16F history (RGB linear HDR, A prior hardware depth). Temporal samplers use separate reciprocal texel sizes: inputPx for current scene color/depth neighborhoods, px for output-history bilinear coordinates. Motion vectors remain current-minus-previous in normalized screen UV, so their coordinates do not require ad-hoc multiplication by the resolution ratio. The shader applies Stage 43 jitter correction, four individually depth-validated previous history taps, current luma/depth confidence, reactive coverage and bounded HDR sharpening. Final tonemap/composite and optional full-resolution UI remain output-size. HD/SDR FXAA is not layered over a successful HDR temporal resolve. Per-view history invalidates/retires on changes to output or input dimensions, camera cuts, projection changes or effect quality. Old targets go through the existing GPU-fence retirement rather than immediate destruction. PrismaStats reports width,height (internal), outputWidth,outputHeight (presentation) and temporalUpscaled (successful spatial/temporal resolution step), which are displayed in the Prisma editor window. MemoryStats already counts private temporal history bytes independently of size-shared scene buffers; when upscaling it counts the two larger output histories. Fallback: GPU output-history/depth allocation or temporal pipeline failure does not erase the source image: the final composite samples the internal-size scene across the full framebuffer (ordinary bilinear enlargement). If this happens after a jittered frame has begun, single-frame instability may still be visible; this path needs native runtime validation and potentially earlier allocation preflight. The previous optional PrismaScreenLighting temporal system is not automatically merged or compatible with simultaneous use.

h: Stage 45 — GPU-sampled adaptive resolution and pre-render stable fallback
x: This stage extends the opt-in Stage 44 source/output temporal scale path. It does not change any defaults or the postfx JSON root, existing MCP IDs, editor tab ID, scene shaders or genre-specific simulation. New effect controls in the existing temporalResolve catalog: adaptiveResolution (boolean, defaults false), targetGpuMs (4..50ms, default 16.6) and minRenderScale (0.5..1, default 0.5). The authored Stage 44 renderScale remains the quality ceiling and cannot be exceeded by the adaptive controller. To opt in, set AIVERSE_PRISMA_ADAPTIVE=1 in addition to all three Stage 44 flags (AIVERSE_PRISMA_TEMPORAL=1, AIVERSE_PRISMA_JITTER=1, AIVERSE_PRISMA_UPSCALE=1), choose HDR/High and author an enabled temporalResolve effect with adaptiveResolution:true. PrismaAdaptiveResolution is a CPU-only, genre-independent policy in engine/render/PrismaAdaptiveResolution.h. It consumes only finite, positive, asynchronously completed Device::gpuFrameMs() readings from new, strictly increasing Device::gpuCompletedFence() tokens. A backend without reliable results (e.g. unsupported GL/Vulkan) stays at the authored scale; the policy never substitutes editor CPU frame time, FPS, frame serials or predicted GPU timings. On Metal the signal measures the whole GPU command frame, not an isolated Prisma pass or editor view; adapting multiple editor views to the same whole-frame measurement is conservative and can shift quality in both. Hysteresis: GPU duration above 115% target for 12 distinct completed samples causes a 1/16 renderScale decrease; GPU duration below 80% target for 36 samples causes a 1/16 increase, up to authored ceiling. A changed scale starts 48 completed samples of cooldown, reducing rapid resize/reallocation loops. The floor and ceiling are clamped and quantized; Prisma::retireView removes per-view controller state when the viewport is closed. Pre-render resource preflight: renderSizeForOutput() on the graphics thread now calls preflightUpscale() before returning any internal resolution smaller than the output. It checks the temporal and motion GPU programs, the guaranteed fallback composite, the HDR RGBA16F size-owned scene/velocity textures, internal scene/depth/scratch, the camera-private pair of output-size HDR temporal histories and the output-size scratch depth. History reallocations use existing GPU-fenced retirement. A failed preflight returns full input/output dimensions and inhibits jitter for that view. Allocation retries are rate-limited (60 render-size queries) so an unsupported or memory-constrained device is not hammered each frame. No GPU wait is introduced in this path. Jitter-safe runtime fallback: if a temporal pass unexpectedly cannot run after a low-resolution jittered scene was already encoded, the final compositor uses graphFrame.zw as a current-jitter sampling offset s + currentJitter for source color and dependent screen effects. The offset is zero during a successful temporal resolve or normal non-jittered presentation. That keeps the fallback image on a stable output pixel grid while still allowing linear bilinear upscaling and HDR color processing. This is a visual stabilization measure, not a guarantee of production image quality or a replacement for real temporal accumulation. HUD and input remain full-size and unjittered. PrismaStats adds adaptiveResolution, requestedRenderScale and temporalFallback; the existing PRISMA editor panel displays them alongside output/internal resolutions and optional asynchronously completed whole-frame GPU milliseconds. No precise GPU time is shown if unsupported. Limitations: backend timing may be absent; whole-frame timing includes other GPU jobs; the fallback can still exhibit simple bilinear aliasing and thin-edge shimmer; a mid-frame device loss cannot be recovered with texture sampling; cached allocation pressure may temporarily rise around scale transitions until actual GPU-completed fences allow reclamation. h: Stage 46 — actual scoped GL33 viewport GPU timings and VRAM-pressure guard
x: The timing distinction matters: RHI gfx::Device now has optional nonblocking beginGpuScope(tag)/endGpuScope() and a separate takeGpuScopeTimings() result queue. Unlike gpuFrameMs() and timeGpuFrame(), a scope measures only GPU commands submitted between its boundaries. Desktop OpenGL 3.3 on supported macOS/Windows paths uses a real GL_TIME_ELAPSED query. The backend refuses to start a scope while a whole-frame elapsed query or another scope is running (OpenGL does not allow nested same-target queries). takeGpuScopeTimings() only returns completed, nonblocking results and does not consume other takeGpuTimings() benchmark results. The bounded queue is capped at 64 pending entries. GL ES/WebGL/Linux fallback, Metal and Vulkan do not claim per-viewport timings: the default API returns false/empty. Metal's gpuFrameMs() is whole-command-buffer duration and must always be labeled as such. Editor opt-in: AIVERSE_PRISMA_VIEWPORT_GPU_TIMING=1. For Scene/Game, the editor begins a GPU timing scope immediately before the graphics Renderer3D::render and ends it after Renderer3D::resolvePrisma and the last viewport pass. This covers rendered shadows, world, post-effects and scene FX in this interval, not prior CPU scene preparation, prior GPU asset streaming or other windows. When supported, the editor polls finished measurements at its pre-render safe boundary, passes them to Prisma::acceptViewGpuTiming(viewId,gpuMs) and lists per-viewport samples through Prisma::viewGpuTimings(). The source is presentation/diagnostic only, not the authoritative simulation or an ECS component. It is opt-in and never enables full-frame timing automatically. Adaptive source selection: the existing PrismaAdaptiveResolution controller now prefers the latest completed scoped GL query for its particular view. Each accepted scoped query increments that view's completed-sample sequence; a repeat value cannot cause repeated hysteresis updates. If no scoped query is available, the controller retains the earlier whole-GPU-frame fallback gated by the genuine Device::gpuCompletedFence(). It does not convert CPU FPS to GPU milliseconds. Scoped interval duration still includes shared GPU shadow/reflection/FX passes and is not a pure postprocess-only cost. On unsupported backends this scope-specific diagnostic is explicitly unavailable. Bounded known-memory pressure: temporalResolve gains maxPrismaMemoryMiB (32..4096, default 256 MiB) as an opt-in adaptive-resolution pressure threshold. Only when the Stage 45 adaptiveResolution effect and AIVERSE_PRISMA_ADAPTIVE=1 are active does the policy compare the threshold against Prisma::memoryStats().liveKnownBytes + Prisma::retirementStats().knownPendingBytes. These estimates count shared size-cache allocations once, add active per-view HDR histories and pending fence-retired textures exactly once, and exclude unknown/unobservable bytes and physical driver overhead. A known lower-bound overage counts as a pressure sample only on a new confirmed GPU completion (actual completed scope query or GPU fence). After 12 over-budget samples it may step scale down 1/16. Over-budget pressure blocks upward quality steps; normal fast/slow GPU timing and the existing 48-completed-sample cooldown continue to apply. Pressure alone does not allow unsafe GPU release, unconditional memory waits, or repeated CPU-frame counting. Without a verified GPU completion, no adaptation is attempted. PrismaStats and the editor report the chosen timing source, last valid GPU milliseconds, known Prisma live+pending bytes, the configured threshold and whether it is exceeded. The Stats window also displays the recent completed GL33 Scene/Game intervals, rather than mislabeling Metal whole-frame timings as isolated view costs. Caveats: gpuFrameMs and GL elapsed queries are GPU-timeline intervals, not identical to busy-time; scopes can include expensive shared renderer passes and do not measure earlier resource uploads. h: Stage 47 — Metal hardware-scoped timings, renderer-owned memory and trustworthy source switching
x: Metal GPU scope implementation: gfx::Device::beginGpuScope, endGpuScope and takeGpuScopeTimings now have a real optional engine/gfx/metal/GfxMetal.mm backend for compatible devices. It checks available MTLDevice.counterSets for timestamp counters and requires support for blit-boundary or stage-boundary counter sampling. It uses two samples per viewport scope in a MTLCounterSampleBuffer, encoded into lightweight blit encoders inside the same Metal command buffer as the actual Scene/Game work. Command-buffer submission/presentation, frame semaphores and GPU fences are unchanged. Metal counters do not necessarily run in CPU nanoseconds. A timing sample is only accepted after the actual command buffer reaches MTLCommandBufferStatusCompleted and resolveCounterRange(NSMakeRange(0,2)) returns both valid timestamp values. The backend obtains correlated CPU/GPU clock pairs using [device sampleTimestamps:&cpuTimestamp gpuTimestamp:&gpuTimestamp] before encoding and after completion. It converts the GPU timestamp interval to CPU-clock nanoseconds by interpolating those clock pairs. Zero, error sentinel, nonmonotonic, nonfinite and out-of-range results are not published as valid time. Results are polled nonblockingly; pending scopes are capped at 64. Hardware without supported counter sampling or a valid sample buffer reports unsupported, with no fabricated scoped GPU time. On desktop GL33 the previous real scoped elapsed GPU-query path remains. Vulkan/GLES/WebGL have not gained scoped timers; Device::gpuFrameMs() remains a whole-frame metric whenever used as an adaptive fallback, never mislabeled per viewport. Editor Scene/Game still use the existing opt-in AIVERSE_PRISMA_VIEWPORT_GPU_TIMING=1, with bounded scopes around GPU rendering and Prisma postresolve; the editor's pre-render poll reads only completed scope results. This excludes GPU work submitted outside the scope (such as previous texture uploads), and can include shared light/reflection passes. Scope durations do not sum to total GPU busy time. New GPU memory lower bound: Renderer3D::residentMemoryStats() uses read-only RHI TextureInfo and BufferInfo to count unique directly owned texture/buffer handles. Included: sun shadow map, renderer's owned selection texture, scene-color capture caches (including depth), trace placeholder textures, own model placeholder textures, per-camera object-motion/depth/reactive textures, and directly owned line/ selection/blit/indirect buffers. Scene cache aliases sceneColor_/sceneDepth_ are not counted twice. Deferred object motion textures are reported separately as pendingMotionKnownBytes. Dynamic buffer versions are noted, but their physical allocator copies cannot be inferred. Compressed texture formats without enough metadata are reported as unknown, not guessed. External Model/Material resources, LightSystem reflection/spot targets, shared persistent scene/ geometry pools, shader/pipeline driver allocations, and Prisma resources are not claimed by this reporter. Integration: Prisma::setExternalRendererGpuMemory(live,pending) is an optional presentation-only host input. Editor Scene/Game and GameClient now invoke Renderer3D::residentMemoryStats() and pass its live texture+buffer known bytes and separately pending motion bytes to the same Prisma instance before renderSizeForOutput. The existing serialized temporalResolve.maxPrismaMemoryMiB key remains unchanged for compatibility, but its pressure comparison now includes the nonoverlapping known lower bounds of Prisma plus that directly owned Renderer3D subset, active and pending. This still does not cover total GPU VRAM, physical device allocation, mips, temporary backbuffer or unknown owners. It does not force GPU idle or premature texture destruction; Stage 35–46 GPU-fenced retirement rules remain in control. Correctness of timing-source switches: a completed Metal/GL scope-query sequence is not comparable with a completed GPU-frame fence token. Stage 47 tracks these as distinct sample doma

Unlike a GPU allocator, it never calls create/destroy, map, GPU wait, readback or query. It uses saturated byte accumulation and never equates a missing texture's bytes to real zero physical VRAM. h: Stage 52 — optional HDR lighting independent of legacy temporal accumulation
x: PrismaScreenLighting is an optional PostProcess adapter around Prisma; do not copy its implementation to SpectraFX or run a second TAA owner. This stage separates its HDR scene-lighting passes from its historical temporal reconstruction. When canonicalTemporalRequested() is true on HDR/High, the adapter delegates jittered() to Prisma::jitteredCamera and resets legacy history. Its bounce shader (screen-space approximate indirect diffuse) and optional shadowed volumetric sun scattering still run on linear HDR SceneColor before Prisma::resolve. The last auxiliary texture is copied back to scene color through a dedicated shader that keeps alpha untouched. Prisma then remains the sole temporal owner. If canonical temporal is not selected and the adapter is enabled on HDR/High, its old two-history TAA / Halton camera jitter is retained, including the old opaque-alpha copy contract. The adapter's temporalShadowResolve() is true only in this legacy mode, so optional PCSS shadow sampling is not accidentally randomized without the matching legacy history. Auxiliary bounce, scatter, history and depth textures are created lazily as requested. Canonical-only mode does not create the two legacy history images or legacy depth attachment; existing allocations from a prior mode remain cached rather than being destroyed on a mode toggle while the GPU may still use them. Full resource teardown on resize/shutdown is inherited from the old adapter and still needs GPU-fence lifecycle validation. A missing sun shadow suppresses volumetric scatter for that frame, even if configured. Without a legacy temporal history the scatter sample sequence has a stable phase to avoid animation noise when a canonical temporal preflight fails. No GPU capability or visual parity is inferred from these source changes. Public API: PrismaScreenLighting::lightingOnly() describes the adapter's current path; running(), passCount(), temporalShadowResolve(), setDiffuseBounceEnabled() and setVolumetricLight() retain compatible semantics, except that the temporal shadow flag no longer treats a non-temporal lighting-only pass as a temporal resolver. The two direct lighting shaders and the separate alpha-preserving copy are included in the adapter's MSL/GLSL pipeline set. Existing postfx JSON, editor/MCP names and UI-after- tone-map ordering are unchanged. Verification: 15/15 source-presence and ordering checks after GitHub readback. Prisma::effectReport(viewId) const returns a pointer to a Prisma::ViewEffectReport captured after the last resolve() of that specific camera. The viewId identifiers are assigned by the host; the value 0 is the inherited default. effectReportViewIds() returns the sorted keys of the stored reports. The result creates no RHI shader/texture, does not call program()/composite(), does not wait for the GPU and does not change ECS. ViewEffectReport: viewId, a sequence counter (only resolve calls for this ID), input dimensions, quality, HDR path, scene readiness and a list of EffectExecution for all elements of the current camera profile, including authored-disabled/low-tier effects. Each entry contains: type — the PrismaType from the standard catalog; authored means present in the current profile. requested — the effect is enabled at the current tier and its opt-in + numeric conditions (if any) are met; a low tier / disabled environment variable gives a specific reason and requested=false. pipelinePrepared — the local cached RHI handles are available. This is not proof of GPU execution; for composite the actually selected variant is checked, and for multi-pass Bloom/TiltShift/SunShafts the specific prepared pipelines. encoded — the corresponding effect actually entered the last render (a draw for MotionBlur/DoF/FXAA/Temporal, a resource attached to the submitted composite for Bloom, LUT, Bloom/etc). A partial failed GPU graph whose result is not used does not count as a successful effect. Shader readiness without a draw does not give encoded. reason — the reason for skipping (camera cut/first frame, history quota, temporal preflight, HDR/tier/opt-in, missing LUT/pipeline, shadergraph/exposure texture-slot conflict, missing target, etc.). Empty for a successfully encoded effect. The per-view report does not mix Scene/Game of the same size. On retireView / retireUnregisteredViews the snapshot is removed together with the camera state; on shutdown() and setSettings() old reports are cleared. An applyCameraVolumes() update is reflected on the next resolve; until then the snapshot is the history of the last render, not a plan of the current settings. Report pointers are invalidated on clearing or map update; do not cache them between frames. The PRISMA — Постобработка editor displays a collapsible matrix View ID / effect / requested / pipeline / encoded / reason without creating resources while viewing. The existing global runtimeCapabilities() still describes the latest data from PrismaStats, not all cameras; for a per-view effect use the new API. Especially important: encoded means GPU draw command issued, not a completed GPU fence, correct pixels, an image in the frame or effect parity across different RHIs. The last four claims are permitted only after real GPU tests. Stage 53 source: engine/render/Prisma.{h,cpp}, apps/editor/windows/PrismaWindow.cpp; exact commits, structural checks and the next stage are in docs/handoffs/prisma-stage-53.md. Actual verification: 18/18 source-presence/lifecycle checks after GitHub readback. NOT RUN: local CMake/clang/CTest, editor, Metal/GL/GLES/Vulkan, shader compile, screenshots, GPU passes, CI. Do not claim performance/pixel verification before a separate test phase.

h: Stage 54 — safe camera closing and deferred GPU retirement
x: In PRISMA, the camera viewId denotes the stable identity of a presentation camera, not its size, so two 1920×1080 cameras have independent temporal/velocity histories. Renderer3D::retireUnregisteredObjectMotionViews(liveViewIds) (a new public genre-independent API) takes the full set of active stable view IDs after all camera passes of the current frame have been submitted. For each missing ID it calls the existing retireObjectMotionView(id,device.gpuSubmissionFence()); only Renderer3D-owned target/depth/reactive textures are queued. They are released via collectCompletedObjectMotion(device.gpuCompletedFence()). A zero submission token keeps the resources in motionUnfenced_ until an explicitly confirmed GPU idle. CPU frameSerial and time cannot replace a GPU fence. Active cameras and size-shared targets are not released. After the Scene/Game render, the editor uses a single activePrismaViews for Prisma::retireUnregisteredViews(...) and Renderer3D::retireUnregisteredObjectMotionViews(...), then Prisma::retireUnreferencedSizeCaches(). The old Scene/Game close transitions are kept and are a no-op if the generic cleanup has already removed the ID; custom-camera cleanup no longer skips independent Renderer3D velocity textures. GameClient keeps 3D view 3 alive while it renders sim_; if a frame contains only a menu or loading, it removes the private Prisma/Renderer3D states and unused size caches. startMatch still explicitly retires the previous camera. On the next render the camera creates a clean history. PrismaScreenLighting keeps exclusive ownership of its bounce_, scatter_, history_[2] and depth_. releaseTargets() on resize or in scenePass() after setEnabled(false) now moves them into a PrismaGpuRetirementQueue<gfx::TextureHandle> bound to Device::gpuSubmissionFence(). Until the device reports gpuCompletedFence(), no actual destroyTexture happens. If the backend provided no submission token, the resource is kept in unfencedTargets_ and is released only via drainRetiredAfterGpuIdle() after an explicit GPU idle wait by the device owner. Public adapter API: collectGpuRetirements() — non-blocking collection by confirmed completion fence; retirementStats() — CPU/GPU-free statistics of the number of fenced/unfenced textures and the last GPU completion token; drainRetiredAfterGpuIdle() — only on known GPU idle; shutdown() also requires GPU idle for safe deletion of pipelines/shaders/vertex buffer, like the historical adapter. The shared Prisma and Renderer3D own their own GPU queues; ScreenLighting never deletes other owners' targets, depth or history. Disabling the adapter removes its current auxiliary resources on the next call of scenePass, not immediately on setEnabled(false). If the adapter is never called again, its GPU owner must continue collectGpuRetirements() and at the end of the lifecycle complete shutdown() after idle. Limitations/checks: only GitHub source readback and 30/30 structural checks of the target transitions/methods. NOT RUN: CMake/clang, CTest, Metal/GL/GLES/Vulkan/WebGL, GPU fence overlap, integrated Editor/GameClient runtime, memory stress and image parity. h: Stage 55 — Auto Exposure together with four Shader Graph textures
x: Before this stage PRISMA reserved a fixed sampler TEX8 for GPU HDR Auto Exposure, while the postfx Shader Graph used bindings TEX5..TEX8 for at most four independent textures. With four textures, author-enabled Auto Exposure was silently disabled, even though all its other conditions were met. This was a functional limitation, not a physical RHI restriction. The new GPU-independent PrismaCompositeTextureLayout.h defines a shared, constexpr-computable resource map. The fixed composite occupies slots 0..4, the Shader Graph 5..8, and HDR Auto Exposure slot 8 while the graph uses 0..3 textures, and slot 9 with four textures. An unsupported texture count (more than 4) is explicitly rejected. Five static_asserts confirm the expected computations when the library is compiled; native compilation has NOT yet been performed. The scheme does not change serialization, JSON or the MCP API. In Prisma.cpp the plan is used both when building ShaderDesc.textureSlots, when forming the masks for GLSL/MSL TEX0..TEX9 and in the actual Device::setTexture. PrismaShaders.h selects TEX9 only with PF_AUTO_EXPOSURE_SLOT9, otherwise it keeps TEX8. The composite cache key remains effectMask + ShaderGraph JSON: this is sufficient, since the layout is uniquely determined by the graph itself. If building the expanded pipeline fails, PRISMA keeps the old fallback: the same composite without Auto Exposure, and if that is also unavailable, the base composite without effects. Do not substitute a failed pass with "effect executed". Prisma::ViewEffectReport now contains shaderGraphTextures and autoExposureTextureSlot. The latter is -1 when the final selected composite pipeline does not contain Auto Exposure; the entry is updated only after the fallback is resolved. The PRISMA — Постобработка editor shows the actual slot for each viewId without triggering a GPU shader compile for displaying diagnostics. RHI source check: GL configures texN from ShaderDesc.textureSlots, the Metal backend contains sampler bindings that include 9, Vulkan allows up to 32 descriptor texture slots; the Shader Graph compiler limits the number of independent textures to four. This is a structural assessment of the sources, not proof of correct operation on all GLES/WebGL/Metal/Vulkan adapters. Actual verification: after GitHub readback, 25/25 structural source/layout/logic checks were performed; NOT RUN: CMake/clang, shader compilation, editor, CTest, GPU resolve, HDR pixel readback, backend stress/CI/benchmarks. See docs/handoffs/prisma-stage-55.md for exact commits, limitations and the next step. PR #26 remains Draft; no changes were made to main.

h: Stage 56 — Depth of Field: distance-based focus and silhouette protection
x: The experimental depthOfField remains part of PRISMA and still requires AIVERSE_PRISMA_DOF=1 and a suitable quality tier. Old maps/JSON automatically use the previous mode: focusDepth and focusRange in hardware depth [0,1]; maxBlur and intensity stay unchanged. In the shader this mode is kept in a separate branch with the original formula and the 10-weight blur scheme, so that the old image is not reinterpreted as a physical distance. New optional parameters of the same effect: Parameter Default Purpose metricFocus false Explicitly enable linear depth from camera data focusDistance 12 Focus plane along the view direction (world units) focusRangeMeters 4 Sharpness interval around the focus plane occlusionToleranceMeters 0.35 Allowed depth difference between the center and a tap before blending is suppressed The "meters" naming applies to projects where one world unit equals one meter. This is linear depth along the camera direction (view-space Z), not the spherical distance from the eye to an arbitrary point. For perspective: z = near * far / (far - depth * (far - near)); for orthographic: z = mix(near, far, depth). Renderer3D::resolvePrisma() already passes PostFrame.depthNear, depthFar and orthographic; the orthographic bounds of the current renderer can be negative -200..1000, which is supported correctly. The Prisma.cpp code checks finite near/far and far > near; perspective additionally requires near > 0. If metricFocus is requested but the input projection is invalid, the RHI draw runs the old hardware depth, and Prisma::EffectExecution for this camera sets encoded=true, degraded=true and a specific reason. This prevents NaN and an empty frame. The report pointer stays read-only; degraded does not mean verified visual correctness of the effect on the GPU. The metric shader computes CoC from linear depth and, among eight neighboring color taps, chooses the weight by the difference in linear depth. Points separated by a silhouette or belonging to sky/background (device depth >= 0.99999) are not blended; the transition between consistent and inconsistent layers is smoothed with smoothstep. GPU sampling stays in linear HDR; output alpha in the metric branch is inherited from the source SceneColor. The legacy branch keeps the previous output alpha=1 for compatibility. The sampled scene depth is never bound as a writable depth attachment; DoF uses a separate scratchDepth. The pass works with src.tex, which may contain the result of the preceding Motion Blur, and now checks that src.tex specifically is present before the draw. PrismaData.cpp automatically exposes the new fields in the shared JSON/editor/MCP/volume-mask schema; do not create a separate implementation for FPS, RTS or SpectraFX. PrismaWindow.cpp gained a hint about mode selection and a visible degraded fallback in the effect matrix per viewId. Any old postfx without metricFocus will keep using the old path. Limitations: this is an 8-tap screen-space defocus, not physically correct bokeh, Gather/Scatter DoF or full separated foreground/background scattering. At intersections of translucent surfaces the depth constraint can suppress blurring, but cannot recover colors hidden behind objects. Depth [0,1] semantics, camera and Metal/GL parity require verification on a real device. Actual checks: after the commits the sources were read back from GitHub and 32/32 source-only structural checks were run. NOT RUN: CMake/clang, GLSL/MSL/Vulkan shader compiler, CTest, Editor/GameClient, Metal/GL/GLES/WebGL/Vulkan GPU pixel/readback, screenshots, profiling and CI. h: Stage 57 — stable HDR Auto Exposure and consistent camera-cut reset
x: autoExposure still requires the effect in the postfx profile, effective HDR and the variable AIVERSE_PRISMA_AUTO_EXPOSURE=1. Luminance measurement stays in linear scene-referred HDR before tonemapping and UI, and its separate 1×1 ping-pong history belongs to a stable viewId, independent of Scene/Game viewport sizes. New optional parameters in the shared PrismaData catalog: Field Default Range Meaning highlightRejection 0 0..0.95 How much to reduce the influence of very bright pixels during metering highlightStartEV 3 -10..16 Threshold where weight reduction starts, in log2(luminance), NOT camera exposure EV highlightSoftnessEV 2 0.1..8 Smoothness of the transition to maximum weight reduction, in log2 stops highlightRejection=0 by default keeps the previous weighted log-luminance estimator and the already existing centerWeight, centerRadius, minMeterLogL, maxMeterLogL, EV clamps and adaptation speeds. This is optional soft highlight weighting, not histogram/percentile metering. The GPU shader kExposureLog computes the luminance of each of the four samples, clamps logL to the current minMeterLogL/maxMeterLogL, then reduces the base spatial weight: weight *= 1 - rejection * smoothstep(startEV, startEV+softnessEV, logL). The bound rejection <= 0.95 guarantees at least 5% of the original weight even for a fully bright frame and rules out a zero metering denominator. The kExposureReduce pyramid reduction still separately carries the weighted sum of log2 luminance and the sum of weights, and kExposureAdapt divides the former by the latter before computing EV. There is no hidden GPU readback or CPU luminance pass. Camera cut: before Stage 57, automatic camera jump detection happened after GPU metering, so the first frame after a teleport could blend with the previous exposure. Now the check of motionView.previousCameraPos, finiteness and a jump of more than 12 world units runs at the start of Prisma::resolve, before Auto Exposure. The reset simultaneously invalidates velocity/temporal history and calls resetAutoExposure(viewId_). Explicit resetMotionHistory(id) / resetMotionHistory() also invalidate per-view/all-view exposure history without deleting GPU textures. The first adaptation pass of the new camera uses historyValid=false and is reinitialized from the current measurement. The reset does not require waiting for the GPU and does not confuse two cameras with the same resolution. Color order is preserved: weighted HDR metering measures scene.tex, the 1×1 exposure is applied to HDR RGB in PF_AUTO_EXPOSURE inside the final composite, then the ColorGrade-authored exposure in HDR enters the pre-tonemap multiplier filt.z, then ACES/sRGB, user display-space grade/LUT and the postfx Shader Graph. These are two independent authored multipliers, not two instances of the auto-adaptation algorithm; GPU history is strictly one per view. Shader Graph resources (slots 5..8) and Auto Exposure (8 or 9) continue to follow the Stage 55 layout and the fallback without Auto Exposure on an unsupported pipeline. Prisma::ViewEffectReport now records autoExposureHighlightRejection only when the finally encoded composite actually contains Auto Exposure. Otherwise the field stays zero, autoExposureTextureSlot=-1, and the Stage 53 per-effect status indicates the effect is absent. The editor shows the value and hints directly in PRISMA — Постобработка; the effect list and the volume editor get the new parameters automatically through the shared catalog. Old postfx JSON, MCP, the saved editor panel id and SpectraFX are not affected. The parameters do not affect authoritative ECS. Limitations: histogram percentile metering, tonal segmentation of skin/sky, AE metering masks and local exposure are not implemented. A globally bright background can still influence the overall result (no less than 5%). Tune highlightStartEV in terms of scene-referred log2 luminance, not camera control EV. Color dynamics quality and GPU shader parity are not yet verified. Verificat

h: Stage 58 — cinematic Exposure Freeze and a circular HDR metering region
x: PRISMA still uses one global Auto Exposure algorithm: HDR scene luminance → kExposureLog → kExposureReduce → kExposureAdapt → 1×1 per-view exposure history → final HDR composite before tonemapping/UI. Stage 58 adds control over its already existing GPU passes, without a new ECS system, a second shader Exposure owner or mandatory JSON parameters.

Field Default Semantics freezeExposure false Hold the last valid 1×1 Auto Exposure value of this camera meterRegionEnabled false Enable local luminance weighting of a circular frame region meterCenterX, meterCenterY 0.5, 0.5 Normalized region center, X left to right, Y bottom to top meterRadius 0.25 Circle radius relative to the frame height, aspect-corrected meterFeather 0.10 Smooth width of the circle edge, as a fraction of frame height meterOutsideWeight 0.05 Weight of pixels outside the circle; guaranteed above 0 (minimum 0.02) All fields are appended to the end of the existing Auto Exposure catalog: old offsets and values do not shift. The generic PrismaData parser/serialization, editor, MCP and PrismaVolumeStack get the new fields automatically. For games without the new keys the previous processing stays functionally unchanged; both modes are off by default. The existing effect still requires HDR, a matching tier and AIVERSE_PRISMA_AUTO_EXPOSURE=1. Freeze: with a valid history ExposureView.history[current] the previous 1×1 GPU texture is simply bound to the final composite. On this frame no extra mip targets are created, and kExposureLog, kExposureReduce or kExposureAdapt are not run; the GPU history is not read and written at the same time. The internal adaptation time is updated so that unfreezing does not produce a large delta-time. On the first active camera, after a camera view ends, a settings reset or a Camera Cut, the history is invalid; freeze performs one new metering / adaptation of the current scene, after which it holds the result again. Explicit camera cuts keep the Stage 57 contract — capture the exposure again, rather than holding the previous frame forever. Disabling the effect itself invalidates its history without destroying resources immediately. Region: kExposureLog gained an additional vec4 region only in its own UBO (ExposureMeterU). SimpleU and the interfaces of other passes did not change. region.z < 0 disables the region without affecting the old formula. When enabled, each of the four source sample UVs is converted back from backend texture orientation into bottom-up screen coordinates TUV(q); X is scaled by the width/height ratio. Weights are computed with smoothstep(radius,radius+feather,physicalDistance), then multiplied with the old centerWeight and the Stage 57 highlightRejection. The outside weight is never zero. The pyramid reduction keeps (weightedLogL, totalWeight) and does not depend on the mask; all other shaders/UBOs stay the same. This is cheap area-weighted metering, not a GPU histogram, segmentation, a user texture mask or local exposure for different parts of the screen.

Prisma.h provides a GPU-free presentation API keyed by a stable view ID, not by camera coordinates or viewport size: prisma.setViewExposureFreeze(viewId, true); prisma.setViewExposureMeterRegion(viewId, { true, 0.5f, 0.5f, 0.25f, 0.10f, 0.05f }); // Чтобы вернуться к наследованию postfx/PrismaVolumeStack: prisma.clearViewExposureFreeze(viewId); prisma.clearViewExposureMeterRegion(viewId); Also, setViewExposureFreeze(id,false) explicitly overrides freezeExposure=true from the profile. setViewExposureMeterRegion checks finiteness and clamps coordinates, radius, feather and outsideWeight on input. Thus two cameras at the same geographic point can have independent freeze and region parameters. After all camera passes finish, the host passes the full set of live identifiers to Prisma::retireUnregisteredViews; the new overrides are included in unionTracked and are removed by retireView/ shutdown together with per-camera state. This is presentation-only, not authoritative ECS and not a change to the global base profile. ViewEffectReport.autoExposureFrozen and autoExposureRegionMetered are updated only if the final encoded composite actually applies Auto Exposure. Frozen means "on this frame a valid history was reused, the meter was not run"; RegionMetered means "on this frame a measurement with a region was performed". When exposure is absent in the final fallback, both are false. The editor window shows them for each viewId and gives hints for the new generic fields; GUI reads do not trigger GPU creation. Verification: after the source commits and GitHub readback, 36/36 structural source checks over the catalog, shader, CPU plan, native API, lifecycle, UI and final fallback. NOT RUN: CMake/clang, CTest, GLSL/MSL/SPIR-V shader compiler, Metal/OpenGL/GLES/Vulkan/WebGL GPU, the editor on a device, luminance readback, alpha/pixel parity, latency/FPS, GPU fences and CI. Structural checks do not prove the build or RHI correctness. Exact SHAs and the next stage — docs/handoffs/prisma-stage-58.md.

h: Stage 59 — Manual EV, rectangular ROI and fault-tolerant HDR metering
x: Manual EV is implemented inside the existing AutoExposure postfx effect; it does not start a second HDR owner, GPU history, a new fullscreen pass or an extra sampler. The PrismaData.cpp catalog extends Stage 58 with the fields: Field Default Purpose manualExposure false Fixed-exposure mode instead of automatic metering manualEV 0 −12…+12 stops, 2^manualEV in linear HDR meterBox false Use a rectangular ROI instead of a circle meterHalfWidth 0.25 Rectangle half-width as a fraction of frame width meterHalfHeight 0.25 Rectangle half-height as a fraction of frame height All new settings are opt-in and appended to the end of the catalog. Old postfx, editor IDs and MCP operations are preserved; for existing projects manualExposure=false and meterBox=false mean no changes. Ordinary automatic exposure still requires AIVERSE_PRISMA_AUTO_EXPOSURE=1, while an explicitly enabled manualExposure works without this flag (but requires an authored autoExposure, enabled postFX, an allowed tier and linear HDR).

In Prisma::resolve manual mode is selected from the camera profile and native override. With manualExposure active, GPU metering, kExposureLog/Reduce/Adapt, the 1×1 exposure history and the texture sampler TEX8/TEX9 are not used. Instead, the already existing CompositeU.filt[2] is multiplied by exp2(manualEV) after the author ColorGrade exposure is computed, but before the final HDR composite / ACES / sRGB / LUT / Shader Graph and UI. This means the fixed EV and the artistic ColorGrade exposure multiply compositionally, but there is no automatic adaptation in manual mode. Manual EV from native calls and the C++ profile is checked for finiteness and clamped to [-12,+12] before HDR; NaN/Inf are not passed into the shader. On switching into/out of manual mode the camera-local exposure history is invalidated; on returning to automatic mode a new measurement of the current scene is taken instead of blending with the old luminance. Manual mode can work immediately on the first frame — unlike freezeExposure, which requires a valid preceding 1×1 adaptation. When a user Shader Graph fails, the fallback to composite(0) keeps the fixed EV, since filt[2] is applied outside PF_GRADE and PF_AUTO_EXPOSURE. With an invalid final pipeline the report does not declare manual EV as executed. Native API: prisma.setViewManualExposure(stableViewId, true, 1.5f); prisma.setViewManualExposure(stableViewId, false, 0.0f); // explicit disable prisma.clearViewManualExposure(stableViewId); // restore profile inheritance Choosing setViewManualExposure(id,false,...) explicitly overrides the authored manualExposure=true; clear returns control to the profile and invalidates the AE history. Overrides belong to the stable presentation viewId, not to camera resolution/position. retireView, retireUnregisteredViews and shutdown remove them together with the rest of per-camera state, without freeing shared GPU texture caches.

The Stage 58 circular region stays the default; Stage 59 adds meterBox=true with parameters meterHalfWidth and meterHalfHeight in normalized viewport coordinates. The radius and feather of the previous region are preserved. ExposureMeterU gained regionBox (a fifth vec4); kExposureLog uses regionBox.z > 0.5 to select a signed-distance box instead of a circle. The X difference is brought to the scale of frame height by the aspect multiplier; the soft edge uses smoothstep(0,feather,signedDistance). TUV(q) ensures the same Y direction in GL/Metal, and the existing meterOutsideWeight >= 0.02 keeps nonzero contributions outside the region. The global reduction (weighted log sum and weight sum) is unchanged. Native ExposureMeterRegion extends the existing fields with bool box=false; float halfWidth=0.25, halfHeight=0.25 at the end of the struct, preserving old aggregate initializers. Setters clamp finite sizes to [0.01,0.5], and the ROI is not part of authoritative ECS. The camera view report is extended with autoExposureBoxMetered (only for actually encoded exposure). In manualEV mode no meterRegion runs on the frame.

If the HDR luminance pyramid did not finish with a complete 1×1 texture (valid=false or pw/ph != 1), Prisma now does not allocate or write ExposureView.history for this measurement. The old per-camera sample is invalidated, the final composite keeps working without sampled Auto Exposure; a new attempt may be made in future frames. Partially encoded mip passes are not presented as successfully adapted lighting, and no separate GPU sync wait was added. ViewEffectReport.manualExposureEncoded and manualExposureEV report only a truly selected and encoded fixed EV on the last resolve. autoExposureTextureSlot stays -1 for manual. The existing effect matrix marks manual as executed via the base/fallback HDR composite, without a false requirement for ExposureLog pipelines. autoExposureBoxMetered is shown together with autoExposureRegionMetered only after a real GPU meter pass and a subsequent successful composite. In the editor these parameters are available from the shared catalog with explanations and per-viewId status. This is not a full arbitrary metering texture mask, GPU histogram, local exposure, a physical camera simulation, TSR or a fix for all Shader Graph errors. The additional render branches remain experimental until real GPU tests. Actual verification: GitHub readback of five changed source files and 49/49 source-only structural checks. NOT RUN: CMake, clang, CTest, GLSL/MSL/SPIR-V compilation, Metal/GL/GLES/ Vulkan/WebGL GPU smoke/pixel capture, editor undo persistence, HDR parity and performance measurement, CI. For exact commits and the next step see docs/handoffs/prisma-stage-59.md.

h: Stage 60 — graceful Shader Graph / LUT fallback that keeps ordinary effects
x: Previously, on a failure of a user postfx Shader Graph (GLSL/MSL compilation, unsupported sampler layout or invalid input textures), Prisma::resolve() could end up jumping straight to composite(0), losing working fixed Bloom, ColorGrade, LUT, Vignette and other effects. PRISMA now uses the following ordered fallback system: The requested variant with Shader Graph and, if present, GPU Auto Exposure. The same Shader Graph, but without Auto Exposure, if the first attempt did not create a pipeline. Without Shader Graph: the full fixed-effect mask with Auto Exposure (if the prepared HDR 1×1 texture is still available). The same fixed-effect mask without Auto Exposure, if the previous pipeline is unsupported. Only as a last resort — composite(0) without fixed effects. If even that is unavailable, diagnostics do not claim a successful draw. The set of fixed effects is kept as a separate copy fixedMask before the Shader Graph attempts. If a user Shader Graph texture is missing or was not uploaded to the GPU, the whole Shader Graph is excluded from the current composite, and working fixed effects keep running. Successfully creating a Shader Graph pipeline does not by itself mean the input textures loaded: graphInputsReady checks graphTextures_[path].valid() for all used paths after the upload attempt. A missing input is no longer silently presented as a valid "black" texture inside an executed Shader Graph. Especially important after Stage 55: in the graph variant with four images, Auto Exposure uses TEX9. If the graph failed and the fixed-only fallback is used, the last actually selected pipeline requires TEX8. PrismaCompositeTextureLayout::plan(...) is now recomputed based on the actually selected Shader Graph, not the original authored texture list. Exactly this exposureSlot is used in GPU binding, ViewEffectReport and the shader variation. In a graphless fallback, textures in slots 5..8 are not bound unnecessarily. Stage 59 HDR manual EV, ColorGrade and Auto Exposure settings are preserved if the resulting variant is supported. The composite(mask,graphData) cache and deferred GPU-retirement ownership are unchanged.

ViewEffectReport.shaderGraphFallback indicates that the authored Shader Graph was skipped, and the rest of the chain could be used where its pipelines are valid. EffectExecution for ShaderGraph gets encoded=false and a specific reason: a missing/failed-upload texture or a shader compile/composite failure. For working fixed effects, encoded is determined by the final GPU mask, not by the facts of the original request. In the PRISMA — Постобработка editor a corresponding warning per stable viewId appeared. In Prisma::lut(), a read error, an invalid LUT strip N²×N and a GPU upload error now set lastError() with a description and project-relative path. LUT is still negative-cached, so the other effects can keep running without it. graphTexture() now also negative-caches GPU upload errors: re-decoding and failing createTexture every frame are not needed. Resetting the cache via the existing setImageLoader() retires successful texture handles behind a real GPU fence and allows reloading; changing a file on disk without calling this procedure is not by itself live-reload and is not promised in this stage. Unchanged: the postfx format in game.json, the PrismaData catalog, MCP API, ECS gameplay, default effect settings, SpectraFX, per-view exposure ownership and user Shader Graph formats. Actual verification: readback from GitHub of Prisma.cpp, Prisma.h, PrismaWindow.cpp and 33/33 source-only checks of fallback logic, GPU input availability, final exposure slot, fixed mask and LUT errors. NOT RUN: clang/CMake, native editor/client, CTest, GLSL/MSL/Vulkan shader compiler, Metal/GL/GLES/WebGL/Vulkan GPU smoke, actual HDR pixels, timed GPU frames, screenshots and CI. Detailed handoff: docs/handoffs/prisma-stage-60.md.

h: Stage 61 — reactive transparent edges for Motion Blur and safe FXAA
x: Stage 61 fixes two specific PRISMA presentation paths: SDR FXAA no longer substitutes an invalid texture for the input when creating the intermediate render target fails, and optional Motion Blur can suppress blending of color taps by the difference in reactive coverage at the edges of translucent objects/particles. The work stays genre-independent and does not touch authoritative ECS or the separate SpectraFX.

A new optional parameter of the existing motionBlur: reactiveTapRejection, range 0..1, default 0. It is appended at the end of the effect catalog in PrismaData.cpp, so all previous numeric offsets, old postfx JSON, presets and native/volume profiles stay compatible. At zero the previous shader weight and previous filter apply. MotionBlurU gained a fifth vec4 tapInfo. Only kMotionBlur uses the extended UBO; other passes (Temporal, DoF, Bloom, FXAA, ExposureLog) and the reactive texture format did not change. tapInfo.x receives reactiveTapRejection only with a valid input MotionTextureInput (RGBA8, size of the current scene render target, a check of declared metadata and the available RHI textureInfo). When the reactive mask is absent/rejected, the value is zero and the shader keeps the previous behavior. If the filter is active, the current pixel and its neighboring color taps read TEX3 reactive R. Taps with substantially different coverage get a reduced weight: keep *= 1 - strength * smoothstep(0.1,0.8,abs(tapReactive-centerReactive)). This is an addition to the already existing depth filtering (hardware or linear depth), not its replacement. If the sum of weights is zero, the original sharp RGB is applied. In new HDR runs Motion Blur returns the original alpha centerColor.a, not 1.0, since the post effect changes radiance RGB, not scene transparency. Canonical TemporalResolve still itself writes depth into its own history alpha — this contract is unchanged. Dependency on real reactive geometry: the mask is built separately by Renderer3D and additional providers (for example, particles/water), and the temporary mask image is NOT kept between frames. This stage does not attempt to fix missing coverage of a specific material or read GPU pixels back on the CPU. ViewEffectReport per stable viewId now stores reactiveInputSupplied, reactiveInputAccepted and motionBlurReactiveEdgesEnabled. This is CPU metadata/RHI acceptance, not GPU pixel validation: a legacy borrowed handle without metadata may be considered acceptable when the backend does not provide introspection. The last field becomes true only when MotionBlur is actually encoded, the required input is verified and strength is greater than zero. The PRISMA editor shows mask availability and filter status.

Previously the SDR prepass did src=target(kAa) before checking whether the creation result was valid. With a failed RGBA8 target or depth attachment, composite could sample an invalid src. Now fxaaInput keeps the original scene/post-chain texture, fxaaOutput is created separately, and the prepass runs only if input/output and depth are valid. Graph FXAA (opt-in) and the ordinary direct draw use the same two verified handles, and src=fxaaOutput is assigned only after an encoded draw. If allocation failed, the rest of the chain continues with the previous src, without a false fxaaEncoded=true. For the HDR fallback FXAA, which is applied after the final Composite and only if TemporalResolve did not run, a check of pipe.valid() was added before starting the intermediate AA target/pass. This rules out reading an empty composite target if the pipeline could not be obtained at all. The output target/depth check is kept. TAA and FXAA remain mutually exclusive on the single HDR presentation output. No new GPU history or shared texture owners were introduced. Rendering keeps the current Stage 54 fence-retirement contracts. Actual verification: GitHub readback of PrismaData.cpp, PrismaShaders.h, Prisma.cpp, Prisma.h, PrismaWindow.cpp and PrismaMotionTextureInput.h, 40/40 source-only structural checks (checking logic and calls in the sources). NOT RUN: CMake/clang, GLSL/MSL/SPIR-V compilation, CTest, Editor/GameClient, Metal/GL/GLES/ Vulkan/WebGL, screenshot/alpha/historical parity, temporal ghosting and performance. The next agent should read docs/handoffs/prisma-stage-61.md.

h: Stage 62 — reactive mask on the first frame, Camera Cut and resize
x: From this stage on, Renderer3D separates two independent presentation producers: (a) object velocity vectors, which require the previous camera and a history of current/previous transforms, and (b) current-frame RGBA8 reactive coverage, which does not need a preceding pose. Previously the whole reactive pass was inside if (history.target.valid() && history.depth.valid()), and the function exited with return on the first frame, on camera cut and on resize. Therefore the transparency of water, particles and morph/skinned translucent objects could be left uncovered by the reactive mask precisely where temporal history is invalid.

renderObjectMotionVectors(PostProcess&) is still called on the final scene frame, before Prisma::resolve. In it, velocityHistoryReady is determined only by previousCameraValid && history.valid && !resize. When previous data is missing, no false/zero object-motion velocity frames are sent to Prisma. Current rigid/animated transform poses are collected as before; after the reactive pass they are saved for the next frame. If the viewport changed size, the target/depth/reactive textures are all placed into the existing GPU-fenced queue via queueObjectMotionTexture(...), rather than destroyed synchronously. This preserves the Stage 54 ownership contract. The new private method Renderer3D::renderCurrentFrameReactiveMask(PostProcess&, ObjectMotionHistory&, gfx::TextureHandle sceneDepth,int w,int h) uses only the current viewProj_, model poses, scene depth and ready framebuffer sizes. This helper is called after the conditional object velocity pass and is not nested in it. It provides its own private depth attachment for reactive-only frames (Depth) and, when the required geometry is present, creates an RGBA8 reactive target. Scene depth from Prisma is passed as a borrowed sampler and never becomes a writable depth attachment. The absence of RGBA16F velocity does not block the helper at the Renderer3D level if a native post hook requested such reactive work and provided scene depth; the ordinary Prisma HDR policy still decides on its own whether it needs MotionBlur/Temporal Resolve at all. Current coverage rendering keeps the previous sources: rigid transparent models and fading LOD, morph/skinned/baked translucent models with the current pose for both motion matrices, immediate water MeshVertex geometry, motionReactiveDraws_ from particles and custom native providers. The mask is still created/cleared only on the current frame, blending merges coverage, and it is passed to Prisma as MotionTextureInput::declared(reactive,w,h,RGBA8). Cases without reactive geometry/callback, or without an available depth/target/pipeline, are not declared a successful reactive pass.

Renderer3D::ObjectMotionStats now has: velocitySeedOnly — first frame / invalid/cut/resize, so as not to present pose initialization as GPU object velocity; and reactiveSubmitted — a separate flag for an actually encoded current-frame mask. The historical submitted remains an indicator of the object-velocity pass, not reactive-only. The PRISMA camera stores ViewEffectReport.objectVelocityInputAccepted and reactiveWithoutObjectVelocity, taking into account a separate MotionTextureInput check: first the declared width/height/format are checked, then RHI textureInfo, if the backend supports introspection. These fields do not prove GPU pixel content. The editor shows mask-only pass for reactive coverage without a valid object velocity texture; the separate MotionBlur reactive edge rejection status still depends on an actually encoded blur and the configured parameter. Kept unchanged: stable per-view identity regardless of two cameras having the same resolution; resetObjectMotionHistory(viewId) and the camera-cut epoch; GPU-fenced retirement; no ECS mutation; Prisma::resolve and HDR temporal history as the sole color history owner; HUD outside post-processing. The reactive mask does not become a long-lived temporal input. Checks actually performed: readback of 6 source files from the connected GitHub, 42/42 structural source checks, static C++ brace scope balance 2/2. NOT RUN: CMake/clang/Obj-C++, CTest, shader compilation, first frame/cut/resize tests on real Metal/GL/GLES/Vulkan/WebGL, pixel capture, reactive coverage screenshots, GPU fences, profiling and CI. Real backend outcomes must be obtained in the shared validation phase, not declared PASS from the sources. Exact commits and the next task: docs/handoffs/prisma-stage-62.md.

h: Stage 63 — exact rigid alpha-cutout / dissolve reactive coverage and lifecycle callbacks
x: This stage extends the current Renderer3D::renderCurrentFrameReactiveMask (Stage 62) without changing the architecture, the Prisma/MCP format, HDR color history or Reactives ownership. The reactive mask remains an RGBA8 current-frame input from Renderer3D to PRISMA; the per-camera motion history is an independent component.

h: Rigid models: exact AlphaMask, dissolve and LOD
x: For rigid models with AlphaMode::Mask or dissolve > 0, a separate shader variant was added: reactive_shaders::kCutoutVS/kCutoutFS/kCutoutMSL and objectMotionReactiveCutoutPipeline_. The main water/transparent/mesh pipeline is left unchanged. The shader repeats the fragment conditions of the ordinary ModelShaders: baseTex alpha, baseColor.a, optional vertex alpha (excluding vertex-occlusion/AO), alphaCutoff, KHR base-UV offset/scale/rotation, screen-space 4×4 LOD dither and the same object-space noise modelNoise3(opos*7)*0.7 + modelNoise3(opos*19)*0.3 for dissolve. TeamMode::BaseAlpha uses baseColor alpha without baseTexture alpha; for TeamMode::VertexAlpha it does not multiply vertex alpha twice, following the material. The scene still samples the foreign sceneDepth read-only; the reactive pass has its own writable history.depth. BlendMode::Screen is used to merge coverage. The shader source provides the same clipping logic in GLSL and Metal, but GPU parity requires real shader tests. New uniforms layout only for this pipeline: ReactiveCutoutUniforms {mvp,params,lod,uv0,uv1,maskInfo}, 144 bytes. Vertex attributes are the real ModelVertex position[0], uv[2], color[4]. AlphaCutout texture bind slot 1, scene depth in slot 0. Since the shader precisely discards alpha holes, reactivity no longer paints the whole triangle for foliage/grilles. Shader Graph vertex displacement and geometry-driven models still require separate coverage producers; do not claim them as supported by this rigid path.

For skinned/morph/baked translucent models, kAnimatedFS and its MSL generator gained an optional U1.reactiveLod (fragment buffer(2)) with exact 4×4 LOD dithering on the current frame. Animated LOD and dissolve now provide coverage even when the previous pose is absent. Dissolve for animated objects is conservative — the mask may cover fragments that the main ModelShaders discards by object-space noise. Exact animated alpha-cutout/actor aperture requires a new current-object-space varying or a separate material-specific shader, not implemented here. In Renderer3D, mask readiness is checked per required source: separately for simple rigid, cutout/dissolve rigid, skinned, baked, MeshVertex or motionReactiveDraws_. The presence of an unsuitable pre-created shader (for example, a skin pipeline when the baked pipeline is missing) is no longer grounds to publish an empty reactive mask. When a callback was registered for the current scene frame but the active postprocess, scene depth or mask pipeline is unavailable, ObjectMotionStats.reactiveCallbacksDropped counts the unexecuted calls; the callback is not carried over to the next frame. The registration contract is unchanged: addMotionReactiveDraw after beginScene, but before resolvePrisma. The renderer invokes callbacks only with the mask pass open: the provider must only record draws, not call beginPass/endPass, keep its GPU resources until submission completes and combine coverage without destroying previous pixels. The list is cleared after resolve, when the postprocess is inactive or at the start of a new scene frame. The intermediate mask is not cached across camera cuts and is not carried between viewIds. Renderer3D::ObjectMotionStats was extended with cutoutReactiveDraws, dissolveReactiveDraws, reactiveCallbacksDropped; the previous reactiveDraws/reactiveAnimatedDraws/ reactiveCallbacks/reactiveSubmitted are kept. The counters mean CPU-encoded submissions / callback invocations, not GPU completion or proven pixel content. The shared per-view Prisma::ViewEffectReport from Stage 62 and the GPU-fenced retirement of Stage 54 were not changed. Actually performed: GitHub readback of Renderer3D.{h,cpp}, Renderer3DReactiveShaders.h, ModelShaders.h and Model.h; 51/51 static source-presence, binding and ownership checks, static balance of C++ and shader header brace scopes. NOT RUN: CMake/clang, Metal/GLSL/MSL shader compilation, native editor/game, CTest, Metal/GL/GLES/Vulkan/WebGL, alpha-mask/dissolve/camera-cut pixel readback, multi-view callbacks, memory/fence stress, profiler and CI. Commit description and the next stage — docs/handoffs/prisma-stage-63.md.

h: Stage 64 — precise animated reactive alpha/dissolve and Actor Reveal
x: Stage 64 completes the bounded functionality of the gap found in Stage 63: animated skin/morph/baked reactive coverage used to be produced only as a conservative silhouette, without applying the material AlphaMode::Mask, object-space dissolve and the local kDrawActorReveal aperture. In the new implementation the ordinary velocity pipeline stays unchanged, and the reactive path gets a separate GPU shader variant.

Renderer3DReactiveShaders.h now provides two testable generation functions: reactive_shaders::animatedVertexGlsl(source,baked) and reactive_shaders::animatedMsl(source,baked). They take the existing kDeformedVS/kDeformedMSL or kBakedVS/kBakedMSL, substitute UV (ModelVertex attribute 2), vertex color/alpha (attribute 4) and the current deformed object-space pose, keeping the previous skin/morph/baked sources (attributes 5/6, U0/U3/U4/U5 and texture 7/8). The resulting local text variants are passed to createShader; the original motion shaders and velocity output stay the same. If the expected source anchor is missing, the generator returns an empty string, and Renderer3D does not create an invalid reactive pipeline. kAnimatedFS (GLSL) and the generated MSL fragment use the new ReactiveAnimatedU1, 160 bytes: lod[4],uv0[4],uv1[4],maskInfo[4],world[16], reveal[4],revealAxis[4]. It occupies the ordinary uniform slot 1 (Metal buffer 2) and does not interfere with the skin/baked deformation slot U3/U4/U5. The shader still renders only current-frame RGBA8 reactive coverage, does not write velocity and does not use previous frame history. Depth is sampled from the foreign sceneDepth, and the writable attachment is the renderer-private history.depth. For animated objects the same current-frame clipping conditions are now reproduced exactly: 4×4 LOD dither, UV offset/scale/rotation, the material cutoff baseTex alpha * baseColor alpha (+ vertex alpha, if allowed), and modelNoise3(currentDeformedLocalPos * 7) * 0.7 + modelNoise3(currentDeformedLocalPos * 19) * 0.3 for dissolve. The TeamMode::BaseAlpha and TeamMode::VertexAlpha settings do not multiply vertex/texture alpha twice; vertex occlusion/AO is not treated as opacity.

h: Actor Reveal for rigid and animated
x: kDrawActorReveal with an active Renderer3D::actorReveal now makes the model a source of reactive coverage, even if it is fully opaque and has no LOD fade/dissolve. Only the main camera pass (geometryMainView_) passes the world-space actor center/radius, camera axis and view-dependent attenuation from the same Renderer3DModels.cpp formula. The fragment shader repeats the aperture: radial=length(delta-axis*depth), radius=actorRadius*max(0.01,1-depth*axisScale), coverage=(1-smoothstep(radius*.48,radius,radial))* smoothstep(.04,.24,depth) and 4×4 dither discard. In the inactive mode reveal.w=0 and this path does not affect the mask. For the rigid alpha/dissolve shader, ReactiveCutoutUniforms was extended from 144 to 240 bytes, by adding the world matrix and reveal/axis in U0. GLSL and Metal receive the vertex's current world position. For animated, the current deformed local position is used, transformed through the passed world matrix in the fragment. This is not a separate draw pass and not an ECS system: the source remains the same current-frame reactive pass from Stage 62. In Renderer3D::renderCurrentFrameReactiveMask, replay of animated materials now sets up ReactiveAnimatedU1, a separate baseTexture sampler slot 1 and the vertex attributes UV/color/skin. Actor reveal, dissolve, alpha cutoff and LOD parameters are set per ModelItem. The statistic ObjectMotionStats.actorRevealReactiveDraws complements the existing cutoutReactiveDraws, dissolveReactiveDraws, lodReactiveDraws. These are CPU-encoded draw counts, not confirmation of GPU visibility. Resources stay with Renderer3D; the existing GPU-fenced target retirement and stable per-viewId ownership are unchanged.

The exact source formula of ordinary alpha/dissolve/reveal is supported for rigid and animated models. Not claimed: per-pixel parity with arbitrary material Shader Graphs, vertex displacement, custom transparent pipelines, GLES/Metal depth conventions or correct multi-layer transparency — these must be provided by separate reactive providers or native GPU validation. The GPU shader permutations have not yet been compiled or run on a device. Actually: GitHub readback and 61/61 static structural/source checks; additionally 4/4 generator fixtures skin/baked × GLSL/MSL with the expected current-pose/UV/alpha output. NOT RUN: CMake/clang/Obj-C++, GLSL/MSL/SPIR-V compilation, CTest, editor/client, Metal/GL/GLES/Vulkan/WebGL, pixel/alpha parity, Actor Reveal cut screenshot, GPU fencing/memory pressure, benchmarks/CI.
