h: Stage 102: model source priorities and estimated GPU-retirement memory
x: The host owns one render::ModelAssetProvider, or a separate provider per presentation scope, not one per animated actor. For native model imports, requestAsync(source, ModelLoadPriority) selects Background, Visible or Interactive for queued CPU jobs; an active worker is never preempted. Call publishReady(device,maxCount,budgetMs) at the render-thread frame boundary, with a hard model-count cap and an advisory elapsed-time cap. The first GPU upload may exceed budgetMs; nothing is published from inside a worker. Preserve source revisions, and detach any old AnimationSourceFrame, graph, pose and borrowed Model* before invalidation. No second MotionWeave evaluation is introduced. ModelResourceCache can now estimate the known, model-owned retirement footprint and apply an optional byte-derived admission limit. ModelResidentEstimate deliberately does not charge borrowed texture leases or shared geometry pages and is NOT an exact VRAM reading. Never release an object because a limit is reached; only its own completed GPU fence authorizes destruction. The standalone aiverse_modelview --provider --no-merge is a second real generic aiverse::View consumer for static raw assets, alongside the editor's opt-in independent raw preview. Precomputed poses on the legacy animated modelview path remain authored by the existing host; View only submits them once. The game-specific GameView adapter is still in use elsewhere and has not been retired. NOT RUN: all CMake, CTest, native modelview/editor, GPU backend, sanitizer, snapshot and visual parity checks remain deferred.

h: Stage 103 — multi-worker source preparation and single-authority View display
x: The general model resource owner can now prepare multiple independent model files on CPU workers without involving the ECS World or GPU: render::ModelAssetProvider::setCpuWorkerCount(1..8), setCpuMaxQueued, and requestAsync(source,priority) forward to AsyncModelCpuQueue. The default remains one worker; an editor or native host can opt into more. Workers have no knowledge of genre, FPS/RTS player types, scene packets or MotionWeave graph evaluation. ModelAssetProvider::publishReady(device,...) uploads prepared Models on the render/device owner thread. Authoring hosts needing validation before GPU publication may instead call takePrepared(result), compile their rig against result.model, then call publishPrepared(device, freshGenerationKey,std::move(result.model)). This path uses the same staging transaction and rejects publication while a Model read lease is active. cancelAsync(source) invalidates pending CPU results without evicting the last-good resident Model; stopAsync() joins the reader before its project is destroyed. Retire the old generation only after successful publication, detaching pose and renderer caches first. Studio's native facial preview uses this split path. One ModelReadLease spans pose evaluation through the synchronous Renderer3D submission. Project changes drain the old owner and its texture cache, so identical relative paths cannot reuse another project's textures. CPU preparation runs in the worker; GPU upload/retirement and the single Animator stay on the render thread. Bad imports retain last-good ownership and report the rejected generation instead of drawing a stale asset. Priorities are Interactive, Visible, Background. Pending jobs of equal priority are FIFO; after sustained high-priority dispatches, an oldest queued request gets scheduled to reduce background starvation. No executing job is preempted. Each CPU result contains its source revision; on asset invalidation it is discarded rather than publishing a stale Model, and on shutdown all worker futures are joined before the reader/texture cache is released. Caller-provided FileReader callbacks must be reentrant when more than one worker is configured. Shared GPU texture ownership is measured once by ModelTextureCache::gpuOwnerEstimate(), never per borrower. The device-global geometry pool remains a separate resource owner; these figures are source-derived RGBA8-equivalent diagnostics, not exact driver VRAM usage. The editor SceneRenderable source now uses the canonical aiverse::View::submitModel and submitMesh for ordinary model and mesh submissions. Selected/hovered specialized mesh silhouettes retain their previous renderer-specific path. The owner still constructs the ModelDraw transformation, tint and outline; View does not run graph animations a second time. The legacy RTS portrait/type-appearance compatibility layer remains active. Validation NOT RUN: native CMake compiler, CTest, sanitizer, actual GPU/Metal/Vulkan/GL/WebGL, FPS/RTS/editor screenshots, multithreaded loader contention and visual parity have not been verified. See the Stage 103 handoff for exact SHA and next action.

h: Stage 104 — persistent multi-worker import and View selection styles
x: The native render::AsyncModelCpuQueue now reuses 1–8 persistent std::thread workers instead of spawning a new asynchronous task for each model file. It uses condition-variable dispatch, bounded waiting/ready queues, source revision invalidation and the existing Visual/Interactive/Background priorities. Configuration is host-owned: the reader and CPU image cache must be reentrant; all GPU upload, source publication and MotionWeave pose state remain on the render owner thread. Changing the worker count joins in-flight tasks; do not reconfigure during an interactive rendering frame. Shared GPU geometry is accounted by page identity, not by the number of animations or imported Models. The geometryPoolReferencedStats(device,modelPointers) API can accept models from multiple render host owners in ONE collection, avoiding double charging a page referenced by many models or views. ModelResourceCache::geometryPoolModelReferences includes currently resident and GPU-retired models. The device's global geometry pool remains the authoritative page capacity owner, and shared textures remain counted by their texture-cache owner. aiverse::view::MeshObject now has genre-independent selectionOutline / selectionColor styling. The editor's SceneRenderable selected/hovered mesh submissions and selection edge lines are routed through aiverse::View::submitMesh/submitLine with the legacy renderer-specific silhouette implementation preserved internally. This does not tick an animation graph or add gameplay selection components to MotionWeave. Full game::GameView retirement is still unfinished. NOT RUN: native build, CTest, desktop/mobile GPU tests, editor selection visual parity, CPU thread sanitizer and geometry pool GPU-lifetime checks. See Stage 104 agent handoff.

A group computes unique model and shared texture ownership, includes retired models waiting on GPU fences and deduplicates shared geometry pages by their device-global identity. Its Ready, PendingGpuRetirement and DeviceUnhealthy statuses are diagnostics/admission policy, not a license to free resources early. Pending GPU work is expected, not an error. Estimates use known source geometry and RGBA8-equivalent texture metadata; never call them exact driver VRAM occupancy. Native editor raw-model preview now groups the main scene, portrait preview and raw-source provider, with an optional group-wide estimated admission budget. Failed GPU health pauses new model publication, leaving all GPU-retired models alive until correct fence completion can be established. game::Portrait::renderAppearance(const render::ModelDraw&, Camera,background) is a generic synchronous offscreen consumer that keeps the host-selected material override, node-material mapping, geometry policy, team tint, variant and any precomputed pose. Raw-model, precomputed-pose and RTS-resolved static portraits delegate to it. Complex animated portraits retain their existing RTS compatibility fallback and its one MotionWeave graph evaluator; no second player or render-side animation tick is introduced. Follow Stage 105 in the animation handoff.

h: Stage 106 — expiring GPU owner references and verified failure states
x: Multiple native model/resource owners can be observed through render::RenderResourceOwnerGroup. Its registrations now carry the caches' weak_ptr lifetime tokens, so a destroyed cache is skipped rather than accessed. The group is still device-owner-thread-only; a weak reference does not make simultaneous GPU resource teardown and snapshot thread-safe. The group doesn't own or shut down render resources. GPU retirement now distinguishes a normal outstanding fence from an actual failed completion token via gfx::Device::resourceRetirementStatus. A failed Model retirement batch remains alive, even when newer tokens signal success. Only a successful full-device GPU idle barrier permits cleanup and abandonRetirementTokenAfterIdle. RenderResourceGroupStats::health reports RetirementFenceFailed separately from PendingGpuRetirement and DeviceUnhealthy. These statuses only affect NEW resource admission, never authoritative gameplay or existing MotionWeave graph clocks. The model material-preview shape now delegates offscreen draw to the same generic Portrait::renderAppearance + aiverse::View::submitModel path as native static models and precomputed poses. Material authoring still happens through the old RTS-compatible host; dynamic/complex animation fallback has not been removed and retains exactly one animation writer. NOT RUN: compilation, CTest, GPU/device-loss tests, editor screenshots, FPS/RTS parity, thread sanitizer and CI. Stage 106 handoff lists exact source refs and next step.

x: The generic render::ModelResourceCache now explicitly binds to one gfx::Device and one owning thread via bindResourceDevice(device). Cross-device or cross-thread GPU model mutation is rejected. x: Native host model caches now support RenderDeviceLifetime::Lease and ModelResourceCache::bindResourceDevice(device,lease) to distinguish re-created GPUs even when a platform reuses the same gfx::Device* address. This is NOT device loss recovery or a way to release unresolved fence-retired resources. h: Source model reimport without losing compatible playback (Stage 146)
x: MotionWeaveSourceBridge::forgetForReimport(World&, sourceIds), surfaced as View::forgetSourcesForReimport(ids), is a synchronous, optional pre-retirement handshake. Call before old CPU Model/compiled Graph destruction; the bridge first captures named graph state and clip phases from a valid presentation player, then forgets its ECS entity. The next sync can consume the seed once when logical source ID/generation, exact copied rig names/parents, explicit different nonzero old/new publication epochs and a distinct Model address all match. No old pointer is retained/dereferenced; the old address is a value-only conservative rejection guard. The record is bounded to 8192 sources and expires after 120 source-sync calls. The existing forget and clear APIs intentionally discard continuity, suitable for despawns or session resets. The adapter does not own CPU/GPU leases, cannot reconstruct an already-destroyed Graph, does not transfer root motion, authored event streams, IK/ragdoll/native solver state or gameplay ECS, and must not run during animation worker dispatch. RTS Model and graph invalidation paths opt in; FPS and editor parity need separate audit. Native compiler/CTest/GPU validation NOT RUN for this source-only stage; see Stage 146 handoff.

h: Stage 148 — universal ECS Graph-only replacement and single source owner

tests/animation/HumanoidLocomotionFixture.h — 53-bone procedural humanoid (+Y up, +Z forward, metres) with planted-foot clips authored through solveTwoBoneIK and baked to 30 Hz keys: Idle 2 s, Walk 1.2 m/s, Run 3.0 m/s, Stop (walk → idle in 0.36 m), TurnLeft (90° in place), their in-place *_IP variants and optional GaitNN speed variants. aiverse_motionweave_core_tests (CTest motionweave_core, 292 checks): sampling, world matrices, blend/mask, sync groups, morph-free path, two-bone IK, rig world reuse, motion matching and a foot-slide regression. aiverse_motionweave_locomotion_review <dir> (tools) drives the humanoid through idle → start → walk → run → walk+turn → stop → idle → turn in place with three graphs (blend, blend-sync, motion-matching) and reports planted-foot slide, pops (joint acceleration, rotation step) and broken poses; tools/animation/motionweave_review_render.py <dir> renders contact sheets, footprints, slide plots and an MP4. Committed output: docs/qa/motionweave-locomotion-2026-11-22/. aiverse_motionweave_humanoid_bench (tools): per-character CPU cost for 1/10/100/1000 actors and the building blocks; uses only graph features that exist on origin/main, so the same source measures before/after.

h: What the review found and what changed
x: Finding Evidence (review) Fix Motion matching wrapped one-shot clips (Stop) to frame 0 35 cm foot teleport in one frame, pop 1298 m/s² database clips accept {"clip":"Stop","loop":false}: clamp at end, search on arrival, trajectory holds the final root; pop now 293 m/s² (= steady run) Motion matching could not pick a turn in place (trajectory had positions only) TurnLeft never chosen; 0.157 m/s slide while turning trajectory samples accept "facing":"<vector param>" (+facingWeight, facingAxis); turn-in-place slide 0.048 m/s Motion matching faded in from the bind pose at spawn straight-leg frame, ankles below ground first selection starts on the match (below-ground frames 27 → 7) Walk/run blend clocks were independent planted-foot slide at w=0.5: 0.94 m/s blend "sync": true locks normalized phase, blended cycle rate: 0.31 m/s (core test) Not fixed (documented limitations, visible in slide.png): state-machine crossfades still start from a frozen outgoing pose, so idle→walk starts (≈0.87 m/s slide for 0.25 s) and walk→stop slide; walking turns slide (no turn clips / foot locking); motion matching with only walk and run speeds slides while the host speed is between them (data coverage), and the idealized 0.6 s lookahead starts stepping before the host moves. No foot-lock IK pass exists yet; that and inertialized state transitions are the next steps.

h: CPU cost (Apple M3 Ultra, Release, 53 bones)
x: Interleaved A/B of the same bench source against the engine before (4a9d15b52 = origin/main + sync groups) and after (d635f8295) the optimisations; the Mac was shared with other agents (load 7–15 on 28 cores), numbers are medians of 3 runs and repeated within ~5 % across rounds. µs per character per frame, sequential MotionWeave::update: scenario 1 10 100 1000 scheduler, 1000 actors clip 2.61 → 2.06 2.97 → 2.34 3.23 → 2.67 4.73 → 3.90 0.65 → 0.57 blend walk/run 4.73 → 3.35 5.15 → 3.75 5.62 → 4.27 7.25 → 6.44 1.04 → 0.88 blend + 2-leg IK 6.83 → 4.72 7.25 → 5.17 7.69 → 5.92 9.48 → 8.37 1.34 → 1.13 motion matching (814 frames) 6.62 → 3.77 7.00 → 4.11 7.44 → 4.33 8.76 → 5.49 1.18 → 0.74 motion matching + IK 8.50 → 5.23 9.10 → 5.68 9.56 → 5.94 10.88 → 7.12 1.47 → 0.97 Building blocks (µs/call): MotionDatabase::search 814×24 15.8 → 1.48; graph update+evaluate: clip 1.60 → 1.19, blend 3.75 → 2.35, blend+IK 5.83 → 3.74, MM 5.64 → 2.75, MM+IK 7.65 → 4.17. Unchanged blocks: sampleClip 0.66, worldMatrices 0.40, solveTwoBoneIK 0.30, bindPose 0.26. Hot spots and what was done: MM query extracted the full feature vector (2–8 extra pose samples, trajectory part discarded) → pose part only, per-thread scratch. MM search: per-frame std::vector rows, double sums → contiguous sqrt(weight)-scaled float matrix, 4-wide sums, early exit (10×). NodePose carries 64 morph weights (296 B vs 40 B of t/r/s): every pose copy and blend touched them → AnimationGraph::morphFree() graphs copy and blend only t/r/s (exact: internal poses keep bind weights). Each rig unit rebuilt all world matrices → reuse after twoBoneIK. Tried and reverted: hand-written affine worldMatrices product was slower (0.44 vs 0.39 µs) than the vectorised generic one. Remaining cost at 1000 sequential actors is memory traffic (per-actor poses and instances; µs/char grows ~1.6× from 1 to 1000 actors) plus the ECS layer (defaults map copy per entity per frame, final worldMatrices). Use the persistent MotionWeaveScheduler (7 workers here): 1000 MM+IK characters cost ≈1 ms/frame.

ui::UiModelView (engine/ui/UiModelView.h) renders one model into a texture exposed to RmlUi as . Create one view per image with init(device, ui, name, width, height), render it outside any open graphics pass before UiLayer::render(), and call shutdown() before destroying the device or UI layer. Dimensions are 16–2048 pixels. The view owns its renderer and color/depth targets; the caller owns models, materials, animation and scene entities. For a scene object, pass the host's already prepared render::ModelDraw and a camera to renderDraw. This preserves its model, materials, transform and current pose. For an independent animated object, keep a separate presentation render::Animator, advance it once per frame and call renderAnimator(model, animator, camera). A host with a MotionWeave graph can instead pass its evaluated render::Pose to renderPose. No UI path mutates authoritative ECS state or advances a scene object's animation twice. ui::UiModelView icon; icon.init(device, uiLayer, "selected", 256, 256); icon.renderDraw(draw, portraitCamera); // draw: scene entity's current packet // RmlUi: render::Animator separateAnimation; separateAnimation.setModel(&model); // Configure a clip with Animator::play, then on each presentation frame: separateAnimation.update(deltaSeconds); icon.renderAnimator(model, separateAnimation, portraitCamera); The source model and any borrowed draw pointers must remain valid through the synchronous render call. Rendering into the target and sampling it in RmlUi must happen in separate passes. Resource retirement still follows the device's GPU completion rules. The host chooses camera framing and any UI image orientation needed by its graphics backend. Source on GitHub: docs/ui-model-view.md

h: VIVID Character Creator и адаптер MetaHuman
x: Character Creator — редактор внешности цифрового человека в AIVERSE Studio. Он работает с персонажем проекта (glTF / GLB / FBX) или с процедурной ДНК VIVID и показывает результат в нативном вьюпорте. Открывается в рабочем пространстве Character (⌘7 или вкладка вверху).

Пресеты → Персонаж: выберите модель, нажмите «Загрузить профиль» и «Показать». Для экспорта MetaHuman нажмите «Проверить и настроить»: роли материалов и меши лица выставятся сами (см. ниже). Меняйте категории слева: Лицо, Скульпт, Кожа, Макияж, Глаза, Волосы, Тело, Одежда, Поза и свет. При включённом «Применять изменения сразу» вьюпорт обновляется на ходу. Сохраните образ в «Образах» (с превью), соберите персонажа в «Одежде» и нажмите «В игру».

Пресеты. Образы-карточки с превью, смешивание двух образов, возраст одним ползунком, случайный персонаж с замками, черновик по описанию («пожилой рыбак, седые волосы…») и запрос для агента, толпа из N вариантов, пакет персонажа .aivchar для переноса между проектами. Лицо. Круг смешивания шести архетипов; отдельные части (нос, рот, глаза, брови, челюсть, скулы) получают свою ручку — кнопкой или кликом по лицу во вьюпорте. Пропорции и импорт лица из скана, фото или отдельной головы. Полупрозрачный референс поверх вьюпорта. Скульпт. Кисть «вытянуть / вдавить» протяжкой по лицу, круг кисти, симметрия, история. Кожа, глаза, волосы. Тон, фактура, поры, веснушки; радужка и склера; цвет и седина прядей. Макияж. Помада, румяна, тени, щетина — слои на текстуре кожи. «Разместить по лицу» находит губы, щёки и веки по геометрии; положение можно поправить вручную. Тело. Рост в сантиметрах, пропорции, линейка с делениями по 10 см во вьюпорте. Одежда. Комплект модели и вещи с примеркой во вьюпорте, цвет каждой вещи, причёски из проекта. Сборка пишет content/Characters/<имя>/model.glb с LOD для скинованных частей и показывает бюджет треугольников; «В игру» добавляет тип юнита с этой моделью. Поза и свет. Мимика для проверки (улыбка, смех, удивление, речь…), позы, клипы модели и анимации из файлов (через <модель>.clips.json), восемь световых пресетов. Сверху: камера Лицо / Торс / Рост, «До/после» (удерживайте — исходная модель), ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z.

Без Unreal и без .dna в рантайме. Адаптер читает обычный экспорт MetaHuman и: узнаёт скелет UE5 (spine_05, neck_02, head), FaceMesh и кости FACIAL_*; расставляет роли материалов: кожа головы и тела, глаза, ресницы, волосы и брови, одежда; оболочки глаз, слёзы, слюна и хрящ скрываются, зубы сохраняют исходный материал; выбирает меши лица и считает, сколько из 52 мимических каналов ARKit есть в модели; в превью ведёт суставы *_half (половина сгиба) и твисты предплечья, а челюсть и глаза — по каналам ARKit, если морфы их ещё не двигают. Проверено на экспортах Ada и Bruce (тест vivid_metahuman_adapter). Не поддерживается: полный RigLogic (корректоры bulge, in/out, fwd/bck стоят в bind pose), анимация остальных лицевых костей (мимика идёт через морфы), грум прядями (только карточки), чтение .dna в игре (только офлайн-инструмент tools/vivid-dna-import). GLB со сжатием Draco распакуйте офлайн: node tools/vivid-dna-import/decompress_draco.cjs <tooling> in.glb out.glb.

Подробный журнал разработки: vivid.md. Source on GitHub: docs/vivid-creator.md

The lighting branch provides an explicit, genre-independent, one-bounce diffuse probe overlay. It composes with existing direct lighting. It does not implicitly enable itself, replace direct-light ownership, or write simulation/ECS state.

Use engine/render/GiMainCpuBridge.h for budgeted CPU tracing and engine/render/GiMainGpuBridge.h for bounded Metal/Vulkan compute. Both consume immutable GiChunkedGeometrySnapshot, stable geometry revisions, linear RGB GiMovingLight sources and optional indirect-only GiEnvironmentLight. apps/renderbench/DynamicGiHost.h is a working native host example. Before CPU mesh arrays are released, build immutable opaque caster chunks with material diffuse albedo. The benchmark retains CPU geometry for opted-in animated assets and republishes posed opaque caster chunks automatically. Initialize a fixed probe lattice. GPU supports up to 8192 triangles, 16 lights, 32 probes per dispatch and 8–64 rays per probe. CPU supports 8–128 rays and uses an adaptive probe budget. Lattices are capped at 20000 probes. A CPU budget is a scheduling target, not a guaranteed frame-time bound for an individual ray. On the render owner thread, publish geometry/light/environment snapshots and update before graphics passes. GPU publication requires an active Device frame. Retry deferred publications after prior compute and graphics reader fences complete. Rejected source data must not be presented as current data. Call renderer.beginScene(...), then renderer.setDynamicGiOverlay(bridge) for every view. beginScene clears previous attachment. The bridge must outlive all submitted draws. Textured Shader Graph receivers reserve tex13 for GI and move graph samplers to tex14+. GPU-instance/ICB uses ordinary draws while GI is attached. PBR receivers support High/Low and multiply GI by material AO. Terrain/custom pipelines bind after selecting their shader: built-in full terrain uses U6/tex21; compact tier0 terrain uses tex8 only without baked, detail or trace features. Generic custom/model samplers use tex13. Detach receivers, establish real GPU idle, then call shutdownAfterGpuIdle() before destroying the Device. Never substitute CPU frame age for completion. GPU scheduler completion is fence-backed. computeDispatchSucceeded() means commands were encoded, not that the GPU completed them. Partial checked uploads keep the result hidden and force coherent geometry recovery. Source rejection states are independent; updating the environment cannot restore rejected lights.

Add an opt-in dynamicGI object to a native renderbench scene: "dynamicGI": { "backend": "auto", "origin": [-12, 0, -6], "dimensions": [8, 4, 4], "spacing": 3, "samples": 32, "distance": 20, "cascades": 1, "scroll": false, "cpuBudgetMs": 2, "sunDirection": [0.35, 1, 0.55], "sunColor": [1, 0.96, 0.9], "sunIntensity": 3, "skyIntensity": 0 } auto uses compute only when device and scene limits allow it, otherwise retaining all captured geometry on CPU. gpu fails explicitly if unsupported; cpu forces the portable path. Sources are not silently truncated. Recipe point lights are converted from the renderer's stored sRGB representation back to linear transport. Environment colors above are already linear and are indirect-only; no implicit copy of direct sun/sky settings occurs. Geometry is split into spatial chunks of about one distance; the GPU path keeps resident only chunks a GI ray can reach (GiGpuResidencyPlanner), so a world above the 8192-triangle GPU budget stays on the GPU while the reachable part fits. cascades (1..3, GPU only) adds nested lattices around the same center, cascade k with spacing·2^k and distance·2^k; all share the one GI atlas (texture 13, U6 nine float4), a point uses the finest cascade that contains it and fades into the next one at its edge. scroll (GPU only) makes the cascades follow the update focus in whole cells with one cell of dead band: probes keep their world cell through a toroidal ring offset (U6 ring.xyz), only cells entering a cascade are recycled, zeroed on the GPU (the GI kernel with zero samples) and re-traced. They show no indirect light until traced, never stale light from another place. The resident geometry is planned for the outer cascade widened by half its size per side and re-planned when the cascade leaves that box. After the first full convergence the GI stays presented while probes update. The benchmark waits for initial convergence before timed frames and reports dynamicGiBackend, dynamicGiFallback, dynamicGiTriangles and dynamicGiConvergenceMs. It reattaches GI on every camera view. The benchmark rejects simultaneous probeGI/staticPointBounce because those recipes reuse the same sources. Its screen-space diffuse bounce is disabled while dynamicGI is active. Direct-light rendering and post-processing remain independent. Animated assets share one sampled pose between renderer, indirect GI and Luma shadows. The verification host holds that pose until its GI converges; it does not claim real-time animated transport latency. Submitted-frame timings exclude convergence-only updates, as recorded in lightingCadence. Editor integration is a separate stage.

All builds and compiler TMPDIR for this work live on KINGSTON, under /Volumes/KINGSTON/AIVERSE/Builds/.temp/lighting-completion-20261120. Run registered checks with ./run-tests.sh --no-build --build-dir <root>/build --filter '^lighting_' after building the selected targets. Enable AIVERSE_BUILD_HDR_TESTS, AIVERSE_BUILD_RENDERBENCH, AIVERSE_BUILD_TESTS; AIVERSE_VULKAN additionally builds real SPIR-V compilation tests. Actual Metal/desktop GL pixel tests cover model and terrain receivers, per-view reset, light removal/restoration and CPU/compute parity. Native host acceptance loads real glTF, verifies JSON completion and compares captured RGB, so native window exit code zero cannot hide a fixture failure. Vulkan backend and GI SPIR-V compile locally; Vulkan GPU execution is not verified on this Mac (no loader). Compact shader testing on desktop GL is not a GLES device performance claim. This is bounded first-bounce L1 interpolation, not multi-bounce path tracing, reflection GI, infinite-world streaming, probe relocation or a proof against all thin-wall light leaks. Performance and mobile/Vulkan hardware acceptance are separate gates; no production quality defaults were changed.

giModelGeometry(model, objectTransform, &pose) in GiModelGeometry.h captures opaque casters with rigid node animation, morph positions and normalized byte skin weights. It reuses worldMatrices / paletteMatrices; skin joint transforms are model-space, so the mesh node transform is not applied twice. Morph precedes skinning. Retain CPU vertices, indices, morph deltas and image samples through uploadModel(..., true) for models whose snapshots will be rebuilt after upload. Missing pose/morph data rejects instead of silently freezing the bind pose. Publish the result as a replacement chunk in GiChunkedGeometryBuilder; old snapshots retain their previous geometry for in-flight tracing. This adapter provides the snapshot, not scheduling or automatic host tracking. Alpha masks, transparent surfaces and Shader Graph vertex displacement are not represented by this opaque triangle approximation. Texture albedo uses bounded average sampling. The native AnimatedLightingGeometry host shares unchanged static chunks and rebuilds only animated caster chunks. It publishes monotonic revisions to both CPU/compute GI and Luma. Reports expose animatedLightingCasters, lightingGeometryRevision and lightingSnapshotTriangles. Geometry capacity errors reject the view; actors are never silently omitted to fit the GPU budget. bake:false preserves the asset's explicit caster exclusion. This fixed-workload host holds the selected pose while compute/convergence is pending, then renders that same pose; a game host must choose and measure its own update cadence.

The optional map renderLighting v1 block is validated by RenderLightingSettings. Studio Lighting controls support native save/undo/redo. RenderLightingRuntime uses the shared DynamicGiHost and LumaHost owners; the viewport renders its existing terrain/document proxies as PBR geometry. This is not full game-asset preview parity. The panel reports actual backend, convergence and fallback.

Dynamic GI texture13 is part of the Metal ICB fragment argument buffer; U6 is snapshotted with the other per-submission uniforms. Both CPU and GPU GI providers pass analytic pixel tests with actual GPU-encoded command submissions. This does not enable experimental ICB by default or imply whole-engine ICB performance.

tools/renderbench/lighting_release_acceptance.py --binary <arm64-renderbench> --scene <GI-scene.json> --output <KINGSTON-artifact-directory> records an OFF/ON/OFF sequence with 30 warmup and 120 measured frames, fixed camera/pose. CPU encode, CPU frame and GPU execution are reported separately from loading and GI convergence. It rejects non-Release/non-arm64/incomplete reports; window pacing must not be presented as FPS. Use --feature luma for direct lighting.

Models without virtual materials retain GI texture13/U6. When the material uses virtual sampling, its existing atlas/page-table and U6 remain unchanged; GI uses U7 and the first texture after the table (after alpha coverage when present). Shader Graph sources remain at 13+ for virtual materials and move to 14+ for nonvirtual GI materials. Resource overflow rejects the pipeline with an explicit diagnostic. Virtual-material + GI and graph + GI use ordinary CPU submission; experimental ICB retains its previously verified plain-PBR GI ABI. These fallbacks preserve the same GPU shading, not a second lighting solver. Vulkan GI uses the shared TextureResources compute ABI: buffers 12..15, storage image 0 and std140 uniform block 16, through bindComputeStorageTexture and dispatchChecked. It no longer defines a competing Vulkan compute backend. Terrain GLSL emits literal sampler names for the Vulkan binding translator. Prepared LENS terrain frames stage GI pipeline variants before publication; callbacks retain immutable texture bindings instead of capturing mutable owners. Source on GitHub: docs/dynamic-gi.md

h: Baked lighting (lightmaps, light probes, the light baker)
x: AIVERSE bakes global illumination itself: an offline CPU path tracer (engine/bake) writes lightmaps for static objects and the terrain plus a light probe grid for everything that moves. The runtime samples them in the lit shaders (GLSL + MSL) and mixes them with the realtime sun like Unity's mixed lighting. Owner: agent-lightbake.

Mark map lights that should be baked: "bake": "mixed" (stays realtime, its bounce is baked) or "bake": "baked" (only in the lightmap / probes; its realtime light and halo sprite switch off once a bake is loaded). MCP: light_add / light_update with bake. Editor → Графика → Запекание света: mode, density, samples, bounces, probes → Запечь. MCP: lightbake_set {quality: "preview"|"medium"|"high", mode, ...}, lightbake_bake {force?}, poll lightbake_status, lightbake_get, lightbake_clear. The result is maps/<map>.bake/ next to the map; the game client loads it when the map starts. Rebakes are skipped when nothing changed: the bake stores a 64-bit content hash of everything it used (geometry, materials, textures, transforms, sun / sky / lights, settings); lightbake_bake without force compares it first.

The bake captures what the Scene view draws with kDrawStatic (Renderer3D::DrawFlags): objects of types that cannot move (structure or speed 0), finished, alive, not flying, without entity fx. Every such model node is a lightmap receiver and an occluder. Anything else (units, projectiles) is lit by the probes. Other renderers can opt in by setting kDrawStatic on their ModelDraw. At runtime a model node finds its lightmap region by model path + node index + world matrix (quantized to 1/256), so no ids have to be stored in the map: an object drawn exactly where it was baked is lightmapped, a moved one falls back to probes. Animated nodes therefore are not lightmapped.

Models with a second UV set use it: glTF TEXCOORD_1, FBX second UV set (Unity's UV2; values in [0, 1]). Unskinned primitives only; stored in ModelVertex::joints as two unorm16 (engine/render/LightmapUv.h), so the vertex layout is unchanged. Otherwise the baker unwraps the mesh with xatlas (MIT, third_party/xatlas, pinned f700c7790aaa030e794b52ba7791a05c085faf0c) and writes <model>.lmuv next to the model; loadModel applies it from then on (it checks a hash of the source geometry, a stale sidecar is ignored with a warning). Commit the .lmuv files with the models. Each mesh has its own [0, 1] space; each placed node gets a region sized by texelsPerUnit × its world area, packed into power-of-two pages.

mode lightmap holds sun on static objects for indirect sky, bounces, emissive, baked-only lights realtime (shadow map) day/night cycles shadowmask (default) as indirect + sun visibility mask realtime, shadow = min(shadow map, mask) static shadows beyond the shadow distance and with shadows off subtractive everything incl. the direct sun baked; realtime shadows of dynamic objects darken it to shadowColor weak phones Dynamic objects always get the realtime sun plus probe ambient. The sky term is exact: an open floor bakes to the same ambient the realtime shader computes (mix(ground, sky, n.y * .5 + .5)), so lightmapped and realtime objects match where nothing occludes.

Renderer3D::setBakedQuality(Off | Low | High), default Low on phones (defaultBakedQualityFor), AIVERSE_BAKED=off|low|high overrides. Low: lightmaps + shadow mask, probes from the nearest probe (3 texel fetches per vertex). High: trilinear probes (24 fetches per vertex). Off: realtime only. Lightmaps cost one RGBM fetch (+ one mask fetch in shadowmask mode) per pixel on every tier.

engine/bake (host library aiverse_bake, also usable without the editor — see tests/bake): SceneBuilder loads models (CPU geometry), unwraps, converts materials (base colour × base texture for albedo, alpha test for masked foliage, emissive; unlit materials glow), adds a terrain mesh from a height function with planar lightmap UVs. Binned-SAH BVH, closest / any hit, alpha test. Per texel: cosine-weighted hemisphere paths (R2 sequence rotated per texel) with next-event estimation of the sun (soft, angle) and point / spot lights at every bounce, sky on miss; sun visibility mask (maskSamples); direct light of baked-only lights; optional AO; texels inside geometry (backface hits) are dropped and refilled by dilation; edge-aware à-trous denoiser on the indirect term. Probes: regular grid over the scene (probeSpacing, probeHeight above the floor, capped by maxProbes), uniform sphere sampling into ambient + gradient (irradiance(n) = a + B n), baked-only lights added analytically; probes inside geometry are refilled from neighbours. Multithreaded (threads, 0 = all cores). Every random stream is keyed by its texel / probe, so the output is bit-identical for any thread count (tested). Presets: preview (16 samples, 1 bounce, 2 texels/m), medium (64, 2, 4), high (256, 3, 8).

lightmap.json (version, hash, mode, RGBM range, pages, regions key -> [page, scale.xy, offset.xy], terrain region, probe grid, settings, stats), lm<i>.png RGBM pages (linear, range rgbmRange), mask<i>.png (shadowmask mode, r = sun visibility), probes.bin (float16 × 12 per probe). PNG and float16 keep the folder small and pack-friendly; the folder is plain content (rpak includes it like any other file). Settings live in the map's "bake" block.

Models: automatic (Renderer3D::drawModel, ModelShaders.h variants LIGHTMAP / PROBES). Terrain and other custom lit shaders: AIVERSE_GLSL_BAKED_TERRAIN(block, lmTex, maskTex) / AIVERSE_MSL_BAKED_TERRAIN (engine/render/BakedShaders.h) and Renderer3D::bindBakedTerrain(uniformSlot, lightmapSlot, maskSlot); the flat terrain (GameTerrainShaders.h) uses U3 + tex19 / tex20. The baker's terrain covers [0, w] × [0, h] of the map.

Before (realtime only) / after (shadowmask bake, AO 1 m, two "bake": "baked" lamps) / the decoded lightmap page (terrain region left, crystal tower and windmill regions top right): Bake: 0.5 s on 4 VM cores (medium: 64 samples, 2 bounces, 52k texels, 2475 probes); a second lightbake_bake reports "up to date" (hash unchanged).

No directional lightmaps (normal maps use the lightmap irradiance only), no baked specular. Albedo of the terrain in the bake is a constant (bounce colour from splat materials is not sampled); vertex colours are ignored in bounces. Planet terrain, sprites and procedural shapes (shape:* models of types without a model file, drawMesh) are not part of the bake: they neither receive lightmaps nor occlude; shape models are lit by the probes. A day/night cycle keeps baked indirect light fixed (use indirect mode). Importing Bakery / Unity lightmaps is not implemented (rebake with the engine's baker; UV2 is read). Metal (MSL) variants are written but compiled only on macOS/iOS builds. Source on GitHub: docs/lightbake.md
